title: observ-infra silently drops PostgreSQL/RKE2/Rancher/mosip-infra-repo variables set in aws.tfvars
content:
Problem description:
## Problem
In `terraform/implementations/aws/observ-infra/aws.tfvars`, 9 variables are set with real values but are never declared anywhere in the observ-infra Terraform chain (`terraform/implementations/aws/observ-infra` → `terraform/observ-infra` → `terraform/observ-infra/aws` → `terraform/modules/aws`):

- `enable_postgresql_setup`
- `postgresql_version`
- `storage_device`
- `mount_point`
- `postgresql_port`
- `rke2_version`
- `rancher_ui_version`
- `mosip_infra_repo_url`
- `mosip_infra_branch`

`terraform plan`/`apply` only emits a `Warning: Value for undeclared variable` for each — it doesn't fail — so the values are silently discarded and the shared `terraform/modules/aws` module falls back to its own defaults instead. Worse, `terraform/observ-infra/aws/main.tf` hardcoded `enable_postgresql_setup = false` in the module call, so even setting it to `true` in `aws.tfvars` had zero effect — PostgreSQL setup could never be enabled for an observability deployment regardless of configuration.

`rke2_version` and `rancher_ui_version` were declared at the innermost layer (`terraform/observ-infra/aws/variables.tf`) but not at the two outer layers, so any override in `aws.tfvars` never actually reached them either — only their hardcoded defaults were ever used.

## Fix
- Declare all 9 variables at every layer of the observ-infra chain, with defaults matching the main infra chain (`enable_postgresql_setup` defaults to `false` to preserve today's observ-infra behavior for anyone not opting in).
- Replace the hardcoded `enable_postgresql_setup = false` with `var.enable_postgresql_setup` in `terraform/observ-infra/aws/main.tf`.
- Add a `terraform test` (mock provider) verifying the `postgresql-setup` submodule's `count` gate (`enable_postgresql_setup && nginx_node_ebs_volume_size_2 > 0`) behaves correctly in all three states.

## Related PRs
Will be linked once opened against `demo` and `develop`.

title: Make Route53 DNS record creation optional (support non-Route53 DNS providers)
content:
Problem description:
## Problem
The AWS infra Terraform (`mosip/infra`) hard-requires a Route53 hosted zone (`zone_id`) and always writes `aws_route53_record` resources for every MOSIP subdomain. This means the module cannot be used cleanly when a domain's authoritative DNS is hosted elsewhere (Azure DNS, Cloudflare, GoDaddy, etc.) — Route53 is not optional today.

## Solution
Add an `enable_route53_records` toggle (default `true`, so existing deployments are unaffected):
- When `true` (default): behavior is unchanged — Route53 records are created automatically as before.
- When `false`: all infrastructure (EC2, K8s, NGINX, security groups) is still created, but no Route53 records are written. The operator creates the equivalent A/CNAME records manually in whatever DNS provider they use, following the same `api`/`api-internal` + subdomain structure the module would otherwise create.

NGINX vhost/cert configuration (`CLUSTER_ENV_DOMAIN`, `MOSIP_PUBLIC_DOMAIN_LIST`) is unaffected either way, since it's derived from input variables rather than the created Route53 resource.

## Related PR
mosip/infra#294

title: Blocker 2 - Cluster import without handing out Rancher admin
content:
Problem description:
**Problem:** Import currently needs a Rancher admin to generate the registration URL; you don't want to give teams admin.

**Execution steps**

1. Keep import Terraform-driven (enable_rancher_import=true + RANCHER_IMPORT_URL) so teams never log into Rancher as admin to import.
2. Generate the registration token programmatically: DevOps creates a Rancher API token (or a scoped service account) once; a small step calls the Rancher API (/v3/clusterregistrationtokens) to mint the import URL per new cluster and feeds it to Terraform as a secret/var.
3. Store the Rancher API token as a repo/org secret used only inside the import step; teams trigger the workflow but never see admin creds.
4. Validate the regex guard in [rke2-cluster/main.tf](https://github.com/mosip/mosip-infra/issues/terraform/modules/aws/rke2-cluster/main.tf) (RANCHER_IMPORT_URL format) still matches API-generated URLs; relax/extend regex if hostname differs.

**Challenges:** API token is powerful (scope it tightly, rotate); regex validation may reject valid URLs; import idempotency on re-runs; cattle-cluster-agent DNS patch already handled in TF.

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: As per the request we have created a workflow which will create a cluster and import the cluster url to our dsf file 

The automated flow replaces that manual step:
- Terraform workflow calls `.github/scripts/rancher-register-cluster.sh`
- The script uses a scoped Rancher API token to find or create the cluster and mint the import URL
- The workflow sets TF_VAR_rancher_import_url and TF_VAR_enable_rancher_import
- During RKE2 provisioning, Ansible runs the import command on the control plane (once)

Important: Rancher itself must already exist. Deploy observ-infra first (or use an existing Rancher management cluster). This guide covers importing the downstream infra cluster only.

title: IStio Circuit breaking R&D [ https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/MOSIP-42535]
content:
Problem description:
### Description

IStio Circuit breaking R&D

### Purpose

Can we do this for the call we have between minio and packet manager?

Also the same for anyone calling packet manager

Then for key manager

And then for audit and continues…

 

Limits will check with @vishwa-vyom 

### Pre-requisites

IStio Circuit breaking R&D

### Basic Flow

IStio Circuit breaking R&D

### Alternate Flows

IStio Circuit breaking R&D

### Scenarios

_No response_

### Data Fields

_No response_

### Business Rules (With Audit)

_No response_

### Acceptance Criteria

Initial Circuit Breaker Setup & Validation
What We Did
Deployed a tight DestinationRule for keymanager in the keymanager namespace, deployed Fortio inside the same namespace with Istio sidecar injection, set up two monitoring terminals, and fired the first 60s load test at max QPS with 10 concurrent workers.

Findings
Circuit breaker fired correctly — 55.1% of 19,420 requests were rejected as 503 UO

UO (Upstream Overflow) is the Envoy signal confirming circuit breaker fired at the proxy layer — the app never saw those requests

503 rejections had near-zero latency (P50: 0ms, P95: 0ms) — Envoy shed load instantly without touching keymanager

maxRequestsPerConnection: 1 was confirmed active — 19,437 sockets opened vs 10 for keepalive, one TCP connection per request

This cluster uses istiocustom.* telemetry format — standard upstream_rq_pending_overflow grep returns nothing; correct signal is response_flags.UO in istiocustom metrics

Terminal 2 watch command must grep response_flags.UO not Envoy native stats for this cluster

keymanager pod stayed healthy throughout — 44.9% of requests got clean 200 responses with stable latency

Protocol Investigation & Targeted Isolation Tests
What We Did
Investigated whether using both http1MaxPendingRequests and http2MaxRequests together in the DR was realistic, determined the actual protocol via istioctl proxy-config, then ran three targeted tests each isolating one circuit breaker property, followed by production DR validation on both HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2.

Findings
Protocol:

keymanager uses useDownstreamProtocolConfig — Envoy mirrors whatever protocol the downstream client speaks

Both http1MaxPendingRequests and http2MaxRequests being set is correct for this config since different callers may use different protocols

Sidecar-to-sidecar mTLS uses TLS 1.2/1.3 with ALPN but the HTTP protocol version depends on the caller

Test 1 — maxConnections in isolation:

maxConnections: 5 with 10 workers produced zero 503s

maxConnections alone never trips the circuit breaker — it only queues excess requests

With maxRequestsPerConnection: 0 (keepalive), sockets dropped from 19,437 → 10 (perfect keepalive)

QPS jumped from 586 → 866 — keepalive eliminated TCP setup overhead per request

maxConnections is a concurrency throttle, not a rejection mechanism

Test 2 — http1MaxPendingRequests in isolation:

Adding http1MaxPendingRequests: 2 back immediately restored 56.7% 503 UO rejections

Reproduced original test almost exactly — confirmed http1MaxPendingRequests is the primary circuit breaker trigger for HTTP/1.1

Requires maxRequestsPerConnection: 1 to sustain pressure — without it connections stay open and the queue never fills

maxConnections and http1MaxPendingRequests must work together to trip the breaker

Test 3 — http2MaxRequests with forced HTTP/2:

HTTP/2 was successfully negotiated — confirmed by 10 sockets serving 14,026 requests via multiplexing

100% of requests failed with 503 even with http2MaxRequests: 200 (production value)

Failure was not a circuit breaker trip — it was keymanager rejecting h2c at the application layer

Dominant flag was URX (upstream retry limit exceeded) not UO (upstream overflow) — critical distinction

New flag URX,UR appeared — upstream reset the connection, confirming app-level rejection

keymanager does not support h2c (HTTP/2 cleartext) — Spring Boot requires explicit configuration for h2c

http2MaxRequests is a dead config for keymanager today

Production DR Validation:

HTTP/1.1: 100% 200s, zero 503s, 971 QPS — highest throughput across all tests

HTTP/2: 100% 503s — confirmed http2MaxRequests irrelevant regardless of limit value

maxRequestsPerConnection: 0 delivered perfect keepalive — 10 sockets for 58,289 requests

Circuit breaker fired correctly — 55.1% of 19,420 requests were rejected as 503 UO

UO (Upstream Overflow) is the Envoy signal confirming circuit breaker fired at the proxy layer — the app never saw those requests

503 rejections had near-zero latency (P50: 0ms, P95: 0ms) — Envoy shed load instantly without touching keymanager

maxRequestsPerConnection: 1 was confirmed active — 19,437 sockets opened vs 10 for keepalive, one TCP connection per request

This cluster uses istiocustom.* telemetry format — standard upstream_rq_pending_overflow grep returns nothing; correct signal is response_flags.UO in istiocustom metrics

Test 1 — maxConnections in isolation:

maxConnections is a concurrency throttle, not a rejection mechanism

title: Add generate-upgrade-init.sh tool to automate Keycloak upgrade diff generation
content:
Problem description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

During MOSIP Keycloak upgrades (e.g. v1.2.x → v1.3.x), operators must manually compare the live Keycloak `mosip` realm state against the target `values.yaml` to identify what realm roles, clients, protocol mappers, service account roles, and client scopes need to be added or removed. This process requires deep familiarity with the Keycloak Admin API and the MOSIP `keycloak-init` Helm chart schema, is error-prone, and risks either missing required additions or flagging country-specific custom clients for deletion.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add a new script `tools/generate-upgrade-init.sh` to the `mosip/keycloak` repository that automates the diff and generates a minimal `upgrade-init-values.yaml` ready to apply via `helm install`.

**What the script does:**
- Authenticates read-only against the live Keycloak instance (GET only — nothing is modified)
- Fetches the target `values.yaml` from a GitHub release tag (or a local file for air-gapped environments)
- Diffs the live realm state against the target across all entity types:
  - Realm roles (added / removed)
  - Client scopes (added / removed)
  - Clients (added / removed / updated — delta only)
  - Per-client: service account realm roles, service account client roles, protocol mappers, assigned client scopes, and config fields
- Emits a **minimal** `upgrade-init-values.yaml` containing only what needs to be added or changed — unchanged clients are omitted entirely
- Appends actionable `kcadm.sh` removal commands (as comments) for everything that must be removed manually
- Writes a `# GENERATION_COMPLETE` marker so operators can verify the file is complete before applying

**Key safety properties:**
- Passwords never on the command line (`--kc-pass` is explicitly rejected); use `export KC_PASS=...` or `--from-k8s`
- `--from-k8s` reads credentials directly from the cluster (`keycloak-env-vars` ConfigMap + `keycloak` Secret)
- Secure `mktemp` work directory (mode 700); wiped on any exit
- Partial output files auto-deleted on error
- Paginated client fetch — no 200-client cap
- Pure Python `urllib` for all Keycloak API calls (no `subprocess curl` per call)
- Keycloak built-in clients (`account`, `broker`, `realm-management`, etc.) and built-in roles (`default-roles-*`, `uma_protection`) excluded from diff automatically
- Country-specific custom clients (present in live but absent from target and not in `clientSecrets`) flagged as `[INFO]` — never flagged for removal

**Usage (recommended):**
```bash
./tools/generate-upgrade-init.sh \
  --from-k8s \
  --kc-url    https://iam.your-domain.com/auth \
  --namespace keycloak \
  --target    v1.3.0 \
  --out       upgrade-init-values.yaml
```

**Apply output:**
```bash
helm -n keycloak install keycloak-upgrade-init mosip/keycloak-init \
  --set frontend=https://$IAM_HOST/auth \
  -f upgrade-init-values.yaml --version <chart-version>
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **Manual diff**: Current approach. Requires operator expertise, takes 1–2 hours per upgrade, and is prone to missed additions or incorrect removals of custom clients.
- **Full re-run of keycloak-init with the new values.yaml**: Re-applies all clients unconditionally. For idempotent adds this is safe, but it overwrites any post-init manual changes and does not handle removals.
- **Keycloak export + diff**: Exporting realm JSON and diffing against the target is noisy (thousands of lines of built-in config) and not directly consumable by `keycloak-init`.

**Additional context**

- Validated against MOSIP `keycloak-init` values.yaml schema for v1.2.0.1 and v1.3.0
- MOSIP-specific conventions hard-coded and verified: `master` auth realm, `oidc-usermodel-attribute` mapper filter, `client_name_secret` naming (28/28 consistent)
- Requires: `kubectl` (if `--from-k8s`), `curl`, `python3`, `python3-yaml`
- Air-gapped environments: use `--target-file /path/to/values.yaml` instead of `--target <git-tag>`

title: [MOSIP-44621] Instead of esignet-globalcm migrate to domainConfig ,this changes required only for helmsman automation
content:
Problem description:
## Parent Issue

mosip/mosip-infra#1790

## Summary

Replace the \`esignet-global\` ConfigMap approach with a \`domainConfig\` map passed directly as Helm values. This allows domain configuration to be injected as individual env vars via a template loop (\`{{- range \$key, \$val := .Values.domainConfig }}\`), removing the hard dependency on a pre-existing ConfigMap in the namespace.

## Affected Repos

| Repo | Feature Branch | PR |
|------|---------------|-----|
| mosip/esignet | \`feature/domain-config\` | mosip/esignet#1988 |
| mosip/esignet-signup | \`feature/domain-config\` | mosip/esignet-signup#935 |
| mosip/esignet-mock-services | \`feature/domain-config\` | mosip/esignet-mock-services#589 |
| mosip/mosip-onboarding | \`feature/domain-config\` | mosip/mosip-onboarding#195 |

## Changes Done in Upstream Helm Charts

- [x] \`helm/*/templates/deployment.yaml\` — added \`domainConfig\` range loop in env section
- [x] \`helm/*/values.yaml\` — removed \`MOSIP_ESIGNET_HOST\` / \`MOSIP_SIGNUP_HOST\` from \`extraEnvVars\`; removed \`envFrom: esignet-global\` from initContainers; added \`domainConfig: {}\`
- [x] \`helm/partner-onboarder/templates/jobs.yaml\` — added \`domainConfig\` range loop
- [x] \`deploy/domain-values.yaml\` — new sample file with all domain keys (\`INSTALLATION_DOMAIN\`, \`MOSIP_VERSION\`, all hosts)
- [x] \`deploy/esignet/install.sh\` + \`deploy/install-prereq.sh\` — updated to use \`domain-values.yaml\`

## Why

\`extraEnvVarsCM: esignet-global\` requires a ConfigMap to exist in every namespace before Helm install. This causes ordering issues and namespace-specific copy steps in hook scripts. The \`domainConfig\` map merges cleanly with \`-f\` values files and eliminates the ConfigMap dependency entirely — each release carries its own domain values.

Discussion and resolution:
[bhumi46]: PR merged, hence closing

title: [MOSIP-44613] Replace hardcoded DB ports with ${db_port} placeholder across all DSFs and workflows
content:
Problem description:
> **Sub-task of**: mosip/mosip-infra#1790 (MOSIP-41302: Rapid Deployment support for eSignet deployment with MOSIP)
> **Branch**: `MOSIP-44613` in `mosip/infra`

---

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

PostgreSQL port values (`5432` for eSignet standalone, `5433` for MOSIP platform profiles) were hardcoded in all DSF files. Changing the port for an environment required editing multiple files across all profiles — error-prone and inconsistent with the runtime variable substitution pattern already used for `${domain_name}`, `${env_name}`, and other config values.

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Replace all hardcoded DB port values with a `${db_port}` placeholder following the exact same pattern as `${domain_name}`:

- **DSF files**: `5432` / `5433` → `${db_port}` (both unquoted integer and quoted string forms)
- **Workflow inputs**: add `db_port` input (type: string, required: false) to `helmsman_external.yml`, `helmsman_esignet.yml`, `helmsman_mosip.yml`, `helmsman_testrigs.yml`
- **Workflow job-level `env:`**: add `db_port: ${{ github.event.inputs.db_port || vars.DB_PORT }}` to each workflow's deploy job so Helmsman inherits it as an env var and resolves `${db_port}` at parse time

**Files changed** (10 DSFs + 4 workflows):

| Profile | DSF files |
|---|---|
| `esignet` standalone | `external-dsf.yaml`, `testrigs-dsf.yaml` |
| `mosip-platform-java11` | `external-dsf.yaml`, `esignet-dsf.yaml`, `mosip-dsf.yaml`, `testrigs-dsf.yaml` |
| `mosip-platform-java21` | `external-dsf.yaml`, `esignet-dsf.yaml`, `mosip-dsf.yaml`, `testrigs-dsf.yaml` |

Workflows updated: `helmsman_external.yml`, `helmsman_esignet.yml`, `helmsman_mosip.yml`, `helmsman_testrigs.yml`

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Keeping profile-specific default values (5432 / 5433) in the workflow and only overriding at dispatch — rejected because it would require per-profile conditional logic in the workflow and still wouldn't let operators override the port without editing the workflow file.

---

**Additional context**

- Set `vars.DB_PORT = 5432` for eSignet standalone environments and `vars.DB_PORT = 5433` for MOSIP platform environments under Repository → Settings → Environments → `<branch-name>` → Variables.
- Falls back to `vars.DB_PORT` on push-triggered runs (same fallback pattern as `vars.DOMAIN_NAME`).
- 57 replacements across 10 DSF files; zero hardcoded port values remain.

title: [MOSIP-44613] Documentation — eSignet multi-namespace deployment (esignet standalone + MOSIP platform profiles)
content:
Problem description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The `docs/` guides were written for the original single-namespace eSignet deployment. After the MOSIP-44613 changes, the existing guides no longer reflect the actual deployment flow for either the **eSignet standalone** profile or the **MOSIP platform** profiles (java11/java21). New users following the current docs will encounter missing steps, incorrect secret names, and an outdated workflow diagram.

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Update the following guides under `docs/` to cover both deployment profiles:

---

### Profile 1 — eSignet Standalone (`Helmsman/dsf/esignet/`)

**`docs/ONBOARDING_GUIDE.md`**
- Add multi-namespace eSignet overview: `esignet` (plugin 1 — mock), `esignet-cre` (plugin 2 — mosip-identity, remote CRE env), `esignet-qa11` (plugin 2 — mosip-identity, remote QA11 env), `esignet-sunbird` (plugin 3 — sunbird-rc)
- Add deployment sequence steps: Signup (step 7) and Testrigs (step 8)
- Document `GH_INFRA_PAT` secret requirement (`actions:write` scope) for esignet → signup auto-trigger chain
- List all new required secrets: `ESIGNET_{CRE,QA11,SUNBIRD}_CAPTCHA_*`, `CRE/QA11_KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `CRE/QA11_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `MOSIP_SIGNUP_CAPTCHA_*`

**`docs/DSF_CONFIGURATION_GUIDE.md`**
- Document updated `external-dsf.yaml`: keycloak-init in keycloak ns (priority -11), per-namespace postgres-init entries with `su` block + `defaultDb` fields, MinIO re-deploy password pass-through
- Document `esignet-dsf.yaml` 4-instance layout: priority order table, per-namespace plugin values files, PMS gateway preInstall requirement, onboarder selection (MISP vs mock-RP)
- Add `signup-dsf.yaml` section: component list, all-disabled-by-default behaviour, prerequisites checklist (postgres-init-signup, Redis, Kafka, Keycloak label guard)
- Add `testrigs-dsf.yaml` section: apitestrig per namespace, signup uitestrig, sequential cronjob trigger via `trigger-test-jobs-esignet.sh`

**`docs/WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md`**
- Add `helmsman_signup.yml`: inputs, `esignet-dsf=completed` namespace label guard, manual vs auto-trigger modes
- Update `helmsman_esignet.yml`: multi-namespace secret inputs, `workflow-caller` job, auto-dispatch chain to signup
- Update workflow diagram (`profile-based-deployment.drawio`): external → esignet → signup auto-trigger; testrigs as manual final step

**`docs/SECRET_GENERATION_GUIDE.md`**
- Add per-namespace captcha secrets (`ESIGNET_CRE_CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, etc.): how to generate, where to store (Environment secrets, not Repository secrets)
- Add `CRE/QA11_KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD`: purpose (REST API client-secrets fetch from remote Keycloak)
- Add `CRE/QA11_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`: purpose (postgres-postgresql-cre/qa11 secret in esignet-cre/qa11 ns)
- Add `GH_INFRA_PAT`: scope requirements (`actions:write`) and creation steps

---

### Profile 2 — MOSIP Platform (`Helmsman/dsf/mosip-platform-java11/` and `mosip-platform-java21/`)

**`docs/ONBOARDING_GUIDE.md`**
- Add profile selection guide: when to use esignet standalone vs mosip-platform-java11 vs mosip-platform-java21
- Document full MOSIP platform deployment sequence: base-infra → observ-infra → infra → external → mosip → esignet (platform profile)
- Document differences between java11 and java21 profiles (chart versions, JVM flags)

**`docs/DSF_CONFIGURATION_GUIDE.md`**
- Add `mosip-dsf.yaml` overview: 22 namespaces, 50+ microservices, deployment order
- Document `esignet-dsf.yaml` differences under mosip-platform profiles vs standalone (no signup auto-trigger, no parallel namespaces)
- Document `keycloak-init-values.yaml` (2 clients only) vs `keycloak-esignet-init-values.yaml` (full 5-client realm) — do not mix

**`docs/WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md`**
- Document `helmsman_external.yml` → `helmsman_mosip.yml` auto-trigger chain (push events: only first detected profile triggers MOSIP dispatch)
- Add note: for multiple profiles use `workflow_dispatch`, not push

---

### Common Updates (both profiles)

**`docs/GLOSSARY.md`**
- Add: `esignet-cre`, `esignet-qa11`, `esignet-sunbird` namespace definitions and plugin mappings
- Add: `esignet-domain-config` — per-namespace CM with 10 domain keys; contrast with `global` CM used in MOSIP platform profile
- Add: `esignet-config-server-share`, `keycloak-client-secrets-{cre,qa11}`, `trigger-test-jobs-esignet.sh`
- Add: MISP onboarder vs mock-RP onboarder — when to enable each
- Add: signup stack — kernel + signup-service + signup-ui component group
- Add: `postgres-init 0.0.1-develop` vs `12.0.1` — why the develop chart is required

**`docs/esignet_README.md`**
- Update quick-start to reference both profiles and the 4-namespace standalone model
- Add plugin selection guide per namespace and corresponding onboarder to enable
- Add signup deployment step (esignet standalone only)

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Creating separate docs for each profile — rejected in favour of updating existing guides with profile-specific sections to avoid duplicating the shared deployment context (Terraform, secrets, GitHub Actions setup).

---

**Additional context**

- `profile-based-deployment.drawio` diagram needs updating for: signup auto-trigger chain, 4-namespace esignet standalone structure, and mosip-platform deployment chain.

title: [MOSIP-44613] Add plugin, keycloak, config-server and testrig values files under Helmsman/utils/
content:
Problem description:
> **Sub-task of**: mosip/mosip-infra#1790 (MOSIP-41302: Rapid Deployment support for eSignet deployment with MOSIP)
> **Branch**: `MOSIP-44613` in `mosip/infra`

---

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The eSignet standalone profile had no committed values files for per-namespace plugin configuration, Keycloak realm setup, Spring Cloud Config Server, or testrigs — making it impossible to deploy any namespace beyond the single default `esignet` instance via the DSF without inline `set:` overrides.

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add the following new values files under `Helmsman/utils/`:

**Plugin values (per namespace):**
- `esignet-plugin-values.yaml` — Plugin 1 (mock): captcha `secretKeyRef` active; plugin 2/3 sections commented out
- `esignet-cre-plugin-values.yaml` — Plugin 2 (mosip-identity): captcha + all IDA service URLs active; `SOFTHSM_ESIGNET_SECURITY_PIN` references `esignet-softhsm-cre` secret; full `extraEnvVars` list override
- `esignet-qa11-plugin-values.yaml` — Plugin 2 (mosip-identity): identical to cre; `SOFTHSM_ESIGNET_SECURITY_PIN` references `esignet-softhsm-qa11`
- `esignet-sunbird-plugin-values.yaml` — Plugin 3 (sunbird-rc): captcha + sunbird registry URL + `NoOpKeyBinder`; `SOFTHSM_ESIGNET_SECURITY_PIN` references `esignet-softhsm-sunbird`
- `esignet-values.yaml` — shared base values for all 4 eSignet instances

**Keycloak init values:**
- `keycloak-esignet-init-values.yaml` — full mosip realm: `realm_config`, 30+ roles, 6 client scopes, 5 clients (`mosip-pms-client`, `mpartner-default-auth`, `mosip-ida-client`, `mosip-deployment-client`, `mpartner-default-mobile`). Authoritative source for eSignet standalone Keycloak realm config.
- `keycloak-signup-init-values.yaml` — mosip-signup-client realm configuration

**Config-server values:**
- `config-server-esignet-values.yaml` — Spring Cloud Config Server for eSignet standalone: `gitRepo: esignet-config @ develop`; all env vars use `configMapKeyRef`/`secretKeyRef`; domain values from `esignet-domain-config` CM

**SoftHSM values (per namespace):**
- `softhsm-esignet-cre-values.yaml`, `softhsm-esignet-qa11-values.yaml`, `softhsm-esignet-sunbird-values.yaml` — independent PVC and pin secret per namespace (identical config, separate files give each namespace isolation)

**Testrig values:**
- `esignet-apitestrig-values.yaml` — shared values for all 4 esignet apitestrig releases: `mosipdev/apitest-esignet:develop` image; `extraEnvVarsCM: [s3, keycloak-host, db, apitestrig, esignet-domain-config]`
- `esignet-signup-apitestrig-values.yaml` — `mosipid/apitest-esignet-signup:1.2.2` image
- `signup-uitestrig-values.yaml` — `mosipdev/uitest-signup:develop` image; `extraEnvVarsCM: [s3, keycloak-host, db, uitestrig]`

**Files**: `esignet-plugin-values.yaml`, `esignet-{cre,qa11,sunbird}-plugin-values.yaml`, `esignet-values.yaml`, `keycloak-esignet-init-values.yaml`, `keycloak-signup-init-values.yaml`, `config-server-esignet-values.yaml`, `softhsm-esignet-{cre,qa11,sunbird}-values.yaml`, `esignet-apitestrig-values.yaml`, `esignet-signup-apitestrig-values.yaml`, `signup-uitestrig-values.yaml`

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Inline `set:` overrides in the DSF for all plugin env vars — rejected: the `extraEnvVars` list is replaced on `helm -f` merge, so partial overrides wipe all `configMapKeyRef`/`secretKeyRef` entries. Full overrides via a committed values file are the only safe approach for list-type values.

---

**Additional context**

`keycloak-esignet-init-values.yaml` must stay in sync with `esignet/deploy/keycloak/keycloak-init-values.yaml` — it is the authoritative eSignet standalone realm config. Do not confuse with `keycloak-init-values.yaml` (Java 11/21 MOSIP platform profiles only, 2 clients, no `realm_config`). SoftHSM values files must NOT use `fullnameOverride` — it renames the share ConfigMap too, breaking downstream consumers.

title: [MOSIP-44613] Update GitHub Actions workflows — new helmsman_signup.yml, multi-secret esignet workflow, auto-trigger chain
content:
Problem description:
> **Sub-task of**: mosip/mosip-infra#1790 (MOSIP-41302: Rapid Deployment support for eSignet deployment with MOSIP)
> **Branch**: `MOSIP-44613` in `mosip/infra`

---

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

There was no GitHub Actions workflow for the Signup stack. The eSignet workflow did not inject the secrets needed by per-namespace hooks (captcha keys for cre/qa11/sunbird, remote Keycloak admin passwords, remote postgres passwords). There was no automated trigger chain from eSignet → Signup. And the external workflow did not preserve MinIO's existing root password on re-deploy.

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**

**New workflow — `helmsman_signup.yml`:**
- Accepts `domain_name`, `profile`, and `env_name` inputs (falls back to GitHub environment vars)
- Guards against running before eSignet is ready: fails fast if `esignet-dsf=completed` namespace label is absent
- Injects `MOSIP_SIGNUP_CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` / `MOSIP_SIGNUP_CAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` secrets as env vars for `signup-service-preinstall.sh`
- Supports manual trigger, push-triggered runs on signup DSF changes, and auto-dispatch from `helmsman_esignet.yml`

**Updated `helmsman_esignet.yml`:**
- Add `workflow-caller` job that dispatches `helmsman_signup.yml` via GitHub API when `profile=esignet` and deploy succeeds (requires `GH_INFRA_PAT` environment secret with `actions:write` scope)
- Inject all per-namespace captcha secrets: `ESIGNET_CRE_CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `ESIGNET_CRE_CAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`, `ESIGNET_QA11_CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `ESIGNET_QA11_CAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`, `ESIGNET_SUNBIRD_CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `ESIGNET_SUNBIRD_CAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`
- Inject remote env credentials: `CRE_KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `QA11_KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `CRE_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `QA11_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`
- Inject mock-RP private keys: `MOCK_RELYING_PARTY_CLIENT_PRIVATE_KEY`, `MOCK_RELYING_PARTY_JWE_PRIVATE_KEY`

**Updated `helmsman_external.yml`:**
- Add "Mask sensitive secrets" step: fetches existing MinIO root password from the `minio` secret and exports as `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD` via `$GITHUB_ENV`; prevents Bitnami PASSWORDS ERROR on re-deploy

**Updated `helmsman_testrigs.yml`:**
- Reference updated `testrigs-dsf.yaml` for eSignet standalone profile

**Files**: `.github/workflows/helmsman_signup.yml` (new), `.github/workflows/helmsman_esignet.yml`, `.github/workflows/helmsman_external.yml`, `.github/workflows/helmsman_testrigs.yml`

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Adding signup deployment as a final step inside `helmsman_esignet.yml` — rejected: separate workflow allows re-deploying signup independently without re-running the full eSignet stack, and preserves the ability to deploy signup on its own via `workflow_dispatch`.

---

**Additional context**

The `workflow-caller` job requires `GH_INFRA_PAT` Environment secret (not Repository secret) with `actions:write` scope. Without it, eSignet deploys successfully but the signup auto-trigger silently fails. The signup workflow validates the `esignet-dsf=completed` label as a guard against running before eSignet pods are healthy.

title: [MOSIP-44613] Add MISP and mock-RP onboarder hooks (replace old partner-onboarder)
content:
Problem description:
> **Sub-task of**: mosip/mosip-infra#1790 (MOSIP-41302: Rapid Deployment support for eSignet deployment with MOSIP)
> **Branch**: `MOSIP-44613` in `mosip/infra`

---

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The old `esignet-partner-onboarder` and `esignet-demo-oidc-partner-onboarder` hooks were monolithic scripts that combined MISP onboarding and mock-RP onboarding into a single flow, could not be run independently, and did not handle Istio injection management (causing onboarder Job pods to hang with sidecars and never reach `Completed` state).

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Replace old partner-onboarder hooks with two dedicated, independently-runnable onboarder pairs:

**MISP onboarder** (for plugin 2 — mosip-identity only):
- `esignet-misp-onboarder-preinstall.sh` — disables Istio injection on esignet ns; deletes stale `esignet-onboarder-config` CM + `esignet-onboarder-secrets` secret; copies `keycloak-env-vars`/`keycloak`/`keycloak-client-secrets` from keycloak ns; builds `s3` secret with `s3-user-secret` key from MinIO root-password; deletes `onboarder-namespace` CM; waits for esignet ready
- `esignet-misp-onboarder-postinstall.sh` — checks job completion; re-enables Istio injection; restarts `esignet-config-server` first (reloads MISP key from secret), then restarts `esignet` to pick up updated config

**Mock-RP onboarder** (for plugin 1 — mock, and plugin 3 — sunbird-rc):
- `esignet-mock-rp-onboarder-preinstall.sh` — disables Istio injection on esignet ns; copies `keycloak-env-vars` CM + `keycloak`/`keycloak-client-secrets` secrets from keycloak ns; builds `s3` secret from MinIO root-password; deletes `onboarder-namespace` CM; waits for esignet ready
- `esignet-mock-rp-onboarder-postinstall.sh` — checks job completion; re-enables Istio injection; restarts `mock-relying-party-service`

**Removed**: `esignet-partner-onboarder-preinstall.sh`, `esignet-partner-onboarder-postinstall.sh`, `esignet-demo-oidc-partner-onboarder-preinstall.sh`, `esignet-demo-oidc-partner-onboarder-postinstall.sh`

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Keeping a combined onboarder script with a flag to select MISP vs mock-RP — rejected: the post-install actions differ (MISP restarts config-server + esignet; mock-RP restarts mock-relying-party-service) and the pre-install cleanup differs (MISP deletes MISP-specific artifacts). Separate scripts are cleaner and independently testable.

---

**Additional context**

- Istio injection is disabled before the onboarder Job runs and re-enabled after — Job pods with Istio sidecars never reach `Completed` state, which blocks the postInstall hook from firing.
- Both onboarders are disabled by default in the DSF; enable the one matching the active plugin.
- `esignet-misp-onboarder` runs at priority `-6` (before mock-RP onboarder at `-5`) so the MISP license key is in place before mock-RP tries to connect.

title: [MOSIP-44613] Add per-namespace hook scripts — config-server, cre/qa11/sunbird preinstalls, keycloak-init fan-out
content:
Problem description:
> **Sub-task of**: mosip/mosip-infra#1790 (MOSIP-41302: Rapid Deployment support for eSignet deployment with MOSIP)
> **Branch**: `MOSIP-44613` in `mosip/infra`

---

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Supporting 4 parallel eSignet namespaces requires namespace-specific preinstall hooks that: create isolated `esignet-domain-config` ConfigMaps (with different `mosip-esignet-host` per namespace), patch `postgres-config` with per-namespace DB names/users, fetch keycloak client secrets from remote CRE/QA11 environments, and propagate the config-server share CM to all non-primary namespaces.

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**

New and updated hook scripts:

**Config-server hooks:**
- `config-server-esignet-setup.sh` — creates esignet ns + Istio label; copies db/redis secrets; creates `esignet-domain-config` CM with 10 keys from `${domain_name}`; pre-creates `esignet-misp-onboarder-key` placeholder
- `config-server-esignet-postinstall.sh` — copies `esignet-config-server-share` CM from `esignet` ns to `esignet-cre`, `esignet-qa11`, `esignet-sunbird`

**Keycloak-init hooks:**
- `esignet-preinstall-keycloak-init.sh` — deletes old releases (migration cleanup); fetches 5 client secrets from keycloak ns for Helmsman `${VAR}` substitution
- `esignet-postinstall-keycloak-init.sh` — fans out `keycloak-host` CM, `keycloak-env-vars` CM, `keycloak` secret, `keycloak-client-secrets` secret from keycloak ns to all 4 esignet namespaces

**Per-namespace eSignet preinstalls:**
- `esignet-cre-preinstall.sh` — sets `ESIGNET_NS=esignet-cre`; calls base `esignet-preinstall.sh`; creates namespace-specific `esignet-domain-config` with CRE-specific hosts (`esignet-mosipid-cre.${domain_name}`); patches `postgres-config` with `mosip_esignet_cre`/`esignetuser_cre`; creates `esignet-misp-onboarder-key` placeholder; creates CRE captcha secret; creates `postgres-postgresql-cre` secret; creates `keycloak-host-cre` CM with remote CRE IAM host; fetches all confidential clients from CRE Keycloak REST API → creates `keycloak-client-secrets-cre`
- `esignet-qa11-preinstall.sh` — same pattern for QA11 env
- `esignet-sunbird-preinstall.sh` — sets `ESIGNET_NS=esignet-sunbird`; calls base preinstall; creates sunbird-specific `esignet-domain-config`; creates sunbird captcha secret

**Namespace-aware thin wrapper hooks:**
- `softhsm-esignet-{cre,qa11,sunbird}-setup.sh` — set `ESIGNET_NS` and exec `softhsm-esignet-setup.sh`
- `oidc-ui-{cre,qa11,sunbird}-preinstall.sh` — set `ESIGNET_NS` and exec `oidc-ui-preinstall.sh`
- `mock-relying-party-service-{cre,qa11,sunbird}-preinstall.sh` — set `ESIGNET_NS` and exec base mock-RP preinstall
- `mock-relying-party-ui-{cre,qa11,sunbird}-preinstall.sh` — namespace creation + service check in correct namespace

**PMS hooks:**
- `pms-partner-cre-preinstall.sh` — creates `pms-partner-cre-gateway` in `esignet-cre` (HTTPS+HTTP, TLS credential `pms-partner-cre-tls`); required because the chart has no Gateway template
- `pms-partner-qa11-preinstall.sh` — creates `pms-partner-qa11-gateway` in `esignet-qa11`

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Using a single shared domain-config ConfigMap for all namespaces — rejected: each namespace has different `mosip-esignet-host` and `mosip-signup-host` values; copying from the esignet ns would give wrong hostnames to cre/qa11/sunbird instances.

---

**Additional context**

- `esignet-cre-preinstall.sh` and `esignet-qa11-preinstall.sh` fetch client secrets via Keycloak REST API (`/admin/realms/mosip/clients`) using `CRE/QA11_KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD` — creates `keycloak-client-secrets-cre/qa11` with one key per confidential client.
- PMS Gateway TLS secrets (`pms-partner-cre-tls`, `pms-partner-qa11-tls`) must exist in `istio-system` before the preInstall hook runs.

title: [MOSIP-44613] Add testrigs-dsf.yaml and testrig hooks for all 4 eSignet namespaces + Signup
content:
Problem description:
> **Sub-task of**: mosip/mosip-infra#1790 (MOSIP-41302: Rapid Deployment support for eSignet deployment with MOSIP)
> **Branch**: `MOSIP-44613` in `mosip/infra`

---

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

There was no `testrigs-dsf.yaml` for the eSignet standalone profile. API testrigs could not be deployed via CI/CD for any of the 4 eSignet namespaces, and there was no signup UI testrig at all.

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add `Helmsman/dsf/esignet/testrigs-dsf.yaml` deploying:
- `esignet-apitestrig` in `esignet` namespace
- `esignet-cre-apitestrig` in `esignet-cre` namespace
- `esignet-qa11-apitestrig` in `esignet-qa11` namespace
- `esignet-sunbird-apitestrig` in `esignet-sunbird` namespace
- `esignet-signup-apitestrig` in `signup` namespace (disabled by default)
- `signup-uitestrig` in `signup-uitestrig` namespace (disabled by default)

New hook scripts:
- `apitestrig-esignet-setup.sh` — deletes stale testrig CMs (`s3`, `db`, `apitestrig`) in `esignet` ns; copies `postgres-postgresql` secret from postgres ns (keycloak resources already present from `esignet-postinstall-keycloak-init.sh`)
- `apitestrig-esignet-cre-setup.sh`, `apitestrig-esignet-qa11-setup.sh`, `apitestrig-esignet-sunbird-setup.sh` — same pattern for respective namespaces
- `apitestrig-signup-setup.sh` — deletes stale testrig CMs in signup ns; copies `postgres-postgresql` from postgres ns
- `uitestrig-signup-setup.sh` — creates `signup-uitestrig` namespace with Istio disabled; copies `keycloak-host`, `keycloak-client-secrets` from keycloak ns, `s3` from minio ns, `postgres-postgresql` from postgres ns
- `trigger-test-jobs-esignet.sh` (postInstall on sunbird-apitestrig) — triggers all cronjobs in esignet/cre/qa11/sunbird namespaces sequentially; optionally triggers signup apitestrig and signup-uitestrig if deployed

**Files**: `testrigs-dsf.yaml`, `apitestrig-esignet-setup.sh`, `apitestrig-esignet-cre-setup.sh`, `apitestrig-esignet-qa11-setup.sh`, `apitestrig-esignet-sunbird-setup.sh`, `apitestrig-signup-setup.sh`, `uitestrig-signup-setup.sh`, `trigger-test-jobs-esignet.sh`, `esignet-apitestrig-values.yaml`, `esignet-signup-apitestrig-values.yaml`, `signup-uitestrig-values.yaml`

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Running testrigs manually via `kubectl create job` — rejected: not reproducible and cannot be tracked as a Helm release or restarted via the workflow.

---

**Additional context**

`trigger-test-jobs-esignet.sh` uses `trigger_all_in_ns` so cronjob names are auto-detected — no hardcoded job name list needed. Sequential triggering ensures test namespaces don't exhaust cluster resources simultaneously. All apitestrig values files share `extraEnvVarsCM: [s3, keycloak-host, db, apitestrig, esignet-domain-config]`; `extraEnvVarsSecret` is overridden per-release in the DSF via indexed `set:`.

title: [MOSIP-44613] Add signup-dsf.yaml and Signup stack hooks (kernel, signup-service, signup-ui)
content:
Problem description:
> **Sub-task of**: mosip/mosip-infra#1790 (MOSIP-41302: Rapid Deployment support for eSignet deployment with MOSIP)
> **Branch**: `MOSIP-44613` in `mosip/infra`

---

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

There was no automated Helmsman DSF or GitHub Actions support for deploying the Signup stack (kernel services + signup-service + signup-ui) in the eSignet standalone profile. Signup had to be deployed manually, could not be triggered automatically after eSignet, and had no idempotent hook scripts for secret/configmap provisioning.

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add `Helmsman/dsf/esignet/signup-dsf.yaml` with the following deployment order (all disabled by default — enable as needed):

| Priority | Component | Namespace |
|---|---|---|
| `-10` | `signup-keycloak-init` | signup | Creates mosip-signup-client; propagates secret to signup ns |
| `-8` | `authmanager`, `auditmanager`, `otpmanager` | kernel | Share `kernel-preinstall.sh` |
| `-7` | `notifier` | kernel | `notifier-postinstall.sh` waits for readiness |
| `-5` | `mock-smtp` | mock-smtp | Dev/test email/SMS |
| `-4` | `signup` | signup | Copies secrets; creates keycloak-host, captcha, keystore, msg-gateway resources |
| `-3` | `signup-ui` | signup | Istio VS on `signup.${domain_name}` |

New hook scripts:
- `signup-keycloak-init-preinstall.sh` — creates signup namespace; copies `keycloak-client-secrets` from keycloak ns
- `signup-keycloak-init-postinstall.sh` — propagates `mosip_signup_client_secret` to signup ns
- `signup-init-db.sh` — initializes mosip_audit, mosip_kernel, mosip_otp DB schemas
- `kernel-preinstall.sh` — creates kernel namespace + `domain-config` CM with API/IAM hosts
- `notifier-postinstall.sh` — waits for notifier rollout readiness
- `signup-service-preinstall.sh` — copies redis/keycloak secrets; creates keycloak-host CM, `signup-captcha` secret (in signup ns + copies to captcha ns + patches captcha deployment), `signup-keystore` secret, `msg-gateway` CM+secret

**Files**: `signup-dsf.yaml`, `signup-keycloak-init-preinstall.sh`, `signup-keycloak-init-postinstall.sh`, `signup-init-db.sh`, `kernel-preinstall.sh`, `notifier-postinstall.sh`, `signup-service-preinstall.sh`

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Adding signup components to `esignet-dsf.yaml` — rejected: creates ordering ambiguity between esignet and signup components and prevents independent re-deployment of just the signup stack.

---

**Additional context**

Prerequisites from `external-dsf.yaml` must be running before signup-dsf is applied: postgres-init-signup, Redis, Kafka, Keycloak (with `keycloak-postinstall` having propagated `keycloak-client-secrets`), and Captcha. The `helmsman_signup.yml` workflow is auto-triggered by `helmsman_esignet.yml` when `profile=esignet`.

[bhumi46]: signup dsf is created but still config and architure changes still needed and it is planned for next release.

title: [MOSIP-44613] Restructure esignet-dsf.yaml — 4 parallel eSignet instances (mock, mosip-identity, sunbird-rc)
content:
Problem description:
> **Sub-task of**: mosip/mosip-infra#1790 (MOSIP-41302: Rapid Deployment support for eSignet deployment with MOSIP)
> **Branch**: `MOSIP-44613` in `mosip/infra`

---

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The previous `esignet-dsf.yaml` deployed a single eSignet instance (mock plugin only) in one namespace. There was no way to simultaneously validate all three plugins in isolated namespaces within a single environment.

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Restructure `esignet-dsf.yaml` to deploy 4 fully isolated eSignet instances:

| Namespace | Plugin | Keycloak / Postgres |
|---|---|---|
| `esignet` | Plugin 1 — mock | Local |
| `esignet-cre` | Plugin 2 — mosip-identity | Remote CRE env |
| `esignet-qa11` | Plugin 2 — mosip-identity | Remote QA11 env |
| `esignet-sunbird` | Plugin 3 — sunbird-rc | Local |

Each namespace gets its own SoftHSM (priority `-16`), eSignet deployment with namespace-specific plugin values file (priority `-14`), OIDC UI with dedicated Istio VirtualService host (priority `-13`), mock relying-party service + UI (priority `-10`/`-9`), and PMS partner + policy charts for cre/qa11 (priority `-9`).

Partner onboarders (disabled by default):
- `esignet-mock-rp-onboarder` — plugin 1 (mock) / plugin 3 (sunbird-rc)
- `esignet-misp-onboarder` — plugin 2 (mosip-identity) only

**Files**: `esignet-dsf.yaml`

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Separate DSF files per namespace — rejected: duplicates shared infra entries and cannot be deployed atomically.

---

**Additional context**

`extraEnvVarsCM[1]: esignet-domain-config` + `extraEnvVarsCM[2]: esignet-config-server-share` override chart defaults `[global, config-server-share]` for cre/qa11 to avoid `configmap "global" not found` error. SoftHSM release names are intentional — the chart creates a secret named after the release, and each eSignet plugin values file references its own namespace-specific secret name.

title: [MOSIP-44613] Restructure external-dsf.yaml — move keycloak-init to keycloak ns and add multi-namespace postgres-init
content:
Problem description:
> **Sub-task of**: mosip/mosip-infra#1790 (MOSIP-41302: Rapid Deployment support for eSignet deployment with MOSIP)
> **Branch**: `MOSIP-44613` in `mosip/infra`

---

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

`esignet-keycloak-init` was deployed into the `esignet` namespace, but the Keycloak Helm chart and all its resources (`keycloak` secret, `keycloak-env-vars` CM) live in the `keycloak` namespace. Running the init job outside its resource context caused lookup failures and required fragile cross-namespace copying. Additionally, a single `postgres-init` entry for `mosip_esignet` could not support 4 parallel eSignet namespaces each needing their own isolated database.

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Move `esignet-keycloak-init` from `esignet` to `keycloak` namespace at priority `-11` (after keycloak at `-12`). The chart now creates `keycloak-host` CM and `keycloak-client-secrets` secret directly in keycloak ns where all dependencies already exist.
- Add per-namespace `postgres-init` entries for `mosip_esignet_cre`, `mosip_esignet_qa11`, `mosip_esignet_sunbird` each with unique `dbName`/`dbUser`, explicit `su` block and `defaultDb` fields.
- Add `postgres-init-mock-identity` entry for `mosip_mockidentitysystem`.
- Add `postgres-init-signup` entry for signup stack (mosip_audit, mosip_kernel, mosip_otp schemas).
- Fix MinIO re-deploy: pass existing `auth.rootPassword` via `${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD}` to prevent Bitnami PASSWORDS ERROR on upgrade.

**Files**: `external-dsf.yaml`, `esignet-init-db.sh`, `esignet-db-postinstall.sh`, `mock-identity-init-db.sh`, `signup-init-db.sh`, `postgres-preinstall.sh`, `postgres-postinstall.sh`

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Keeping keycloak-init in the esignet namespace and copying all keycloak resources into it — rejected because it duplicates secret management and creates fragile copy-ordering dependencies.

---

**Additional context**

`postgres-init` chart version is `0.0.1-develop` — supports dynamic `databases:` map. New DB entries must explicitly set `su.user`, `su.secret.name/key`, and `defaultDb`; omitting any causes nil pointer or wrong-DB schema errors at render time.

title: Remove the static PV configuration and it should create volumes dynamically based on the respective StorageClass
content:
Problem description:
Static NFS Persistent Volume (PV) configurations requires explicit pv.yaml definitions along with nfs_server and nfs_path parameters. This approach increases maintenance overhead and creates dependency on manually managed storage resources.

The NFS CSI driver supports dynamic provisioning, allowing Persistent Volumes to be automatically created and managed through Kubernetes StorageClasses.

## Summary
Automate the process of linking pull requests (PRs) to their respective issues to improve traceability and workflow efficiency in the repository.

## Problem
Currently, contributors may forget to link PRs to issues, which can lead to tracking challenges and reduced visibility on the progress of enhancements, bug fixes, or new features.

## Proposed Solution
Implement a workflow automation (e.g., GitHub Actions or a bot) that automatically links PRs to issues based on keywords or issue references in the PR description/title.

- Document the solution in the repository's CONTRIBUTING.md.

- Ensures issues are properly linked, improving project management and traceability.
- Minimizes manual errors or omissions by contributors.
- Saves maintainers' time in cross-referencing PRs and issues.

Leverage the primary repository languages, Shell and Python, for implementation.

title: Blocker 1 - WireGuard access for new environments
content:
Problem description:
As part of the rapid deployment handover for Dev and QA environments (parent issue #1728), ensure that WireGuard access is established and validated for all new environments.

Problem: New env = manual peer generation + manual GitHub env secret creation; peer count is fixed at base-infra creation.

**Scope:**
- Set up WireGuard VPN access specific to newly provisioned environments (Dev & QA).
- Document prerequisites and provide connection instructions for Dev and QA teams.
- Validate connectivity post-provisioning.
- Include troubleshooting and access escalation guidance.
- Ensure the access requirements align with existing security protocols.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- WireGuard is configured and functional for all new environments.
- Connection details and required steps are documented and accessible.
- Dev and QA team members can successfully connect after provisioning.
- Troubleshooting materials are available.
- Security and compliance requirements are met.

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: Blocker 1 — WireGuard onboarding for new environments

- scripts/wg-onboard.sh — pulls 2 free peer configs from the jumpserver, publishes TF_WG_CONFIG / CLUSTER_WIREGUARD_WG0 / CLUSTER_WIREGUARD_WG1 as per-environment GitHub secrets, creates the GitHub Environment, and is idempotent on re-runs.
- scripts/wg-peer-allocation.tsv — tracks peer→env allocation (no secret material).
- .github/workflows/wireguard-onboard.yml — self-service workflow wrapping the script (with dry-run). The peer pool was already generous at wireguard_peers = 30.

[Ivanmeneges]: Created a workflow with the scripts and below is the workflow process 

This is how a team uses it without local tooling/SSH key.

Make sure these repo secrets exist:

- PAT_TOKEN — a PAT with repo admin (used to create the environment + secrets and to commit the allocation file).
- The jumpserver SSH private key stored as a repo secret (e.g. SSH_PRIVATE_KEY).
- GitHub → Actions → WireGuard onboard environment → Run workflow, with:
- ENV_NAME = test-env
- JUMPSERVER_HOST = <JUMPSERVER_IP>
- SSH_PRIVATE_KEY = name of the secret holding the key (e.g. SSH_PRIVATE_KEY)
- DRY_RUN = true first, then false
- Watch the run logs; on a real (DRY_RUN=false) run it creates the environment, sets the 3 secrets, and commits the updated scripts/wg-peer-allocation.tsv.
- Common failure points
- "ssh key not found" → wrong --ssh-key path or not chmod 600.
- "Could not read …/peerN.conf" → jumpserver unreachable, wrong key, or WireGuard container not up yet (ssh … 'sudo docker logs wireguard').
- gh secret set … --env 403 → token lacks repo admin / secrets write.
- mapfile: command not found or grep: invalid option -- P → you're on macOS/BSD; use Linux/WSL or the workflow.
- Want me to add a --no-gh/offline allocation-only test mode to the script so it can be exercised without a live jumpserver or gh?

[Ivanmeneges]: The script now matches your wireguard_env_2026 workflow instead of my earlier assumption:

- Reads /home/ubuntu/wireguard_env_2026/assigned.txt as the source of truth and config/peerN/peerN.conf for the client configs (configurable via --wg-dir).
- Allocates 3 distinct peers per environment — one each for TF_WG_CONFIG, CLUSTER_WIREGUARD_WG0, CLUSTER_WIREGUARD_WG1 — exactly like your qaj21 → peer4/5/6 pattern. It picks the next free peers (peers with a blank/missing entry in assigned.txt).
- Appends to assigned.txt on the VM in your format: peerN <env>(<SECRET_NAME>), with an optional --ticket (e.g. dev01(DSD-10264)(TF_WG_CONFIG)).
- Transforms each conf: strips the DNS = ... line and rewrites AllowedIPs to 172.31.0.0/16 (configurable via --allowed-ips).
- Publishes the three transformed confs as environment secrets on the branch/env named after --env.
- Idempotent: re-running an existing env reuses its peers and does not duplicate assigned.txt lines.
- The wireguard-onboard.yml workflow gained TICKET, WG_DIR, and ALLOWED_IPS inputs, and scripts/wg-peer-allocation.tsv now tracks tf_peer/wg0_peer/wg1_peer.

- Validation (with mocks replaying your real data)
- New env dev01 → allocated peer1/peer2/peer3 (lowest free), correct assigned.txt lines.
- Reuse of qaj21 → correctly found peer4/5/6 and reused them.
- Real run → assigned.txt appended correctly; each secret body had DNS removed and AllowedIPs = 172.31.0.0/16.
- Idempotent re-run → reused peers, no duplicate appends, single tracker row.

title: MOSIP-44259: PMS - OIDC flow fails due to unresolved eSignet mapping file URLs
content:
Problem description:
While testing the *OIDC flow*, OIDC client creation fails with a *500 Internal Server Error*.
The issue occurs because the required *eSignet mapping file URLs are not resolved*, causing PMS to fail while fetching configuration files from the *mosip-config (*https://github.com/mosip/mosip-config/blob/dev/partner-management-default.properties#L319).

esignet claims mapping file url

{{mosip.pms.esignet.claims-mapping-file-url=${spring_config_url_env}/application/${active_profile_env}/${spring_config_label_env}/identity-mapping.json}}

esignet amr-acr mapping file url

{{mosip.pms.esignet.amr-acr-mapping-file-url=${spring_config_url_env}/application/${active_profile_env}/${spring_config_label_env}/amr-acr-mapping.json}}

After updating the configuration to use *raw GitHub URLs*, the issue is resolved and the OIDC flow works successfully.
`mosip.pms.esignet.claims-mapping-file-url=`
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mosip/mosip-config/refs/heads/dev/identity-mapping.json`

`mosip.pms.esignet.amr-acr-mapping-file-url=`
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mosip/mosip-config/refs/heads/dev/amr-acr-mapping.json`

title: MOSIP-24211: Single point of failure with config-server (No pod priority )
content:
Problem description:
## ⚠️ *Problem Summary*

- You have *only 1 replica (pod)* of Config Server

- *No pod priority / scheduling rules*

- If:
** Node goes down
** Pod gets evicted
** Rolling update happens

👉 *Entire system may fail to fetch configs → cascading failures*

----

## 🧱 *How SPOF Happens*

```App Pods  ---> Config Server (1 pod) ❌
                |
             Node Down
                ↓
         No Config → App crash
```

----

## ✅ *Solution: Make Config Server Highly Available*

### 1. 🔁 *Increase Replicas*

```replicas: 2  # minimum
```

👉 Recommended:

- *2 replicas* → minimum HA

- *3 replicas* → production-grade

----

### 2. 🧠 *Pod Anti-Affinity (CRITICAL)*

Ensure pods are NOT on the same node:

```affinity:
  podAntiAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:

      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: config-server
        topologyKey: "kubernetes.io/hostname"
```

👉 Prevents both pods landing on same node

----

### 3. 🚨 *Pod Priority Class*

Create high priority:

```apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: high-priority
value: 100000
globalDefault: false
description: "Critical system component"
```

Attach to deployment:

```priorityClassName: high-priority
```

👉 Ensures:

- Config server pods are *not evicted first*

----

### 4. 🔄 *Pod Disruption Budget (PDB)*

```apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: config-server-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: config-server
```

👉 Prevents:

- Both pods getting killed during maintenance

----

### 5. ❤️ *Liveness & Readiness Probes*

```livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /actuator/health
    port: 8888
  initialDelaySeconds: 30
  periodSeconds: 10

readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /actuator/health
    port: 8888
  initialDelaySeconds: 20
  periodSeconds: 5
```

👉 Ensures traffic only goes to healthy pods

----

### 6. ⚖️ *Service Load Balancing*

Make sure you use:

```type: ClusterIP
```

And access via:

```http://config-server:8888
```

👉 Kubernetes will load balance across pods

title: MOSIP-41293: Upgrade eSignet service to the latest version
content:
Problem description:
### *Upgrade Deployment(upgrading eSignet to new version):*

Steps to be followed if the user is trying to upgrade the eSignet to the newer version:

*Steps to upgrade:*

1. Run upgrade-all.sh file to upgrade eSignet version:
## `./upgrade-all.sh` (We should check if we can only deploy folder to be downloaded and cloning and other things script takes care user )
## Upgrade script should be able to identify the version user is using and upgrade to the version from where the they are using the upgrade script
### [“eSignetbackup“] = “Please confirm with 'y' to start the back up process: “(Check if this can be done with the script)
#### If user chooses to reply with 'n' and do not confirm to start the back up process, then the upgrade script should throw an error and upgrade should be halted
#### Once user confirms the process to start the back up, user should be displayed with the information on what is getting backed up in form of running comments and total progress
### Upgrade process should start, if in any case the upgrade is halted for any unseen circumstances, script should be able to start the rollback
### If user halts the upgrade process then user should have option to manually initiate the rollback process to the current version of the eSignet that user has
## Once the upgrade is completed to verify the eSignet flow, user should be able install the api test suites and run it. Below steps are to be followed:
### Create a directory for api test suites on the NFS server at `/srv/nfs/mosip//apitestrig/`:

title: MOSIP-41451: Missing UUID Mapping in Terraform Script for /etc/fstab – Causes Volume Mount Failure on Reboot
content:
Problem description:
The Terraform module for AWS resource creation in the https://github.com/mosip/infra-priv/blob/3df7a03bb42367a98a4024bcb948a5eca5fc414d/terraform/modules/aws/aws-resource-creation/variables.tf#L115 currently does *not configure the UUID of the attached storage device* (e.g., `/dev/nvme1n1`) in `/etc/fstab`.

Due to this, when the instance is rebooted, *device names may change dynamically*, leading to incorrect or failed mounts for critical volumes (e.g., `/srv/nfs`). This recently resulted in *data inaccessibility for NFS clients*, impacting dependent services.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

1. Provision an instance using the current Terraform module.

1. Mount the attached volume using device name (e.g., `/dev/nvme1n1`) without referencing UUID.

1. Reboot the instance.

1. Observe mount failure and data inaccessibility due to incorrect device mapping.

*Expected Behavior:*
The Terraform provisioner should:

- Retrieve the UUID of the attached block device using `blkid`.

- Automatically update `/etc/fstab` using the UUID (not the device name) to ensure persistent and reliable mounts.

title: MOSIP-43063: Optimize Keycloak Postgres queries by adding targeted indexes
content:
Problem description:
*Description*
We observed slow response times (~6s) for single-user fetches on the `/userdetails` path, with p90 latency around 5–7s. Investigation showed that the Auth → Keycloak user-lookup path was the bottleneck due to inefficient Postgres queries and missing indexes.

*What we saw*

- Sync service timers indicated the Keycloak DB leg dominated total request time.

- Queries without `realm_id` filters caused Postgres to fall back to sequential scans instead of using existing composite indexes.

- Example (before optimization):

```EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)
SELECT ue.username, ue.email
FROM public.user_entity ue
WHERE ue.username = 'performance';

-- Result: Seq Scan ... ~8 ms, but cumulative impact under load ~6s
```

- After adding indexes, query planner switched to index scans (~0.05 ms).

*Root cause*

- Missing targeted indexes on frequently accessed columns.

- Chatty Auth → Keycloak API usage patterns (list-then-filter, multiple per-user role lookups).

*Fix implemented*
Added the following *non-blocking concurrent indexes* in production:

```CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_entity_username
  ON public.user_entity (username);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_attr_userid_name
  ON public.user_attribute (user_id, name);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_attr_userpassword
  ON public.user_attribute (user_id) WHERE name = 'userPassword';

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_credential_user_id
  ON public.credential (user_id);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_role_user
  ON public.user_role_mapping (user_id);
```

*Impact*

- Reduced `/userdetails` p90 latency from 5–7s → ~0.8–1.0s.

- Single-user fetches are now sub-second.

- DB IO load decreased (no full scans).

- Auth/Keycloak CPU usage reduced due to fewer HTTP calls.

*Verification*

- Verified via `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` → index scans used across target queries.

- Service logs show improved timings: single-user fetch now ;}}.

- Application changes backward-compatible (fallback to old fetch path if required).

*Follow-ups*

- Consider adding trigram GIN index for fuzzy search endpoints:

```CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_username_trgm
  ON public.user_entity USING gin (username gin_trgm_ops);
```

- Add Grafana dashboards to monitor:
** Auth/Keycloak API latency
** Token reuse / refresh rates
** Postgres index hit ratios, slow query logs

title: MOSIP-42975: Enhancement in helm chart
content:
Problem description:
lifecycle: preStop: exec: command: ["sleep", "10"] after startupProbe: what is use of it

What actually happens on termination

1. Kubernetes starts terminating the pod → *runs* `preStop` *first*.

1. While `preStop` runs (your `sleep 10`), the pod is marked *Terminating* and is *removed from Service endpoints* (readiness goes false). Traffic _should_ stop being routed to it, but there’s a small propagation delay.

1. After `preStop` finishes, kubelet sends *SIGTERM* to the container. Then your app’s *graceful shutdown* begins (e.g., `server.shutdown=graceful`).

1. If the app hasn’t exited by `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, kubelet sends *SIGKILL*.

Why the sleep helps

- It gives *10s for the load balancer/endpoints to drain*, so *no new* requests arrive before SIGTERM.

- Any *in-flight* requests can complete during this pause, reducing errors like “Interrupted during connection acquisition”.

Notes

- YAML order (preStop appearing after startupProbe) doesn’t affect semantics—they’re separate features:
** *startupProbe*: only during startup.
** *preStop*: only during shutdown/drain.

- 10s is okay; many teams use *20–30s* depending on LB propagation and request duration. Pair it with a larger `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` (e.g., *60s*) so the app then has time to do its graceful shutdown after the drain pause.

*Rule of thumb:*
 `preStop sleep ≈ LB drain time` → then *SIGTERM* → app graceful shutdown within `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`.

title: MOSIP-44213: minio data backup and restore activity.
content:
Problem description:
we have seen that when using mc client for minio data backup and restore the objects doesn't have metadata after restoring so need to RnD on the same to make sure the objects have metadat after restoring the minio data.

Discussion and resolution:
[exalate-issue-sync[bot]]: Mohan E commented: We are facing an error while upgrading minio version from 10.1.6 to 15.0.6 i,e {{FATAL Unable to use the drive /bitnami/minio/data: drive not found: Invalid arguments specified}} usually indicates a *breaking change in how MinIO handles data storage* between your old version (10.1.6) and the new version (15.0.6).

In late 2022, MinIO removed support for the legacy "Filesystem" (FS) mode. Newer versions now require the data to be in the "Single-Node Single-Drive" (SNSD) format. If you mount a volume containing the old FS-style data to a new MinIO container, it will fail to start because it doesn't recognize the old structure as a valid MinIO drive.

h3. The Problem: Legacy FS vs. SNSD

* *Version 10.1.6 (Old):* Used a simpler directory structure.
* *Version 15.0.6 (New):* Expects a {{.minio.sys}} metadata directory formatted for the new backend.
* *Bitnami Specifics:* Bitnami containers run as non-root (UID 1001). If the folder permissions on your "rescued" PVC are still owned by the old user or root, the container cannot initialize the new metadata, leading to the "drive not found" error.

cc: [~accountid:5d4159ed4125b20c3159b1ed] [~accountid:712020:d3c2f437-f0b7-4582-b791-2801ccb3eb83]

[exalate-issue-sync[bot]]: Mohan E commented: things that were tried:

* preserve option  ---> still not able to retrieve metadata
* replicate option ---> need multiple servers i,e older version and uograde version to be live at the sametime to work.
* minio upgrade ---> upgrade is done from older version to latest version but the pod fails to come up because, In late 2022, MinIO removed support for the legacy "Filesystem" (FS) mode. Newer versions now require the data to be in the "Single-Node Single-Drive" (SNSD) format. If you mount a volume containing the old FS-style data to a new MinIO container, it will fail to start because it doesn't recognize the old structure as a valid MinIO drive.

[exalate-issue-sync[bot]]: Mohan E commented: GPT suggestions: 

h3. The Solution: The "Sidecar" Migration

Since you cannot simply "point" the new version at the old data, you must perform a data migration.

h4. 1. Temporarily Roll Back to a "Bridge" Version

You need a running MinIO instance to "get the data out." Install a version close to your original that is compatible with the old data.

* *Option A:* Reinstall the 10.1.6 chart using your existing PVC.
* *Option B:* Spin up a standalone pod using the old image just to access the files.

h4. 2. Use {{mc mirror}} to Move Data

Once the old MinIO is running and you can see your files:

# *Deploy a "Clean" MinIO 15.0.6* with a *NEW, empty PVC*.
# *Use the MinIO Client (*{{mc}}*)* to sync data from the old one to the new one.

{noformat}Bash{noformat}

{noformat}# Example commands using the MinIO Client (mc)
mc alias set old_minio http://old-minio-svc:9000 admin password
mc alias set new_minio http://new-minio-svc:9000 admin password

# Sync all buckets and data
mc mirror old_minio new_minio{noformat}


But for us the above suggestion won’t work because using mc client to mirror data will lead to loss of metadata of objects which is necessary for us.

title: MOSIP-44736: Keycloak client secrets overwritten with empty values during eSignet prerequisite initialization
labels: bug, github_movement_2026, DST-Engg, devops, devops_gh, dst-1-2-1-0, devsecops
content:
Problem description:
*Description:*

During eSignet prerequisite initialization (`initialise-prereq.sh` → `keycloak-init.sh`), the script overwrites the existing `keycloak-client-secrets` in the `keycloak` namespace with empty values. Additionally, the `keycloak-client-secrets` is not consistently created in the `esignet` namespace.

This issue occurs when deploying *eSignet* alongside an *existing MOSIP Platform* deployment and affects all tested eSignet versions (v1.5.0 → v1.7.1). As a result, MOSIP clients *(PMS, IDA, Deployment-client, mPartner-default-auth & mPartner-default-mobile)* fail authentication, and eSignet clients may not initialize properly.

*Affected Versions:*

- eSignet v1.5.0 → v1.7.1

- MOSIP Platform (pre-deployed)

*Steps to Reproduce:*

1. Deploy MOSIP Platform with Keycloak initialized.

1. Run eSignet prerequisites:
```./initialise-prereq.sh [kubeconfig]
```

1. Select `y` to initialize Keycloak.

1. Inspect secrets:
```kubectl -n keycloak get secret keycloak-client-secrets -o yaml
kubectl -n esignet get secret keycloak-client-secrets -o yaml
```

*Expected Result:*

- Existing MOSIP Keycloak client secrets remain intact in Keycloak Namespace.

- eSignet clients are created without overwriting existing secrets.

- `keycloak-client-secrets` exists correctly in the `esignet` namespace.

*Actual Result:*

- Secret values in `keycloak-client-secrets` are overwritten with empty values (`""`) in Keycloak Namespace

- `keycloak-client-secrets` is not created in the `esignet` namespace

- Leads to authentication failures in dependent services 

*Root Cause Analysis:*

1. `keycloak-init.sh` uses incorrect variable references (e.g., `.data.$DEPLOYMENT_CLIENT_SECRET_VALUE` instead of `.data.$DEPLOYMENT_CLIENT_SECRET_KEY`).

1. The script overwrites secrets without checking for empty values.

1. Cross-namespace secret copy (`$COPY_UTIL`) may fail silently.

1. Helm job failures during Keycloak initialization are not properly handled.

## 📎 Attachments

- [eSignet-Keycloak-init.PNG](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/MOSIP-44736)

title: MOSIP-44389: Env creation handover through rapid deployment to Dev, QA
content:
Problem description:
As a *DevOps team*,
we want to *handover environment creation using Rapid Deployment to Dev and QA teams*,
so that *Dev and QA environments can be provisioned quickly, consistently, and with minimal manual intervention*, *dependency.*

This story covers documenting, validating, and handing over the Rapid Deployment process for creating Dev and QA environments, including access, prerequisites, and troubleshooting guidance.

### *Acceptance Criteria*

- Rapid Deployment process for *Dev* environment is documented and verified

- Rapid Deployment process for *QA* environment is documented and verified

- All required *inputs, configurations, and prerequisites* are clearly documented

- Environment creation steps are reproducible without devops team involvement

- Access permissions for Dev & QA teams are validated

- Rollback and failure-handling steps are documented

- Handover walkthrough session completed with Dev & QA teams

- Sign-off received from Dev & QA representatives

----

### *Scope / Inclusions*

- Dev & QA environment provisioning

- Rapid Deployment scripts/pipelines

- Configuration parameters

- Secrets and access handling (high level)

- Validation checklist post deployment

### *Dependencies*

- Rapid Deployment pipelines/scripts available and stable

- Required cloud/K8s access configured

- Secrets and credentials provisioned

----

### *Tasks*

1. Review existing Rapid Deployment setup

1. Finalize Dev environment deployment steps

1. Finalize QA environment deployment steps

1. Create handover documentation

1. Validate access for Dev & QA teams

1. Conduct knowledge transfer session

1. Collect sign-off

During the installation of config-server, the `install.sh` script prompts:

title: MOSIP-44794: Deployment Failures and Documentation Mismatch in k8s-infra v1.2.1.1 & v1.2.1.0
labels: bug, github_movement_2026, DST-Engg, devops, devops_gh, dst-1-2-1-0, devsecops
content:
Problem description:
### *Environment:*

- Component: k8s-infra

- Versions: v1.2.1.0, v1.2.1.1

- MOSIP GitHub repository:
[[https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/tree/v1.2.1.1](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/tree/v1.2.1.1|smart-link)](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/tree/v1.2.1.1](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/tree/v1.2.1.1|smart-link)) 

### *Description:*

There are multiple inconsistencies between the documentation and actual script behavior during the setup of infrastructure components such as NFS, Istio, RKE2 cluster, and Nginx. These issues lead to confusion and failed executions when following the documented steps.

*Issues Identified:*

#### *1. RKE2 Cluster Setup – Invalid Hostname Format in Documentation*

*Document Reference:* `host.ini.sample`

*Issue:*
The sample hostname provided:

```control-subsequent_plane-1
```

contains an underscore (`_`), which causes the cluster creation to fail.

*Observed Behavior:*

- Cluster setup fails when using the documented hostname. 

*Expected Behavior:*

- Hostnames should follow valid naming conventions (no underscores). 

*Workaround:*

- Changing the hostname to: 

```control-subsequent-plane-1
```

allows successful cluster creation.

*Error Observed:*

```fatal: [control-subsequent_plane-1]: FAILED! => {
  "msg": "The task includes an option with an undefined variable.. 
```

#### *2. Istio Ingress Installation – Missing CRDs Dependency Not Documented*

*Issue:*
While installing Istio ingress, the following errors are observed:

```no matches for kind "PodMonitor" in version "monitoring.coreos.com/v1"
no matches for kind "ServiceMonitor" in version "monitoring.coreos.com/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first
```

*Observed Behavior:*

- Script throws errors related to missing CRDs. 

- However, pods in `istio-system` namespace are still up and running. 

*Expected Behavior:*

- Installation should complete without errors when following documented steps. 

*Root Cause / Finding:*

- Required CRDs ([monitoring.coreos.com](http://monitoring.coreos.com)) are not installed prior to Istio setup. 

*Workaround:*

- Install `cattle-monitoring-system` before installing Istio. 

- After this, the script executes successfully without errors. 

*Documentation Gap:*

- Current documentation places monitoring setup after Istio installation, which is incorrect. 

#### *3. NFS Server & Client Setup – Mismatch Between Documentation and Script*

##### *NFS Server Installation*

*Document Says:*

- User must provide environment name.

- Expected path:

```/srv/nfs/mosip/
```

*Observed Behavior:*

- Script uses `/srv/nfs` directly. 

- No prompt for {{}}. 

- Installation completes successfully without environment input. 

*Issue:*

- Documentation does not match actual script behavior. 

##### *NFS Client Installation*

*Document Says:*
 User will be prompted for:

```Please provide NFS SERVER: 
Please provide NFS Path: 
```

*Observed Behavior:*

- Script fails with error: 

```./install-nfs-csi.sh: line 21: NFS_SERVER: unbound variable
```

*Expected Behavior:*

- Script should prompt for required inputs or handle missing variables gracefully. 

#### *StorageClass Configuration Mismatch (Volume Expansion Disabled)*

*Documentation States:*
Post-installation expected output:

```NAME        PROVISIONER              RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE   ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION
nfs-csi     cluster.local/nfs-csi    Retain          Immediate           true
```

----

*Actual Observed Output:*

```NAME                PROVISIONER      RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE   ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION
nfs-csi (default)   nfs.csi.k8s.io   Delete          Immediate           false
```

#### *Post Installation Validation Command Mismatch*

*Documentation States:*
 Check deployment:

```kubectl
-n nfs get deployment.apps/csi-driver-nfs
```

*Actual Observed Behavior:*

```kubectl get deploy -n nfs

NAME                 READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE
csi-nfs-controller   1/1     1            1kubectl
-n nfs get deployment.apps/csi-nfs-controller
```

*Findings:*

- Deployment name differs: 
** *Documented:* `csi-driver-nfs` 
** *Actual:* `csi-nfs-controller` 

#### *4. Nginx Setup – Incorrect Host Group in Sample Configuration*

*Document Reference:* `hosts.ini.sample`

*Sample Provided:*

```[cluster]
node1 ansible_host= ansible_user=root ansible_ssh_private_key_file=
```

*Observed Behavior:*

- Script execution fails with: 

```skipping: no hosts matched
```

*Expected Behavior:*

- Script should execute successfully using provided sample configuration. 

*Workaround:*

- Changing the host group from `[cluster]` to `[nginx]` allows successful execution.

*5. Cattle-logging-system:*

The cattle-logging-system deployment is failing in the Kubernetes cluster, where all Elasticsearch-related pods are stuck in `CrashLoopBackOff` or `Init:CrashLoopBackOff` state. This issue is reproducible on both Ubuntu 22.04 and Ubuntu 24.04 nodes.

- OS: *Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS*

- Elasticsearch Image: mosipint/elasticsearch:7.17.2-debian-10-r4
** init-containerImage: [mosipint/os-shell:12-debian-12-r46](http://docker.io/mosipint/os-shell:12-debian-12-r46)

- Kibana Image: mosipint/kibana:7.17.2-debian-10-r0

*Actual Result:*
Elasticsearch container fails during startup with the following error:

```Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "jdk.internal.platform.CgroupInfo.getMountPoint()" because "anyController" is null
    at jdk.internal.platform.cgroupv2.CgroupV2Subsystem.getInstance(...)
    at jdk.internal.platform.CgroupSubsystemFactory.create(...)
    at jdk.internal.platform.CgroupMetrics.getInstance(...)
    ...
```

### *Impact:*

- Users face failures and confusion when following official documentation. 

- Additional troubleshooting required, increasing setup time. 

- Potential blocker for new deployments. 

### *Expected Resolution:*

- Align documentation with actual script behavior. 

- Fix script inconsistencies where applicable. 

- Update setup sequence (for monitoring and Istio dependencies if required).
