title: Partner Onboarder: Jobs fail due to unknown MOSIP root CA (v3)
content:
Problem description:
When installing the partner onboarder, at the end the demo jobs are run. In the generated reports it turns out that checks fail. It seems like the jobs try to upload certificates as intermediate CA. However their root CA is not present in the partner management, so that the intermediate certificates are rejected.

It looks to me like this is a general problem not related to the system running in an internal network.

I have eventually been able to work around this problem by downloading the root certificate and then uploading it to the partner management. However the solution is rather ugly, because the partner management services need to be up in order for this to succeed, and as the jobs are run within the same `helm` call as the installation, there's a bit of a chicken-egg problem.

The solution is to run `helm` twice: once for installation only, no jobs, then again for the jobs. Hence there's 2 `values.yaml` files.

`values-bootstrap.yaml` is for installation only, all jobs disabled (the first 3 blocks are workarounds for the use of a corporate CA as described in #1714, may not be relevant for everybody):
```yaml
extraEnvVars:
  - name: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS
    value: /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ca.pem

extraVolumes:
  - name: corporate-ca
    secret:
      secretName: corporate-ca

extraVolumeMounts:
  - name: corporate-ca
    mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ca.pem
    subPath: corporate-ca.pem
    readOnly: true

onboarding:
  modules:
    - name: ida
      enabled: false
    - name: print
      enabled: false
    - name: abis
      enabled: false
    - name: resident
      enabled: false
    - name: digitalcard
      enabled: false
```

The file `values.yaml` is identical, just every onboarding module's `enabled` set to `true`.

Then split the `helm` calls in `install.sh` and add code for downloading / uploading the certificate (the `--post-renderer` arguments are workarounds for the use of a corporate CA as described in #1714, may not be relevant for everybody):

```shell
  echo Install onboarding module
  helm -n $NS install partner-onboarder mosip/partner-onboarder \
  $NFS_OPTION \
  $S3_OPTION \
  --set onboarding.variables.push_reports_to_s3=$push_reports_to_s3 \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[0]=global \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[1]=keycloak-env-vars \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[2]=keycloak-host \
  $ENABLE_INSECURE \
  -f values-bootstrap.yaml \
  --version $CHART_VERSION \
  --wait-for-jobs \
  --post-renderer ./post-render.sh


  API_HOST="$(kubectl -n onboarder get configmap global -o jsonpath='{.data.mosip-api-internal-host}')"
  CLIENT_SECRET="$(kubectl -n onboarder get secret keycloak-client-secrets -o jsonpath='{.data}' | jq | grep mosip_deployment_client_secret | awk '{ print $2 }' | tr -d '",' | base64 -d)"
  AUTH_JSON="{
  \"id\":\"string\",
  \"metadata\":{},
  \"request\":{
    \"appId\":\"ida\",
    \"clientId\":\"mosip-deployment-client\",
    \"secretKey\":\"$CLIENT_SECRET\"
  },
  \"requesttime\":\"2026-04-08T09:43:52.913Z\",
  \"version\":\"string\"
}"
  echo 1>&2
  echo

  echo Download session cookie to headers.txt:
  curl -sk -D headers.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$AUTH_JSON" "https://${API_HOST}/v1/authmanager/authenticate/clientidsecretkey"
  SESSION_COOKIE="$(grep -i '^set-cookie: Authorization=' headers.txt | sed 's/^set-cookie: //I' | cut -d';' -f1)"
  echo 1>&2
  echo

  echo Download root-ca.pem:
  curl -sk -H "Cookie: $SESSION_COOKIE" "https://${API_HOST}/v1/keymanager/getCertificate?applicationId=ROOT" | jq .response.certificate | perl -pe 's/"//g; s/\\n/\n/g' >root-ca.pem
  echo 1>&2
  echo

  echo Upload root-ca.pem, ignore KER-PCM-003 if it is already there:
  curl -sk -X POST "https://${API_HOST}/v1/partnermanager/partners/certificate/ca/upload" -H "Cookie: $SESSION_COOKIE" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @- <<EOF
{
  "id": "string",
  "metadata": {},
  "request": {
    "certificateData": "$(awk '{printf "%s\\n", $0}' root-ca.pem)",
    "partnerDomain": "AUTH"
  },
  "requesttime": "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z)",
  "version": "string"
}
EOF
  echo 1>&2
  echo

  echo Run onboarding jobs
  helm -n $NS upgrade partner-onboarder mosip/partner-onboarder \
  $NFS_OPTION \
  $S3_OPTION \
  --set onboarding.variables.push_reports_to_s3=$push_reports_to_s3 \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[0]=global \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[1]=keycloak-env-vars \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[2]=keycloak-host \
  $ENABLE_INSECURE \
  -f values.yaml \
  --version $CHART_VERSION \
  --wait-for-jobs \
  --post-renderer ./post-render.sh
```

title: Partner Onboarder: Jobs fail in sandbox environment due to missing trust for corporate CA (v3)
content:
Problem description:
Similar to the issue described in #1713 the Partner Onboarder talks to Keycloak for authentication through `${mosip-api-internal-host}`. The ingress uses a certificate signed by our corporate CA. This is not known by the pods running the onboarding jobs. 

I believe that support for such environments (corporate CA, certificates not automatically trusted) is relevant for MOSIP as people need to be able to deploy and run the system in their own, internal networks, at least for development and testing. 

I have eventually been able to work around this problem. This involves patching the job manifests using `kustomize` which isn't exactly pretty (this is why having builtin support for this would be really helpful). But here we go.

**1. Create a secret from the corporate CA**

```shell
kubectl -n onboarder create secret generic corporate-ca   --from-file=corporate-ca.pem=/path/to/corp-ca.pem
```

**2. Create post-render.sh script**

Note that for more than one job the rendered manifest is syntactically invalid as the upstream PV and PVC manifests  have no `---` separators. Hence the call to `perl` in the middle.

```shell
#!/bin/bash

command -V kustomize >/dev/null || { echo "Error, 'kustomize' command is not installed on your local system." 1>&2; exit 1; }

set -euo pipefail

tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Save helm output
cat > "$tmp/rendered.yaml"

echo "Patching '$tmp/rendered.yaml' which is missing the '---' between manifests it contains." 1>&2
perl -0pi -e 's/\n(apiVersion: v1\nkind: PersistentVolume\n)/\n---\n$1/g; s/\n(apiVersion: v1\nkind: PersistentVolumeClaim\n)/\n---\n$1/g' "$tmp/rendered.yaml"

# Copy kustomize files next to rendered.yaml
cp ./kustomization.yaml patch-partner-onboarder-*.yaml "$tmp/"

# Build patched output
kustomize build "$tmp"
```

**3. Create kustomization.yaml**

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - rendered.yaml

patches:
  - path: patch-partner-onboarder-digitalcard.yaml
    target:
      kind: Job
      name: partner-onboarder-digitalcard
  - path: patch-partner-onboarder-ida.yaml
    target:
      kind: Job
      name: partner-onboarder-ida
  - path: patch-partner-onboarder-print.yaml
    target:
      kind: Job
      name: partner-onboarder-print
  - path: patch-partner-onboarder-abis.yaml
    target:
      kind: Job
      name: partner-onboarder-abis
  - path: patch-partner-onboarder-resident.yaml
    target:
      kind: Job
      name: partner-onboarder-resident
```

**4. Create patches**

```yaml
# patch-partner-onboarder-abis.yaml
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: partner-onboarder-abis
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: partner-onboarder-abis
          volumeMounts:
            - name: corporate-ca
              mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ca.pem
              subPath: corporate-ca.pem
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: corporate-ca
          secret:
            secretName: corporate-ca
```

```yaml
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:

            secretName: corporate-ca
```


**5. Extend values.yaml**

```diff
--- a/deployment/v3/mosip/partner-onboarder/values.yaml
+++ b/deployment/v3/mosip/partner-onboarder/values.yaml
@@ -1,3 +1,18 @@
+extraEnvVars:
```

**6. Necessary changes to install.sh**

```
  --post-renderer ./post-render.sh
```

title: Admin module not working due to missing trust for corporate CA (Keycloak TLS / JWKS / token endpoint) (v3)
content:
Problem description:
_[moved here from **[k8s-infra repository](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/issues/189)**]_

My sandbox installation uses an ingress certificate signed by our organisation's internal CA. It has turned out that the admin module has its problems when running without public certificates. 

The first obstacle is login. After having entered `globaluser` and password, this error is displayed in the browser:
```
{"id":null,"version":null,"responsetime":"2026-04-01T11:19:39.560Z","metadata":null,"response":null,"errors":[{"errorCode":"KER-MSD-500","message":"Both provided Keys cannot be null."}]}
```

The main reason seems to be that my ingress certificate presented by the external IAM URL is unknown to the JVM in which admin-service runs. Having successfully worked around this, I found that token issuer comparison was unsuccessful.

Long story short, it looks like currently MOSIP's v3 deployment is not ready for such scenarios out of the box. I really think it should be (and this should also be verified by QA), because sandbox installations using internal CAs can be assumed to be a rather common scenario.

I have eventually succeded in getting the admin UI to work. For your reference, here's what I did (and I cannot rule out some of these steps being unnecessary):

**1. Change the configuration in admin-default.properties**

```diff
diff --git a/admin-default.properties b/admin-default.properties
index 2548bc7d..2954c663 100644
--- a/admin-default.properties
+++ b/admin-default.properties
@@ -208,7 +208,7 @@ mosip.iam.module.login_flow.response_type=code
 mosip.iam.authorization_endpoint=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/auth
 mosip.iam.module.admin_realm_id=mosip
 mosip.iam.token_endpoint=${keycloak.internal.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/token
-mosip.iam.certs_endpoint=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/certs
+mosip.iam.certs_endpoint=${keycloak.internal.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/certs

 regproc.token.request.appid=regproc
 regproc.token.request.clientId=mosip-regproc-client
@@ -221,7 +221,8 @@ KEYBASEDTOKENAPI=${mosip.kernel.authmanager.url}/v1/authmanager/authenticate/cli
 mosip.iam.adapter.appid=admin
 mosip.iam.adapter.clientid=mosip-admin-client
 mosip.iam.adapter.clientsecret=${mosip.admin.client.secret}
-mosip.iam.adapter.issuerURL=${keycloak.internal.url}/auth/realms/mosip
+mosip.iam.adapter.issuerURL=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip
+mosip.keycloak.issuerUrl=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip
 mosip.authmanager.client-token-endpoint=${mosip.kernel.authmanager.url}/v1/authmanager/authenticate/clientidsecretkey
 # in minutes
 mosip.iam.adapter.validate-expiry-check-rate=1440
@@ -229,6 +230,7 @@ mosip.iam.adapter.validate-expiry-check-rate=1440
 mosip.iam.adapter.renewal-before-expiry-interval=1440
 #this should be false if you don?t use this restTemplate true if you do
 mosip.iam.adapter.self-token-renewal-enable=true
+auth-token-generator.rest.issuerUrl=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip

 # LostRid
 mosip.registration.processor.lostrid.id=mosip.registration.lostrid
@@ -277,6 +279,8 @@ mosip.kernel.jsonvalidator.file-storage-uri=LOCAL

 mosip.kernel.machineid.length=5
 auth.server.admin.issuer.uri=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/
+auth.server.admin.issuer.internal.uri=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/
+auth.server.admin.issuer.domain.validate=false
 MACHINE_GET_API=${mosip.kernel.masterdata.url}/v1/masterdata/machines/mappedmachines/
 CRYPTOMANAGERDECRYPT_API=${mosip.kernel.keymanager.url}/v1/keymanager/decrypt
 CRYPTOMANAGER_DECRYPT=${mosip.kernel.keymanager.url}/v1/keymanager/decrypt

```

**2. Create file with our certificate chain**

This file will need to be made known to the admin-service JVM before it starts. We will "inject" it later:
```shell
cat my-ingress-host.cer our-corporate-ca.pem >corp-ca-chain.pem
```

**3. Patch the helm installation for an initContainer to the admin-service deployment**

Install `kustomize` on your local host:
```shell
dnf install -y kustomize
```

Create a `post-render.sh` script:
```shell
#!/bin/bash

command -V kustomize >/dev/null || { echo "Error, 'kustomize' command is not installed on your local system." 1>&2; exit 1; }

set -euo pipefail

tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Save helm output
cat > "$tmp/rendered.yaml"

# Copy kustomize files next to rendered.yaml
cp ./kustomization.yaml "$tmp/kustomization.yaml"

# Build patched output
kustomize build "$tmp"
```

Create a `kustomization.yaml` file:
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - rendered.yaml

patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: admin-service
    patch: |-
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: Deployment
      metadata:
        name: admin-service
      spec:
        template:
          spec:
            volumes:
              - name: corporate-ca
                secret:
                  secretName: corporate-ca
              - name: java-truststore
                emptyDir: {}
            initContainers:
              - name: import-corporate-ca
                image: eclipse-temurin:21-jre
                command:
                  - /bin/sh
                  - -c
                  - |
                    set -e
                    cp /opt/java/openjdk/lib/security/cacerts /work/cacerts
                    keytool -importcert \
                      -alias corporate-ca \
                      -file /ca/corp-ca.crt \
                      -keystore /work/cacerts \
                      -storepass changeit \
                      -noprompt
                volumeMounts:
                  - name: corporate-ca
                    mountPath: /ca
                    readOnly: true
                  - name: java-truststore
                    mountPath: /work
            containers:
              - name: admin-service
                env:
                  - name: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
                    value: >-
                      -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/work/cacerts
                      -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=changeit
                volumeMounts:
                  - name: java-truststore
                    mountPath: /work
```

Patch `install.sh` to (a) create a `secret` from the above `.pem` file and (b) activate post-render for the `admin-service` installation:
```diff
diff --git a/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh b/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh
index 9a08a24a..e450773f 100755
--- a/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh
+++ b/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh
@@ -18,6 +18,15 @@ function installing_admin() {
   kubectl label ns $NS istio-injection=enabled --overwrite
   helm repo update

+  if [ -r ../corp-ca-chain.pem ]; then
+    echo "File '../corp-ca-chain.pem' found, preparing for sandbox installation with internal CA root."
+    kubectl -n admin delete secret corporate-ca 2>/dev/null || /bin/true
+    kubectl -n admin create secret generic corporate-ca --from-file=corp-ca.crt=../corp-ca-chain.pem || errorExit "Error creating 'corporate-ca' secret."
+    ADMIN_SERVICE_HELM_POST_RENDER='--post-renderer ./post-render.sh'
+  else
+    echo "No file '../corp-ca-chain.pem' found, assuming non-sandbox install."
+  fi
+
   echo Copy configmaps
   sed -i 's/\r$//' copy_cm.sh
   ./copy_cm.sh
@@ -32,7 +41,7 @@ function installing_admin() {
   helm -n $NS install admin-hotlist mosip/admin-hotlist --version $CHART_VERSION

   echo Installing admin service. Will wait till service gets installed.
-  helm -n $NS install admin-service mosip/admin-service --set istio.corsPolicy.allowOrigins\[0\].prefix=https://$ADMIN_HOST --wait --version $CHART_VERSION
+  helm -n $NS install admin-service mosip/admin-service --set istio.corsPolicy.allowOrigins\[0\].prefix=https://$ADMIN_HOST --wait --version $CHART_VERSION $ADMIN_SERVICE_HELM_POST_RENDER

   echo Installing admin-ui
   helm -n $NS install admin-ui mosip/admin-ui --set admin.apiUrl=https://$API_HOST/v1/ --set istio.hosts\[0\]=$ADMIN_HOST --version $CHART_VERSION
```

Note that the `corp-ca-chain.pem` file is expected to reside in the `mosip-infra/deployment/v3/mosip` directory, because I assume that this problem will eventually also need to be fixed for other MOSIP modules, too.

title: RegProc: group2 never gets healthy due to a missing health endpoint (v3)
content:

title: Config Server renders invalid values when installed with helm chart version 1.3.0 (v3)
content:
Problem description:
I use a single remote, public git repository for the config server. My `values.yaml` looks like this:
```
activeProfileEnv: default

gitRepo:
  uri: "https://my.server/repo.git"
  version: mybranch
  searchFolders: ""
  private: false

spring_profiles:
  enabled: false

localRepo:
  enabled: false

extraEnvVars:
  - enabled: true
    name: SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE
    value: git

extraEnvVars:
  - name: SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE
    value: default
  - name: SPRING_CLOUD_CONFIG_SERVER_GIT_URI
    value: "https://my.server/repo.git"
  - name: SPRING_CLOUD_CONFIG_SERVER_GIT_DEFAULT_LABEL
    value: "mybranch"
  - name: SPRING_CLOUD_CONFIG_SERVER_GIT_CLONE_ON_START
    value: "true"
  - name: SPRING_CLOUD_CONFIG_SERVER_GIT_FORCE_PULL
    value: "true"
```

After installation the configmap `config-server-share` contains placeholders for the branch name:
```
kubectl -n config-server get configmap config-server-share -o yaml

apiVersion: v1
data:
  active_profile_env: git
  cache_config_url_env: http://config-server.config-server/config/application/git/<
    branch-name >/hazelcast_cache.xml
  consolidator_config_file_url_env: http://config-server.config-server/config/application/git/<
    branch-name >/websub-consolidator.toml
  hub_config_file_url_env: http://config-server.config-server/config/application/git/<
    branch-name >/websub-service.toml
  spring_config_label_env: < branch-name >
  spring_config_url_env: http://config-server.config-server/config
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  annotations:
    meta.helm.sh/release-name: config-server
    meta.helm.sh/release-namespace: config-server
  creationTimestamp: "2026-03-17T18:43:15Z"
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: Helm
  name: config-server-share
  namespace: config-server
  resourceVersion: "210306"
  uid: 59e7f637-eb7d-4338-9fbc-8e9cf75ea546
```

After some digging it has turned out that this problem can be fixed by switching to a more recent version of the helm chart in `install.sh`:
```
CHART_VERSION=12.0.3
```

title: Installation / execution of config server fails (v3)
content:
Problem description:
With recent changes from 2025 config server installation stopped working.

First issue: missing configmap `postgres-setup-config`. I have found it mentioned somewhere in the repo, but it is not created automatically anywhere. Creating it manually seems to work:
```
    kubectl -n config-server create configmap postgres-setup-config \
      --from-literal=mosip-database-hostname-override=postgres-postgresql.postgres \
      --from-literal=mosip-database-port-override=5432
```

Also as of now it looks like "composite" spring profile for configuring the git repo(s) containing the configuration cannot easily be overridden to use a single remote git repo. The following settings in `values.yaml` used to work:
```
gitRepo:
  uri: "https://github.com/mosip/mosip-config.git"
  version: release-1.3.x
  ## Folders within the base repo where properties may be found.
  searchFolders: ""
  private: false
  ## User name of user who has access to the private repo. Ignore for public repo
  username: ""
  token: ""
```

This is however no longer the case. Now I need to override defaults using the environment, which does not seem right:
```
activeProfileEnv: default

gitRepo:
  uri: "https://my.server/repo.git"
  version: mybranch
  searchFolders: ""
  private: false

spring_profiles:
  enabled: false
```

title: ActiveMQ CrashLoop because of startupProbe being too strict (v3)
content:
Problem description:
In thre provided ActiveMQ installation the `startupProbe` is too strict (netcat 61616) causing `CrashLoopBackOff` on slow storage/VMs; needs configurable probes or higher thresholds.

Current workaround:
```
diff --git a/deployment/v3/external/activemq/install.sh b/deployment/v3/external/activemq/install.sh
index e7c331cd..4bf5430d 100755
--- a/deployment/v3/external/activemq/install.sh
+++ b/deployment/v3/external/activemq/install.sh
@@ -20,7 +20,7 @@ function installing_Activemq() {
   echo Installing Activemq
   ACTIVEMQ_HOST=$(kubectl get cm global -o jsonpath={.data.mosip-activemq-host})
   echo Activemq host: $ACTIVEMQ_HOST
-  helm -n $NS install activemq mosip/activemq-artemis -f values.yaml --set istio.hosts[0]="$ACTIVEMQ_HOST" --wait
+  helm -n $NS install activemq mosip/activemq-artemis -f values.yaml --set istio.hosts[0]="$ACTIVEMQ_HOST" --post-renderer ./post-render.sh --wait
   return 0
 }
```

post-render.sh:
```
#!/bin/sh

command -V kustomize >/dev/null || { echo "Error, 'kustomize' command is not installed on your local system." 1>&2; exit 1; }

set -euo pipefail

tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Save helm output
cat > "$tmp/rendered.yaml"

# Copy kustomize files next to rendered.yaml
cp ./kustomization.yaml "$tmp/kustomization.yaml"

# Build patched output
kustomize build "$tmp"
```

kustomization.yaml:
```
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: activemq

resources:
  - rendered.yaml

patches:
  - target:
      group: apps
      version: v1
      kind: StatefulSet
      name: activemq-activemq-artemis-slave
    patch: |-
      - op: replace
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/startupProbe
        value:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 8161
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 5
          failureThreshold: 12
```

title: MinIO installation fails due to unresolvable images (v3)
content:
Problem description:
bitnami has moved the image referenced in the repo away, so that mosip-infra/deployment/v3/external/object-store/minio/install.sh fails:

- The `minio` image needs to be pulled from the legacy repo. The exact image is not available there, but the same version with a slightly different tag.
- The `minio-console` image seems to have completely disappeared. Hence it must be disabled (as it does not seem to be necessary for running MinIO).
- In that configuration with an NFS-based PV I found that the corresponding PVC was ignored so that the container failed when trying to write to the readonly-mounted cotainer FS. I needed extra settings for the helm chart in order to enforce using the PVC.

The following change works for me:
```
diff --git a/deployment/v3/external/object-store/minio/install.sh b/deployment/v3/external/object-store/minio/install.sh
index bf3f677e..dee12fdc 100755
--- a/deployment/v3/external/object-store/minio/install.sh
+++ b/deployment/v3/external/object-store/minio/install.sh
@@ -14,7 +14,14 @@ kubectl label ns $NS istio-injection=enabled --overwrite

 function installing_minio() {
   echo Installing minio
-  helm -n minio install minio mosip/minio --version 10.1.6
+  helm upgrade --install minio bitnami/minio -n minio \
+    --set image.repository=bitnamilegacy/minio \
+    --set image.tag=2022.2.7 \
+    --set console.enabled=false \
+    --set persistence.mountPath=/data \
+    --set extraVolumeMounts[0].name=empty-dir \
+    --set extraVolumeMounts[0].mountPath=/.minio \
+    --set extraVolumeMounts[0].subPath=dot-minio

   echo Installing gateways and virtualservice
   EXTERNAL_HOST=$(kubectl get cm global -o jsonpath={.data.mosip-minio-host})
```

Discussion and resolution:
[mbert]: With the changes from December 2 and December 24 the installation still does not work:
```
Create minio namespace
namespace/minio created
namespace/minio labeled
Installing minio
Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: execution error at (minio/templates/NOTES.txt:81:4):

⚠ ERROR: Original containers have been substituted for unrecognized ones. Deploying this chart with non-standard containers is likely to cause degraded security and performance, broken chart features, and missing environment variables.

Unrecognized images:
  - docker.io/mosipid/minio:2025.2.28-debian-12-r1

If you are sure you want to proceed with non-standard containers, you can skip container image verification by setting the global parameter 'global.security.allowInsecureImages' to true.
Further information can be obtained at https://github.com/bitnami/charts/issues/30850
```

Also the file `istio-addons-values.yaml` is missing.

title: PMS API Automation :  Automation failures in dev2 env — AddBioExtractors, InsertDBData, DBValidator
content:
Problem description:
**Suites**: AddBioExtractors, InsertDBData, DBValidator
**Environment**: pmp-dev.dev2.mosip.net

## Description

**AddBioExtractors** — `POST /partner-policy-requests/{requestId}/bio-extractors-request`: an invalid `attributeName` ("invalid") is accepted with a success response instead of the expected `PMS_PRT_099` validation error. This also causes 3 related negative tests (missing/empty extractor version, invalid biometric) to fail with "already mapped" (`PMS_PRT_283`) since they reuse the same `requestId`.

**InsertDBData** — All 3 test cases fail while inserting API key records into `pms.partner_policy` (10/15/30-day expiry variants), throwing `AdminTestException: Exception occured error executing work` at `DBIntegration.java:94`.

**DBValidator** — `TC_PMS_DBValidator_05` fails while validating that OIDCClient data is correctly stored and consistent in the pms database, throwing `AdminTestException: Failed at output validation` at `DBValidator.java:107`.


Report: 

[mosip-api-internal.dev2-pms-2026-07-16_05-01-full-report_T-1821_P-1782_S-15_F-24_I-0_KI-0.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30112712/mosip-api-internal.dev2-pms-2026-07-16_05-01-full-report_T-1821_P-1782_S-15_F-24_I-0_KI-0.html)

title: PMS API Automation - Validate "Attribute Name" & "Credential Data Format" fields in Bio-Extractor APIs
content:
Problem description:
Related to: #1897

## Purpose

#1897 adds two new mandatory fields — **Attribute Name** and **Credential Data Format** — to the Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration. Automation is needed to verify these fields work correctly across the following APIs.

## APIs to Cover

- `POST /bio-extractor-configurations`
- `POST /partner-policy-requests/{requestId}/bio-extractors-request`
- `GET /bio-extractor-configurations/{bioExtractorConfigurationId}`
- `GET /bio-extractor-configuration`

## Test Coverage

- Create a configuration with valid Raw Data + attribute values (Photo/Iris/Finger)
- Create a configuration with valid Template Data + configured attribute values
- Verify mandatory validation when either field is missing
- Verify GET by ID and GET list return the correct field values
- Submit a policy mapping request and confirm the values persist in `partner_policy_extract`
- After approval, confirm the values persist in `partner_policy_bioextractor`

## Acceptance Criteria

- New fields validate, save, and return correctly across all 4 APIs.

title: [Feature]: Enable Partner Certificate expiry Notifications for MOSIP Internal default partners
content:
Problem description:
**1. Problem Statement**

MOSIP's PMS (Partner Management System) has a set of default/internal partners that are pre-provisioned in the system `(e.g., MOSIP.PROXY.SBI, mpartner-default-cert, mpartner-default-adjudication, mpartner-default-mobile, mpartner-default-print, mpartner-default-abis, mpartner-default-resident, mpartner-default-auth, mpartner-default-digitalcard, mpartner-default-esignet)`. These default partners also have Partner Certificates uploaded/associated with them, which are subject to expiry like any other partner certificate.

Currently, the certificate-expiry notification feature (via notification panel and email) is defined/implemented for regular onboarded partners (as covered in MOSIP-39304 / MOSIP-40079), but there is no equivalent, explicit coverage for the default internal partners. If these default partner certificates expire without any proactive notification, it can lead to unplanned service disruptions for core system integrations (SBI, ABIS, print, resident services, eSignet, digital card, etc.) that depend on these default partners.

This issue is to extend the existing Partner Certificate expiry notification capability (notification panel + email) to explicitly cover this list of default internal partners, using the same underlying expiry-detection logic and the same notification template already defined for regular partners.

***Purpose***

- To ensure default/internal partner certificates nearing expiry are proactively flagged, just like regular partner certificates, preventing unplanned outages of core dependent services.
- To maintain consistency in the notification experience (panel + email) across both regular and default internal partners, reusing existing logic and templates rather than building a parallel system.
- To close a gap where system-critical default partners could silently have expiring certificates with no alerting mechanism.

***Pre-Requisites***

- The certificate expiry detection/batch job logic (as implemented for regular partners per MOSIP-39304) must already be in place and configurable (trigger period, e.g., 30/15/10-0 days before expiry).
- The notification template (title, description format, date/time formatting, dismiss behavior, 60-day auto-removal, etc.) as defined in the referenced story must remain unchanged and be reused as-is.
- Email notification infrastructure/service used elsewhere in PMS for partner communications must be available and configured for use with default internal partners.
- The list of default internal partners must be identifiable/flaggable in the system so the batch job and notification service can include them in scope:
```
  - MOSIP.PROXY.SBI
  - mpartner-default-cert
  - mpartner-default-adjudication
  - mpartner-default-mobile
  - mpartner-default-print
  - mpartner-default-abis
  - mpartner-default-resident
  - mpartner-default-auth
  - mpartner-default-digitalcard
  - mpartner-default-esignet
```
- Each default internal partner must have a valid registered email/contact and language preference on record for email notifications to be sent correctly.

**2. Goals**

- Extend the existing Partner Certificate expiry notification logic (batch job, expiry detection, 30-day lookback window) to include all default internal partners listed above, using the same trigger logic as regular partners.
- Display Partner Certificate expiry notifications for default internal partners in the Notification Panel, following the same UI/UX, title, description format, dismiss behavior, and 4-notification display limit as defined for regular partners.
- Send email notifications to default internal partners when their Partner Certificate is nearing expiry, using the same underlying trigger logic and existing notification template/content structure (adapted for email format).
- Ensure notifications (panel and email) are specific to each default internal partner — i.e., a given default partner only receives notifications for its own uploaded/associated certificate(s).
- Ensure the same lifecycle rules apply as for regular partners: dismiss behavior, 60-day auto-removal from panel/page, cancellation of future notifications on renewal, and retry-on-downtime behavior for the batch/notification job.
- Ensure notifications for default internal partners appear consistently across all screens (via the notification icon/panel) and are included in the "View all notifications" / Notifications page listing alongside regular partner notifications (or clearly identifiable as pertaining to a default/internal partner).

**3. Out of Scope**

- Any change to the core certificate expiry detection/batch job logic itself — this issue only extends its applicability to default internal partners; the logic remains as implemented for MOSIP-39304.
- Any change to the notification template content, structure, or design — the existing template (panel and to-be-defined email format) is reused as-is.
- Notifications for certificate types other than Partner Certificate (e.g., API Key, SBI, FTM Chip Certificate notifications) — unless a default internal partner already falls under existing coverage for those per MOSIP-39304/40079.
- Onboarding, creation, or configuration changes to the default internal partners themselves (their existing setup is assumed as-is).
- Design/redesign of the email template's visual branding — only content parity with the existing notification message is expected, formatted appropriately for email.
- Notification preferences/opt-out configuration UI (if not already present for regular partners).

**4. Acceptance Criteria**

- Given a default internal partner (from the listed set) has an uploaded Partner Certificate due to expire within the next 30 days, When the batch job runs, Then a notification shall be generated for that partner in the same way as for regular partners.
- Given a default internal partner logs into the PMS portal, When they click the notification icon, Then they shall see Partner Certificate expiration notifications relevant to their own uploaded certificate(s), consistent with the existing notification panel behavior.
- Given a default internal partner has a Partner Certificate nearing expiry, When the notification trigger condition is met, Then an email notification shall be sent to the partner's registered email address using the existing notification content/template.
- Given multiple default internal partners exist in the system, When notifications are generated, Then each partner shall only receive notifications (panel and email) for certificates uploaded/associated with itself, not for other partners' certificates.
- Given a default internal partner dismisses a notification in the panel, When the dismissal is processed, Then the notification shall be removed from both the panel and the Notifications page, consistent with existing behavior for regular partners.
- Given a default internal partner's certificate is renewed before expiry, When the renewal is processed, Then all future notifications (panel and email) related to that certificate shall be automatically canceled.
- Given a notification is older than 60 days, When the retention period elapses, Then the notification shall be automatically removed from the Notifications Panel/Page for the default internal partner, same as for regular partners.
- Given the notification trigger period (e.g., 30/15/10-0 days) is configurable, When the configuration is applied, Then it shall apply uniformly to both regular and default internal partners.

**Business Rules**

- Given the certificate belongs to a default internal partner listed in scope, When the expiry batch job evaluates certificates, Then it shall be included in the same evaluation cycle as regular partner certificates (no separate schedule).
- Given the existing notification template (panel) is defined for regular partners, When applied to default internal partners, Then the same title, description format, and date/time formatting rules shall be used without modification.
- Given an email notification is triggered, When composed, Then it shall reuse the same core message content as the panel notification (e.g., "Partner Certificate for <partner_domain_name> domain is set to expire on <Month Date, Year>. Renew it now to avoid any disruptions."), adapted to an email format (subject + body).
- Given a default internal partner has a registered notification language preference, When a notification (panel or email) is generated, Then it shall respect the language selected during login (overriding the registration-time language), consistent with existing behavior for regular partners.

**Exceptions & Error Handling**

- Given the batch job fails to trigger a notification for a default internal partner at the scheduled interval (30/15/10-0 days), When this is detected, Then the notification service/cron job schedule shall be checked, and a retry mechanism shall attempt to trigger the notification once the system/service is back online.
- Given a batch job is manually re-triggered after a missed run, When re-run, Then the notification (panel and email) shall be sent again to the affected default internal partner(s).
- Given a default internal partner does not have a valid/registered email address on file, When an email notification is attempted, Then the system shall handle this gracefully (e.g., log the failure, skip email dispatch, but still generate the in-panel notification) rather than failing the entire batch job.
- Given an email notification fails to send due to a transient email service failure, When detected, Then the system shall retry sending as per existing email notification retry mechanisms used elsewhere in PMS.

**Basic Flow**

- Batch job runs on schedule and evaluates all partner certificates (regular and default internal) for expiry within the next 30 days.
- For a default internal partner certificate nearing expiry, the system generates a Partner Certificate Expiration notification.
- The notification is added to the default internal partner's Notification Panel (following existing panel rules: latest 4 shown, red alert indicator, dismiss/view-all behavior).
- In parallel, an email notification is composed using the same content and sent to the default internal partner's registered email address.
- The default internal partner can view, dismiss, or navigate to "View all notifications" from the panel, same as regular partners.
- If the certificate is renewed before expiry, all future notifications (panel and email) for that certificate are automatically canceled.
- Notifications older than 60 days are automatically purged from the panel/page.

**Scenarios**

- A default internal partner (e.g., mpartner-default-auth) has a certificate expiring in 25 days — notification appears in panel and email is sent.
- Two different default internal partners each have certificates nearing expiry — each receives notifications only for their own certificate, not the other's.
- A default internal partner dismisses a panel notification — it disappears from panel and Notifications page, but the same certificate still triggers the next scheduled notification interval (e.g., at 15 days, then 10-0 days) if not yet renewed.
- A default internal partner renews their certificate after receiving a 30-day notification — no further notifications (15-day, 10-0 day) are triggered for that certificate.
- The batch job fails to run on the scheduled day due to system downtime; once the system is restored, the retry mechanism triggers the missed notification for the affected default internal partner(s).
- A default internal partner has no registered email on file — panel notification is still generated, but email dispatch is skipped/logged as a known gap.

**Data Fields**

- Partner ID (default internal) — Enum/List — Mandatory — Must be one of the defined default internal partner IDs (MOSIP.PROXY.SBI, mpartner-default-cert, mpartner-default-adjudication, mpartner-default-mobile, mpartner-default-print, mpartner-default-abis, mpartner-default-resident, mpartner-default-auth, mpartner-default-digitalcard, mpartner-default-esignet)
- Partner Domain Name — String — Mandatory — Must correspond to a valid registered domain for the partner
- Certificate Expiry Date — Date — Mandatory — Must be a valid future/near-future date within notification window
- Notification Title — String — Mandatory — Fixed value: "Partner Certificate Expiration"
- Notification Description — Text — Mandatory — Format: "Partner Certificate for <partner_domain_name> domain is set to expire on <Month Date, Year>. Renew it now to avoid any disruptions."
- Notification Created Date/Time — DateTime — Mandatory — Displayed per browser/system time settings
- Dismiss Link — Button/Link — Optional — Always enabled when notification is present
- Registered Email Address — String — Mandatory (for email notification) — Must be a valid email format; error (internal/log): "No valid email address found for partner"
- Email Subject — String — Mandatory — Derived from notification title/content
- Email Body — Text — Mandatory — Reuses panel notification description content, formatted for email
- Notification Language — Enum — Mandatory — Based on language selected at login

**Non-Functional Requirements**

- Notification Panel behavior must remain compatible across all major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari) on desktop and mobile, consistent with the existing requirement for regular partners.
- Email notifications must render correctly across common email clients (to be validated as part of testing, e.g., Gmail, Outlook).
- The extension to default internal partners must not degrade performance or processing time of the existing batch job for regular partners.
- Must maintain backward compatibility with existing notification panel/page behavior for regular partners — no regression expected.
- Email notification dispatch must reuse existing PMS email service/integration rather than introducing a new email delivery mechanism.

**Definition of Done**

- [ ] Code implemented
- [ ] Unit tests added
- [ ] Integration tests added (if applicable)
- [ ] Existing tests passing
- [ ] Documentation updated
- [ ] Acceptance criteria validated

**5. References**

**Documentation**

- Base story/reference (Notification Panel for Partner Certificate Expiry — regular partners): MOSIP-39304
- Notifications Page (Partner Certificate tab): MOSIP-40079

**UI/UX Design Link**

https://www.figma.com/proto/AcdT4y2HVIcRDG5FQ1c95d/PMS_Revamp?page-id=5484%3A16106&node-id=6219-24984&p=f&viewport=347%2C240%2C0.06&t=5VSVeCDveCEve8TS-1&scaling=contain&content-scaling=fixed&starting-point-node-id=6219%3A24737&show-proto-sidebar=1

**Git Discussion Link**

- (Add link to related design/technical discussion, if any, on extending notifications to default internal partners)

**Related Issues**

- Related to: MOSIP-39304 (Partner Certificate Expiry Notification — Notification Panel, regular partners)
- Related to: MOSIP-40079 (Notifications Page — Partner Certificate tab)
- Related to: Any existing PMS email notification service implementation

title: Inconsistent validation for notificationType filter in /notifications API returns contradictory error messages
content:
Problem description:
**Description**

The GET/notifications endpoint returns contradictory validation messages for the notificationType filter.

When a notification type other than MISP_LICENSE_KEY_EXPIRY is provided, the API returns an error stating that only certificate expiry notification types (ROOT_CERT_EXPIRY, INTERMEDIATE_CERT_EXPIRY, PARTNER_CERT_EXPIRY) are allowed.
However, when any of those certificate expiry notification types are provided, the API returns another error stating that only MISP_LICENSE_KEY_EXPIRY is allowed.

**Steps to Reproduce**

Invoke the GET /notifications endpoint.
Pass notificationType=MISP_LICENSE_KEY_EXPIRY.
Observe the response.
Invoke the same endpoint with notificationType=ROOT_CERT_EXPIRY.
Repeat with INTERMEDIATE_CERT_EXPIRY and PARTNER_CERT_EXPIRY.
Observe the responses.

**Actual Result**

**Case 1:** When using notification types other than MISP_LICENSE_KEY_EXPIRY, the API returns:

{
  "errorCode": "PMS_NOTIFICATION_ERROR_021",
  "message": "The selected notification type is invalid. Only 'ROOT_CERT_EXPIRY', 'INTERMEDIATE_CERT_EXPIRY', or 'PARTNER_CERT_EXPIRY' types are allowed for this filter."
}

**Case 2**: When using any of the allowed certificate expiry notification types (ROOT_CERT_EXPIRY, INTERMEDIATE_CERT_EXPIRY, PARTNER_CERT_EXPIRY), the API returns:

{
  "errorCode": "PMS_NOTIFICATION_ERROR_027",
  "message": "The selected notification type is invalid. Only 'MISP_LICENSE_KEY_EXPIRY' type is allowed for this filter."
}

**Expected Result**

The API should have consistent validation logic.

title: PMS-Automation : Partner certificate deleted in Key Manager but reference still exists in PMS, causing KER-PCM-012 on partner details fetch
content:
Problem description:
## Summary

When a partner's certificate is deleted from **Key Manager** (via the PMS-Automation cleanup/deletion job), only the certificate in Key Manager is removed. The corresponding `certificate_alias` reference in the PMS database (`pms.partner.certificate_alias`) is not cleared or updated.

As a result, PMS continues to assume the partner has a valid certificate and attempts to retrieve it from Key Manager during subsequent requests. Since the certificate no longer exists, the request fails.

The **GET `/partners/{partnerId}`** (Partner Details V2 API: `mosip.pms.partner.details.v2.get`) returns the following error:

```json
{
  "errorCode": "KER-PCM-012",
  "message": "Partner Certificate not found for the given ID."
}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Log in as **Partner Admin**.
2. Navigate to the **Partners** list.
3. Select an automation-created partner whose certificate has been deleted by the PMS-Automation cleanup job.
4. Click **View**.
5. Observe that the Partner Details page fails with a certificate-related error.

## Actual Behavior

- Certificate is deleted only from **Key Manager**.
- `pms.partner.certificate_alias` still contains the deleted certificate alias.
- PMS attempts to fetch the certificate using the stale alias.
- `GET /partners/{partnerId}` fails with:

```json
{
  "errorCode": "KER-PCM-012",
  "message": "Partner Certificate not found for the given ID."
}
```

## Expected Behavior

When a partner certificate is deleted from **Key Manager**, the PMS-Automation cleanup/deletion job should also clear (`NULL`) the corresponding `certificate_alias` field in the `pms.partner` table.

This ensures that:

- `GET /partners/{partnerId}` returns `isCertificateAvailable: false` instead of throwing an error.
- PMS and Key Manager remain synchronized.
- The Partner Details page loads successfully even when no certificate exists.

## Impact

- Partner Details API (`GET /partners/{partnerId}`) fails for affected partners.
- Partner View page cannot be opened from the UI.
- PMS and Key Manager become inconsistent due to stale certificate references.
- Manual database cleanup is required to restore functionality.

title: Fix the Snyk with Claude security-scan issues
content:
Problem description:
Comments from @Mahesh-Binayak 

Integrated Snyk with Claude to security-scan the Partner Management System — both the services backend and the portal frontend (release-1.3.x) — across dependencies, source code, container images, and Helm/IaC. Instead of raw scanner output, every finding is verified twice against the actual code, removing false positives and re-rating severity on real exploitability so developers act only on confirmed issues. Results are delivered as interactive HTML reports that club findings by package version, mark them fixable (orange) or not-yet-fixable (red), and pinpoint the exact file and line to change. The workflow is packaged as a reusable skill any developer can run on any repository to reproduce the same verified, actionable reports.

title: PMS Automation - Update Bio Extractor Request and DB Validator Test Cases
content:
Problem description:
## Description

The following automation issues were observed during the latest PMS automation execution and require updates.

### 1. Bio Extractor Request API Failure (`PMS_PRT_283`)

While executing the automation for the **Bio Extractor Request API**, the test fails with the following error:

```json
{
  "errorCode": "PMS_PRT_283",
  "message": "Bio extractor request already mapped for the given partner policy request id."
}
```

#### Observed Behavior

The automation attempts to create a bio extractor request for a partner policy request that already has an existing bio extractor request mapping, resulting in the `PMS_PRT_283` error.

#### Expected Behavior

The automation should create a **new partner policy request** before invoking the Bio Extractor Request API to ensure that no existing bio extractor request mapping is present.

**Automation Report:**
`mosip-api-internal.qajava21-pms-2026-07-05_21-06-full-report_T-1791_P-1764_S-7_F-20_I-0_KI-0.html`

#### Error Response

```json
{
  "id": "mosip.partnermanagement",
  "version": "1.0",
  "responsetime": "2026-07-05T21:07:00.290Z",
  "metadata": null,
  "response": null,
  "errors": [
    {
      "errorCode": "PMS_PRT_283",
      "message": "Bio extractor request already mapped for the given partner policy request id."
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### 2. Update DB Validator Automation

The automation for the following test case also requires an update:

**Test Case:** `TC_PMS_DBValidator_04`
**Objective:** Validate that data created using the MISP module is correctly stored and remains consistent in the database.

#### Expected Behavior

The automation should:

* Create the required data using the MISP module.
* Verify that the corresponding records are successfully persisted in the database.
* Validate that the stored database values match the API response and remain consistent across the relevant database tables.

## Impact

* The Bio Extractor Request API automation consistently fails because it reuses a partner policy request that already has an associated bio extractor request.
* The DB Validator automation does not perform the required validation for data created through the MISP module.

## Action Required

title: DSL: Multiple Online Verification Partner Creation Causing DSL Report Failures (36 Failures Observed)
content: Problem description: **Description:** Creating multiple Online Verification partners results in failures in the DSL report. The latest execution reported 36 failures, indicating that the application is unable to handle multiple partner creation requests consistently. **Steps to Reproduce:** Log in to the PMS Portal as a Partner Admin. Navigate to Partners > Create Partner. Select Online Verification Partner as the partner type. Create multiple Online Verification partners using unique valid data. Allow the DSL suite to execute the partner creation scenarios. Review the DSL execution report. Actual Result "The DSL report shows 36 failures during the Online Verification Partner creation execution." **Expected behaviour** The DSL report should complete without failures Discussion and resolution: [kameshsr]: ## Root Cause Analysis While debugging the `qajava21` DSL failure ("UIN not available in database") with the DevOps team, I traced the issue as follows: **Debugging steps:** 1. Took the RID from the DSL report and checked the `registration_transaction` table to find the timestamp when the packet reached the **UIN generator stage**. 2. At the same timestamp, checked the `credential_transaction` table in the `mosip_credential` DB — the credential issuance was **failing** with status comment: `Failed to fetch policy details`. 3. Decrypted one of the failing requests from the DB: ```json { "id": "2384532416475614", "credentialType": "auth", "issuer": "ovp02s10", "recepiant": "IDA", "user": "", "encrypt": false, "encryptionKey": null, "sharableAttributes": null, "additionalData": { "SALT": "1hDfApwGuqMu4X+33AIf4A==", "MODULO": "453", "expiry_timestamp": "+10000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "transaction_limit": null, "id_hash": "7FC1D80AF9E083408F64977EBF8FF8BBA79386C923588395BF750AD997640454", "TOKEN": "252813259604185339898615423021471220" }, "requestId": null } ``` **Findings:** - The issuer in the request is partner `ovp02s10` (created by @swethan1718 ). - ID Repo calls the PMS API to fetch the policy: `{{url}}/v1/partnermanager/partners/ovp02s10/credentialtype/auth/policies` - This call fails because the partner was created but the **policy was not mapped properly / not present**. PMS returns: ```json { "id": "mosip.partnermanagement", "version": "1.0", "responsetime": "2026-07-02T07:56:50.620Z", "metadata": null, "response": null, "errors": [ { "errorCode": "PMS_PRT_064", "message": "No details found" } ] } ``` **Conclusion:** - The policy fetch failure for partner `ovp02s10` is the root cause of credential issuance failing, which in turn caused the "UIN not available in DB" DSL failure. - @chetankh239 confirmed the DSL was **not tested against this feature in the dev environment**. - In other environments there is only **1 online verification partner**, whereas in `qajava21` more than 10 partners were created — which is how this surfaced. **Recommendation:** This feature should be dev-tested against DSL before release. [Prafulrakhade]: We are encountering multiple failures when executing the full test suite as mentioned above. Additionally, I executed one of the scenarios that consistently fails during the full suite run as an individual test. The same scenario completed successfully when run independently. **Scenario:** Scenario_232 Single Scenario Report: https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29588661/DSL-api-internal.qajava21-full-run-1782908822885-report_T-3_P-3_KI-0_I-0_S-0_F-0.html [mayuradesh]: @kameshsr @Prafulrakhade The "Online Verification Partner" feature for PMS is part of recently delivered build to QA in (qajava21). If this env is to be used by Platform team as well then we can deploy PMS(develop images) in a separate namespace in qajava21 to unblock the Platform team. [mayuradesh]: Hi @swethan1718 @n-chandrasekhar I have checked this DSL failures issue in `qajava21` env. Root cause analysis done by @kameshsr was very helpful. Issue is happening since QA is creating multiple Online_Verification_Partner in `qajava21` env and many of these have Rejected partner policy requests like partner_id=`ovp02s10`. ID Repo is expecting valid setup for Online_Verification_Partner which is normally only for partner_id=`mpartner-default-auth` and this will correspond to IDA module. In this case you have two options: 1. DSL failures will happen unless you have only valid data in PMS for Online_Verification_Partner, so you can delete all invalid Online_Verification_Partner from DB to get green DSL report. 2. While doing the feature testing of Online_Verification_Partner, ignore the DSL. Post testing done, remove invalid data. cc: @HariKrishnaReddyP696 @rachik-hue

title: PMS API -  Add V2 Admin Partner Endpoints and Extend Partner Creation Payload - logoUrl & additionalInfo
content:
Problem description:
# Add V2 Admin Partner Endpoints and Extend Partner Creation Payload

## Summary

Introduce V2 versions of the Admin Partner endpoints that expose additional partner configuration data required by Resident Portal and Physical Card ordering flows. Also extend the existing partner creation endpoint to accept these new fields.

## Background

The following partner attributes are required by downstream consumers but are not available through the existing Admin Partner APIs:

### `logoUrl`

* Used by Resident UI to display the partner logo.
* Used by Resident service templates (PDF generation and notification logo rendering).

### `additionalInfo`

* Container for partner-specific configuration and metadata.
* One current use case is `additionalInfo.orderRedirectUrl`, which is used by the Order Physical Card flow to redirect users to the partner's ordering page.
* If `orderRedirectUrl` is not configured when required, the flow fails with `REDIRECT_URL_NOT_FOUND`.

## Requirements

### 1. Add V2 endpoint for listing admin partners

#### New endpoint

```http
GET /admin-partners/v2
```

#### Response changes

Include the following additional attributes in the response:

```json
{
  "logoUrl": "string",
  "additionalInfo": {
    "...": "..."
  }
}
```

#### Deprecation

Deprecate:

```http
GET /admin-partners
```

---

### 2. Add V2 endpoint for retrieving a single admin partner

#### New endpoint

```http
GET /admin-partners/v2/{partnerId}
```

#### Response changes

Include the following additional attributes in the response:

```json
{
  "logoUrl": "string",
  "additionalInfo": {
    "...": "..."
  }
}
```

#### Deprecation

Deprecate:

```http
GET /admin-partners/{partnerId}
```

---

### 3. Extend partner creation endpoint

#### Endpoint

```http
POST /partners/v3
```

#### Request changes

Accept the following additional attributes in the request body:

```json
{
  "logoUrl": "string",
  "additionalInfo": {
    "...": "..."
  }
}
```

#### Deprecation

No deprecation required.

`POST /partners/v3` was introduced in version `1.3.0-beta.3`, so the contract can be updated directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

* `GET /admin-partners/v2` returns `logoUrl` and `additionalInfo` for all partners.
* `GET /admin-partners/v2/{partnerId}` returns `logoUrl` and `additionalInfo`.
* Existing Admin Partner endpoints are marked as deprecated.
* `POST /partners/v3` accepts and persists `logoUrl` and `additionalInfo`.
* Existing consumers can access `additionalInfo.orderRedirectUrl` through the new endpoints when configured.
* API documentation is updated to reflect the new request/response schemas and deprecation notices.
* Existing consumers remain unaffected until migrated to the V2 endpoints.

title: PMS API : Create new API GET /partners/{partnerId}/credentialtypes/{policyId}
content:
Problem description:
## Purpose

Currently, there is no API to fetch the credential type(s) directly from the partner_policy_credential_type table using a partnerId and policyId.

This API fills that gap by enabling a direct lookup — useful for admins managing partner configurations and for partners who want to verify their mapped credential type(s).

---

## Endpoint

GET /partners/{partnerId}/credentialtypes/{policyId}

Path Parameters

* partnerId (String, Path) — Partner identifier
* policyId (String, Path) — Policy identifier

Request Body

No request body.

---

## Response

200 OK — Active record(s) found

```json
{
  "id": null,
  "version": null,
  "responsetime": "2026-06-10T10:00:00.000Z",
  "errors": null,
  "response": {
    "credentialTypes": [
      "euin"
    ]
  }
}
```

200 OK — No active record found

```json
{
  "id": null,
  "version": null,
  "responsetime": "2026-06-10T10:00:00.000Z",
  "response": null,
  "errors": [
    {
      "errorCode": "PMS_PRT_064",
      "message": "No details found"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## Behaviour

* For non-admin users, validates that the given partnerId belongs to the requesting user (PMS_POLICY_ERROR_010 if not).
* Validates the partner exists and that its partner type is one of the types configured to support credential types (PMS_PRT_070 if not allowed).
* Validates the partner's policy group, then checks that policyId is an active policy under that policy group (PMS_PRT_098 if not).
* Queries partner_policy_credential_type for active (is_active = true, not deleted) records matching the given partnerId and policyId.
* Returns NO_DETAILS_FOUND (PMS_PRT_064) when no active record exists.
* Returns a credentialTypes array — typically a single entry per partner-policy pair, but the response supports multiple values since the table's primary key is (part_id, policy_id, credential_type).

---

## Roles Allowed

* PARTNER
* CREDENTIAL_PARTNER
* PARTNER_ADMIN
* CREDENTIAL_ISSUANCE
* CREATE_SHARE
* ONLINE_VERIFICATION_PARTNER

title: PMS Automation API Test Rig Using Hardcoded Expired Certificate — Update Required
content: Problem description: ### Short Summary of the Bug Generate dynamic root certificates for each test case execution ### Description ## Background The PMS Automation API Test Rig is currently configured with a hardcoded certificate that has expired, causing automation failures. During debugging, it was identified that the certificate intended for use by the automation framework has the following details: | Property | Value | |-----------|---------| | Created On | 05 July 2024 | | Expiry Date | 01 April 2027 | | Common Name (CN) | PMS_API_ABC_ORG | | Issuer | PMS_API_SUB_CA | | Key Size | 4096 bits | | Algorithm | RSA | | Signature Algorithm | sha256WithRSAEncryption | However, the automation configuration is still referencing an older certificate with a shorter validity period that has already expired. --- ## Issue The PMS Automation API Test Rig is: - Using a hardcoded certificate. - Not dynamically fetching the latest certificate. - Not aligned with PMS certificate rotation mechanisms. This results in: - API authentication failures. - Automation execution failures. - TLS handshake issues in certain environments. --- ## Root Cause The issue is caused by: - Hardcoded certificate configuration within the automation test rig. - Lack of certificate rotation support. - Absence of configuration-driven certificate loading. --- ## Impact ### Affected Areas - PMS Automation API Test Rig. - Partner API automation. - Credential and Partner workflow automation. - CI/CD pipeline executions. --- ## Expected Behavior The automation framework should: - Always use a valid certificate. - Support certificate rotation without code changes. - Avoid hardcoded certificate references. - Load certificates through configuration or centralized secret management. --- ## Proposed Fix ### Option 1 (Recommended) Implement configuration-driven certificate management by: - Using a configurable certificate path. - Loading certificates from a secure vault or secret management solution. - Supporting certificate rotation without requiring framework code updates. ### Option 2 Generate and configure a new certificate by: - Creating a certificate with the appropriate validity period. - Uploading the certificate to the automation framework. - Updating the automation configuration to reference the new certificate. --- ## Acceptance Criteria - Automation framework uses a valid certificate. - No expired certificates are referenced by the automation framework. - PMS Automation APIs execute successfully. - No TLS handshake failures occur. - No certificate-related authentication failures occur. - Certificate updates can be managed without modifying automation code. """ [mosip-api-internal.released-pms-2026-04-05_22-07-error-report_T-169_S-118_F-39_I-0_KI-12.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28501114/mosip-api-internal.released-pms-2026-04-05_22-07-error-report_T-169_S-118_F-39_I-0_KI-12.html) ### Attachments / Evidence / Links _No response_

title: PMS Revamp UI Automation: Request and Manage ABIS Partner Policy Linking
content:
Problem description:
### 1. Purpose/Description

Automate the validation that a Partner Admin can navigate to the Policies screen and perform end-to-end ABIS Partner Policy Linking activities. This includes requesting policy linkage to an ABIS Partner, approving or rejecting policy requests, viewing policy request statuses, and accessing detailed information for submitted requests.

### 2. Key Validations

* Verify that the **Policies** option is available on the home page and successfully navigates the user to the Policies screen.
* Validate that a Partner Admin can create a new policy linking request for an ABIS Partner.
* Verify that eligible policies are displayed correctly for selection during the policy linking request process.
* Validate mandatory field checks and business rule validations during policy request submission.
* Verify that a successfully submitted policy request is reflected in the policy requests listing.
* Validate that submitted policy requests display the correct approval status in the tabular view.
* Verify that a Partner Admin can view the complete details of a submitted policy request in read-only mode.
* Validate the **Approve** workflow and confirm that approved requests display the correct updated status.
* Verify the **Reject** workflow and confirm that rejected requests display the correct updated status.
* Validate that status transitions are reflected accurately in both list and detail views.
* Verify that policy request history and previously submitted requests are displayed correctly in the tabular view.
* Validate search, filtering, sorting, and pagination functionality for policy request records where applicable.
* Verify appropriate success, warning, and error messages during request creation, approval, and rejection operations.
* Validate role-based access controls to ensure only authorized users can perform policy management actions.
* Verify error handling for failed request submissions, approval failures, rejection failures, and backend service unavailability.
* Ensure that existing policy management functionality remains unaffected while supporting ABIS Partner Policy Linking workflows.

title: PMS Revamp UI Automation - MISP License Key Notification: Via Email (Partner Admin)
content:
Problem description:
**1. Purpose/Description**
Automate the validation that a Partner Admin receives **email notifications when MISP License Keys are nearing expiry**, ensuring timely reminders for renewal even when the Partner Admin is not actively logged into the PMS portal. This covers the correctness of email content, delivery timing, recipient accuracy, and expected behaviour across various expiry scenarios.

**2. Key Validations**
- Verify that an **email notification is triggered and delivered** to the correct Partner Admin email address when a MISP License Key reaches the defined nearing-expiry threshold, and that the email is received within the expected delivery timeframe.
- Validate that the **email content is accurate and complete** — including the correct license key name, partner ID, expiry date, and a clear call-to-action prompting the Partner Admin to renew the key, with no missing or incorrect dynamic values.
- Confirm that **email notifications are not triggered for already expired MISP License Keys** — only keys within the defined nearing-expiry window should generate email alerts, and fully expired keys should be excluded from triggering new email notifications.
- Ensure that **duplicate emails are not sent** for the same nearing-expiry event — validate that the notification system respects the intended frequency (e.g., once per threshold breach or once per day) and does not flood the Partner Admin's inbox with repeated alerts for the same key.
- Validate **edge case scenarios** — including behaviour when a key is renewed before the expiry date (no further emails should be sent), when multiple keys are nearing expiry simultaneously (separate or consolidated emails as per design), and when the Partner Admin's email address is updated in the system.

**3. Reference JIRA Story**
https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/MOSIP-43187

title: PMS Revamp UI Automation - Policies (Partner Admin): Save & Publish Policy During Policy Creation
content:
Problem description:
**1. Purpose/Description**
Automate the validation that a Partner Admin can **publish a policy immediately after saving it as a draft** during the policy creation flow, without having to navigate back to the policy list page. This ensures a streamlined policy creation experience where the policy becomes active and available for partner selection in a single, uninterrupted workflow.

**2. Key Validations**
- Verify that the **Save & Publish option is available** on the policy creation screen after filling in the required policy details, and that clicking it successfully saves the policy as a draft and publishes it in a single action without redirecting the user to the policy list page.
- Validate that upon successful Save & Publish, the **policy status is updated to 'Active'** (or the appropriate published state) and the policy becomes immediately available for partner selection, confirming the change is reflected correctly in both the UI and the database.
- Confirm that appropriate **success notifications or confirmation messages** are displayed to the Partner Admin upon successfully saving and publishing the policy, and that error messages are shown clearly if the action fails due to missing or invalid inputs.
- Ensure that **mandatory field validations** are enforced before the Save & Publish action is executed — the system should prevent publishing and highlight missing or incorrectly filled fields if the policy form is incomplete.
- Validate that a policy created via **Save & Publish behaves identically** to a policy that was first saved as a draft and then published separately — it should appear correctly in the policy list, be selectable by partners, and retain all entered policy details without data loss.

**3. Reference JIRA Story**
https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/MOSIP-43256

title: PMS Revamp UI Automation - MISP License Key Notification in Notification Panel (Partner Admin)
content:

Automate the validation that a Partner Admin can view notifications for **MISP License Keys nearing expiration** within the PMS portal's notification panel. This ensures the Partner Admin is promptly informed about upcoming key expirations directly from the notification panel, enabling timely renewals and preventing service disruptions.

**2. Key Validations**
- Verify that **MISP License Key expiration notifications appear in the notification panel** for a Partner Admin when one or more keys are nearing expiry, and that each notification displays the correct details — key name, partner ID, and expiry date — in the expected format.
- Validate that the **notification panel count/badge** accurately reflects the number of unread or unactioned MISP License Key expiration notifications, and updates correctly when notifications are dismissed or acted upon.
- Confirm that clicking on a notification within the panel either **navigates the user to the relevant screen** or provides sufficient detail to take action, and that the "View All Notifications" link correctly redirects to the full notifications page with the MISP License Key tab in focus.
- Ensure that **notifications are not generated for already expired MISP License Keys** — only keys within the defined nearing-expiry window should appear in the panel, and fully expired keys should be excluded from the notification panel.
- Validate the **dismiss functionality** within the notification panel — dismissing a notification removes it from both the panel and the View All Notifications page, the panel count decrements accordingly, and the empty state message is displayed correctly when all notifications are dismissed.

title: PMS Revamp UI Automation - MISP License Key Notification: Dashboard Badge (Partner Admin)
content:
Problem description:

Automate the validation that a Partner Admin can view a **badge on the Partner Admin dashboard** displaying the count of MISP License Keys nearing expiry. This ensures the Partner Admin is immediately alerted about pending renewals upon login, enabling proactive action before keys expire and cause disruption.

**2. Key Validations**

title: PMS Revamp UI Automation - MISP License Key Notification: View All Notifications Page (Partner Admin)
content:
Problem description:
**1. Purpose/Description**
Automate the validation that a Partner Admin can view all notifications related to expiring MISP License Keys on the **"View All Notifications"** page. This includes verifying correct navigation from the notification panel, accurate display of notification content, tab ordering, filter functionality, pagination, dismiss behavior, and edge case scenarios such as empty states and already-expired keys.

**2. Key Validations**
- Verify that clicking **"View All Notifications"** from the notification panel correctly redirects the Partner Admin to the Notifications page, and that the default tab loaded is **Root CA Certificate**, with the MISP License Key tab accessible in the correct sequence — Root CA Certificate → Intermediate CA Certificate → MISP License Key → Weekly Summary - Partner.
- Validate that the **MISP License Key notifications table** displays all required fields accurately — Title as "MISP License Key Expiration", Date & Time in browser local format (stored in UTC), and the Description with correct dynamic values for `<license_key_name>`, `<partner_id>`, and `<expiry_date>`.

title: Standalone eSignet Deployment Limitation: PMS Supports Only One Connected eSignet Instance
content:
Problem description:
### Short Summary of the Bug

Currently, PMS allows only a single eSignet instance to be connected at a time. This limitation prevents the deployment and management of multiple standalone eSignet instances within the same PMS environment. Support for multiple eSignet instance associations is required to enable scalable standalone deployments.

### Description

During standalone eSignet deployment, it was observed that PMS supports association with only one eSignet instance at a time. When an additional eSignet instance is configured, the existing association is overwritten or the new instance cannot be registered successfully.
This limitation prevents deploying and managing multiple standalone eSignet environments using the same PMS instance, which is required for multi-environment or multi-tenant use cases.
**Expected Behavior:**
PMS should support registration and management of multiple eSignet instances simultaneously without impacting existing associations.
**Current Behavior:**
Only one eSignet instance can be associated with PMS at any given time. Subsequent configurations are not supported or override the existing setup.
**Impact:**
Blocks deployment of multiple standalone eSignet instances.
Limits scalability and environment isolation.
Requires separate PMS instances for each eSignet deployment.

title: Biometric Extractor and Credential Type Details Not Displayed for CSV-Created default partners
content: Problem description: ## Description When a mosip default Partner created directly through CSV upload and the policy is already in Approved state, the UI does not display the associated Biometric Extractor Provider Mapping details and Credential Type details for the default Credential Partner/online verification partner. This issue occurs because CSV-based onboarding inserts records directly into the final policy mapping tables and does not create entries in the newly introduced request tables (`*_request` tables). As a result, the UI is unable to fetch and display the mapping details for such partners. This issue is applicable for all Partners that: * have Biometric Extractor Provider Mapping configured **(Default credential partners and Online verification partners )** * have Partner Policy linking in Approved state * were created directly through CSV during deployment or migration activities This issue does not occur for partners created through the UI flow because the request tables are populated correctly in that scenario. --- ## To Reproduce 1. Create a Credential Partner and Partner Policy mapping directly through CSV import. 2. Ensure the policy is inserted in Approved state. 3. Ensure Biometric Extractor Provider Mapping and Credential Type mappings are added directly into final mapping tables. 4. Login to PMS. 5. Navigate to the Partner Policy details or approval view page for the imported partner. 6. Observe the Biometric Extractor and Credential Type sections. --- ## Expected behavior The UI should display: * Biometric Extractor Provider Mapping details * Credential Type details for all approved Credential Partners, including those onboarded directly through CSV import. The UI behavior should remain consistent irrespective of whether the partner and policy mappings were created through: * UI workflow * CSV-based onboarding/import --- ## Screenshots --- ## Environment * QA21 Discussion and resolution: [chetankh239]: Implemented status-based endpoint handling for policy details by introducing approval-aware logic to dynamically switch between partner-scoped and request-scoped endpoints for bio-extractor and credential-type fetching. Applied changes for both Credential Partner and Online Verification Partner request types, ensuring correct data retrieval based on approval status.
