title: Enhancement: Add “Attribute Name” & "Credential Data Format" fields to Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration and Policy Mapping Workflow
content:
Problem description:
# 1. Purpose

As a Partner Admin, I want to add and manage an additional field named “Attribute Name” in the Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration so that the system can determine whether biometric data should be shared with the Credential Partner in format or Raw format during biometric extractor mapping and policy approval workflows.

---

# 2. Overview

This enhancement introduces a 2 mandatory fields named **“Attribute Name”** and **"Credential Data Format"** in the Create Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration form.

The fields will be populated by the Partner Admin while creating a Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration and will become part of the configuration metadata used across biometric extractor mapping and partner policy approval workflows.

The added Attribute Name and Credential Data Format values will later be visible to the Credential Partner during policy mapping and request creation and will also be displayed to the Partner Admin during policy approval review.


---
# 3. Field Name:

**Attribute Name**
**Credential Data Format**

---

# 4.  Pre-Requisites

- The user must be logged into PMS.
- The user must have the PARTNER_ADMIN role.
- The Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration card must be visible on the dashboard.
- The Create Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration form must already be accessible.

---

# 5. Basic Flow

1. Partner Admin logs into PMS.
2. The Dashboard is displayed.
3. The user clicks the Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration card.
4. The system navigates to the Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration Listing Page.
5. The user clicks Create Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration.
6. The Create Configuration Form is displayed.
7. The Partner Admin enters all required configuration details including the new Attribute Name and Credential Data Format fields.
8. The Partner Admin submits the configuration.
9. The system stores the new field value along with the configuration details.
10. A confirmation message is displayed.
11. The user is redirected to the Configuration Listing Page where the newly created configuration appears.

---

# 6. Enhancement Details

A new fields **“Attribute Name”** and **"Credential Data Format"** must be added to the Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration form.

This fields will determine how biometric data is shared with the Credential Partner:

**“Credential Data Format”**
- It is dropdown field with below 2 values:
> Raw Data
> Template Data
- If the value selected is "Raw Data, then Attribute name dropdown has below values:
> Photo
> Iris
> Finger
- If the value selected is "Template Data", then Attribute name dropdown has below values:
> Values configured in the default_application.properties file. (Pre configured by the implementer as per ID schema used)

**“Attribute Name”**
- It is a dropdown filed and the values in the dropdown are decided based in the value of the Credential Data Format field.
- If the chosen value matches the exact attribute name defined in the ID Schema, biometric data will be shared in format.
- If the value does not match the ID Schema attribute name, biometric data will be shared in Raw format.
- The values for the Attribute name are added as the configuration in the default application properties.
- The configuration name should be - 

The values added by the Partner Admin for the above 2 fields must flow through the following stages:

- Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration creation
- Credential Partner request policy mapping
- Partner Admin approval review
- Final approved biometric extractor policy mapping storage

---

# 7. Configuration Form Fields

The form must now include the following additional fields:

| Field Name | Type | Mandatory |
|---|---|---|
| Attribute Name | Dropdown | Yes |
| Credential Data Format| Dropdown | Yes |

---

# 8. Tooltip / Information Icon

An information icon (“i”) must be displayed beside the both the fields.

Please refer the UI/UX for the information icon messages.

---

# 9. Field Validation

## Mandatory Validation

- The Attribute Name field is mandatory.
- If the field is left empty and the user attempts submission, an inline validation message must be displayed:

> “This field is required.”

- The Credential Data format field is mandatory.
- If the field is left empty and the user attempts submission, an inline validation message must be displayed:

> “This field is required.”

---

# Submit Button Behaviour

- The Submit button must remain disabled until the new Attribute Name and credential data format field is populated along with all other mandatory fields.

---

# 10. Credential Partner Flow Enhancement

When a Credential Partner selects a Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration during request policy creation:

- The Attribute Name and Credential Data format fields, must also be visible along with the existing biometric extractor configuration details.
- The Credential Partner must be able to view the configured value before submitting the request policy for approval.

---

# 11. Policy Approval Flow Enhancement

When a Credential Partner submits a request policy containing biometric extractor and credential type mappings:

- The Partner Admin approval screen must display the **Attribute Name** and **Credential Data format** fields value along with the other Biometric Extractor Provider Mapping details.
- The Partner Admin must be able to review this value before approving or rejecting the policy request.

---

# 12. Database Enhancement

## partner_policy_request Table

A new column must be added to the `partner_policy_extract` table to store the **Attribute Name** and **Credential Data format** fields value when the Credential Partner submits a request policy using the selected Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration.

The field values selected from the configuration must be persisted in this table as part of the biometric extractor mapping request details.

---

## partner_policy_bioextractor Table

Once the Partner Admin approves the request policy:

- The **Attribute Name** and **Credential Data forma**t values must also be stored in the `partner_policy_bioextractor` table.
- The approved value must persist as part of the final biometric extractor mapping configuration.

---

# 11. Acceptance Criteria

## Form Display

The Create Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration form must display the new fields:

- Attribute Name
- Credential Data format

The fields must:

- Be mandatory
- Dropddowns
- Display an information icon with helper text

---

## Tooltip Behaviour

When the user interacts with the information icon beside the **Attribute Name** and **Credential Data format** fields the system must display the configured helper text explaining Template vs Raw data sharing behaviour.

---

## Mandatory Validation

If the **Attribute Name** and **Credential Data format** fields field is left empty:

- Form submission must be prevented
- Inline error message must appear:

> “This field is required.”

---

## Submit Button Behaviour

The Submit button must remain disabled until:

- Attribute Name and Credential Data format fields
- and all other mandatory fields

are populated successfully.

---

## Configuration Creation

When the configuration is created successfully:

- The Attribute Name and Credential Data format field values must be stored along with the Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration details.

---

## Credential Partner Visibility

During request policy creation:

- The Credential Partner must be able to view the Attribute Name and Credential Data format field values associated with the selected Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration.

---

## Partner Admin Approval Visibility

During policy approval review:

- The Partner Admin must be able to view the Attribute Name and Credential Data format field values under the Biometric Extractor Provider Mapping details section before taking an approval decision.

---

## Database Persistence

The  Attribute Name and Credential Data format field values must be stored successfully in:

- partner_policy_extract table
- partner_policy_bioextractor table

as part of the biometric extractor mapping workflow.

---

# 12. System Behaviour

- The system must preserve the Attribute Name and Credential Data format field values consistently across all related workflow stages.
- The selected language during login must remain consistent across screens.
- The UI must remain responsive across desktop and tablet devices.

---

# 13. Browser Compatibility

The enhancement must function across major browsers:

- Google Chrome
- Mozilla Firefox
- Microsoft Edge
- Safari

title: PMS API Review: MISP License API Refactor  & UUID-Based Resource Migration
content:
Problem description:
# MISP License API Refactor & UUID-Based Resource Migration

## Summary

Refactor the MISP License APIs and database schema to introduce UUID-based resource identification using `mispLicenseId`, simplify the API lifecycle, and remove legacy regeneration behavior.

This change enables:

- Cleaner REST semantics
- Stable resource identification
- Support for multiple license keys per partner
- Simplified update operations
- UUID-based resource access
- Enforcement of a single active MISP license per partner

---

## DB Changes

**Table: `pms.misp_licence`**

**Add new column:**

```sql
ALTER TABLE pms.misp_licence
ADD COLUMN misp_license_id UUID;
```

**Migration requirements:** Generate and populate a unique UUID for all existing rows in `pms.misp_licence`. Even duplicate rows must receive different UUIDs.

**Backfill script:**

```sql
UPDATE pms.misp_licence
SET misp_license_id = gen_random_uuid()
WHERE misp_license_id IS NULL;
```

**Constraints:**

```sql
ALTER TABLE pms.misp_licence
ALTER COLUMN misp_license_id SET NOT NULL;
```

Drop the existing composite primary key `(mispId, licenseKey)` and replace with `mispLicenseId` as the new primary key:

```sql
ALTER TABLE pms.misp_licence
DROP CONSTRAINT <existing_composite_pk_constraint_name>;

ALTER TABLE pms.misp_licence
ADD CONSTRAINT pk_misp_license_id
PRIMARY KEY (misp_license_id);
```

---

## API Changes

### 1. POST `/misp-licenses`

Create a new MISP license. This endpoint also serves as the license regeneration endpoint. Any regenerate action from the UI must invoke this endpoint.

**Request:**

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "version": "string",
  "requestTime": "2026-05-26T05:52:28.714Z",
  "metadata": {},
  "request": {
    "partnerId": "string",
    "policyId": "string",
    "licenseKeyName": "string",
    "expiryDate": "2026-05-26"
  }
}
```

**Behavior:**

_Case 1: No existing active license found for the partner_

- Create a new ACTIVE MISP license.
- Publish the `MISP_LICENSE_GENERATED` event.
- Return the newly created license.

_Case 2: One or more existing active licenses found for the partner_

- Mark all existing active licenses for the partner as INACTIVE in PMS. Deactivation is scoped to `partnerId` only — `policyId` is not factored in.
- Do not publish any WebSub events while deactivating the existing licenses.
- Create a new ACTIVE MISP license.
- Publish the `MISP_LICENSE_UPDATED` event.
- Return the newly created license.

**Business rules:**

- At any given time, there must be only one ACTIVE MISP license per partner in both PMS and IDA.
- `policyId` is optional. If not provided, the license is created with `policyId = null`. Deactivation logic remains the same regardless of whether `policyId` is provided.
- `policyId` is purely informational in PMS and carries no enforcement behavior in IDA.
- `licenseKeyName` must be unique per `partnerId` across all records, including deactivated ones. The uniqueness check scope changes from `partnerId + policyId + licenseKeyName` to `partnerId + licenseKeyName`. If a user attempts to create a license with a name already used by any record (active or inactive) for that partner, the API must return a validation error. Users must provide a new unique name each time they generate or regenerate a MISP License Key.

**Example response:**

```json
{
  "mispLicenseId": "2f4f8a9f-cce0-4f92-a1d7-f49cb4b65d77",
  "partnerId": "partner-1",
  "policyId": "policy-1",
  "licenseKeyName": "prod-license",
  "licenseKey": "XXXXX-XXXXX",
  "status": "ACTIVE",
  "expiryDate": "2026-05-26"
}
```

> **Note for UI:** Display a recommendation to the user to select a Policy Group and Policy Name before generating a MISP License Key. This should be a non-blocking warning, not a validation error.

> **Note for API consumers:** `policyId` is optional in the POST `/misp-licenses` request. If not provided, the license will be created without a policy association. Associating a policy is recommended for consistency but not enforced.

---

### 2. GET `/misp-licenses`

Retrieve all MISP licenses with pagination, sorting, and filtering. Return `mispLicenseId` in every record of the response.

---

### 3. Replace `GET /misp-licenses/{partnerId}` → `GET /misp-licenses/{mispLicenseId}`

`partnerId` is no longer a unique identifier because multiple license records (active and inactive) are supported per partner. Replace the path parameter with `mispLicenseId`.

> **Breaking change:** Existing consumers using `partnerId` as the path parameter must migrate to `mispLicenseId`.

---

### 4. Replace `PATCH /misp-licenses/{partnerId}` → `PATCH /misp-licenses/{mispLicenseId}`

Replace the path parameter with `mispLicenseId`.

**Supported updates:**

- `status`

> **Breaking change:** Existing consumers using `partnerId` as the path parameter must migrate to `mispLicenseId`.

> **Future enhancement:** Editing the expiry date of non-expired MISP licenses may be supported in a future release.

---

### 5. Remove `PUT /misp-licenses/{partnerId}`

Remove this endpoint completely. License regeneration is now handled exclusively through `POST /misp-licenses`.

---

## Deprecation of Legacy License Generation Endpoint

**Deprecated endpoint:** `GET /misps/{mispId}/licenseKey`

> Note: `mispId` represents the same value as `partnerId`.

**Existing behavior:**

1. Retrieves the active MISP license for the specified partner where `valid_to_date > current time`.
2. If an active license exists — returns the existing license, does not create a new license, does not publish any WebSub event.
3. If no active license exists — creates a new MISP license using the configured validity period, publishes the `MISP_LICENSE_UPDATED` event to WebSub (consumed by IDA), and returns the newly created license.

**New behavior:** Deprecate this endpoint and add a note that consumers should instead generate a new MISP license using`POST /misp-licenses` directly. 

**Reason:**

- Removes side effects from a GET endpoint.
- Aligns with REST principles.
- Consolidates all license generation and regeneration into POST.
- Supports the business rule that only one ACTIVE MISP license exists per partner.

---

## Final Resource Model

```
MISP License
 ├── mispLicenseId     (UUID, PK)
 ├── partnerId
 ├── policyId          (optional)
 ├── licenseKeyName    (unique per partnerId across all records)
 ├── licenseKey
 ├── expiryDate
 └── status
```

title: Online Verification Partner: View Online Verification Partner Policy Request Details
content:
Problem description:
# 1. Description

Implement the functionality that allows Partner Admin users to open and view the complete details of an Online Verification Partner policy request in a structured read-only format within PMS.

This feature must provide complete visibility into the policy request lifecycle, including:

- Policy request details submitted during Step 1
- Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration mappings completed during Step 2
- Credential Type mapping completed during Step 3
- Approval lifecycle status
- Administrative comments and decision history
- Workflow progression state

The screen must support partial workflow visibility, preserve historical configuration data, and provide a consistent read-only representation of the Online Verification Partner policy request throughout its lifecycle.

---

# 2. Purpose

As a Partner Admin, I should be able to open and view the details of a submitted Online Verification Partner policy request so that I can:

- Review the complete policy configuration associated with the Online Verification Partner.
- Verify the biometric extractor provider mappings configured for the policy.
- Review the credential type associated with the policy request.
- Understand the current approval state of the request.
- View comments, review notes, and approval/rejection decisions associated with the policy.
- Track the complete interaction history related to the policy request lifecycle.

This feature represents Step 3 of the Online Verification Partner policy onboarding workflow and enables the Partner Admin to define the credential type associated with the selected policy request before the request is submitted for approval.

The implementation should support credential type selection, step-based workflow navigation, validation handling, acknowledgement flow, and policy lifecycle progression while ensuring that only one credential type can be mapped for a single policy request.

As a Partner Admin, I should be able to map a credential type for an Online Verification Partner policy request so that the system clearly understands the credential generation or credential delivery mechanism associated with the selected policy.

- euin
- reprint
- auth

- eUIN_with_QR

- vercred

- Only one credential type can be mapped for a single Online Verification Partner policy request.

# 6. Scenarios

- Submit successfully completes the workflow.

## Negative Scenarios

content:
Problem description:
# 1. Description

Implement the functionality that allows Partner Admin users to map biometric extractor provider configurations for Online Verification Partner policy requests within PMS.

The feature should enable Partner Admin users to associate one or more biometric modalities with valid and active biometric extractor provider configurations as part of the Online Verification Partner policy onboarding workflow.

This functionality represents Step 2 of the policy onboarding journey and must support multi-modality configuration mapping, draft persistence, navigation between steps, and continuation of incomplete workflows.

The implementation should ensure that only valid and active biometric extractor provider configurations are available for selection and that duplicate modality mapping is prevented for the same policy request.

---

# 2. Purpose

As a Partner Admin, I should be able to map biometric extractor provider configurations for an Online Verification Partner policy request so that the selected policy can support biometric-based online verification operations using approved biometric extractor provider configurations.

---

# 3. Pre-requisite

- Step 1 – Request Policy must already be completed successfully.
- The policy request must exist in:
  - Pending for Approval status, or
  - Draft/In-Progress state as applicable.
- Online Verification Partner must already exist in PMS.
- Biometric Extractor Provider Configurations must already be created and activated by authorized administrators.
- Partner Admin user must be authenticated and logged into PMS.
- User must possess the `PARTNER_ADMIN` role.
- Policy request should already be linked to:
  - Online Verification Partner
  - Policy Group
  - Policy Name

---

# 4. Basic Flow

1. Partner Admin logs into PMS.

2. Partner Admin navigates to:
   Dashboard → Partner Policy Linking

3. Partner Admin opens an Online Verification Partner policy request that requires biometric extractor provider mapping.

4. System navigates the user to:
   - Step 2 – Map Biometric Extractor Provider

---

## Page Details

### Title
- Map Biometric Extractor Provider

---

## Mandatory Information Banner

The following banner message must be prominently displayed on the page:

> “For Online Verification Partners, mapping the policy to a Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration and Credential Type is mandatory. If this mapping is not completed, the policy request cannot be approved. Please follow the steps on this page to complete the required mapping.”

The banner should:
- Remain visible throughout the page lifecycle.
- Follow approved PMS UX styling guidelines.
- Be responsive across supported screen sizes.

---

## Auto-Populated Read-Only Fields

The following fields should auto-populate based on the selected policy request and remain non-editable:

- Partner ID
- Partner Type
- Policy Group
- Policy Name

---

## Field Details

### Biometric Modality*
Dropdown field containing:

- Face
- Iris
- Finger

---

### Modality Selection Rules

- Only unmapped modalities should appear in subsequent dropdown selections.
- Once a modality is selected and saved:
  - It should no longer appear in the dropdown for additional rows.
- Duplicate modality mapping must not be permitted for the same policy request.

Example:
- If Face is already mapped:
  - Remaining dropdown values should display only:
    - Iris
    - Finger

---

### Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration*
Dropdown field displaying:

- Only ACTIVE biometric extractor provider configurations
- Configurations created and managed within PMS

Inactive, disabled, or deleted configurations must not appear in the dropdown.

---

## Add More Functionality

After successfully adding one modality configuration mapping:

- An “Add More” option should become available.
- Clicking Add More should:
  - Add a new mapping row dynamically
  - Allow selection of another unmapped modality
  - Allow selection of another active biometric extractor provider configuration

---

## Maximum Mapping Rules

A maximum of three mappings should be allowed corresponding to:

- Face
- Iris
- Finger

Only one configuration should be allowed per modality.

---

# Action Buttons

## Save & Proceed

### Behaviour
On clicking Save & Proceed:

- System validates all mandatory fields.
- System validates duplicate modality restrictions.
- System persists biometric extractor provider mapping data.
- System navigates the user to:
  - Step 3 – Map Credential Type

---

## Clear Form

### Behaviour
On clicking Clear Form:

- All unsaved values entered on the current screen should reset.
- Previously saved mappings should remain unaffected.

---

## Cancel

### Behaviour
On clicking Cancel:

- User is redirected to:
  - Partner Policy Request listing page
- Policy request status should remain:
  - Pending for Approval

---

## Action Menu Behaviour after Cancel

After returning to the listing page, the Action menu should display:

- View
- Map Biometric Extractor Provider
- Map Credential Type

---

## Action Navigation Rules

### Map Biometric Extractor Provider
Navigates user back to:
- Step 2 – Map Biometric Extractor Provider

### Map Credential Type
- The option is greyed out

---

# 5. Alternate Flow

### Scenario 1 – Incomplete Mapping
If mandatory fields are incomplete:
- Save & Proceed should remain disabled or validation should trigger.
- User should remain on the same screen until validation succeeds.

---

### Scenario 2 – Duplicate Modality Selection
If the same modality is attempted more than once:
- System should block duplicate selection.
- Appropriate validation message should display.

---

### Scenario 3 – No Active Configurations Available
If no active biometric extractor provider configurations exist:
- Dropdown should remain empty or disabled.
- User should not be able to proceed.

---

### Scenario 4 – Session Timeout During Mapping
If user session expires during mapping:
- User should be redirected to login page.
- Unsaved data may be lost unless auto-save exists.

---

### Scenario 5 – Technical Failure During Save
If backend/API failure occurs:
- Mapping data should not persist partially.
- User should remain on the same page.
- Appropriate error message should display.

---

# 6. Scenarios

## Positive Scenarios

- Partner Admin successfully maps one biometric modality.
- Partner Admin successfully maps all three modalities.
- Save & Proceed successfully navigates to Credential Type mapping.
- Previously entered mapping data remains retained during navigation.

---

## Negative Scenarios

- Attempt to map duplicate biometric modalities.
- Attempt to proceed without mandatory values.
- Attempt to select inactive biometric extractor configurations.
- API failure during save operation.
- Invalid navigation attempts after deactivation.

---

# 7. Data Fields

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Partner ID | Auto-populated Online Verification Partner identifier |
| Partner Type | Auto-populated as Online Verification Partner |
| Policy Group | Auto-populated associated policy group |
| Policy Name | Auto-populated selected policy |
| Biometric Modality | Dropdown for Face, Iris, Finger |
| Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration | Dropdown containing active configurations |
| Add More | Dynamically adds additional mapping rows |
| Save & Proceed | Saves mappings and navigates to Step 3 |
| Previous Step | Navigates back to Step 1 |
| Cancel | Redirects to policy request listing |
| Clear Form | Clears current unsaved values |

---

# 8. Business Rules

- Only Partner Admin users should be authorized to perform biometric extractor provider mapping for Online Verification Partner policy requests.
- Only ACTIVE biometric extractor provider configurations should be displayed.
- One modality can have only one configuration mapping.
- Duplicate biometric modality mappings must not be allowed.
- A maximum of three mappings should be permitted corresponding to:
  - Face
  - Iris
  - Finger
- Save & Proceed should only succeed after all validations pass successfully.
- Mapping data should persist before navigation to Step 3.
- Previous Step navigation should retain previously entered mapping data.
- Cancel action should not delete saved mappings.
- Policy request should remain in Pending for Approval state until approval workflow is completed.

---

# 9. Acceptance Criteria

## Read-Only Field Validation

- Auto-populated fields must display correctly.
- Auto-populated fields must remain non-editable.

---

## Modality Validation

- Only Face, Iris, and Finger modalities should appear.
- Previously selected modalities should not reappear in subsequent rows.
- Duplicate modality selection should be prevented.

---

## Configuration Validation

- Only ACTIVE biometric extractor provider configurations should appear in the dropdown.
- Inactive or disabled configurations should not display.

---

## Add More Validation

- Add More option should appear after adding one mapping.
- Additional rows should support remaining unmapped modalities only.

---

## Save & Proceed Validation

On clicking Save & Proceed:
- Mandatory field validations should execute successfully.
- Mapping data should persist successfully.
- User should navigate to:
  - Step 3 – Map Credential Type

---

## Navigation Validation

- Previous Step should retain mapping data.
- Cancel should redirect user to policy request listing.
- Action menu options should appear correctly after cancellation.

---

## UI & UX Validation

- Mandatory informational banner should display prominently.
- Screen should align with approved PMS UX references.
- Page should remain responsive across supported devices.
- Language selected during login should persist.

---

# 10. Exceptions

- Unauthorized access attempt to biometric mapping workflow.
- Invalid policy request identifier.
- Duplicate biometric modality selection.
- No active biometric extractor provider configurations available.
- API/service failure during save operation.
- Session expiration during workflow progression.

title: Online Verification Partner:  Tabular View of Online Verification Partner Policy Requests in PMS Portal
content:
Problem description:
# 1. Description

Implement the functionality that allows Partner Admin users to view and manage a consolidated tabular list of policy requests associated with Online Verification Partners within the PMS portal.

The feature should provide a centralized and filterable overview of all submitted Online Verification Partner policy requests along with their approval lifecycle status, policy details, partner details, and mapping progression status.

The screen should additionally support sorting, filtering, pagination, conditional action rendering, and status-based row behavior to help Partner Admin users efficiently manage policy onboarding and approval workflows for Online Verification Partners.

---

# 2. Purpose

As a Partner Admin, I should be able to view a tabular list of all policy requests submitted for Online Verification Partners along with their complete details and approval status, so that I can monitor policy onboarding progress, track approval lifecycle states, perform mapping-related actions, and access detailed policy request information whenever required.

---

# 3. Pre-requisite

- Partner Admin user must be authenticated and logged into PMS successfully.
- User must have the `PARTNER_ADMIN` role assigned.
- Online Verification Partner entities must already exist within PMS.
- Policy request creation workflow for Online Verification Partners must already be implemented.
- Partner Policy Linking module must be accessible from the PMS dashboard or navigation menu.
- Policy requests for Online Verification Partners must already exist in the system for populated-state rendering.
- User authorization and policy visibility APIs must be operational.

---

# 4. Basic Flow

1. Partner Admin logs into PMS using valid credentials.

2. Partner Admin navigates to:
   Dashboard → Partner Policy Linking

3. System opens the:
   - Partner Policy Linking tabular view page

4. The page displays:
   - All submitted policy requests
   - Policies currently in approval workflow
   - Policies across all supported statuses for All Partners

5. The listing page must display policy records in descending order of:
   - Created Date
   - Created Time

6. Latest submitted records must always appear at the top of the table.

---

## Page Layout

### Main Title
- Policies

### Dynamic Record Count
The numeric value displayed beside the Policies title should represent:
- Total number of Online Verification Partner policy request records currently visible in the listing.

Example:
- Policies (10)

The count should dynamically update based on applied filters.

---

## Request Policy Button

### Placement
- Displayed at the top-right section of the page.

### Behavior
- Clicking the button navigates the user to:
  - Request Policy workflow for Online Verification Partner

The button must remain visible irrespective of:
- Applied filters
- Empty state
- Pagination state

---

## Sub Title

- List of Policy Requests

---

# Filter Functionality

A Filter button must be available above the table.

---

## Filter Button Behaviour

### First Click
- Expands the filter panel.

### Second Click
- Collapses the filter panel.

---

## Expanded Filter Section

The expanded filter panel should contain dropdown filters for:

- Partner ID
- Partner Type
- Policy Group
- Policy Name
- Status

---

## Filter Rules

Each filter must:
- Be rendered as a dropdown.
- Dynamically populate values based on available policy request records.
- Prevent duplicate dropdown values.
- Support immediate result updates upon selection.
- Support multi-filter combinations.

---

## Multi-Filter Behaviour

Partner Admin users must be able to combine multiple filters simultaneously.

Examples:
- Partner ID + Status
- Policy Group + Status
- Policy Name + Partner Type

Filtered results should dynamically refresh without requiring page reload.

---

## Clear Filter Functionality

When the filter panel is expanded:
- A Clear Filter link must appear beside the Filter button.

On clicking Clear Filter:
- All selected filters should reset.
- Full dataset should be restored.
- Dynamic record count should reset accordingly.

When filter panel is collapsed:
- Clear Filter link should not be visible.

---

# Tabular View Specifications

The table must display the following columns:

- Partner ID
- Partner Type
- Policy Group
- Policy Name
- Created Date
- Status
- Action

---

# Default Sorting Behaviour

- Records must default to descending order of Created Date and Time.
- Most recently created records must appear first.
- Older records must appear later in the list.

---

# Sorting Functionality

Each table column header must contain a sort icon.

Clicking the sort icon should:
- Toggle between ascending and descending sorting.

Sorting should function:
- Independently
- Along with active filters

Sorting behavior:
- Alphabetical sorting for textual fields
- Chronological sorting for date fields

---

# Row Behaviour

Each row should remain clickable except for deactivated records.

Clicking a row should navigate to:
- Online Verification Partner Policy Request Details page

---

# Action Column Behaviour

The Action column should conditionally display actions based on workflow state.

---

## View Action

The View option should be available for:
- Approved
- Pending for Approval
- Rejected

The View option should not be available for:
- Deactivated records

---

## Mapping Actions

If policy request workflow is incomplete and the partner has not completed:
- Biometric Extractor Provider Mapping
- Credential Type Mapping

Then the Action menu should additionally display:

- Map Biometric Extractor Provider
- Map Credential Type

These actions should allow Partner Admin users to continue incomplete workflow stages.

---

# Status Display Rules

Status should be visually distinguishable using color coding aligned with UX specifications.

Supported statuses include:
- Approved
- Pending for Approval
- Rejected
- Deactivated

Color representation must follow approved PMS UX standards.

---

# Deactivation Behaviour

If a policy request has been deactivated:

- Entire row should appear greyed out.
- Row should become non-clickable.
- Action column should not allow navigation or actions.
- Status column must clearly display:
  - Deactivated

---

# Pagination

The table should support:

- Pagination controls
- Configurable records per page
- Navigation between pages
- Proper pagination reset when filters are applied

Pagination state should remain stable during sorting operations.

---

# Alternate Navigation Flow

Partner Admin users may navigate to this page:

- Directly from Partner Policy Linking option from dashboard
- After successful completion of:
  - Request Policy workflow
  - Mapping workflows
  - Approval workflows

In all cases:
- Latest records must appear at the top.

---

# Data Visibility Rules

All Online Verification Partner policy request records should be visible to:
- Authorized Partner Admin users

Records should not be restricted based on:
- Individual creator
- Session owner

This ensures centralized administrative visibility and governance.

---

# 5. Alternate Flow

### Scenario 1 – Empty State
If no Online Verification Partner policy requests exist:
- Empty-state UI should render.
- Request Policy button should remain visible.
- Filters may remain hidden or disabled based on UX behavior.

---

### Scenario 2 – Filter Produces No Results
If applied filters return no matching records:
- Table should display empty result state.
- Record count should display:
  - Policies (0)

---

### Scenario 3 – Deactivated Policy Record
If a policy request is deactivated:
- Row should become non-clickable.
- Actions should be disabled.
- Greyed-out rendering should apply consistently.

---

### Scenario 4 – Incomplete Mapping Workflow
If biometric extractor mapping or credential type mapping is incomplete:
- Additional mapping actions should appear in the Action column.

---

# 6. Scenarios

### Positive Scenarios
- Partner Admin successfully views all Online Verification Partner policy requests.
- Filters dynamically update results.
- Sorting works correctly on filtered datasets.
- Request Policy navigation works successfully.
- Mapping continuation actions display correctly.

### Negative Scenarios
- Invalid filter combinations resulting in empty datasets.
- Attempt to interact with deactivated records.
- API/service failure while fetching policy request records.
- Pagination inconsistencies after filtering or sorting.

---

# 7. Data Fields

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Partner ID | Identifier of Online Verification Partner |
| Partner Type | Displays Online Verification Partner |
| Policy Group | Associated Policy Group |
| Policy Name | Name of requested policy |
| Created Date | Date and time of request creation |
| Status | Current approval lifecycle state |
| Action | Contextual actions based on workflow state |
| Filter Controls | Dynamic dropdown filters |
| Request Policy Button | Navigates to Request Policy workflow |

---

# 8. Business Rules

- Records must always default to descending Created Date sorting.
- Filters should dynamically update visible records.
- Sorting must work on filtered datasets.
- Duplicate dropdown filter values should not appear.
- Deactivated policy records must remain non-clickable.
- Record count should update dynamically for filtered and unfiltered states.
- Request Policy button must remain persistently visible.
- Mapping actions should appear only for incomplete workflow stages.
- Language selected at login should persist across the screen.
- All policy records for Online Verification Partners should remain visible to authorized Partner Admin users.

---

# 9. Acceptance Criteria

### Page Rendering Validation
- Policies page must render correctly for:
  - Empty state
  - Populated state

---

### Record Visibility Validation
- All Online Verification Partner policy requests must display correctly in the table.
- Latest created records must appear first.

---

### Filter Validation
- Filter expand/collapse behavior must function correctly.
- Multi-filter combinations must work successfully.
- Clear Filter must reset all filter selections.

---

### Sorting Validation
- Sorting must work across all sortable columns.
- Sorting must work on filtered datasets.
- Default sorting must remain descending by Created Date.

---

### Action Validation
- Request Policy button must navigate correctly.
- View action must work for applicable statuses.
- Mapping actions must appear for incomplete workflow stages.

---

### Deactivation Validation
- Deactivated rows must appear greyed out.
- Deactivated rows must remain non-clickable.
- Action menu must remain disabled for deactivated records.

---

### Pagination Validation
- Pagination controls must function correctly.
- Records per page configuration must work successfully.

---

### UI & UX Validation
- UI implementation must align with approved PMS UX references.
- Screen must remain responsive across supported devices.
- Language consistency must persist across navigation flows.

---

# 10. Exceptions

- Unauthorized access to Partner Policy Linking module.
- API/service failure during policy retrieval.
- Pagination failure during large dataset rendering.
- Filter synchronization issues.
- Sorting inconsistencies after dynamic updates.
- Session timeout during navigation.

---

# 11. Documentation

- PMS Partner Policy Linking Functional Specification
- Online Verification Partner Workflow Documentation
- Policy Request Management Documentation
- Mapping Workflow Functional Documentation
- Role-Based Access Control Documentation
- UX Design Reference

---

# 12. Compatible Browsers

- Google Chrome
- Mozilla Firefox
- Microsoft Edge
- Safari

---

# 13. Implementation Details

- Implement Partner Policy Linking listing page for Online Verification Partner workflows.
- Implement dynamic filtering and sorting APIs.
- Implement pagination and record count handling.
- Implement conditional rendering for mapping continuation actions.
- Implement status-based row rendering and interaction restrictions.
- Implement default latest-first sorting behavior.
- Integrate Request Policy navigation workflow.
- Ensure dynamic dataset updates without full page refresh.
- Implement responsive rendering for all supported screen sizes.

---

# 14. UI/UX:

https://www.figma.com/design/AcdT4y2HVIcRDG5FQ1c95d/PMS_Revamp?node-id=10888-8282&t=XaNXCz3F5PIHQuOW-1

title: Online Verification Partner: Request Policy for Online Verification Partner in PMS Portal
content:
Problem description:
# 1. Description

Implement the functionality that allows Partner Admin users to request policy linkage for Online Verification Partners through the PMS portal. The feature should enable Partner Admin users to initiate a new partner-policy request by selecting an eligible Online Verification Partner, associating an active policy under the linked policy group, and proceeding to the biometric extractor provider configuration mapping stage.

The workflow should ensure that policy requests are created only for valid and eligible Online Verification Partners whose certificates are successfully uploaded and whose policy groups are already configured.

The feature should additionally support validation mechanisms to prevent duplicate policy requests in Approved or Pending for Approval status while allowing re-submission for previously Rejected policy requests.

---

# 2. Purpose

As a Partner Admin, I should be able to request a policy to be linked to an Online Verification Partner ID, so that the partner can proceed with biometric extractor provider configuration mapping and subsequent policy approval workflows required for operational enablement.

---

# 3. Pre-requisite

- Partner Admin must be authenticated and logged into PMS using valid credentials.
- User must have the `PARTNER_ADMIN` role assigned.
- Partner Admin must have already navigated to the PMS Home Page.
- Online Verification Partner records must already exist in PMS.
- The corresponding Online Verification Partner certificate must be successfully uploaded.
- Policy Group must already be linked to the Online Verification Partner either:
  - During partner creation, or
  - Through policy group assignment workflow.
- Active policies must already exist under the associated Policy Group.
- Partner Policy Linking module and APIs must be accessible and operational.

---

# 4. Basic Flow

1. Partner Admin logs into PMS.

2. Partner Admin navigates to:
   Dashboard → Partner Policy Linking

3. System displays the Partner Policy Linking landing page containing policy requests for all supported partner types.

4. Partner Admin clicks:
   - Request Policy

The Request Policy button should be displayed:
- At the center of the page when no policy requests are available.
- At the top-right section of the page when policy requests already exist.

5. System navigates the user to the:
   - Request Policy screen

---

## Request Policy Screen

### Title
- Request Policy

### Sub Title
- All fields marked with * are mandatory

---

## Request Policy Form Fields

### Partner Type
- Auto-populated as:
  - Online Verification Partner
- Field remains disabled for editing.

---

### Partner ID
- Dropdown field

#### Help Text
- Select partner ID

#### Behavior
- Displays only Online Verification Partner IDs where:
  - Partner certificate upload status is successful

#### Information Icon Text
- Only those partner IDs whose partner certificate is uploaded are available in the dropdown. If you don't find your partner ID, please upload partner certificate first.

---

### Policy Group
- Auto-populated based on selected Partner ID.
- Field remains disabled for editing.

#### If Policy Group is unavailable:
- Field remains blank.
- Placeholder displayed:
  - No policy group linked to the given Partner ID.

---

### Policy Name
- Dropdown field

#### Help Text
- Select policy name

#### Behavior
- Displays only ACTIVE policies associated with the selected Policy Group.
- Dropdown includes search functionality.
- Each dropdown item displays:
  - Policy Name
  - Policy Description

---

### Comments
- Textarea field

#### Help Text
- Mention the purpose of requesting the policy

---

## Actions

### Save & Proceed
- Enabled only after all mandatory fields are completed successfully.

#### On clicking Save & Proceed:
- System validates all entered details.
- Policy request is created successfully.
- System navigates the user to:
  - Step 2 – Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration Mapping

---

### Cancel
- Navigates back to Partner Policy Linking listing page without saving any data.

---

### Clear Form
- Clears all entered values from the form fields.

---

## Successful Save & Proceed Flow

After successful policy request creation:
- Policy request record is saved successfully.
- Initial policy request status becomes:
  - Draft / In Progress (as applicable)
- User is redirected to:
  - Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration Mapping screen

---

# 5. Alternate Flow

### Scenario 1 – Missing Policy Group
If no Policy Group is linked to the selected Online Verification Partner:
- Policy Group field should remain blank.
- Policy Name dropdown should remain disabled or empty.
- User should not be allowed to proceed further until a valid Policy Group is linked.

---

### Scenario 2 – Duplicate Policy Request
If the selected policy is already associated with the same Online Verification Partner in:
- Approved status, or
- Pending for Approval status

Then:
- Duplicate policy request should not be allowed.
- Appropriate validation message should be displayed.

---

### Scenario 3 – Previously Rejected Policy Request
If the same policy was previously rejected:
- System should allow creation of a new policy request.
- Previous rejected request should remain available for audit/reference purposes.

---

### Scenario 4 – Technical Failure During Request Creation
If backend/API failure occurs while creating the policy request:
- Policy request should not be saved partially.
- Appropriate technical error message should be displayed.
- User should remain on the Request Policy screen.

---

# 6. Scenarios

### Positive Scenarios
- Partner Admin successfully creates a policy request for an Online Verification Partner.
- System successfully redirects user to Step 2 – Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration Mapping.
- Policy Group and Policy Name values populate correctly based on selected Partner ID.

### Negative Scenarios
- Attempt to request duplicate policy already in Approved status.
- Attempt to request duplicate policy already in Pending for Approval status.
- Attempt to proceed without mandatory fields.
- Attempt to request policy for partner without uploaded certificate.
- API/service failure during request creation.

---

# 7. Data Fields

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Partner Type | Auto-populated as Online Verification Partner |
| Partner ID | Dropdown containing eligible Online Verification Partner IDs |
| Policy Group | Auto-populated based on selected Partner ID |
| Policy Name | Dropdown displaying active policies under selected Policy Group |
| Comments | Free-text field for policy request purpose |
| Save & Proceed | Saves request and navigates to biometric mapping configuration |
| Cancel | Returns user to listing page without saving |
| Clear Form | Clears entered field values |

---

# 8. Business Rules

- Only users with the `PARTNER_ADMIN` role should be authorized to create Online Verification Partner policy requests.
- Only Online Verification Partners with successfully uploaded certificates should appear in the Partner ID dropdown.
- Policy Group should auto-populate based on selected Partner ID and remain non-editable.
- Only ACTIVE policies under the linked Policy Group should appear in the Policy Name dropdown.
- Duplicate policy requests should not be allowed for:
  - Approved policies
  - Pending for Approval policies
- Previously Rejected policy requests may be re-requested.
- Save & Proceed action should only be enabled after mandatory fields are completed successfully.
- Successful Save & Proceed action should always navigate the user to:
  - Step 2 – Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration Mapping
- Policy request creation should not automatically approve or activate the policy linkage.

---

# 9. Acceptance Criteria

### Request Policy Navigation Validation
- Given a Partner Admin logs into PMS,
- When the admin navigates to Partner Policy Linking,
- And clicks Request Policy,
- Then the system must open the Request Policy screen.

---

### Partner Type Validation
- Partner Type field must display:
  - Online Verification Partner
- Field must remain disabled for editing.

---

### Partner ID Validation
- Partner ID dropdown must display only Online Verification Partners with successfully uploaded certificates.
- Information icon text must display correctly.

---

### Policy Group Validation
- Policy Group must auto-populate based on selected Partner ID.
- Field must remain disabled for editing.
- If no Policy Group exists:
  - Appropriate placeholder text must display.

---

### Policy Name Validation
- Policy Name dropdown must display only ACTIVE policies under the linked Policy Group.
- Dropdown must support search functionality.
- Policy Name and Policy Description must display correctly.

---

### Save & Proceed Validation
- Save & Proceed button must remain disabled until all mandatory fields are completed.
- On clicking Save & Proceed:
  - Policy request must be created successfully.
  - User must be redirected to:
    - Step 2 – Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration Mapping

---

### Duplicate Policy Validation
- Duplicate policy requests in Approved or Pending for Approval status must be blocked.
- Appropriate validation message must be displayed.

---

### UI & Behaviour Validation
- UI implementation must align with approved PMS UX references.
- Language selected during login must persist across all screens.
- The Request Policy screen must remain responsive across supported devices and resolutions.
-  Mandatory Banner Message Displayed on page:
“For Online Verification Partners, mapping the policy to a Biometric Extractor Configuration and Credential Type is mandatory. If this mapping is not completed, the policy request cannot be approved. Please follow the steps on this page to complete the required mapping”

---

# 10. Exceptions

- Unauthorized access attempt for policy request creation.
- Partner ID not found or invalid.
- Policy Group unavailable for selected partner.
- Duplicate policy request submission.
- Backend/API failure during request creation.
- Session timeout during policy request workflow.

---

# 11. Documentation

- PMS Partner Policy Linking Functional Specification
- Online Verification Partner Workflow Documentation
- Policy Request Creation API Documentation
- Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration Documentation
- Role-Based Access Control Documentation
- UX Design Reference

---

# 12. Compatible Browsers

- Google Chrome
- Mozilla Firefox
- Microsoft Edge
- Safari

---

# 13. Implementation Details

- Implement Request Policy workflow for Online Verification Partner type within Partner Policy Linking module.
- Integrate Partner ID dropdown with certificate validation status.
- Implement auto-population logic for Policy Group based on selected Partner ID.
- Fetch and display only ACTIVE policies associated with the linked Policy Group.
- Implement duplicate policy request validation for Approved and Pending for Approval records.
- Implement Save & Proceed navigation to:
  - Step 2 – Biometric Extractor Provider Configuration Mapping
- Ensure incomplete or failed requests are not persisted partially in the database.
- Maintain audit logs for policy request creation activities.

---

# 14. UI/UX

Implemented the **Request Policy workflow for Online Verification Partner** in the PMS portal, enabling Partner Admin users to request policy linkage for eligible Online Verification Partners and proceed with biometric extractor provider configuration mapping.

- Added **Request Policy flow** under **Partner Policy Linking** for **Online Verification Partner** type.
- Implemented **Partner ID dropdown validation** to display only partners with successfully uploaded certificates.
- Added **auto-population of Policy Group** based on selected Partner ID (read-only field behavior).
- Implemented logic to fetch and display **only ACTIVE policies** linked to the associated Policy Group.

### Description

Login with the same user into PMS portal.

image-20250605-085514.png
Expected result:

When user attributes are missing from Keycloak, the message should display as proper actionable suggestion for the users.

## Title
Update GET `/notifications` response fields

## Description

The `GET /notifications` API was introduced in `v1.3.0-beta.1`.

This endpoint retrieves notifications from the `pms.notifications` table and supports:
- pagination
- sorting
- filtering via optional query parameters

## Requested Changes

The API response should:
- no longer include `notificationPartnerId`
- expose the raw/actual `notificationType` value from `pms.notifications`

* `ROOT_CERT_EXPIRY`

title: PMS API Review: Update credential-types request POST endpoint to use requestId
content:
Problem description:
## Title
Update credential-types request POST endpoint to use requestId

## Description

The current endpoint:

```http
POST /{partnerId}/policies/{policyId}/credential-types-request
```

should be renamed to:

```http
POST /partner-policy-requests/{requestId}/credential-types-request
```

## Reason for Change

The credential types request is associated with a specific `partner-policy-request`, so using `requestId` in the endpoint path better reflects the underlying resource relationship and simplifies the API structure.

Since `partnerId` and `policyId` are being removed from the endpoint path, they should instead be resolved internally using `requestId`.

## Expected Outcome

- Replace the existing endpoint with:

  ```http
  POST /partner-policy-requests/{requestId}/credential-types-request
  ```

- Update API contract and controller mappings accordingly.
- Resolve `partnerId` and `policyId` internally using `requestId`.
- Ensure related test cases and documentation are updated.
- Update the UI to use the new endpoint structure.

title: Online Verification Partner: Approve or Reject Online Verification Partner Policy Requests in PMS Portal
content:
Problem description:
# 1. Description

Enable Partner Admin users to review, approve, or reject policy requests submitted by Online Verification Partners through the PMS portal. The feature should ensure that only policy requests with all mandatory mappings and configurations completed are approved and linked to the partner, enabling the partner to perform authorized operations based on the approved policy association.

---

# 2. Purpose

As a Partner Admin, I should be able to approve or reject policy requests submitted by Online Verification Partners so that only fully configured and valid policies are approved and linked to the partner, enabling them to perform activities based on the policy association.

---

# 3. Pre-requisite

- Partner Admin must be authenticated and logged into PMS using valid credentials.
- User must have the `PARTNER_ADMIN` role assigned.
- Online Verification Partner must have initiated a policy request.
- The policy request must currently be in:
  - Pending for Approval status
- The Online Verification Partner must have completed at least Step 1:
  - Add Policy Request
- Partner policy requests must be visible in the List of Policy Linkages section.

---

# 4. Basic Flow

1. Partner Admin logs into PMS.

2. Partner Admin navigates to:
   Dashboard → Partner Policy Linkages

3. System displays the List of Policy Requests page.

4. Partner Admin identifies policy requests with:
   - Pending for Approval status

5. Each policy request row contains a three-dot (⋮) action menu.

6. Partner Admin clicks the action menu corresponding to the required Online Verification Partner policy request.

7. The system displays:
   - Approve / Reject

8. Partner Admin selects:
   - Approve / Reject

9. System opens the Approval Popup Screen.

---

## Approval Popup Screen

### Main Title
- Policy Name along with Policy ID is displayed dynamically.

### Sub Title
- Do you want to Approve/Reject the Policy?

### Description
- Please review the policy details carefully before taking appropriate action.

---

## Sections Displayed in Popup

### Policy Details
Displays details captured during:
- Step 1 – Add Policy Request

### Biometric Extractor Configuration Mapping
Displays details configured during:
- Step 2 – Biometric Mapping

### Credential Type Mapping
Displays details configured during:
- Step 3 – Credential Type Mapping

If any mappings are incomplete:
- Corresponding sections remain visible.
- Sections display empty or incomplete data accordingly.

---

## Approve Flow

1. Partner Admin clicks:
   - Approve

2. System validates whether all required mappings are completed:
   - Biometric Extractor Configuration Mapping
   - Credential Type Mapping

3. If all mappings are completed successfully:
   - Policy request is approved.
   - Status is updated to:
     - Approved
   - Data is moved from:
     - pms.partner_policy_bioextract_request
     - pms.partner_policy_credential_type_request

   To:
     - partner_policy_bioextract
     - partner_policy_credential_type

4. System redirects the admin back to:
   - List of Partner-Policy Linkages

---

## Incomplete Mapping Validation

If any mandatory mappings are incomplete:
- Approval process is blocked.
- Appropriate validation message is displayed.
- Policy status remains:
  - Pending for Approval
- No data movement occurs.

---

## Reject Flow

1. Partner Admin clicks:
   - Reject

2. System updates policy request status to:
   - Rejected

3. System redirects admin back to:
   - List of Partner-Policy Linkages

4. Online Verification Partner must create a new policy request for future processing if required.

---

## Close Action

1. Partner Admin clicks the Close icon in the popup window.

2. System closes the popup.

3. No updates are made to the policy request.

4. User is redirected back to:
   - List of Partner-Policy Linkages

---

# 5. Alternate Flow

### Scenario 1 – Incomplete Configuration Mapping
If the Online Verification Partner has completed only Step 1 or partially completed Step 2 or Step 3:
- Partner Admin should still be able to view the policy request.
- Mapping sections should remain visible but incomplete.
- Approval should be prevented until all mandatory mappings are completed.

---

### Scenario 2 – Policy Rejection
If the Partner Admin rejects the policy request:
- Policy status should update to:
  - Rejected
- Policy request should become non-reusable.
- Online Verification Partner must submit a new policy request for future approval.

---

### Scenario 3 – Close Without Action
If the Partner Admin closes the popup without selecting Approve or Reject:
- No changes should be made to the policy request.
- Existing policy status should remain unchanged.

---

# 6. Scenarios

### Positive Scenarios
- Partner Admin successfully approves a fully configured Online Verification Partner policy request.
- Policy status changes successfully to Approved.
- Policy mapping data is moved successfully to final linkage tables.
- Partner Admin successfully rejects a policy request.

### Negative Scenarios
- Approval attempted with incomplete biometric mappings.
- Approval attempted with incomplete credential type mappings.
- Backend/API failure during approval or rejection processing.
- Unauthorized user attempts policy approval or rejection.
- Data migration failure while moving approved policy mappings to final tables.

---

# 7. Data Fields

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Policy ID | Unique identifier associated with the policy request |
| Policy Name | Name of the requested policy |
| Policy Status | Displays Pending for Approval, Approved, or Rejected |
| Partner Type | Must display Online Verification Partner |
| Policy Details | Displays policy request information from Step 1 |
| Biometric Extractor Configuration Mapping | Displays biometric mapping information from Step 2 |
| Credential Type Mapping | Displays credential type mapping information from Step 3 |
| Approve Button | Used to approve completed policy requests |
| Reject Button | Used to reject policy requests |
| Close Icon | Used to close popup without taking action |

---

# 8. Business Rules

- Only users with the `PARTNER_ADMIN` role should be authorized to approve or reject Online Verification Partner policy requests.
- Policy requests must remain in:
  - Pending for Approval status
  until explicitly approved or rejected.
- Approval should be allowed only when all mandatory mappings are completed successfully.
- Incomplete biometric extractor mappings must block approval.
- Incomplete credential type mappings must block approval.
- Rejected policy requests must not be reused for future processing.
- Upon successful approval:
  - Data must move from request tables to final policy linkage tables.
- Data must remain in request tables until approval is completed successfully.
- Policy approval or rejection must not modify unrelated partner configuration data.

---

# 9. Acceptance Criteria

### Policy Request Listing Validation
- Partner Admin must be able to view all policy requests currently in Pending for Approval status.
- The Approve / Reject option must be available through the action menu for eligible policy requests.

---

### Approval Popup Validation
- Clicking Approve / Reject must open the approval popup window.
- Popup must display:
  - Policy details
  - Biometric mapping details
  - Credential type mapping details

- If mappings are incomplete:
  - Sections should remain visible but incomplete.

---

### Approval Validation
- If all mappings are completed successfully:
  - Approval must succeed.
  - Policy status must update to Approved.
  - Data must move to final linkage tables.
  - User must be redirected back to the List of Partner-Policy Linkages page.

---

### Incomplete Mapping Validation
- If mandatory mappings are incomplete:
  - Approval must be blocked.
  - Appropriate validation message must be displayed.
  - Policy status must remain Pending for Approval.

---

### Reject Flow Validation
- On clicking Reject:
  - Policy status must update to Rejected.
  - User must be redirected back to the listing page.

---

### Close Action Validation
- On clicking Close:
  - No changes should be made to policy data or status.
  - User should be redirected back to the listing page.

---

### UI & Behaviour Validation

Problem description:
# 1. Description

Enable Partner Admin users to deactivate an existing Online Verification Partner through the PMS portal. The feature should ensure that partners whose services are no longer required are prevented from remaining in active operational state within the system, while preserving all historical partner data and associated records for audit and traceability purposes.

---

# 2. Purpose

As a Dev, I want to implement the feature that allows a Partner Admin to deactivate an existing Online Verification Partner, so that the partner can no longer remain active in the system when their services are no longer required.

---

# 3. Pre-requisite

- Partner Admin must be authenticated and logged into PMS with valid credentials.
- User must have the `PARTNER_ADMIN` role assigned.
- Online Verification Partner records must already exist in PMS.
- The selected partner must currently be in ACTIVE status.
- Partner listing APIs and status management services must be available and accessible.

---

# 4. Basic Flow

1. Partner Admin logs into PMS.

2. Partner Admin navigates to:
   Dashboard → Partners Card → List of Partners

3. The system displays the List of Partners page with the latest created partner records appearing at the top of the list.

4. The Partner Admin can use:
   - Search functionality
   - Filter functionality

5. The admin filters specifically for:
   - Online Verification Partner

6. Each Online Verification Partner row contains a three-dot (⋮) action menu at the end of the row.

7. The Partner Admin clicks the three-dot action menu.

8. The system displays the available options:
   - View
   - Deactivate

9. The admin selects:
   - Deactivate

10. The system displays a confirmation popup window with the following message:

    Do you want to deactivate partner with <Partner ID> belonging to Organisation: <Org ID>?

11. The popup contains the following actions:
   - Confirm
   - Cancel

12. If the admin clicks Confirm:
   - The system updates the partner status to Deactivated.
   - The partner becomes inactive within PMS.
   - The admin is redirected back to the List of Partners page.
   - Updated partner status is reflected immediately in the tabular view.

13. If the admin clicks Cancel:
   - The popup closes.
   - No changes are made to the partner record.
   - The admin remains on the List of Partners page.

---

# 5. Alternate Flow

If the selected Online Verification Partner is already in Deactivated status:

- Appropriate error handling message should be displayed.
- User should remain on the List of Partners page.

---

### Scenario 3 – User Cancels Deactivation
If the admin clicks Cancel in the confirmation popup:
- Popup should close immediately.
- No status update should occur.
- Existing partner information should remain unchanged.

# 6. Scenarios

### Positive Scenarios

| Partner Status | Displays ACTIVE or DEACTIVATED |
| Action Menu | Displays available actions for the partner |
| Confirmation Popup Message | Displays dynamic Partner ID and Organisation ID values |

---

# 8. Business Rules

- Only users with the `PARTNER_ADMIN` role should be authorized to deactivate Online Verification Partners.
- Only partners currently in ACTIVE status should be eligible for deactivation.
- Deactivation should update only the partner status field.
- No partner records, certificates, organisation mappings, or policy configurations should be deleted or modified during deactivation.
- Once deactivated, the partner status should display:
  - Deactivated
- Deactivation must always require explicit confirmation through the confirmation popup window.
- Deactivation should not proceed automatically without user confirmation.
- Updated status should be reflected immediately within the List of Partners page.
- Search and filter functionality should continue to work correctly for deactivated partner records.

Do you want to deactivate partner with <Partner ID> belonging to Organisation: <Org ID>?

title: Online Verification Partner:  Upload / Re-Upload Online Verification Partner Certificate in PMS Portal
content:
Problem description:
### Description

Enable Partner Admin users to upload or re-upload a CA-signed certificate for an Online Verification Partner through the PMS portal.

### Purpose

As a Partner Admin, I should be able to upload / re-upload a Partner Certificate so that the Online Verification Partner is treated as a valid partner and a MOSIP-signed certificate is generated in return.

### Pre-requisites

1. Partner Admin must be logged into PMS with valid credentials.
2. Partner Admin must have successfully created an Online Verification Partner.
3. Corresponding Root CA and Intermediate CA certificates must already be uploaded into the system.
4. Partner Admin must have access to the Partners module and certificate management functionality.
5. The Upload Certificate and Re-Upload Certificate framework-level functionality should already be available in PMS.

### Basic Flow

## A. Upload Online Verification Partner Certificate

After the successful creation of an Online Verification Partner, the system transitions to a success screen designed to initiate the security onboarding phase.

### 1. Initial Access
The success screen provides the following navigational options:
* **Upload Partner Certificate**: Directs the user to the certificate submission flow.
* **Home**: Returns the user to the main dashboard.

### 2. The Upload Process
When the Partner Admin clicks the **Upload Partner Certificate** button:
1.  The system opens the **Upload Certificate** popup window.
2.  **Popup Title**: `Upload Partner Certificate`
3.  **Popup Subtitle**: Displays the corresponding `Partner ID`.
4.  **Read-Only Metadata**: The following fields are pre-filled and disabled:
    * **Partner Type**: `Online Verification Partner`
    * **Partner Domain**: `AUTH`

### 3. Validation Logic
The Partner Admin uploads the CA-signed partner certificate. The system performs the following rigorous checks:
* **Certificate Format**: Ensures the file type and structure are valid (e.g., .pem, .cer).
* **Certificate Chain**: Validates the path up to the Trusted Root Authority.
* **Certificate Signature**: Verifies the authenticity of the CA signature.
* **Validity Period**: Checks that the certificate is not expired and is currently active.
* **Data Mapping**: Matches the `ORGANIZATION` attribute in the certificate against the Partner Information entered during creation.

### 4. Post-Upload Actions
On successful validation:
* The certificate is stored securely.
* The partner is officially recognized as a **valid Online Verification Partner**.
* The **MOSIP-signed certificate generation** process is automatically initiated.
* **System Status Updates**:
    * `Certificate Upload Status` updates to **Uploaded**.
    * `Overall Partner Status` updates to **ACTIVE**.
* A success confirmation message is displayed to the Partner Admin.

---

## B. Re-Upload Online Verification Partner Certificate

This flow is used when a certificate needs replacement due to expiry, compromise, or organizational changes.

### 1. Navigation
1.  Partner Admin navigates to: **Dashboard** → **Partners** → **List of Partners**.
2.  The admin searches or filters for the specific existing Online Verification Partner.
3.  The admin clicks the **three-dot action menu** (vertical ellipsis) for that partner row.

### 2. Action Selection
The system displays the following contextual menu:
* **View**: See partner details.
* **Upload / Re-upload Certificate**: Initiates the replacement flow.
* **Deactivate**: Suspends the partner.

### 3. Re-Upload Conditions
The **Re-Upload Certificate** popup is applicable only if:
* **Certificate Upload Status**: `Uploaded`
* **Overall Partner Status**: `ACTIVE`

### 4. The Re-Upload Process
1.  **Popup Title**: `Re-Upload Partner Certificate`
2.  **Popup Subtitle**: Displays the corresponding `Partner ID`.
3.  **Pre-filled Values (Non-editable)**:
    * **Partner Type**: `Online Verification Partner`
    * **Partner Domain**: `AUTH`
4.  The Admin uploads the new replacement certificate.

### 5. Validation and Finalization
The system validates the new certificate using the same logic as the initial upload. Upon success:
* The **existing certificate is replaced** and the previous one is revoked.
* A **new MOSIP-signed certificate** generation process is triggered.
* The system displays a successful re-upload confirmation to the user.

### Alternate Flows

### Scenario 1 – Deferred Certificate Upload
If the Partner Admin chooses not to upload the certificate immediately after partner creation:
- The partner record remains available in the List of Partners page.
- Certificate Upload Status remains:
  - Not Uploaded
- Overall Partner Status remains:
  - INACTIVE

The admin can later initiate upload using:
- Upload / Re-upload Certificate option from the action menu.

---

### Scenario 2 – Certificate Validation Failure
If the uploaded certificate fails validation due to invalid format, expired certificate, mismatched organization details, or invalid certificate chain:
- Upload process should fail.
- Appropriate validation message should be displayed.
- Existing certificate data, if any, should remain unchanged.

---

### Scenario 3 – Re-upload Failure
If re-upload processing fails after submission:
- Existing active certificate should remain valid.
- Partner should continue in ACTIVE state using the previously uploaded certificate.

### Data Fields

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Partner ID | Unique identifier of the Online Verification Partner |
| Partner Type | Pre-filled as Online Verification Partner |
| Partner Domain | Pre-filled as AUTH |
| Certificate Upload Status | Displays Uploaded / Not Uploaded |
| Overall Partner Status | Displays ACTIVE / INACTIVE |
| Upload Certificate | Allows first-time certificate upload |
| Re-Upload Certificate | Allows replacement of previously uploaded certificate |

### Business Rules (With Audit)

- Only users with `PARTNER_ADMIN` role should be allowed to upload or re-upload partner certificates.
- Partner Type must always display:
  - Online Verification Partner
- Partner Domain must always display:
  - AUTH
- Partner Type and Partner Domain fields must remain non-editable in upload and re-upload flows.
- A partner without an uploaded certificate must remain in:
  - INACTIVE status
- A partner becomes ACTIVE only after successful certificate upload and validation.
- Certificate upload must validate:
  - Certificate chain
  - CA signature
  - Certificate expiry
  - Organization name mapping
- During re-upload:
  - Newly uploaded certificate must replace the previously uploaded certificate.
  - Previously active certificate must be revoked after successful replacement.
- MOSIP-signed certificate generation must be triggered after successful upload or re-upload.

### Acceptance Criteria

### Upload Certificate Validation
- Given a Partner Admin successfully creates an Online Verification Partner,
- When the admin clicks Upload Partner Certificate,
- Then the system must open the Upload Certificate popup window.

### Upload Popup Validation
The popup must display:
- Title:
  - Upload Partner Certificate
- Subtitle:
  - Corresponding Partner ID
- Partner Type:
  - Online Verification Partner
- Partner Domain:
  - AUTH

The Partner Type and Partner Domain fields must be disabled for editing.

---

### Upload Processing Validation
- System must validate uploaded certificates successfully before processing.
- On successful upload:
  - Partner status must become ACTIVE.
  - Certificate Upload Status must become Uploaded.
  - MOSIP-signed certificate generation process must be triggered.

---

### Re-Upload Validation
- Given an ACTIVE Online Verification Partner with an uploaded certificate exists,
- When the admin selects Upload / Re-upload Certificate,
- Then the system must open the Re-Upload Certificate popup window.

### Re-Upload Processing Validation
- System must validate newly uploaded certificate successfully.
- Previously uploaded certificate must be revoked after successful replacement.
- New certificate must become the active certificate associated with the partner.

---

### Deferred Upload Validation
- If certificate upload is skipped after partner creation:
  - Partner must remain in INACTIVE status.
  - Upload / Re-upload Certificate option must remain available from the partner listing page.

### Reference UX
https://www.figma.com/design/AcdT4y2HVIcRDG5FQ1c95d/PMS_Revamp?node-id=10888-8282&t=XaNXCz3F5PIHQuOW-1

### Compatibility

- Google Chrome - Mozilla Firefox - Microsoft Edge - Safari

### Implementation Details

- Integrate Online Verification Partner certificate upload flow with existing certificate upload framework.
- Implement upload and re-upload popup flows using shared certificate management components.
- Validate uploaded certificates against configured CA chain before activation.
- Implement certificate replacement and revocation logic during re-upload.
- Trigger MOSIP-signed certificate generation workflow after successful validation.
- Ensure upload status and partner status are updated atomically after successful processing.
- Maintain audit logs for certificate upload and replacement activities.
