title: Draft API Integration – Creation of New Stage Before Quality Classifier
content:
Problem description:

Title:

Enhance the Draft API Implementation by Introducing a New "Create Draft" Stage Before the Quality Classifier Stage

Description:

As a developer, I want to introduce a new “Create Draft” stage in the registration processing pipeline, placed before the Quality Classifier stage, so that the Draft API is created and updated earlier in the workflow. This change replaces the current dependency on the Packet Manager for demographic and biometric data retrieval, improves modularity, and aligns with the updated ID Repository workflow.

The new stage will handle Draft API creation and updates for NEW and UPDATE packets, ensuring data consistency and improving performance during downstream stage processing.

Acceptance Criteria

1. Create Draft API – New Stage Integration

  • A new stage called “create_draft” must be introduced in the registration processor workflow.

  • The create_draft stage should be positioned before the Quality Classifier stage for both NEW and UPDATEpackets.

  • The stage will handle the creation and updating of the Draft for each packet, containing both demographic and biometric data (excluding evidence files).

  • UIN allocation is mandatory during Draft creation.

  • If a Draft already exists for a given RID, it should be deleted and re-created.

  • Drafts must be discarded if the packet processing fails or is rejected.

  • In case of a reprocess, the Draft must remain active until the packet processing completes.

  • Once the UIN is successfully generated, the Draft must be published and then discarded.

2. Replacement of Packet Manager Calls

  • Post create_draft stage, subsequent stages like Demo Dedup, Bio Dedup, ABIS Handler, Manual Adjudication, and Verification must use the Draft API instead of the Packet Manager for data retrieval.

  • The Draft API must provide granular retrieval options:

    • Retrieve demographics only

    • Retrieve biometrics only

    • Retrieve both, when no filter is applied (default behavior)

  • Evidence files are not part of the Draft data.

3. Quality Classifier Stage Alignment

  • The new create_draft stage should seamlessly pass validated data to the Quality Classifier stage.

  • The Quality Classifier will not be modified functionally but must consume data from the newly created Draft rather than the packet manager.

4. UIN Generator Stage Update

  • The UIN Generator stage will no longer create Drafts for NEW or UPDATE packets.

  • It will only handle Draft creation for Lost Packets after ABIS stages, as per existing logic.

  • On successful UIN generation, the corresponding Draft must be updated and published to the ID Repository, after which it is discarded.

5. Validation and Error Handling

  • Implement strong validation rules for Draft creation to ensure a unique draft per RID.

  • Proper error handling must be added for transition failures between stages.

  • Draft API operations must not alter existing business rules except for the new stage insertion and timing of Draft creation.

6. Backward Compatibility

  • Maintain backward compatibility for existing UIN Generator workflows.

  • Default retrieval behavior must remain unchanged when no type parameter is specified.

Use Cases

Use Case #1: New Registration

Basic Flow

  1. A resident submits a new registration packet.

  2. The packet passes all validation stages up to the Quality Classifier.

  3. Before entering Quality Classifier, the create_draft stage triggers Draft creation using the Draft API.

    • Draft is tagged as “New” and stores demographics and biometrics (no evidence data).

  4. Subsequent stages (Demo Dedup, Bio Dedup, etc.) retrieve required data via Draft API.

  5. Once UIN is generated, the Draft is updated and published to the ID Repository.

  6. After publishing, the Draft is discarded.

Alternate Flow #1:
If the packet fails or is rejected, the corresponding Draft must be deleted immediately.

Alternate Flow #2:
If the packet is marked for reprocessing, the Draft must remain active until completion.

Use Case #2: Update Registration

Basic Flow

  1. A resident with an existing UIN updates their demographic or biometric details.

  2. The packet passes validation up to the Quality Classifier.

  3. Before entering Quality Classifier, the create_draft stage creates/updates the Draft API tagged as “Update”.

  4. Downstream stages retrieve data from the Draft API instead of Packet Manager.

  5. After UIN regeneration, the updated UIN is stored in the Draft, which is then published and discarded.

Alternate Flow #1:
If the packet fails or is rejected, the corresponding Draft must be deleted.

Alternate Flow #2:
If the packet is marked for reprocessing, the Draft must remain until successful completion.

Technical Implementation Overview (from Impact Analysis v1.3)

High-Level Summary

The Draft API replaces Packet Manager calls from the Demo Dedup stage onward.
Changes include:

  • Addition of a new “create_draft” stage before the Quality Classifier.

  • Enhancements to Draft API for granular retrieval (demographics, biometrics, or both).

  • Updates to affected stages to consume data from the Draft API.

  • UIN Generator stage refactoring to remove Draft creation logic for NEW/UPDATE packets.

Component-Level Impacts

Component | Change Summary -- | -- Draft API | Add query parameter-based retrieval (type=demographics, type=biometrics). New Stage (create_draft) | Create/Update Drafts for NEW & UPDATE packets, before Quality Classifier. Demo Dedup / Bio Dedup / ABIS / Verification / Manual Adjudication | Replace Packet Manager reads with Draft API calls. UIN Generator | Remove Draft creation logic for NEW/UPDATE packets; retain only for lost packets. Packet Classifier | Add handling for anonymous tag file creation and object store storage. Work Manager | Update to use enriched getTags API to retrieve anonymous data instead of Packet Manager.

Definition of Done

  • New create_draft stage implemented and placed before Quality Classifier.

  • Draft API enhanced to support granular data retrieval.

  • All dependent stages refactored to use Draft API instead of Packet Manager.

  • UIN Generator logic updated as per new design.

  • Backward compatibility verified.

  • All unit, integration, and regression tests successfully executed.

title: Consolidate ID-Repository Services into a Single Deployable Spring Boot Service
content:
Problem description:
## 1. Problem Statement

The ID-Repository capability is currently delivered through four separately deployed services — Identity, VID, Credential Request, and Credential Issuance. This fragmented setup creates:


High operational cost: four services to deploy, scale, monitor, patch, and release independently.
Slow and fragile credential issuance: issuing a credential today is an asynchronous, background-job-driven process that passes through multiple internal service-to-service calls. This adds delay (polling-based processing), extra failure points, and makes issuance status harder to track.
Duplicated functionality: each service maintains its own copies of common capabilities (API documentation, security, caching, event subscriptions, and system credentials), increasing maintenance effort and inconsistency risk.

### Purpose (Mandatory)

Consolidate the four ID-Repository services into one service, delivered incrementally (one service absorbed at a time) so each step can be tested and released independently and safely rolled back. The consolidation must be completely invisible to all consumers: every API, event notification, and data structure remains exactly as it is today. The end result is a simpler system to operate (one HTTP service plus one background-jobs worker), faster credential issuance (immediate, direct issuance instead of background-job processing), and clear, immediate feedback to callers on success or failure.

---

## 2. Goals (Mandatory)

1. Deliver ID-Repository as a single consolidated service, absorbing one existing service per phase, with each phase independently testable, releasable, and reversible.
2. Guarantee zero impact on consumers: all existing APIs (identity, VID, credential request, credential issuance), event notifications, error codes/messages, and data remain unchanged at every phase — Registration Processor, ID Authentication, Resident Service, Print Service, and partner systems require no changes.
3. Replace the background-job-based credential issuance pipeline with direct, immediate issuance: a credential is issued as part of the triggering request itself, and the outcome (success or failure) is returned to the caller in the same response.
4. Ensure the consolidated service continues to record credential request and transaction history exactly as today, so existing reporting and downstream expectations are preserved.
5. Consolidate duplicated capabilities (security credentials, event subscriptions, caching, API documentation) into single, unified versions within the merged service.
6. Simplify operations to two deployable units — the main service handling all API traffic, and a separate worker handling scheduled/background activities — each independently scalable.
7. Meet the performance target: end-to-end credential issuance (from the triggering event to the credential-issued notification being published) completes within 1 second, with no performance regression elsewhere compared to the current setup.

---

## 3. Out of Scope (OOS) (Mandatory)

1. **`id-repository-core` merge** — remains a separate shared Maven library (consumed by id-auth, resident-services, etc.).
2. **`salt-generator` merge** — remains a standalone one-shot K8s Job on the same image.
3. **Caller-side retry implementation** — retry handling for synchronous issuance failures in Registration Processor (`CredentialGeneratorStage` → mark packet `REPROCESS`), Resident Service (UX/retry), and consumer-side duplicate/expiry handling in IDA and Print are tracked as separate issues in those components (impact assessment only here).
4. **IDA direct data-source persistence** — publishing credential data directly to the IDA DB instead of WebSub is a noted future enhancement only; the design must not close off this path, but no implementation now.
5. **IDA downstream flow performance** — the 1 s target ends at WebSub publish; IDA processing after that is unchanged and out of scope.
6. **External API changes of any kind** — no new endpoints, no URL/versioning changes, no request/response schema changes, no DB schema migrations.
7. **Git history rewriting** — Code Copy does not preserve per-file history; `git filter-repo` migration is not planned.
8. **Draining in-flight `credential_request_status` rows inside the merged service** — draining is a pre-cutover operational task using the old services against the live DB.

---

## 4. Acceptance Criteria (Mandatory)

**AC-1 (Single consolidated service):**
Given the Identity, VID, Credential Request, and Credential Issuance services consolidated into one service, When the consolidated service is deployed in place of the individual services, Then all ID-Repository functionality (identity management, VID lifecycle, credential requests, and credential issuance) shall be available from the single service.

**AC-2 (Zero consumer impact):**
Given any existing consumer (Registration Processor, ID Authentication, Resident Service, Print Service, or partner systems), When it invokes any existing ID-Repository API or receives any event notification from the consolidated service, Then the behavior shall be identical to the current individual services — same endpoints, same responses, same error codes and messages, same notifications — with no change required on the consumer side.

**AC-3 (Direct credential issuance):**
Given the consolidated service with the background issuance jobs removed, When any event that triggers credential issuance occurs (UIN create/update/deactivate/block, VID create/revoke, or a direct credential request), Then the credential shall be issued immediately as part of that request, and the outcome (success or failure) returned to the caller in the same response.

**AC-4 (Record-keeping and notifications preserved):**
Given the shift to direct issuance, When a credential is issued, Then the credential shall be formatted, secured, and shared as today, the issuance notification published unchanged, and the same request/transaction records written so history, reporting, and audit remain intact.

**AC-5 (Simplified operations):**
Given the completed consolidation, When the system is running in production, Then it shall consist of exactly two deployable units — one serving all API traffic and one handling background/scheduled work — each independently scalable, with the old individual services decommissioned.

**AC-6 (Performance target):**
Given the consolidated service under load equivalent to the pre-consolidation baseline, When a credential issuance is triggered,
Then the end-to-end issuance — from the triggering event to the credential-issued notification being published — shall complete within 1 second, with no performance regression on other operations.

**AC-7 (Tested upgrade approach):**
Given a live deployment running the current four-service version,
When the documented upgrade approach is followed step by step in a production-like environment,
Then the deployment shall be upgraded to the consolidated version with no data loss, no consumer disruption, and all validation checks passing; and if the rollback procedure is invoked at any defined point, the deployment shall return to the previous working version with full functionality.

**Business Rules**

BR-1 (Consumer transparency):
Given any existing consumer of any ID-Repository API or event,
When it interacts with the consolidated system at any point during or after the consolidation,
Then it shall observe identical behavior — same endpoints, same responses, same error codes and messages, same notifications.

BR-2 (Record-keeping continuity):
Given the shift to direct issuance,
When a credential is issued,
Then the same request and transaction records shall continue to be written as today, so history, reporting, and audit remain intact.

BR-3 (Safe transition):
Given the transition from individual services to the consolidated service,
When old and new components coexist during the transition,
Then they shall continue to work together exactly as the individual services do today — every transitional state is production-valid.

BR-4 (Rollback by configuration):
Given any internal integration that has been converted to run inside the consolidated service,
When an issue is found in production,
Then that integration shall be revertible to its previous mode through configuration alone, without code changes or consumer impact.

BR-5 (Policy freshness):
Given a change to partner policy, When the policy is updated, Then the consolidated service shall apply the updated policy within 5 minutes.

### Exceptions & Error Handling

EH-1 (Immediate failure feedback):
Given direct issuance with no background retry, When credential issuance fails for any reason,
Then the failure shall be returned to the caller in the same response, with the same error codes and messages callers receive today, so the caller can decide to retry.

EH-2 (Unknown identity):
Given a credential request for an identity that does not exist, When the request is processed,
Then the caller shall receive the same "record not found" error outcome (code and message) as the current system produces.

EH-3 (Duplicate / expired credentials):
Given that background filtering of duplicate and expired credentials is removed,
When such credentials reach consumers, Then this is accepted behaviour of the new design, and it shall be clearly communicated in release notes that consumers must handle duplicates and expiry on their side.

EH-4 (Pending queue at upgrade):
Given pending credential requests exist at the time of cutover,
When cutover is attempted,
Then cutover shall not proceed until the pending queue has been fully processed using the existing mechanism.

EH-5 (Safe shutdown):
Given the background-jobs worker is being stopped (e.g., during scaling or upgrade),
When work is in progress,
Then in-flight work shall complete or stop safely without leaving records in an inconsistent state.


### Basic Flow (As Applicable)

Basic Flow (As Applicable)

1. A consumer invokes an existing ID-Repository API (e.g., create identity, create VID, or request a credential) — the API is unchanged.
2. The consolidated service performs the operation and, where applicable, issues the credential immediately as part of the same request.
3. The credential-issued notification is published, and the standard request/transaction records are written.
4. The consumer receives the outcome — success or failure — directly in the API response.

### Scenarios (As Applicable)

| # | Scenario | Expected Outcome |
|---|----------|------------------|
| 1 | UIN Create | Identity saved, credential issued immediately, and notification published. |
| 2 | UIN Update (Active) | Identity updated successfully, credential re-issued immediately, and notification published. |
| 3 | UIN Block / Deactivate | Appropriate deactivation or removal notification published to ID Authentication. |
| 4 | VID Create | VID created successfully and issued to the resident. |
| 5 | VID Revoke | VID revoked successfully and notification sent. |
| 6 | New Credential Request | Credential issued successfully and returned in the response. |
| 7 | Issuance Failure | Error returned synchronously; no background retry is triggered. |
| 8 | Rollback of an Edge | Edge reverts to the HTTP fallback adapter and resumes normal operation. |
| 9 | Draft APIs, ID/VID Lookups, Auth Types Status, VID Regenerate/Deactivate/Reactivate, Update Counts, ID/VID Metadata/Search | Existing behavior remains unchanged and all current URLs continue to function identically. |


### Non-Functional Requirements (As Applicable)
- API compatibility: full backward compatibility of every consumer-facing API at every phase.
- Integration compatibility: all event notifications and integrations with partner-management, key-management, data-share, and downstream consumers unchanged (except a single consolidated system credential for outgoing calls).
- Backward compatibility & rollback: configuration supports both old and new setups during transition; every phase and every converted integration can be rolled back.
- Performance: credential issuance end-to-end within 1 second; no regression on other operations versus the pre-consolidation baseline.
- Scalability: API traffic and background work scale independently.
- Auditability: existing logging, audit, and record-keeping behavior preserved.

### Definition of Done (Mandatory)

- [ ] Code implemented (all phases 0–4, Code Copy approach, collision tables applied)
- [ ] Unit tests added (adapter contract-preservation tests: mock service throws `IdRepoAppException`, caller receives correct error code; migrated module tests moved with code)
- [ ] Integration tests added (Phase 1/Phase 2 multi-datasource gate tests; in-process conversion gate tests per edge; jobs-flag on/off context tests)
- [ ] Existing tests passing (full pre-merge suite + existing automation suite green against merged service)
- [ ] Documentation updated (LLDs, release notes — queue drain requirement, consumer-side duplicate/expiry handling, caller retry impacts; config docs for new flags)
- [ ] Acceptance criteria validated (all AC/BR/EH above, functional-document validation, performance baseline vs. merged ≤ 1 s issuance)
- [ ] Upgrade approach delivered — detailed step-by-step upgrade document (pre-checks, upgrade sequence, validation checklist, rollback procedure)
- [ ] Upgrade approach tested — full upgrade and rollback executed successfully in a production-like environment, with results recorded
---

title: ID-Repository Automation Bug
content:
Problem description:
## Summary

During automation testing of the Identity APIs (Add Identity / Update Identity), test failures were observed related to request wrapper field validation. After code analysis on `release-1.2.4.x`, it is confirmed that **only the `id` field is validated** in the request wrapper. Automation tests asserting validation errors for `version` and other wrapper fields are **incorrect** and need to be updated.

---

## Code Behaviour (release-1.2.4.x)

### What is validated in the request wrapper

**Only `id` is validated.**

This happens explicitly in `IdRepoController` before anything else runs:

```java
// addIdentity
validator.validateId(idRequestDTO.getId(), CREATE);

// updateIdentity  
validator.validateId(idRequestDTO.getId(), UPDATE);
```

`BaseIdRepoValidator.validateId()`:
```java
public void validateId(String id, String operation) throws IdRepoAppException {
    if (Objects.isNull(id)) {
        throw new IdRepoAppException(MISSING_INPUT_PARAMETER...);   // IDR-IDC-001
    } else if (!this.id.get(operation).equals(id)) {
        throw new IdRepoAppException(INVALID_INPUT_PARAMETER...);   // IDR-IDC-002
    }
}
```

- If `id` is **null** → `IDR-IDC-001` Missing Input Parameter
- If `id` is **wrong value** → `IDR-IDC-002` Invalid Input Parameter
- If `id` is **correct** → proceeds normally

### What is NOT validated

The following request wrapper fields are **not validated** by design in id-repository:

| Field | Validated? |
|-------|-----------|
| `id` | ✅ Yes — validated in controller |
| `version` | ❌ No |
| `requesttime` | ❌ No — method exists in base class but not enforced |

> **Note:** `validateVersion()` exists in `BaseIdRepoValidator` and is called inside `IdRequestValidator.validate()`, but cross-verification confirms it does **not** produce an effective validation error for the id-repository identity service. Only `id` validation is enforced.

---

## Issue with Automation

Automation test cases are asserting that invalid/missing `version` (and possibly other wrapper fields) should return validation error responses. This is **incorrect behaviour to test** — id-repository does not validate these fields.

### Action Required from Automation Team

- Remove or update all test cases that assert validation errors for `version`, `requesttime`, or any other wrapper field other than `id`
- Test cases for `id` validation (null and invalid value) are **valid** and should be retained
- Do not assert `IDR-IDC-001` or `IDR-IDC-002` for `version` field

---

## Other Open Items (from same testing cycle)

### 1. `registrationId` — No Validation
`registrationId` has no null/empty check and no format validation in id-repository.

**Expected behaviour:**
- Null/empty `registrationId` → `IDR-IDC-001` (Missing Input Parameter)
- Invalid format → `IDR-IDC-002` (Invalid Input Parameter)

**Current behaviour:** No error thrown.

### 2. `IDSchemaVersion` — Type Check (String vs Number)
Schema defines `IDSchemaVersion` as `number`. Passing a string value (e.g. `"1.2"` instead of `1.2`) is not rejected.

**Action:** Verify schema definition and confirm whether type enforcement is applied.

### 3. Known Issue — Update Identity with Empty Claim (Deferred)
When updating identity with an empty claim/field value, the system should update the record with null/empty. Instead it incorrectly throws a missing/invalid error.

**Status:** Acknowledged as known issue. Deferred to next release. Automation

title: feat: Wire MOSIP KeyManager JWT signature verification into UnsubscribeController.verifyAndExtractEmail()
content:
Problem description:
## Summary

This issue tracks the production hardening of the JWT token verification in the unsubscribe workflow introduced in #1524.

## Background

PR #1524 (https://github.com/mosip/id-repository/pull/1524) added a public unsubscribe endpoint that requires a JWT token to prove email ownership before allowing UIN deactivation. However, the current implementation in `UnsubscribeController.verifyAndExtractEmail()` uses an **insecure fallback** — it only base64-decodes the JWT payload without verifying the signature:

```java
// INSECURE FALLBACK — marked PRODUCTION TODO in source
String payload = new String(Base64.getUrlDecoder().decode(token.split(".")[1]));
JsonNode claims = new ObjectMapper().readTree(payload);
```

This means a forged token (e.g., `alg: none`) can trigger UIN deactivation for any email address.

## Required Work

Replace the insecure fallback with MOSIP KeyManager / TokenValidator-backed JWT signature verification, for example:

```java
// Pseudo-code
Claims claims = mosipTokenValidator.validateAndGetClaims(token);
String email = claims.get("email", String.class);
```

Steps:
1. Identify the correct MOSIP KeyManager or token validator API available in the id-repository service context.
2. Wire it into `UnsubscribeController.verifyAndExtractEmail()`.
3. Handle `SignatureException` and `ExpiredJwtException` by throwing `IdRepoAppException("INVALID_TOKEN", ...)`.
4. Remove the `// INSECURE FALLBACK` block and `// PRODUCTION TODO` comment.
5. Add unit tests covering: valid token, forged/tampered token, expired token, missing email claim.

## Priority

**High** — the insecure fallback must not reach a production deployment.

## References

- PR #1524: https://github.com/mosip/id-repository/pull/1524
- Review comment: https://github.com/mosip/id-repository/pull/1524#discussion_r3268006955

Requested by: @yakshithkd23

title: [dev11] Automation Test Failures - IdRepo AddIdentity & UpdateIdentity Array Handle TCs
content:
Problem description:
## Summary
Multiple automation test cases are failing on the **dev11** environment for the
**IdRepo (ID Repository)** module after the new Identity Schema (Array of Handles
+ tag support) was published. Root cause has been identified.

## Environment
- **Environment:** dev11
- **Module:** IdRepo (ID Repository)

## Root Cause
The test request body is not constructed per the new schema definition.

In the **new schema**, `email` is a `simpleListType` — an array of objects 
with `value` and optional `tags` (`handle`, `notification`):

```json
"email": [
  {
    "value": "test@example.com",
    "tags": ["handle", "notification"]
  }
]
```

The automation requests are still sending `email` as a plain `string`, 
which fails schema validation before any functional logic runs — causing 
the entire batch of AddIdentity TCs to fail.

## Impact
- ~70 failures across AddIdentity and UpdateIdentity Array Handle TCs
- id-repo module also affected with the same error

## Failing Test Cases

### AddIdentity - Array Handle
| Test Case ID | Status |
|---|---|
| TC_IDRepo_AddIdentityArrayHandle_03 | ❌ Failing |
| TC_IDRepo_AddIdentityArrayHandle_08 | ❌ Failing |
| TC_IDRepo_AddIdentityArrayHandle_09 | ❌ Failing |
| TC_IDRepo_AddIdentityArrayHandle_13 | ❌ Failing |
| TC_IDRepo_AddIdentityArrayHandle_39 | ❌ Failing |
| TC_IDRepo_AddIdentityArrayHandle_40 | ❌ Failing |
| TC_IDRepo_AddIdentityArrayHandle_41 | ❌ Failing |

### UpdateIdentity - Array Handle
| Test Case ID | Status |
|---|---|
| TC_IDRepo_UpdateIdentityArrayHandle_29 | ❌ Failing |
| TC_IDRepo_UpdateIdentityArrayHandle_31 | ❌ Failing |

## Action Required
- [ ] Update request payload for `email` field from `string` → 
`array of handle objects` as per the new `simpleListType` schema
- [ ] Re-verify all failing TCs after the fix — current failures hit 
validation before reaching functional checks, so a full re-run is needed

title: Revamp of Full & Patch Upgrades (Launcher-Orchestrated, Manifest-Driven)
content:
Problem description:
### Problem Statement

From 1.3.0 onwards, the registration client's upgrade mechanism needs to be reworked. In versions <1.3.0, softwareUpdateHandler downloaded artifacts directly into lib/ (blocking, foreground) and run.bat simply picked up the new JARs on the next launch. This model is limited:

Downloads were foreground and blocking, with no resumable support — an interrupted download or lost network meant restarting the fetch from scratch.
The update handler made placement decisions and wrote directly into lib/, leaving no single point of control over what happens to downloaded artifacts.
Integrity was tracked through a single manifest, with no clean separation between version/upgrade orchestration and per-file integrity verification.
There was no consistent, signature-verified, recoverable flow for both full upgrades and lib-only patch upgrades.

The revamp introduces a two-phase, manifest-driven model: softwareUpdateHandler is reduced to a pure download-and-record role (downloads artifacts to .artifacts/, updates ./MANIFEST.MF, prompts restart), and _launcher.jar becomes the sole entry point that, on restart, verifies signatures, compares versions across a dual-manifest model, and orchestrates the correct upgrade path (full or lib-only patch) with resumable downloads and integrity-based recovery.

Note: The Java 11 → Java 21 JRE migration is already delivered. This story focuses only on the upgrade mechanism.

### Goals

- Reduce softwareUpdateHandler to a pure download-and-record role: download artifacts to .artifacts/ (resumable, background, with progress) and update ./MANIFEST.MF. It never unzips, never copies to lib/, and never touches run.bat.
- Prompt the operator to restart only after all .artifacts/ downloads complete — no auto-restart.
- Make _launcher.jar the single decision point and entry point on every startup: verify the ./MANIFEST.MF signature, compare ./MANIFEST.MF vs lib/MANIFEST.MF, and select the correct path.
- Support a lib-only patch upgrade path: download and verify lib/MANIFEST.MF, resumable-download lib.zip, verify its hash, and unzip to .TEMP/; run.bat applies .TEMP/* → lib/ on the next operator-initiated start.
- Implement the dual-manifest model: root ./MANIFEST.MF drives version tracking and upgrade orchestration (no lib.zip entry); lib/MANIFEST.MF, delivered inside lib.zip, drives ClientPreLoader per-file integrity checks.
- Implement the signature/integrity verification flow with recovery Cases A–D (re-download on trusted-manifest local tamper; hard-abort on invalid or MITM signature).
- Make all upgrade downloads resumable (byte-range), so interrupted or network-lost downloads continue from the last byte on restart/reconnect.
- Always download lib.zip on-demand when a version difference is detected; never download anything directly to lib/.
- Clean up leftover upgrade artefacts on the first matched-version startup (step 6 cleanup).
- Update the build/server pipeline to sign both manifests, restructure the server manifest, and bundle lib/MANIFEST.MF inside lib.zip.

### Non-Goals
- The Java 11 → Java 21 JRE migration and the native migration.exe / rollback.exe executables — already delivered; not in scope here.
- Modifying run.bat, run.exe, or anything in the application root by the upgrade handler (the immutable-launcher constraint stands; run.bat's existing .TEMP/ → lib/ copy behaviour is reused, not changed).
- Any auto-restart behaviour — the operator is always prompted.
- Changes to the application's functional/business behaviour beyond upgrade orchestration.
- Re-signing or re-keying infrastructure beyond producing the .sig artifacts described here.

### Acceptance Criteria
AC1 — Download relocation & resumability
Given a version mismatch between ./MANIFEST.MF and maven-metadata.xml, when softwareUpdateHandler runs, then artifacts are downloaded to .artifacts/ (not lib/) using resumable, background downloads with progress indication.
AC2 — Handler invariant
Given softwareUpdateHandler completes, then it has only downloaded artifacts and updated ./MANIFEST.MF — it has not unzipped anything, copied to lib/, or modified run.bat.
AC3 — Restart prompt timing
Given downloads are in progress, then the operator is prompted to restart only after all .artifacts/ downloads complete; the application never auto-restarts.
AC4 — Single entry point
Given the application starts, then _launcher.jar's Initialization class is the sole entry point and registration-client.jar has no main() entry point.
AC5 — Signature verification on startup
Given startup, when _launcher.jar runs, then it verifies the ./MANIFEST.MF signature using the embedded public key before any upgrade decision.
AC6 — Version comparison & path selection
Given a valid signature, when _launcher.jar compares ./MANIFEST.MF vs lib/MANIFEST.MF, then: if versions match it proceeds to normal startup; if they differ it triggers the correct upgrade path.
AC7 — Lib-only patch upgrade path
Given versions differ and the JRE is the supported runtime, then _launcher.jar downloads and verifies lib/MANIFEST.MF (+ .sig) to .TEMP/, resumable-downloads lib.zip to .TEMP/lib.zip, verifies its hash against lib/MANIFEST.MF, unzips to .TEMP/, and prompts restart.
AC8 — Applying staged updates
Given staged files in .TEMP/, when the operator restarts via run.bat, then run.bat copies .TEMP/* → lib/, versions now match, and normal startup proceeds with ClientPreLoader verifying hashes against lib/MANIFEST.MF.
AC9 — Dual-manifest contract
Given the upgrade model, then root ./MANIFEST.MF is used for version tracking/orchestration and contains no lib.zip entry, while lib/MANIFEST.MF is delivered inside lib.zip and is used by ClientPreLoader for per-file hash verification.
AC10 — On-demand lib.zip
Given a version difference is detected, then lib.zip is always downloaded on-demand; nothing is downloaded directly to lib/ from 1.3.0 onwards.
AC11 — Case A (valid manifest sig, file hash fails)
Given ./MANIFEST.MF.sig (or lib/MANIFEST.MF.sig) is valid but a file hash fails, then the file is re-downloaded to .TEMP/, its hash re-verified, the operator is informed to restart, and run.bat (for lib/ files) or _launcher.jar (for root files) places it on restart.
AC12 — Case B (invalid manifest sig)
Given the manifest signature is invalid, then a security alert is shown, nothing is re-downloaded, and the JVM exits.
AC13 — Case C (missing manifest sig)
Given MANIFEST.MF.sig is missing, then it is downloaded from the upgrade server and its integrity checked; if verification fails, Case B handling applies.
AC14 — Resumable downloads
Given any upgrade download (artifacts, manifests, or lib.zip) is interrupted or loses network, when the operator restarts or reconnects, then the download resumes from the last byte rather than restarting.
AC15 — Post-upgrade cleanup
Given versions match on startup after a completed upgrade, then _launcher.jar removes leftover upgrade artefacts (e.g. .artifacts/ and other migration artefacts) before proceeding to normal startup.
AC16 — Server / build pipeline
Given the build pipeline, then configure.sh signs ./MANIFEST.MF and lib/MANIFEST.MF (producing .sig files), the server ./MANIFEST.MF excludes lib.zip, lib/MANIFEST.MF is bundled inside lib.zip, and all files under lib/** are zipped as lib.zip and hosted on the upgrade server.
AC17 — Headless safety
Given a headless environment, when an operator dialog would be shown, then _launcher.jar guards with GraphicsEnvironment.isHeadless() and degrades gracefully instead of throwing.

### Sub-Tasks

title: <Feature> Document Quality Check at Upload and Pre-Packet Stages (Online & Offline)
content:
Problem description:
As a **registration operator **
I want the registration client — in both online and offline modes — to **validate the authenticity of uploaded documents and confirm that keyed-in demographic data matches those documents**, routing any discrepancy to a supervisor for an approve-or-reject decision
So that only genuine, issuer-authorised, and consistent registrations become packets, with a controlled human checkpoint for exceptions.

## Description

The registration client today accepts scanned supporting documents (PDF/DOC) and lets the operator key in demographic data, with no automated check on document genuineness or on whether the entered data agrees with the document. This feature introduces an automated Document Quality Check (DQC) at two points, and it must operate identically in **online and offline registration**:

- **Stage 1 — Authenticity at upload.** Right after upload in an allowed format, the system validates whether the document is a genuine scanned original and whether it comes from an authorised issuer, using barcode/MRZ parsing, hologram/watermark detection, or AI/ML anomaly detection.
- **Stage 2 — Demographic consistency before packet creation.** Before the packet is created, the system runs OCR and cross-verifies entered demographic fields against the document, with the field set driven by the document category (identity proof → name, gender, DOB; address proof → name, address; etc.).
When Stage 2 finds a discrepancy, the packet is **not** created automatically. The registration is held for a **supervisor decision**: the supervisor either **approves** it to proceed (packet created) or **rejects** it, in which case no packet is created and the **resident must re-register**. The entire DQC capability is **configurable at country level** and is only active where the country requires it.

---

## Problem Statement

There is currently no guarantee that an uploaded document is authentic or that captured demographic data corresponds to it. Fraudulent, tampered, or mismatched submissions are caught late or not at all, driving rejections, rework, cost, and fraud risk — and the operator gets no feedback at the point of capture, where correction is cheapest. The control must work even when centres operate offline, and exceptions must be governed by a supervisor rather than silently passed or blocked.

---

## Goals

- Detect tampered/regenerated/forged documents and unauthorised issuers at upload.
- Verify operator-entered demographics against the document, per document category.
- Operate consistently in **both online and offline registration** modes.
- On a Stage 2 discrepancy, enforce a **supervisor approve/reject checkpoint**, with rejection leading to resident re-registration.
- Keep the whole feature **configurable per country** (enable/disable), plus configurable field mappings, match thresholds, and hard-stop vs. warning behaviour.
- Give operators and supervisors clear, field-level, actionable results.
- Record every check and every supervisor decision in the audit trail.

---

## Non-Goals

- Does not replace supervisor judgement — it flags; the supervisor decides on exceptions.
- Does not auto-populate or auto-correct demographic fields from OCR (verification only).
- Does not perform biometrics or de-duplication (separate flows).
- Does not perform live external issuer-database lookups in this iteration; issuer validation is against a locally configured/synced issuer registry.
- Does not change the standard flow at all when the country configuration disables DQC.

---

## Configuration & Modes

- **Country-level switch.** A country/policy configuration flag enables or disables DQC end-to-end. When disabled, registration behaves exactly as today with no checks invoked.
- **Online mode.** Checks may use remote services (OCR, anomaly model, issuer registry) where configured; otherwise local equivalents are used.
- **Offline mode.** Checks run on-device or via a local service, using configuration and the issuer registry synced to the client. If a specific check genuinely cannot run offline, the configured fallback applies (defer-and-recheck on next sync, or mandatory manual review) — it must never silently auto-pass.
- **Parity requirement.** Outcomes, operator feedback, and the supervisor workflow behave consistently across both modes; only the execution location and any deferral differ.
- Field-to-category mappings, match thresholds (exact/normalised/fuzzy), and hard-stop vs. warning classification are all configurable.

---

## Supervisor Approval Workflow (Stage 2 discrepancy)

1. Stage 2 detects a discrepancy on one or more required fields (mismatch beyond configured tolerance).
2. Packet creation is **halted**; the registration enters a **Pending Supervisor Approval** state showing field-level details (entered value vs. OCR-extracted value, confidence).
3. An authorised supervisor authenticates (online or via offline credentials) and chooses one of:
   - **Approve / Proceed** — supervisor records a reason; the packet is created and the decision is audited.
   - **Reject** — supervisor records a reason; no packet is created, the registration is discarded/marked rejected, and the **resident must re-register**.
4. The decision, supervisor identity, reason, timestamp, mode (online/offline), and the underlying discrepancy are written to the audit trail.
5. The workflow functions identically in offline mode; if no supervisor is available, the registration remains in the Pending state per the configured handling rather than auto-proceeding.

> **Stage 1 is a hard stop.** If a document is found **invalid or tampered**, the operator **cannot proceed** under any circumstances — there is no supervisor override to continue. The system blocks the document and **prompts the operator to re-upload a valid document**. The supervisor approve/reject workflow above applies **only** to Stage 2 demographic-data discrepancies, never to Stage 1 authenticity failures.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Document quality check can be enabled/disabled at **country level**; when disabled, no checks run and the registration flow is unchanged.
2. When enabled, both **online and offline** registration run Stage 1 and Stage 2, with outcomes and the supervisor workflow behaving consistently across modes.
3. Stage 1 runs automatically on upload and evaluates genuineness (scanned original, not tampered/recaptured) and authorised-issuer status via barcode/MRZ, hologram/watermark, and ML anomaly signals; each result resolves to Pass / Warning / Fail with a readable reason. A **Fail** (invalid or tampered) is a **hard stop**: the operator cannot proceed, the system prompts re-upload of a valid document, and there is no override to continue with an invalid/tampered document.
4. Stage 2 verifies entered demographics against OCR-extracted values, using the configured category→field mapping and configurable match rules, producing per-field and overall results.
5. On a Stage 2 discrepancy, packet creation is halted and the registration is placed in **Pending Supervisor Approval**; it cannot become a packet without a supervisor decision.
6. A supervisor can **Approve/Proceed** (authenticated, reason captured → packet created) or **Reject** (authenticated, reason captured → no packet, registration rejected, resident must re-register).
7. The supervisor decision and its context (identity, reason, timestamp, mode, discrepancy details) are recorded in the audit trail, along with all Stage 1/Stage 2 outcomes.
8. Imperfect-input behaviour is defined and graceful: unreadable barcode/MRZ, low OCR confidence, unsupported/corrupt files, and offline-unavailable checks follow configured fallbacks rather than silent pass/fail.
9. Each check completes within an agreed performance budget; on timeout or service unavailability (especially offline), the defined fallback (retry/defer/manual review) applies.
10. Configuration covers: country enable/disable, per-category field mapping, match thresholds.

---

## Scenario-wise Expected Behaviour

**Legend — Flow Type:** `Main` = happy/primary path · `Alternate` = valid non-happy variation · `Exception` = error/edge handling.

### Configuration

| ID | Scenario | Flow Type | Mode | Given (Precondition) | When (Trigger) | Then (Expected Behaviour) |
|----|----------|-----------|------|----------------------|----------------|---------------------------|
| CFG-01 | DQC enabled | Main | Both | Country config has DQC enabled | Operator uploads documents and proceeds to packet creation | Stage 1 and Stage 2 checks run per configured rules |
| CFG-02 | DQC disabled | Alternate | Both | Country config has DQC disabled | Operator uploads documents and creates a packet | No authenticity/consistency checks run; flow is identical to current behaviour |

### Stage 1 — Authenticity at Upload

| ID | Scenario | Flow Type | Mode | Given (Precondition) | When (Trigger) | Then (Expected Behaviour) |
|----|----------|-----------|------|----------------------|----------------|---------------------------|
| S1-01 | Genuine, authorised document | Main | Both | Valid scanned PDF/DOC in an allowed format | Authenticity check runs on upload | MRZ/barcode parses, watermark & anomaly checks pass, issuer recognised → marked **Pass**, accepted |
| S1-02 | Tampered / digitally altered | Exception | Both | Anomaly model detects manipulation (edits, splicing, inconsistent fonts/compression) | Check runs | **Hard stop** — marked **Fail**, operator **cannot proceed**, system **prompts re-upload of a valid document**, reason "possible tampering detected" shown, event logged |
| S1-03 | Invalid / not a scanned original | Exception | Both | File is a screenshot, recapture, photo of a screen, or otherwise invalid | Check runs | **Hard stop** — marked **Fail**, operator **cannot proceed**, system **prompts re-upload of a valid document**, reason "not a valid scanned original" shown, event logged |
| S1-04 | Unauthorised / unknown issuer | Alternate | Both | Issuer not present in authorised issuer registry | Check runs | Marked **Fail/Warning** per policy, reason "issuer not recognised"; proceeding requires configured path |
| S1-05 | Barcode/MRZ unreadable | Exception | Both | MRZ/barcode absent, damaged, or unreadable | Parsing fails | No silent pass; falls back to watermark/anomaly signals → resolves to **Warning / manual review** |
| S1-06 | Unsupported / corrupt file | Exception | Both | File outside allowed formats or corrupt | File uploaded | Rejected with format/integrity error **before** authenticity checks run |
| S1-07 | Offline execution | Alternate | Offline | Client is offline; config & issuer registry synced locally | Document uploaded | Checks run on-device/locally; any check that can't run offline follows configured deferral/manual-review fallback with a clear pending state |
| S1-08 | Authenticity service unavailable | Exception | Online | Remote authenticity service/model unreachable | Upload occurs | Configured fallback applies (defer-and-recheck / queue / allow-with-mandatory-review); pending state shown, no silent fail |

### Stage 2 — Demographic Consistency & Supervisor Workflow

| ID | Scenario | Flow Type | Mode | Given (Precondition) | When (Trigger) | Then (Expected Behaviour) |
|----|----------|-----------|------|----------------------|----------------|---------------------------|
| S2-01 | All fields match (identity proof) | Main | Both | Identity proof; entered name, gender, DOB | OCR extracts fields, all match within tolerance | Result **Pass**; packet creation allowed |
| S2-02 | All fields match (address proof) | Main | Both | Address proof; entered name, address | OCR extracts fields, both match within tolerance | Result **Pass**; only category-relevant fields evaluated (DOB/gender not required) |
| S2-03 | Discrepancy → supervisor approves | Alternate | Both | One or more required fields mismatch beyond tolerance | Check runs; supervisor authenticates and approves with reason | Registration enters **Pending Supervisor Approval** → packet created on approval; decision audited |
| S2-04 | Discrepancy → supervisor rejects | Alternate | Both | Same pending-discrepancy state | Supervisor authenticates and rejects with reason | No packet created; registration marked **rejected/discarded**; **resident must re-register**; decision audited |
| S2-05 | Discrepancy offline | Alternate | Offline | Client offline; discrepancy detected | Supervisor authenticates with offline credentials and decides | Approve/reject workflow behaves identically; decision recorded with mode = offline |
| S2-06 | No supervisor available (offline) | Exception | Offline | Pending discrepancy and no supervisor present | Operator cannot escalate | Registration stays in **Pending** per configured handling; does **not** auto-proceed |
| S2-07 | Low OCR confidence / field not found | Exception | Both | Required field can't be read reliably (poor scan, handwriting, layout) | Check runs | Field flagged **low-confidence/not-found**; routed to supervisor checkpoint; not auto-passed or auto-failed |
| S2-08 | Fuzzy match within tolerance | Alternate | Both | Minor variations (initials, transliteration, date formats) | Matched under configured fuzzy/normalisation rules | Resolves to **match** (or grey-zone **Warning**), not a hard discrepancy |
| S2-09 | Multiple documents | Alternate | Both | More than one supporting document uploaded | Check runs | Each document verified against fields mapped to its own category; overall result aggregates per-document outcomes |
| S2-10 | Connectivity lost mid-flow | Exception | Online→Offline | Connectivity drops after upload | Stage 2 runs | Client completes checks locally where possible or defers per fallback; same supervisor workflow preserved at decision point |

title: [BUG] Unmanaged thread proliferation in JobConfigurationServiceImpl causes potential resource exhaustion
content:
Problem description:
**Describe the bug**
`JobConfigurationServiceImpl.java` uses raw thread creation via:
```java
new Thread(() -> executeMissedTrigger(jobId, syncFrequency)).start();
```
(line 735) to execute missed job triggers asynchronously.
This call is executed inside a `forEach` loop over all active sync jobs, meaning a new unmanaged thread is spawned for every job during application startup or missed-trigger recovery operations. Because these threads are created outside any managed `ExecutorService` or Spring-managed thread pool, the application has no mechanism to:
- Limit the number of concurrent threads
- Monitor or observe running threads
- Gracefully shut down threads during application exit
- Handle and propagate exceptions properly
- Reuse threads efficiently
Under heavy load, large job configurations, or repeated application restarts, this can lead to uncontrolled thread growth and potential JVM resource exhaustion. Additionally, unhandled exceptions inside these anonymous threads may be silently swallowed without centralized logging or recovery.

---

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Configure multiple active sync jobs in the Registration Client database.
2. Stop the application long enough for several scheduled triggers to be missed.
3. Launch the Registration Client.
4. During startup, observe that one raw thread is spawned per missed job trigger.
5. Repeatedly restart the application or invoke `executeMissedTriggers()`.
6. Monitor JVM thread count using JConsole, VisualVM, or thread dumps.
7. Observe increasing numbers of unmanaged anonymous threads.

---

**Expected behavior**
Missed trigger executions should be submitted to a managed `ExecutorService` (such as a bounded/fixed thread pool) or use Spring's `@Async` support with a configured `TaskExecutor`.
This would ensure:
- Bounded thread creation
- Controlled concurrency
- Proper lifecycle management
- Graceful shutdown handling
- Centralized exception logging and recovery
- Better resource utilization through thread reuse

---

**Screenshots**
N/A (Backend threading issue — observable through JVM monitoring tools such as JConsole or VisualVM)

---

**Environment:**
- Server OS: N/A
- Client OS : macOS
- Build : master branch
- Browser : N/A (Desktop Application)

---

**Attach logs**
No direct exception is typically thrown.
Observable via thread dump showing large numbers of anonymous threads:
```
"Thread-42" #42 prio=5 os_prio=0 tid=0x... nid=0x... runnable
"Thread-43" #43 prio=5 os_prio=0 tid=0x... nid=0x... runnable
"Thread-44" #44 prio=5 os_prio=0 tid=0x... nid=0x... runnable
...
```

---

**Additional context**
The problematic code exists in `JobConfigurationServiceImpl.java` around Line 735:
```java
new Thread(() -> executeMissedTrigger(jobId, syncFrequency)).start();
```
This logic is executed inside a loop iterating over all active sync jobs. As a result, the number of unmanaged threads created is directly proportional to the number of configured jobs, with no upper bound or throttling mechanism.

title: [BUG]  Fix non-thread-safe global state and race conditions in ApplicationContext
content:
Problem description:
**Describe the bug**
Potential race condition and data corruption issue in `ApplicationContext.java` due to the use of global static `HashMap` structures (`applicationMap` and `resourceBundleMap`) that are accessed and modified concurrently by multiple threads. The shared maps are accessed across the JavaFX UI thread and several background jobs such as `JobConfigurationServiceImpl`, `MasterSyncJob`, and packet synchronization tasks. Since `HashMap` is not thread-safe, concurrent read/write operations can lead to:
- `ConcurrentModificationException`
- Data corruption
- Inconsistent application state
- Intermittent UI freezes or crashes
Additionally, the `getInstance()` singleton accessor lacks synchronization, which may result in double initialization or inconsistent singleton state when multiple threads attempt to initialize `ApplicationContext` simultaneously.
This issue becomes more visible during simultaneous sync operations while the UI is actively accessing global configuration values.

---

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Launch the MOSIP Registration Client and log in.
2. Initiate a manual **"Sync All"** operation or wait for multiple scheduled background jobs (e.g., Packet Sync, Master Data Sync) to execute simultaneously.
3. While synchronization is running, navigate through the UI or perform actions that access global settings:
   - Open Settings
   - Start a new registration
   - Trigger policy/configuration refresh
4. Observe intermittent application freezes or crashes.
5. Check logs for `ConcurrentModificationException`.

---

**Expected behavior**
Global application state and resource bundles should be maintained using thread-safe containers such as `ConcurrentHashMap` or synchronized access mechanisms to ensure safe concurrent reads/writes across UI and background threads. The Singleton pattern in `ApplicationContext` should also be implemented with proper synchronization to prevent race conditions during first-time initialization. The application should remain stable and configuration data should stay consistent even when multiple background jobs update shared state simultaneously.

---

**Screenshots**
N/A (Backend concurrency/thread-safety issue)

---

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- Server OS: N/A (Client-side issue)
- Client OS : macOS
- Build : master branch
- Browser : Chrome

---

**Attach logs**
```text

    at java.base/java.util.HashMap$EntryIterator.next(HashMap.java:1630)

title: [BUG] CloseableHttpClient never closed in MosipDeviceSpecificationHelper.getHttpClientResponse()
content:
Problem description:
### Short Summary of the Bug

getHttpClientResponse() creates a new CloseableHttpClient for every MDM request but never closes it, causing socket/file descriptor leaks during repeated biometric operations.

### Description

**Description**

## What

`getHttpClientResponse()` creates a `CloseableHttpClient` instance on every invocation but does not close it before returning the response.

**Affected file:**
`registration-services/src/main/java/io/mosip/registration/mdm/service/impl/MosipDeviceSpecificationHelper.java`

```java
public CloseableHttpResponse getHttpClientResponse(String url, String method, String body)
        throws IOException {
    CloseableHttpClient client = HttpClients.createDefault(); // never closed
    // ...
    return client.execute(httpUriRequest);
}
```

The method returns `CloseableHttpResponse` directly, leaving the underlying `CloseableHttpClient` unmanaged and leaking sockets/connections for every request.

---

## Why it matters

The same class already follows the correct resource-management pattern in `getHttpClientResponseEntity()` using try-with-resources:

```java
try (CloseableHttpClient client = HttpClients.createDefault()) {
    ...
}
```

However, `getHttpClientResponse()` is actively used by biometric MDM operations such as:

* rcapture
* stream
* device info requests

These operations occur repeatedly during normal registration workflows. Over time, unclosed HTTP clients accumulate open sockets/file descriptors, eventually exhausting JVM or OS resources.

This can lead to:

* random connection failures
* device communication errors
* degraded registration performance
* unexpected client crashes during long sessions

---

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Registration Client with MDM spec version `0.9.5`
2. Perform repeated biometric captures and streaming operations
3. Monitor open sockets/file descriptors:

```bash
lsof -p <pid> | grep socket
```

4. Observe continuously increasing socket count
5. After sustained use, connection-related failures begin appearing

---

## Expected behavior

`CloseableHttpClient` and `CloseableHttpResponse` should both be closed properly after request execution using try-with-resources.

title: [BUG] NullPointerException in BioServiceImpl.getSDKScore() when SDK omits modality key from quality score map
content:
Problem description:
### Short Summary of the Bug

SDK's getModalityQuality() may return no entry for the queried BiometricType; auto-unboxing causes NPE

### Description

## Summary
`getSDKScore()` auto-unboxes the `Float` returned by `scoreMap.get(biometricType)` directly to `double`.

If the SDK's `getModalityQuality()` does not populate an entry for the queried `BiometricType`,
`get()` returns `null` and the unboxing throws an unchecked `NullPointerException`.

## Affected File
`registration-services/src/main/java/io/mosip/registration/service/bio/impl/BioServiceImpl.java`

## Code 
```java
Map<BiometricType, Float> scoreMap = bioAPIFactory
        .getBioProvider(biometricType, BiometricFunction.QUALITY_CHECK)
        .getModalityQuality(birList, null);

return scoreMap.get(biometricType); // NPE if key absent — Float null unboxed to double
```

## Impact
The NPE is not a `BiometricException`, so it escapes the catch block at line ~104 and
falls into the generic `catch (Throwable t)` at line ~114, where it gets re-thrown as
`MDS_RCAPTURE_ERROR` — misclassifying an SDK quality check failure as an MDM capture failure.

This makes root cause diagnosis significantly harder.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure `mosip.registration.quality_check_with_sdk=Enable`
2. Use an SDK implementation whose `getModalityQuality()` returns a map without an entry
   for the captured modality (e.g., IRIS when only FINGER is keyed)
3. Attempt biometric capture — registration client throws `MDS_RCAPTURE_ERROR`
   with no MDM involvement

## Expected Behavior
A null-safe check with a descriptive `BiometricException`:

```java
Float score = scoreMap.get(biometricType);

if (score == null) {
    throw new BiometricException(
        "SDK_SCORE_NULL",
        "SDK did not return quality score for " + biometricType
    );
}

return score.doubleValue();
```

title: getMDMQualityThreshold() missing EXCEPTION_PHOTO case

Switch Statement doesnt include EXCEPTION_PHOTO even though its a valid modality

### Description

The switch statement handles FINGERPRINT_SLAB_LEFT, FINGERPRINT_SLAB_RIGHT FINGERPRINT_SLAB_THUMBS, IRIS_DOUBLE, and FACE but has no case for EXCEPTION_PHOTO. The Modality enum defines EXCEPTION_PHOTO as a valid modality and getRetryCount() already handles it, making the omission in getMDMQualityThreshold() an inconsistency. The method falls through to return 0, meaning exception photos bypass quality threshold validation entirely and any score passes.

title: [DMP 2026]: Define Biometric Quality Through SDK During Biometric Capture
content:
Problem description: ### Ticket Contents ## Description **User Story:** As a registration system, I want the registration client to support SDK-based biometric quality evaluation with SBI fallback, so that biometric capture quality is validated in real time. **As-Is:** Currently, the registration client validates biometric quality using the SBI-provided quality score, and the score is compared against the existing configurable biometric quality threshold defined in the system configuration. **To-Be:** The registration client should support evaluating biometric quality using an SDK during biometric capture, while continuing to use the existing configuration-based threshold validation mechanism. The SDK-generated score will be validated against the same threshold currently used for SBI. If the SDK is unavailable or fails, the system will fall back to SBI quality scores. ### Goals & Mid-Point Milestone **Goals** - Enable SDK-based biometric quality evaluation during capture - Reuse the existing biometric quality threshold configuration without modification - Provide real-time feedback to operators for biometric quality validation - Ensure seamless fallback to SBI quality scores when SDK is unavailable or fails **Goals Achieved By Mid-point Milestone** - SDK integration framework enabled in the registration client - Ability to fetch and process SDK-based quality scores - Initial validation of SDK scores against existing thresholds - Basic fallback mechanism to SBI implemented ### Setup/Installation This feature has to be implemented as part of the Registration Client. Please refer to the [developer guide](https://docs.mosip.io/1.2.0/id-lifecycle-management/identity-issuance/registration-client/develop/registration-client-developers-guide) for further details. ### Expected Outcome - Biometric quality is evaluated in real time using SDK where available - Existing threshold validation mechanism continues unchanged - Operators are prompted to re-capture biometrics when quality is below threshold - System falls back to SBI scoring seamlessly without disrupting the flow - Registration is blocked if no valid quality score is available ### Acceptance Criteria - Registration client supports SDK-based biometric quality evaluation - SDK-generated scores are validated against existing configurable thresholds - SBI fallback is triggered when SDK is unavailable, disabled, or fails - Re-capture is enforced when quality scores fall below threshold - System handles error scenarios including invalid SDK responses, timeouts, and partial captures - Registration is blocked when both SDK and SBI scores are unavailable - All quality evaluations, fallbacks, and errors are logged for audit purposes

Alternate Scenarios

Scenario ID Scenario Condition System Behavior User/System Message
AS-01 SDK-based Quality Evaluation SDK available and valid SDK score used against existing threshold Biometric quality captured successfully.
AS-02 SBI Fallback SDK unavailable SBI score used against existing threshold Using system default quality score for validation.
AS-03 SDK Disabled SDK turned off in configuration SBI quality validation continues SDK-based quality evaluation is disabled. Using default scoring.
AS-04 Re-capture Flow Quality below threshold Re-capture enforced Captured biometric quality is below acceptable threshold. Please re-capture.

Scenario Condition System Behavior Error Message
Invalid SDK Score SDK configured, returns null / invalid value Display error, block registration, and prompt operator to re-capture biometrics. No fallback to SBI. Invalid biometric quality score received from SDK.
SDK Timeout SDK configured, response delayed Display error, block progression, and prompt re-capture. No fallback to SBI. Biometric quality evaluation timed out. Please re-capture biometrics.
SDK Exception SDK configured, runtime/integration error Display error, block registration, and prompt re-capture. No fallback to SBI. Error occurred during SDK-based quality evaluation. Please retry capture.
Missing SBI Score SBI configured as quality source but no score returned Block registration and prompt re-capture or retry. Default biometric quality score unavailable.
No Quality Source Neither SDK nor SBI configured Block registration and prevent further processing. Biometric quality evaluation is not configured. Registration cannot proceed.
Quality Below Threshold Score (SDK or SBI) below threshold Enforce re-capture of biometrics before proceeding. Biometric quality below acceptable threshold. Please re-capture.
Partial Capture Missing required biometric modality Block progression and prompt completion of all required biometric captures. Incomplete biometric capture. Please capture all required biometrics.
Corrupt Data Invalid or unreadable biometric data Reject captured data and prompt re-capture. Captured biometric data is invalid. Please re-capture.
Configuration Error Invalid or missing threshold/config setup Block process and notify administrator. Biometric quality configuration error. Please contact administrator.

title: [C4GT Community]: Enhancement: Track Supervisor ID in Registration Packet Processing
content:
Problem description:
### Ticket Contents

## Description
As a registration system, I want to capture the supervisor ID along with approval/rejection actions during resident registration packet processing, so that country representatives can generate reports mapping supervisors to approved/rejected packets.

### Goals

## Goals
- [ ] Enable identification of the supervisor responsible for approving or rejecting registration packets.
- [ ] Ensure supervisor details are captured for audit and reporting purposes.
- [ ] Support accurate reporting of supervisor-wise approved and rejected packets.
- [ ] Strengthen validation by including supervisor verification during packet processing.

## You can refer to this link to know more about the registration client and the steps to follow for the installation:
- [Registration Client Overview](https://docs.mosip.io/1.2.0/id-lifecycle-management/identity-issuance/registration-client)
- [Developers Guide](https://docs.mosip.io/1.2.0/id-lifecycle-management/identity-issuance/registration-client/develop/registration-client-developers-guide)

### Expected Outcome

Supervisor ID is captured and stored whenever a packet is approved or rejected.
The system maintains a complete audit trail including supervisor comments and timestamps.
Country representatives can generate reports based on supervisor activity.
Packet processing enforces validation rules related to supervisor identification.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. **Supervisor Enablement & Access**
-   The user must be registered as a supervisor with valid credentials and supervisor ID.
-   The supervisor should be mapped to relevant centers and have access to view and process resident packets.

2. **Packet Approval/Rejection Flow**
The supervisor should be able to:
-   Log in to the registration client.
-   Navigate to the pending approval page.
-   View resident and packet details.
-   Approve or reject the packet with optional comments.

3. **Supervisor ID Capture**
When a supervisor approves a packet:

- The system must capture and store:
  Supervisor ID
  Approval status
  Supervisor comments (if any)
  Timestamp

- When a supervisor rejects a packet:
   The system must capture and store the same details as above.

4. **Admin Handling**
When an admin approves and uploads a packet:
- Admin ID must be captured and treated as the supervisor ID.
- Packets approved and uploaded by admins should be tracked and marked separately.

Validation rules should differ for:
- Supervisor-uploaded packets (validated)
- Admin-uploaded packets (validation skipped where applicable)

5. **Validation Mechanism**
- Supervisor validation must be included during packet processing.
- If supervisor ID is missing or null during approval/rejection:
       Packet validation must fail at the CMD stage.

6. **Reporting Capability**
The system administrator or country representative must be able to use supervisor ID to generate reports showing:

- Supervisor vs approved packets
- Supervisor vs rejected packets

### Ticket Contents

## Description
As a registration system, I want the registration client to define biometric quality using an SDK during biometric collection, so that the quality of captured biometrics is validated in real time and meets predefined standards.


### Goals

## Goals
- [ ] Enable integration of biometric quality evaluation through an SDK.
- [ ] Ensure real-time feedback on biometric quality during capture.
- [ ] Provide a fallback mechanism using SBI quality scores when SDK is unavailable.
- [ ] Maintain consistent validation and traceability of biometric quality checks.
