title: Fix double-hash issue in TokenIDGenerator: migrate from HMACUtils to HMACUtils2
content:
Problem description:
## Problem
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  `TokenIDGenerator.generateTokenID()` was migrated from `HMACUtils` to `HMACUtils2` but the call pattern was not updated, causing a double-hash bug.                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  ### Root Cause
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  `HMACUtils.digestAsPlainText(byte[])` only hex-encodes the input — hashing is done by the caller.                                                                                                                                                    
  `HMACUtils2.digestAsPlainText(byte[])` hashes AND hex-encodes internally.                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                           
  When `HMACUtils2` was introduced in commons, the old call pattern was carried over unchanged, causing double-hashing:                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  ```java
  // Wrong - generateHash() called twice (once explicitly, once inside digestAsPlainText)                                                                                                                                                                
  HMACUtils2.digestAsPlainText(HMACUtils2.generateHash(input))                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  Fix
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  File: kernel/kernel-keymanager-service/src/main/java/io/mosip/kernel/tokenidgenerator/generator/TokenIDGenerator.java                                                                                                                                  
   
  Before:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
  String uinHash = HMACUtils2.digestAsPlainText(HMACUtils2.generateHash((uin + uinSalt).getBytes()));                                                                                                                                                  
  String hash = HMACUtils2.digestAsPlainText(HMACUtils2.generateHash((partnerCodeSalt + partnerCode + uinHash).getBytes()));

  After:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  String uinHash = HMACUtils2.digestAsPlainText((uin + uinSalt).getBytes());
  String hash = HMACUtils2.digestAsPlainText((partnerCodeSalt + partnerCode + uinHash).getBytes());                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  Impact
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  - Fixes double-hash bug introduced when migrating from HMACUtils to HMACUtils2                                                                                                                                                                         
  - Token ID now hashed exactly once as intended
  - Added try-catch for NoSuchAlgorithmException thrown by HMACUtils2.digestAsPlainText()

title: KER-KMS-500: nextBytes() failed under concurrent load when using SoftHSM
content: Problem description: In the qaj21 environment, all API test cases are failing with the following error: KER-KMS-500: nextBytes() failed Initially, restarting SoftHSM and KeyManager resolved the issue. However, the same error continues to reoccur and is now being observed across multiple environments. **Observed behavior:** Restart SoftHSM and KeyManager → APIs work successfully. After some time / under load → APIs start failing with KER-KMS-500: nextBytes() failed. Restarting the services again temporarily restores functionality. SoftHSM logs also show PKCS#11-related errors such as: ``` [PKCS11 function C_GetTokenInfo failed: rv = CKR_SLOT_ID_INVALID (0x3)] (error: PKCS11 function C_GetTokenInfo failed: rv = CKR_SLOT_ID_INVALID (0x3) 2026-06-10T05:57:06.824749599Z Aborting. 2026-06-10T05:57:07.287583270Z Using slot 0 with a present token (0x6a490964) 2026-06-10T05:57:07.409966524Z User PIN successfully initialized 35938595f83923504751b40535570342f706a634 2032875c95563c15cf77395f924191fdd6a1b33f this is softhsm logs) ``` Attaching the KeyManager logs for reference. [keymanager-7c7bbb487b-jbvks_keymanager.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28791296/keymanager-7c7bbb487b-jbvks_keymanager.log) Discussion and resolution: [nagendra0721]: **Root cause**: with mosip.kernel.keygenerator.rng.provider.enable=true, KeyManager routes its random byte generation (SecureRandom.nextBytes()) through the **PKCS#11** **RNG** provider backed by SoftHSM (C_GenerateRandom). SoftHSM isn't built to handle production-style concurrent load, so under sustained/parallel traffic the PKCS#11 session and slot handles become invalid **(CKR_SLOT_ID_INVALID)**, and the **nextBytes()** call fails with **KER-KMS-500.** A service restart re-initializes the sessions, which is why APIs recover temporarily — but the failure returns once load builds up again. Fix: setting **`mosip.kernel.keygenerator.rng.provider.enable=false`** makes KeyManager fall back to the JVM's default SecureRandom, which on Linux seeds from /dev/urandom instead of going through the HSM for every random-byte request. This removes the PKCS#11 session contention against SoftHSM entirely, and the nextBytes() failed errors no longer reoccur under load.

title: <Performance Enhancement> Enable Key Manager to Support 500K Packet Processing per Day (MOSIP Release 1.4.x)
content:
Problem description:
### Description:
This task focuses on enhancing the performance of the Key Manager component in MOSIP to reliably support a target throughput of 500,000 packets per day. The objective is to optimize key management operations and system efficiency to handle sustained high-volume workloads without compromising security or stability.
The implementation involves identifying bottlenecks and applying optimizations across cryptographic operations, memory handling, caching, and concurrency management. These improvements will be validated through comprehensive performance testing to ensure the system meets the desired throughput benchmarks.
All validated changes should be merged into the release/1.4.x branch following standard review and release practices.

### Key Areas of Enhancement:
1. ThreadLocal JCA Object Reuse
JCA objects such as Cipher, KeyFactory, MessageDigest, SecureRandom, KeyGenerator, CertPathValidator, and CertificateFactory are expensive to instantiate due to provider lookups and SPI loading.
 - Introduced ThreadLocal caching to reuse these objects per thread and eliminate repeated allocations under concurrent load
- Applied across:
  - CryptoCore — Cipher, SecretKeyFactory, SecureRandom
  - ZKCryptoManagerServiceImpl — Cipher, MessageDigest
  - SignatureServiceImpl — KeyFactory, MessageDigest
  - RandomKeysGenerator — KeyGenerator, Cipher, SecureRandom
  - PartnerCertificateManagerServiceImpl — CertPathValidator, CertificateFactory
- Ensured proper cleanup using @PreDestroy to prevent memory leaks in thread-pooled environments
2. Multi-Layer Caching
- Implemented certificate path caching (Cache2k with TTL and ~2000 entries) to avoid repeated PKIX chain validations
- Introduced domain index caching using DN and SKI for constant-time issuer lookup
- Added ConcurrentHashMap-based caches in SignatureServiceImpl for:
  - Decoded PublicKey objects
  - Parsed X509Certificate objects
  - JWS headers
  - Certificate trust validation results
3. Byte Array Copy Optimization
- Replaced Arrays.copyOfRange() with System.arraycopy() in performance-critical paths
- Applied across components such as CryptomanagerServiceImpl, ClientCryptoFacade, SessionKeyDecryptorHelper, KeymanagerUtil, and CryptomanagerUtils
- Reduced unnecessary array allocations and minimized bounds-check overhead

### Acceptance Criteria:
- System successfully processes 500,000 packets per day under performance test conditions
- ThreadLocal reuse implemented and validated without memory leaks
- Multi-layer caching reduces redundant cryptographic and certificate validation overhead
- Byte array optimizations reduce memory footprint and improve execution speed
- Performance benchmarks demonstrate measurable improvement over baseline
- No functional or security regressions observed
- Code reviewed and merged into release/1.4.x branch
- Documentation updated to reflect performance enhancements and configurations

title: Enable MOSIP to support ECC Algorithm during encryption & decryption
content:
Problem description:
**Description:**
As an identity and access management system user, I want the MOSIP to support encryption and decryption using the ECC algorithm So that user credentials and sensitive data can be securely encrypted, transmitted, and decrypted to prevent unauthorised access.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. **ECC Encryption:** 
- The IDA module must allow encryption of sensitive auth data (e.g., auth request, otp, KYC data) using ECC public keys before transmitting data.

2. **ECC Decryption:**
- The IDA module must decrypt incoming encrypted data (auth request) using the ECC algorithm
- During KYC authentication decryption process must ensure that only authorized users with valid private keys can decrypt the data.

3. Authentication & Authorization:
- ECC encryption must be used during user authentication (e.g., signing or encrypting access tokens) to ensure that only legitimate users gain access to resources.
- The IDA module must verify digital signatures using ECC during authorization to validate requests and responses.

4. **Error Handling & Security Alerts:**
- The system must provide clear error messages when ECC encryption or decryption fails, without exposing sensitive details.

5. **Compliance & Auditability:**
- Encryption and decryption events should be logged for audit purposes, ensuring traceability and accountability in the identity and access lifecycle.

6. Backward Compatibility:
- Enabling system to sign downloaded UIN with RSA, ECC, Eddsa Algorithm

7. Migration Compatibility:
- Allowing the users to switch between RSA, ECC and Eddsa (Xdh - for encryption/decryption)

title: R&D on Quantum-Resistant Cryptography Adoption in Key Manager
content:
Problem description:
**Title:** 
Research and prototype integration of quantum-safe crypto algorithms (Kyber, Dilithium, SPHINCS+) in Key Manager

As a security architect or cryptography engineer I want to conduct R&D to evaluate and prototype the adoption of quantum-safe cryptographic algorithms —  Kyber, Dilithium , and SPHINCS within the Key Manager component So that our system can be prepared for post-quantum security and ensure long-term cryptographic resilience against quantum attacks.

**Description**
This R&D aims to explore the integration of post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) algorithms  (Kyber, Dilithium, SPHINCS+) into the existing Key Manager service. The effort includes identifying available libraries, assessing compatibility with the Java  21 tech stack, and designing a prototype implementation.

**Key outcomes expected include:**
- Comparative analysis of at least two Java-compatible PQC libraries (license, maturity, performance, native deps).
- Working Java 21 prototypes for Kyber, Dilithium and SPHINCS+ demonstrating key lifecycle + crypto operations.
- HSM support plan and prototype integration
- Integration using PKCS#11 or Java JCE provider interfaces.
- Performance benchmarks (key sizes, generation, sign/verify, encrypt/decrypt timings) and memory/CPU observations.
- Security / compliance assessment
- Documents: R&D summary, technical design for integration into Key Manager, and an upgrade/migration guide.

**Acceptance Criteria**

1. Library Evaluation
      Identify and document at least two stable Java-compatible PQC libraries (e.g., BouncyCastle PQC, OpenQuantumSafe bindings, LibOQS-JNI).
      Evaluate license, performance, and implementation maturity for each.
2. Algorithm Coverage
        Demonstrate basic use of:
          - Kyber 
          - Dilithium 
          - SPHINCS+ 
        Each demo must include sample inputs and expected outputs.
3. Prototype Implementation
    - Implement Java 21 prototypes (non-production sandbox) inside a Key Manager test module for:
             - Key generation.
             - Secure storage and retrieval (in-memory and simulated persistent store).
             - Sign and verify (Dilithium, SPHINCS+).
             - Encrypt / decrypt or KEM flows (Kyber).
4. Integration Feasibility
        - Produce a technical integration plan showing:
                 - How PQC primitives map to existing Key Manager interfaces (KeyPairGenerator, Signature-like APIs, Cipher/KEM-like APIs).
                 - JCE provider integration strategy (wrap PQC libs as a JCE provider or use existing providers).
                 - PKCS#11 / HSM interaction approach and required vendor considerations.
       - Provide performance benchmark table (key sizes, generation time, sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt latency, memory footprint) with comparison to RSA/ECC equivalents.
5. HSM & JCE/PKCS#11 Support
       - Demonstrate or provide a clear prototype path to enable HSM support:
               - Show how to expose PQC keys via PKCS#11 slots assuming HSM vendor support and document required PKCS#11 extensions or limitations.
               - Provide JCE integration plan so existing Key Manager APIs (keyGen, encrypt/decrypt, sign/verify) continue to work with PQC keys with minimal changes.
               - Identify and document any native/JNI dependencies and fallback (software) implementations when HSM lacks PQC support.
6. Security & Compliance
        - Provide NIST PQC standardization assessment — indicate how chosen parameter sets align with NIST recommendations as of the R&D date.
        - Document key sizes, expected security levels and cryptographic assumptions.
        - Identify any third-party dependencies with security risk (e.g., native libs, JNI) and mitigation.
7. Deliverable
         - Submit R&D summarizing findings, 
         - Prototype artifacts (code, build instructions, tests).
         - Technical design document for production integration.
         - Upgrade/migration document covering steps to adopt PQC in Key Manager and HSM considerations.

**Tasks**
1. Research Phase
    - Review NIST PQC outcomes and relevant publications for Kyber/Dilithium/SPHINCS+.
    - Identify Java 21 compatible PQC libraries and bindings (list ≥2).
    - Create evaluation matrix (license, maturity, JNI/native, API surface).
2. Environment Setup
    - Create isolated Key Manager sandbox project (Java 21).
    - Add build scripts (Maven/Gradle) to import PQC libraries and test harness.
    - Prepare test vectors and example messages.
3. Prototype Development
    - Implement Kyber KEM flows (keygen, encapsulate/decapsulate) in sandbox.
    - Implement Dilithium.
    - Implement SPHINCS+.
    - Integrate basic key lifecycle (generate, store, retrieve) using existing Key Manager abstractions.
4. JCE / PKCS#11 / HSM Integration
    - Design and implement a JCE adapter or provider wrapper for the chosen PQC library.
    - Build a PKCS#11 shim/proxy or use a simulated PKCS#11 provider for testing.
    - Attempt HSM vendor integration checklist: vendor PQC support, PKCS#11 extensions, firmware constraints.
5. Documentation
     - Produce technical design doc: API changes (if any), JCE provider plan, PKCS#11/HSM integration notes, migration strategy.
     - Produce upgrade document with step-by-step instructions to bring PQC into production, including fallback paths and dual-stack migration (PQ+classical hybrid signatures/encryption).

title: <Feature> Retrieve Lost AID (with Face Capture & Match Verification)
content:
Problem description:
## Purpose
As a registration_support_user, I should be able to search for an AID based on the resident details provided in order to identify the lost AID and share it with the respective resident. Before the AID is shared, the resident's identity must be confirmed through a live face capture and a face match against the biometric enrolled for that AID, so that the acknowledgement is only resent to a verified resident.

As part of this story, a new role named **registration_support_user** must be introduced in the system. Only users assigned this role are able to see and access the Retrieve Lost AID option in the admin portal.

Note: registration_support_user will be termed as **User** hereafter.

## Pre-Requisites
- The **registration_support_user** role must be created and available in the system's identity/access management (IAM) configuration.
- A user must be assigned the **registration_support_user** role in the admin portal.
- User should have logged into the admin portal.
- Only users with the **registration_support_user** role should be able to view and access the **Retrieve Lost AID** feature in the admin portal.
- A working SBI (Secure Biometric Interface) compliant face capture device should be available and connected for the verification step.

## Role & Access Control
- A new role **registration_support_user** is introduced as part of this feature.
- The role must be defined in the IAM/authorization configuration (e.g. realm roles in Keycloak) and made assignable to users through the admin portal's user/role management.
- The **Retrieve Lost AID** menu/sub-menu option is displayed in the admin portal **only** to users who hold the **registration_support_user** role; for all other users the option is hidden.
- Menu visibility is driven by the logged-in user's role(s) — the option must not appear for users without this role.
- The Retrieve Lost AID APIs/endpoints must also be **authorized** for the **registration_support_user** role at the backend, so that the functionality cannot be invoked by users lacking the role even if the UI control were bypassed.
- A user who does not hold the **registration_support_user** role attempting to access the feature directly should receive an appropriate authorization error (e.g. 403 Forbidden) handled via the standard error page.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Basic Flow
0. The **Retrieve Lost AID** option is visible in the admin portal sub-menu only because the logged-in User holds the **registration_support_user** role. (A user without this role does not see the option.)
1. User navigates to **Retrieve Lost AID** by clicking on the option present in the sub menu.
2. Once navigated, user should be able to view the below fields to search:
   - **Registration From date & To date** – Mandatory field (date field)
   - **Full Name** – text box which allows only alphabetical input.
   - **Email** – text box which allows alphabetic letters & special characters.
   - **Phone Number** – text box which allows only numerical input.
   - **Location** – the support user should be able to select region, province, city, zone or postal code and search (should be based on the ID Schema).
   - **Centre Name**
   - **Type** (Update, New)
   - **Enquiry mode** – (In person, Phone)
3. The User should select the date and must fill one or more inputs, then click on **Search**.
4. A list of resident details is displayed with details such as **AID, Full Name, Centre Name, Registration Date, Status** and an **Action** column with a **View** button placed on it.

#### Identity Verification via Face Capture & Match (new)
5. When the User clicks on the **View** button, a **Resident Details** pop-up is displayed with **Name, AID, profile picture, enrolled date and status** for the User to review.
6. To proceed, the User initiates **Capture Face**. The resident's live face is captured using the SBI-compliant biometric capture device.
7. The system performs a **1:1 face match** of the captured live face against the face biometric enrolled for that AID.
8. **On a successful match** (match score greater than or equal to the configurable threshold):
   - A success indicator is displayed to the User.
   - The **Resend Acknowledgement** action (and the **Print** actions, where applicable) is enabled.
9. **On an unsuccessful match** (score below threshold):
   - A clear "Face did not match" message is displayed.
   - The User may **recapture and retry** up to the configurable number of attempts.
   - The Resend Acknowledgement and Print actions remain **disabled** until a successful match is achieved.
10. Once the face is matched and identity is verified, the User clicks on **Resend Acknowledgement** to send the acknowledgement with the AID through the registered email id and phone number.
11. The User should also be able to **print the acknowledgement** and share it with the resident.
12. If the status of the application process has already reached the printing stage and processing is completed, the User should be able to **print the ID card** and issue it to the resident.
13. Once the card is printed and issued, the status should be updated accordingly for the specific AID/UIN.
14. This feature should support multi-language. The alignment of the data on the screen should follow the same as the current flow: for the Arabic language, the screen should display text and alignment from right to left (RTL). This applies to the face capture/verification pop-up as well.

### Alternate Flow – Records not available
- If the records are not available, an error message should be displayed:
  - **Heading:** 'Results not found.'
  - **Message:** 'Sorry! No Records Found'
  - **Button:** Ok — when the User clicks on the Ok button, the popup should be closed and the User should be navigated back to the search page.

### Alternate Flow – Face match unsuccessful (new)
- When the captured face does not match the enrolled biometric:
  - A message "Face did not match. Please try again." is displayed.
  - The User can retry up to the configured number of attempts.
  - After all attempts are exhausted, the Resend Acknowledgement and Print actions stay disabled, and the User is returned to the resident list / search page. The attempt is recorded for audit.

## Business Rules
- The **Retrieve Lost AID** option and its functionality are accessible only to users with the **registration_support_user** role; the option is hidden for all other users and the backend APIs are authorized for this role.
- Except for Registration From and To date, all other fields should not be mandatory.
- When the User searches for records, in addition to Registration From and To date, at least any one parameter needs to be provided by the User to continue the search. If not, an error should be displayed. Search criteria should follow an **AND** query.
- The total number of records displayed once the User clicks on Search should be restricted to **10**. This should be configurable.
- The number of searches allowed per day per logged-in User should be restricted to **30**. This value should be configurable.
- If the number of results for the search is more than the restricted number of records to display (i.e. 10), an alert should be displayed: "Please refine your search criteria and search again as the number of records fetched are more than configured."
- **Resend Acknowledgement, Print Acknowledgement and Print ID Card actions are gated behind a successful 1:1 face match** — they remain disabled until the captured face matches the enrolled biometric for the selected AID.
- The **face match threshold** (minimum acceptable match score) should be configurable.
- The **number of face capture/match retry attempts** per record should be configurable (e.g. 3).
- Every face capture and match attempt (success or failure) should be **logged for audit**, including the User, AID, timestamp and outcome (the captured image should not be persisted beyond what policy permits).
- If **no face biometric is enrolled** for the selected AID, the system should handle this per the configurable fallback policy (e.g. block the resend with an appropriate message, or allow a policy-controlled manual override), and the action should not silently succeed.

## Data Fields

### Retrieve Lost AID – Landing / Search Page
| Field Name | Data Type | Field Type | Mandatory | Field Validations | Error Messages |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Registration From Date | Date | Date Picker | Mandatory | — | Please Select Registration From Date |
| Registration To Date | Date | Date Picker | Mandatory | Future dates disabled; user cannot select a future date | Please Select Registration To Date |
| Email | Text | Text input | Non-Mandatory | Validate that the entered email is valid | Please enter a valid email |
| Phone | Number | Text input | Non-Mandatory | Only numerical values allowed | Please enter a valid phone number |
| Full Name | Text | Text input | Non-Mandatory | Allow alphanumerical values | — |
| Zone | Text | Dropdown | Non-Mandatory | Zones mapped to the user are listed; displayed based on ID schema | — |
| Province | Text | Dropdown | Non-Mandatory | Provinces mapped to the selected Zone are listed; displayed based on ID schema | — |
| Region | Text | Dropdown | Non-Mandatory | Regions mapped to the selected Province are listed; displayed based on ID schema | — |
| City | Text | Dropdown | Non-Mandatory | Cities mapped to the selected Region are listed; displayed based on ID schema | — |
| Postal Code | Text | Dropdown | Non-Mandatory | Postal codes mapped to the selected City and assigned to the current user; displayed based on ID schema | — |
| Centre Name | Text | Dropdown | Non-Mandatory | Centre Names mapped to the current user and selected city; displayed based on ID schema | — |
| Type | Text | Value: New / Update | Non-Mandatory | — | — |

### AID List (results table)
| Column | Data Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| AID | Text | Alphanumeric value allowed |
| Full Name | Text | Alphanumeric value allowed |
| Centre Name | Text | Alphanumeric value allowed |
| Registration Date | Date | — |
| Action | Link | View button → resident details page |

### Resident Details (pop-up)
| Field | Data Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Application ID | Text | Non-editable, display only |
| Resident Full Name | Text | Non-editable, display only |
| Registered Date | Date | Non-editable, display only |
| Status | Text | Non-editable, display only |
| Profile Picture | Image | Non-editable, display only |

### Face Capture & Match (new – within Resident Details verification)
| Field | Data Type | Field Type | Mandatory | Notes / Validations | Error Messages |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capture Face | Biometric (face image) | Capture control | Mandatory before resend/print | Live capture via SBI-compliant device; quality check on capture | Device not detected / Capture failed, please try again |
| Match Score | Number | Internal/display | System-generated | Compared against configurable threshold | — |
| Match Status | Text | Display | System-generated | Values: Matched / Not Matched | Face did not match. Please try again. |

## Exceptions
- As per the basic flow and data definition.
- Generic error pages — designed as per UX.
- Common error page to handle the below HTTP response status codes:
  - 5XX → 500, 502, 503, 504
  - 4XX → 400, 403, 404, 405, 415
- Should have a standard image as per the image embedded in UX indicating "Something went wrong". Only the error message should vary based on the error code.
- For all error messages, the main error message as per the error code can appear in bold, followed by the statement "Our experts are working hard to make things working again. Please try again later."
- All error messages should be retained for 10 seconds (configurable) and should disappear either at the end of 10 seconds or when the User clicks on the 'OK' button.

### Face Capture & Match exceptions (new)
- **Biometric device not connected / not detected** — display an appropriate message prompting the User to connect the device and retry.
- **Capture timeout or poor-quality capture** — prompt the User to recapture.
- **Face match service unavailable** (5XX) — handle via the standard "Something went wrong" error page.
- **No face biometric enrolled for the AID** — display the appropriate message and handle per the configurable fallback policy (resend/print not enabled by default).

## Reference UX
- Retrieve Lost RID (existing flow) for layout, alignment and error-handling patterns.

title: To harden keycloak (using stricter policy,stricter role provision, removing unwanted authorizations)
content:
Problem description:
keycloak-jboss runs jboss/keycloak:9.0.0 (keycloak-jboss/Dockerfile:1) — released ~2020, long end-of-life, WildFly-based (Keycloak moved to Quarkus at v17). Many known CVEs. This is the single biggest risk.
keycloak-artemis bundles Keycloak 16.1.1 on minideb:buster (keycloak-artemis/Dockerfile) — Keycloak 16 is EOL, and Debian 10 "buster" is EOL for standard support. Upgrade to a current supported Keycloak (26.x line) on a maintained base.
Old, vulnerable Python deps in requirements.txt: python-keycloak==0.26.1, requests==2.25.1, urllib3==1.26.5, PyYAML==5.4.1. Several have published CVEs. Pin to current patched versions. 

"redirectUris": ['*'] — wildcard redirect URIs on all clients. Classic open-redirect / token-exfiltration vector. Set explicit, per-client allow-lists.
"directAccessGrantsEnabled": True — enables the ROPC (password) grant everywhere. Disable except where truly required.
"authorizationServicesEnabled": True — turns on fine-grained authorization services for every client, expanding attack surface unnecessarily. Enable only where used.
Public client uses "fullScopeAllowed": True  — the token gets all realm roles. Restrict client scope.

title: Documentation outdated: NFS Server & Client Setup – Mismatch Between Documentation and Script
content:
Problem description:
The `storage-class/nfs/README.md` incorrectly states that executing `install-nfs-server.sh` will prompt for an "Environment Name", and only shows interactive prompts for `install-nfs-csi.sh`.

However, both scripts support non-interactive execution via environment variables:
For `install-nfs-server.sh`:
- `NFS_SERVER_LOCATION` (default `/srv/nfs`)
- `NFS_USER` (default `nfsnobody`)

For `install-nfs-csi.sh`:
- `NFS_SERVER`
- `NFS_SERVER_LOCATION`

The README needs to be updated to reflect the non-interactive usage with environment variables for both the server and client provisioner scripts.

title: Feature Request: Add uninstall script for NFS server
content:
Problem description:
The [nfs storage class directory](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/tree/master/storage-class/nfs) includes an `install-nfs-server.sh` script to set up the NFS server on a VM, and a `delete-nfs-cient-csi.sh` to remove the client provisioner.

However, there is no `uninstall-nfs-server.sh` (or `delete-nfs-server.sh`) script to properly clean up and remove the NFS server from the host machine. A script should be added to stop the service, remove the `nfs-kernel-server` package, clean up `/etc/exports`, and remove the created NFS user.

title: Bug: Incorrect host group in nginx hosts.ini.sample
content:
Problem description:
In the nginx Ansible directory (`nginx/mosip`), the [hosts.ini.sample]%2(https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/blob/master/nginx/mosip/hosts.ini.sample%2) file defines the host group as `[cluster]`.

However, the associated Ansible playbooks (e.g., `nginx_ports.yaml`) expect the host group to be named `[nginx]`. This mismatch causes Ansible commands to fail with "skipping: no hosts matched".

The sample file should be updated to use `[nginx]` instead of `[cluster]`.

title: Bug: Sequencing issue in README.md (Monitoring should precede Ingress)
content:
Problem description:
In the main [README.md](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/blob/master/README.md) "Contents" section, `Ingress` is currently listed before `monitoring`.

However, the Monitoring stack (along with logging and alerting) should be executed and set up before Ingress. The sequencing in the documentation should be updated so users follow the cluster setup in the correct order.

title: Bug: README.md is missing automated Ansible deployment instructions for RKE2
content:
Problem description:
The current [README.md in the rke2 directory](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/blob/master/k8-cluster/on-prem/rke2/README.md) only documents the manual steps for installing and configuring the RKE2 cluster (e.g., curling the install script, copying config.yaml, and starting systemctl manually).

However, there is a full automated Ansible deployment available in the `ansible` directory (using `main.yaml`). The documentation should be updated to include instructions on how to use these automated Ansible playbooks for the full cluster installation, as they are the preferred and less error-prone way to deploy the cluster.

title: Bug: Typo in subsequent control plane node names in hosts.ini.sample
content:
Problem description:
In the rke2 ansible directory, the sample inventory file (hosts.ini.sample) and default configurations use an underscore in the node names (e.g., `control-subsequent_plane-1`).

Kubernetes node names must be valid RFC 1123 DNS subdomains, which means underscores are invalid. This causes issues when configuring the nodes.

It should be changed to use a hyphen instead (e.g., `control-subsequent-plane-1`).

title: Admin module not working due to missing trust for corporate CA (Keycloak TLS / JWKS / token endpoint) (v3)
content:
Problem description:
My sandbox installation uses an ingress certificate signed by our organisation's internal CA. It has turned out that the admin module has its problems when running without public certificates. 

The first obstacle is login. After having entered `globaluser` and password, this error is displayed in the browser:
```
{"id":null,"version":null,"responsetime":"2026-04-01T11:19:39.560Z","metadata":null,"response":null,"errors":[{"errorCode":"KER-MSD-500","message":"Both provided Keys cannot be null."}]}
```

The main reason seems to be that my ingress certificate presented by the external IAM URL is unknown to the JVM in which admin-service runs. Having successfully worked around this, I found that token issuer comparison was unsuccessful.

Long story short, it looks like currently MOSIP's v3 deployment is not ready for such scenarios out of the box. I really think it should be (and this should also be verified by QA), because sandbox installations using internal CAs can be assumed to be a rather common scenario.

I have eventually succeded in getting the admin UI to work. For your reference, here's what I did (and I cannot rule out some of these steps being unnecessary):

**1. Change the configuration in admin-default.properties**

```diff
diff --git a/admin-default.properties b/admin-default.properties
index 2548bc7d..2954c663 100644
--- a/admin-default.properties
+++ b/admin-default.properties
@@ -208,7 +208,7 @@ mosip.iam.module.login_flow.response_type=code
 mosip.iam.authorization_endpoint=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/auth
 mosip.iam.module.admin_realm_id=mosip
 mosip.iam.token_endpoint=${keycloak.internal.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/token
-mosip.iam.certs_endpoint=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/certs
+mosip.iam.certs_endpoint=${keycloak.internal.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/certs

 regproc.token.request.appid=regproc
 regproc.token.request.clientId=mosip-regproc-client
@@ -221,7 +221,8 @@ KEYBASEDTOKENAPI=${mosip.kernel.authmanager.url}/v1/authmanager/authenticate/cli
 mosip.iam.adapter.appid=admin
 mosip.iam.adapter.clientid=mosip-admin-client
 mosip.iam.adapter.clientsecret=${mosip.admin.client.secret}
-mosip.iam.adapter.issuerURL=${keycloak.internal.url}/auth/realms/mosip
+mosip.iam.adapter.issuerURL=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip
+mosip.keycloak.issuerUrl=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip
 mosip.authmanager.client-token-endpoint=${mosip.kernel.authmanager.url}/v1/authmanager/authenticate/clientidsecretkey
 # in minutes
 mosip.iam.adapter.validate-expiry-check-rate=1440
@@ -229,6 +230,7 @@ mosip.iam.adapter.validate-expiry-check-rate=1440
 mosip.iam.adapter.renewal-before-expiry-interval=1440
 #this should be false if you don?t use this restTemplate true if you do
 mosip.iam.adapter.self-token-renewal-enable=true
+auth-token-generator.rest.issuerUrl=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip

 # LostRid
 mosip.registration.processor.lostrid.id=mosip.registration.lostrid
@@ -277,6 +279,8 @@ mosip.kernel.jsonvalidator.file-storage-uri=LOCAL

 mosip.kernel.machineid.length=5
 auth.server.admin.issuer.uri=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/
+auth.server.admin.issuer.internal.uri=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/
+auth.server.admin.issuer.domain.validate=false
 MACHINE_GET_API=${mosip.kernel.masterdata.url}/v1/masterdata/machines/mappedmachines/
 CRYPTOMANAGERDECRYPT_API=${mosip.kernel.keymanager.url}/v1/keymanager/decrypt
 CRYPTOMANAGER_DECRYPT=${mosip.kernel.keymanager.url}/v1/keymanager/decrypt

```

**2. Create file with our certificate chain**

This file will need to be made known to the admin-service JVM before it starts. We will "inject" it later:
```shell
cat my-ingress-host.cer our-corporate-ca.pem >corp-ca-chain.pem
```

**3. Patch the helm installation for an initContainer to the admin-service deployment**

Install `kustomize` on your local host:
```shell
dnf install -y kustomize
```

Create a `post-render.sh` script:
```shell
#!/bin/bash

command -V kustomize >/dev/null || { echo "Error, 'kustomize' command is not installed on your local system." 1>&2; exit 1; }

set -euo pipefail

tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Save helm output
cat > "$tmp/rendered.yaml"

# Copy kustomize files next to rendered.yaml
cp ./kustomization.yaml "$tmp/kustomization.yaml"

# Build patched output
kustomize build "$tmp"
```

Create a `kustomization.yaml` file:
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - rendered.yaml

patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: admin-service
    patch: |-
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: Deployment
      metadata:
        name: admin-service
      spec:
        template:
          spec:
            volumes:
              - name: corporate-ca
                secret:
                  secretName: corporate-ca
              - name: java-truststore
                emptyDir: {}
            initContainers:
              - name: import-corporate-ca
                image: eclipse-temurin:21-jre
                command:
                  - /bin/sh
                  - -c
                  - |
                    set -e
                    cp /opt/java/openjdk/lib/security/cacerts /work/cacerts
                    keytool -importcert \
                      -alias corporate-ca \
                      -file /ca/corp-ca.crt \
                      -keystore /work/cacerts \
                      -storepass changeit \
                      -noprompt
                volumeMounts:
                  - name: corporate-ca
                    mountPath: /ca
                    readOnly: true
                  - name: java-truststore
                    mountPath: /work
            containers:
              - name: admin-service
                env:
                  - name: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
                    value: >-
                      -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/work/cacerts
                      -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=changeit
                volumeMounts:
                  - name: java-truststore
                    mountPath: /work
```

Patch `install.sh` to (a) create a `secret` from the above `.pem` file and (b) activate post-render for the `admin-service` installation:
```diff
diff --git a/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh b/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh
index 9a08a24a..e450773f 100755
--- a/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh
+++ b/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh
@@ -18,6 +18,15 @@ function installing_admin() {
   kubectl label ns $NS istio-injection=enabled --overwrite
   helm repo update

+  if [ -r ../corp-ca-chain.pem ]; then
+    echo "File '../corp-ca-chain.pem' found, preparing for sandbox installation with internal CA root."
+    kubectl -n admin delete secret corporate-ca 2>/dev/null || /bin/true
+    kubectl -n admin create secret generic corporate-ca --from-file=corp-ca.crt=../corp-ca-chain.pem || errorExit "Error creating 'corporate-ca' secret."
+    ADMIN_SERVICE_HELM_POST_RENDER='--post-renderer ./post-render.sh'
+  else
+    echo "No file '../corp-ca-chain.pem' found, assuming non-sandbox install."
+  fi
+
   echo Copy configmaps
   sed -i 's/\r$//' copy_cm.sh
   ./copy_cm.sh
@@ -32,7 +41,7 @@ function installing_admin() {
   helm -n $NS install admin-hotlist mosip/admin-hotlist --version $CHART_VERSION

   echo Installing admin service. Will wait till service gets installed.
-  helm -n $NS install admin-service mosip/admin-service --set istio.corsPolicy.allowOrigins\[0\].prefix=https://$ADMIN_HOST --wait --version $CHART_VERSION
+  helm -n $NS install admin-service mosip/admin-service --set istio.corsPolicy.allowOrigins\[0\].prefix=https://$ADMIN_HOST --wait --version $CHART_VERSION $ADMIN_SERVICE_HELM_POST_RENDER

   echo Installing admin-ui
   helm -n $NS install admin-ui mosip/admin-ui --set admin.apiUrl=https://$API_HOST/v1/ --set istio.hosts\[0\]=$ADMIN_HOST --version $CHART_VERSION
```

Note that the `corp-ca-chain.pem` file is expected to reside in the `mosip-infra/deployment/v3/mosip` directory, because I assume that this problem will eventually also need to be fixed for other MOSIP modules, too.

Discussion and resolution:
[mbert]: I noticed that I filed this issue in the wrong repo, should have gone to `mosip-infra`. I am closing this and have opened the issue in [the mosip-infra repo](https://github.com/mosip/mosip-infra/issues/1713). Sorry for the confusion.

title: Install in logging/ - inconsistent to documentation and not working for rke1 clusters, istio-addons-values.yaml broken
content:
Problem description:
The `install.sh` script tries to install `rancher-logging-crd` and `rancher-logging`. According to the documentation on docs.mosip.io this was to be installed through the Rancher UI. However the `logging` charts are no longer exposed in the Rancher UI for versions from 2.8.x which is why it makes sense to use `install.sh` for this. But here we need to specify a version, because an `rke1` cluster requires quite old docker and kubernetes versions. Hence we need to enforce using a version that works with these. 

Also the `rancher-logging` chart requires some additional arguments in order to work with an `rke1` cluster.

Second issue: in the file `istio-addons-values.yaml` the hostname `kibana.sandbox.xyz.net` is hardcoded and not replaced. It should be configured by `install.sh` (my example below edits the file automatically which is probably not ideal since that file is under version control, so you may want to make `istio-addons-values.yaml` a template from which you expand and generate the actual file).

This is what worked for me (note that some of the stuff below is only for `rke1` clusters):
```
diff --git a/logging/install.sh b/logging/install.sh
index 21b54dd..36aced8 100755
--- a/logging/install.sh
+++ b/logging/install.sh
@@ -24,6 +24,10 @@ function check_and_update_kibana_host() {
   # Store Kibana Host in a ConfigMap for easy retrieval
   kubectl -n $NS create configmap kibana-config --from-literal=mosip_kibana_host=$KIBANA_HOST --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
   echo "Kibana Host stored in ConfigMap: kibana-config"
+
+  # Fix default host name in istio-addons-values.yaml
+  sed -i "s/^\( *\)host:.*/\1host: $KIBANA_HOST/" istio-addons-values.yaml
+  echo "Kibana Host fixed in istio-addons-values.yaml"
 }
 
 check_and_update_kibana_host
@@ -32,6 +36,7 @@ function installing_logging() {
   echo Updating helm repos
   helm repo add bitnami https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
   helm repo add banzaicloud-stable https://charts.helm.sh/stable
+  helm repo add rancher-charts https://charts.rancher.io
   helm repo update
 
   echo Installing Bitnami Elasticsearch and Kibana istio objects
@@ -53,10 +58,12 @@ function installing_logging() {
   helm -n $NS install istio-addons mosip/istio-addons --version $ISTIO_ADDONS_CHART_VERSION -f istio-addons-values.yaml
 
   echo Installing crds for logging operator
-  helm -n $NS install rancher-logging-crd mosip/rancher-logging-crd --wait
+  helm -n $NS install rancher-logging-crd rancher-charts/rancher-logging-crd --version 106.0.4+up4.10.0-rancher.9 --wait
   echo Installed crds for logging operator
   echo Installing logging operator
-  helm -n $NS install rancher-logging mosip/rancher-logging -f values.yaml
+  helm -n $NS install rancher-logging rancher-charts/rancher-logging --version 106.0.4+up4.10.0-rancher.9 -f values.yaml \
+    --set additionalLoggingSources.rke.enabled=true \
+    --set additionalLoggingSources.rke2.enabled=false
   echo Installed logging operator
   return 0
 }
```

title: Keycloak SAML client integration into Rancher (observation cluster) does not work as documented
content:
Problem description:
Setup as described in the documentation:

**Keycloak side**

1. Make sure the admin user has a full name and an email address [1]
2. Create a SAML client with only "Sign Documents" and "Sign Assertions" ON, Client ID: <rancher-baseURL>/v1-saml/keycloak/saml/metadata, Valid Redirect URI: <rancher-baseURL>/v1-saml/keycloak/saml/acs [2]
3. Add all Builtin Protocol Mappers [2]
4. Not mentioned (but it should!), but leads to errors if omitted: change the attribute values so that the match what needs to be entered into Rancher [1]
5. Create a new "Group List" mapper and set the Group attribute name to "member" [2]
6. Create a User Property mapper "username" with Name, Property, Friendly Name, SAML Attribute Name "username" [1]
7. Navigate to Realm Settings / General, click "SMAL 2.0 Identity Provider Metadata" and copy the XML to the clipboard [2]
8. log out of Keycloak

**Rancher side**

1. Fill in the form for adding a Keycloak SAML Auth Provider as described in [1]
2. Submit the form.
3. Enter Keycloak admin credentials.

**Result**

In the popup various, like:
- "An error occurred logging in: Invalid saml attributes"
- An error occurred logging in: An error occurred logging in. Please try again.

In the Auth Provider form: "Access was not authorized"

Sometimes the auth provider turns out to be enabled anyway, only a little later.
Usually it does not. 

The method should really be documented all in one place (see #174), but also it should really work.

[1] from https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/blob/main/apps/keycloak/README.md
[2] from https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/how-to-guides/new-user-guides/authentication-permissions-and-global-configuration/authentication-config/configure-keycloak-saml

Keycloak version (installed via helm): 16.1.1
Rancher version (installed via helm): v2.8.3

title: Integration of Keycloak and Rancher UI is a manual process and very error-prone
content:
Problem description:
The documentation apps/keycloak/README.md is a bit problematic in several ways.

1. It is a manual process. In both, Keycloak and Rancher, complex configuration needs to be entered in the respective web UIs. If any mistake is made the process will not succeed, and no help is provided in tracking down the source of the problem. Hence: this process really needs some automation. 
2. The documentation is fragmented. There is a link to the Rancher documentation and some additional remarks underneath. This even increases the likeliness of errors. Even at the risk of doing additional copy-paste, at the least we should have one comprehensive step-by-step guide to the process.

[santhosh-7777]: @mbert is this issue open?

title: UI/UX Redesign Task – Resident Portal
content:
Problem description:
### Title
Redesign MOSIP Resident Portal for improved usability, accessibility, and inclusivity aligned with GenderMag & Sensemaking (SenseMag) principles

### Background & Context
The MOSIP Resident Portal is a self-service web application that enables residents to manage their identity (UIN/VID), update data, track requests, and access services.
It includes features such as:
- Dashboard with key services
- UIN services (history, VID management, secure ID, etc.)
- Data sharing and updates
- Notifications, profile, multilingual support
- While functionally rich, the current experience:
- Feels feature-heavy and workflow-fragmented
- Lacks intuitive navigation and interaction patterns
- Needs stronger accessibility and inclusivity alignment

### Objective
Redesign the Resident Portal to be:
- User-friendly and intuitive
- Accessible and inclusive (GenderMag & SenseMag compliant)
- Modern, interactive, and scalable
- Aligned with real user mental models and workflows

### Scope (Pages to Redesign)
The designer should redesign end-to-end experience, including:
1. Entry & Navigation
- Login / Authentication flows (OTP, biometrics, etc.)
- Consent screen
- Global navigation (menu, header, profile, language)

2. Dashboard
- Overview of key services
- Notifications & activity feed
- Personalization

3. UIN Services
- View History
- Manage VID
- Secure My ID
- Track Requests
- Get Personalized Card
- Share My Data
- Update My Data

4. Informational Services
- Registration Centers
- Supporting Documents

5. Utility Flows
- Get My UIN
- Verify Email/Phone
- Appointment Booking

6. Profile & Settings
- User profile
- Language preferences
- Accessibility settings

### Key Design Principles
1. Usability & Clarity
- Reduce cognitive load
- Clear task-based navigation (not system-based)
- Progressive disclosure for complex actions

2. GenderMag Alignment
Ensure design supports diverse cognitive styles:
- Support risk-averse users (clear confirmations, undo options)
- Provide step-by-step guidance
- Avoid over-reliance on exploration-based learning
- Use clear, non-technical language

3. Sensemaking (SenseMag) Alignment
- Help users understand:
  - Where they are
  - What they can do
  - What just happened
- Strong feedback loops
- Clear system status visibility

4. Accessibility (Critical)
- Color contrast, readable typography
- Keyboard navigation
- Screen reader compatibility
- Multi-language support (already supported but needs UX refinement)
- Align with MOSIP Design theme

5. Interaction & ExperienceMicro-interactions for feedback
- Guided workflows (especially for complex flows like data update)
- Visual hierarchy and prioritisation

### Expected Deliverables
- Design Artifacts
  - User flows (current vs improved)
  - Information architecture (IA)
  - Wireframes (low fidelity)
  - High-fidelity UI designs
  - Interactive prototypes (Figma preferred)
- UX Enhancements
  - Journey maps for key tasks:
  - Update data
  - Manage VID
  - Track request
  - Pain point identification + improvements
- Accessibility Deliverables
  - Accessibility checklist
  - Color palette with contrast validation
  - Typography scale
- Design System Alignment
  - Component library (buttons, cards, forms, alerts)
  - Reusable patterns for:
  - Forms
  - Status tracking
  - Notifications

### Acceptance Criteria
- Users can complete key tasks (e.g., update data, track request) in ≤ 3–5 steps
- Navigation is task-oriented, not feature-oriented
- All flows provide clear feedback and status visibility
- Demonstrates GenderMag alignment:
   - Clear instructions
   - Reduced ambiguity
   - Confidence-building UX
- Improved engagement and usability (qualitative testing)

### Non-Functional Requirements
- Responsive design (mobile + tablet + desktop)
- Performance-friendly UI (lightweight components)
- Scalable for future services
- Localization-ready

### Suggested Enhancements 
- Introduce “Guided Mode” for first-time users
- Add task-based dashboard (e.g., “What do you want to do?”)
- Use status trackers (progress bars for requests)
- Add contextual help/tooltips
- Introduce visual service cards instead of text-heavy lists

### References
- Existing Portal: https://resident.collab.mosip.net/#/dashboard
- MOSIP Documentation (features & flows)

title: Feature: Allow resident services to log in even when all the modalities are locked
content:
Problem description:
Add Support for allowing locked Authentication Types to Login to Resident Portal.

Problem statement: When Resident lock the all authentication types resident will not be able to unlock any Authentication Types back again as they are not allowed for login into resident portal itself. 

Solution:

If  resident is allowed to login to selected authentication types though it is locked for other partners, user will be able to login to resident portal and unlock any authentication types back. So this will happen on specific authentication types after user gives their consent by selecting the specific authentication types for excluding resident portal from the authentication lock validation.



Steps:

Authentication type locking with exclusion for resident portal login:



Authentication in IDA after the exclusion for resident partner:



Changes needed:

ID Repo:

Accept lockExcludedAuthPartners=["resident-partner"] for locked Auth Types in the Auth Type Lock API. 

Add a column in uin_auth_lock table called lockExcludedAuthPartners VarChar(256), nullable. Update in both db scripts and update/rollback scripts. 

Probagate lockExcludedAuthPartners=["resident-partner"] for locked Auth Types to IDA as part of websub event.

IDA:

Accept lockExcludedAuthPartners=["resident-partner"] for locked Auth Types in the websub event. 

Add a column in uin_auth_lock table called lockExcludedAuthPartners VarChar(256), nullable. Update in both db scripts and update/rollback scripts. 

During any Authentication, check if the Auth Type is having exclusion of the incoming partner ID.

Resident Service (endpoint- /resident/v1/auth-lock-unlock):

Send lockExcludedAuthPartners attribute to ID Repo for the lock excluded Auth Types, lockExcludedAuthPartners=["resident-partner"] . Here the resident-partner ID needs to come from the resident service configuration mosip-resident-service-partner-id. This needs to be configured as part of resident oidc client on boarding script. (It should be informed to the devops team to update the on boarding script to additionally set this property. ) 

The sets of Auth Types that can be Excluded as above in the UI should come from a Resident Service configuration. ( resident.auth-types-groups.exclusion-for-resident-login=["otp-email","otp-phone","bio-Finger", "bio-Iris", "bio-Face"]  ) . Note here demo is not in the exclusion set.  So no validation is performed on that. This property should be optional and if it is not there it should behave like earlier.

DevOps (onboarding script):

It should be informed to the devops team to update the on boarding script to additionally set the property as explained under Resident-service section.

Descoped: 

Resident UI: (Descoped)

Add Option on Lockable Auth Type for "Exclude for Resident Portal Login".

The sets of Auth Types that can be Excluded as above in the UI should come from a Resident Service configuration. ( resident.auth-types-groups.exclusion-for-resident-login=["otp-email","otp-phone","bio-Finger", "bio-Iris", "bio-Face"]  ) . Note here demo is not in the exclusion set.  So no validation is performed on that.

Whenever user locks an authentication type within an exclusion set, by default it can be marked for exclusion by the UI. But resident should be able to unselect which Auth types he/she doesn't to exclude in that set provided at least one of them is kept for the exclusion. 

Whenever any auth type is locked the option for excluding it for resident portal login should not be shown. 

Validate if All Auth Types locked in each exclusion set, atleast one Auth type is selected among them for "Exclude for Resident Portal Login".

On submission, send excludeLockForResidentLogin=true for the selected AuthTypes Locking selections. For unlocked Auth Types this flag should be set to null.

title: eSignet-Thunder: [BUG] Flow Execute — Individual ID endpoint fails with FES-1004 "Invalid flow execution ID" via Postman, though the same execution ID works correctly in the U
content:
Problem description:
## Description

While testing the `Flow Execute — Individual ID` endpoint against the eSignet Thunder collab environment for MOSIP ID (`https://esignet-thunder.esdev.mosip.net/v1/esignet`), the API call fails with error code `FES-1004 - Invalid flow execution ID provided in the request`, even though the exact same flow execution ID is valid and works as expected when the flow is run through the UI in the same collab environment.

This suggests the issue is not with the validity of the execution ID itself, but likely with how the request is being constructed/sent from Postman (e.g., missing/incorrect headers, session/cookie handling, encoding of the execution ID, or a mismatch in how the ID is passed as a path/query/body parameter) compared to how the UI sends the request internally.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Initiate a flow (e.g., login/auth flow) via the eSignet Thunder UI in the collab environment for MOSIP ID and note the flow execution ID generated.
2. Confirm the flow proceeds and completes as expected end-to-end via the UI using this execution ID.
3. Open Postman and call the `Flow Execute — Individual ID` endpoint against:
   `https://esignet-thunder.esdev.mosip.net/v1/esignet`
4. Pass the same flow execution ID (captured in step 1) in the request as required by the endpoint.
5. Send the request.
6. Observe the response returned.

## Expected Behavior

- The `Flow Execute — Individual ID` endpoint should accept the valid, active flow execution ID and process the request successfully (same as it does when triggered via the UI).
- The API response should return the expected flow execution result/status, not an "Invalid execution ID" error, since the ID is confirmed valid and working in the UI for the same environment.

## Actual Behavior

The API call fails with the following error:

```json
{
    "code": "FES-1004",
    "message": {
        "key": "error.flowexecservice.invalid_execution_id",
        "defaultValue": "Invalid request"
    },
    "description": {
        "key": "error.flowexecservice.invalid_execution_id_description",
        "defaultValue": "Invalid flow execution ID provided in the request"
    }
}
```

## Screenshot

*(Attach screenshot of the Postman request — headers, body/params, and response — alongside a screenshot of the successful UI flow using the same execution ID, for comparison)*

## Logs
*(Attach backend service logs from the flow execution service for the corresponding timeframe of the Postman call, including the request ID/trace ID if available, to help correlate the failure with the exact request received by the server. Also attach the Postman console/network log showing the exact request sent — headers, URL, and body — so it can be compared against the request captured from the UI network trace.)*


**Environment:**
- Environment: ES Dev / Collab (MOSIP ID)
- Endpoint: `https://esignet-thunder.esdev.mosip.net/v1/esignet`
- API: Flow Execute — Individual ID
- Client: Postman
- Comparison: Same execution ID works via UI in the same collab environment

**Additional Notes:**
- Since the same ID works in the UI but fails via Postman, this points to a likely difference in how the request is formed/sent (e.g., session cookies, auth headers, content-type, or ID encoding) rather than the execution ID being genuinely invalid or expired.

title: eSignet-Thunder:[TASK] Run FAPI Conformance Test Suite against eSignet (Go/Thunder) in ES Dev Environment
content:
Problem description:
## 1. Description

eSignet has been re-implemented in Go (Thunder) with support for FAPI-related features — PAR, DPoP, and Authorization Server Issuer Identifier. Before this implementation can be considered production-ready and FAPI-compliant, it needs to be validated using the official FAPI Conformance Test Suite.

This task involves setting up and running the FAPI Conformance Test Suite against the Go-based eSignet application deployed in the ES dev environment, using a mock Relying Party (RP) as the test client. The resulting conformance test reports must then be compared against the baseline conformance report previously generated for eSignet 1.8.1 (Java version), to confirm that the Go implementation achieves equivalent conformance results.

Any discrepancies or regressions identified between the two reports should be documented and raised as separate defects for follow-up.

## 2. Scope

- Configure the FAPI Conformance Test Suite to target the Go-based eSignet (Thunder) instance running in the ES dev environment.
- Set up and register a mock RP client compatible with the conformance suite's test plans (PAR, DPoP, Auth Server Issuer Identifier, and the applicable FAPI profile as implemented).
- Execute the relevant FAPI conformance test plans against the Go-based eSignet application.
- Capture and archive the full conformance test execution reports/logs.
- Compare the Go-based eSignet conformance results against the corresponding eSignet 1.8.1 (Java) conformance report, test case by test case.
- Document discrepancies, failures, or gaps between the two reports.
- Log defects/issues for any conformance failures specific to the Go implementation that do not match the Java baseline.
- Produce a summary comparison report indicating overall conformance parity status.

**Out of Scope:**
- Fixing/implementing any FAPI feature code (defects found will be raised as separate issues).
- Running the conformance suite against staging/UAT/production environments.
- Conformance testing of standard (non-FAPI) OIDC flows.
- Setting up a new instance of the FAPI Conformance Test Suite tool itself, if a shared instance already exists.
- Performance/load testing.
- Automating conformance suite execution into CI/CD pipelines.

## 3. Acceptance Criteria

- Given the ES dev environment is deployed with the Go-based eSignet application, When the FAPI Conformance Test Suite is configured against it, Then the suite shall be able to successfully discover and connect to the eSignet endpoints (authorization, PAR, token, userinfo, `.well-known` configuration).
- Given a mock RP client is registered in the dev environment, When the conformance suite initiates a test plan, Then the client shall be able to complete the authorization flow using PAR and DPoP as required by the selected FAPI test plan.
- Given the conformance test plan includes Auth Server Issuer Identifier validation, When the authorization response is returned, Then the `iss` parameter shall be validated successfully by the conformance suite.
- Given the full applicable FAPI test plan(s) are executed, When execution completes, Then a conformance test report shall be generated and saved for the Go-based eSignet application.
- Given the eSignet 1.8.1 (Java) conformance report is available, When compared with the Go-based eSignet report, Then the pass/fail status of each equivalent test case shall be documented side-by-side.
- Given any test case fails in the Go implementation but passed in the Java 1.8.1 baseline, When identified, Then it shall be logged as a defect/discrepancy with supporting evidence (logs, screenshots, test case ID).
- Given the comparison is complete, When the task is closed, Then a summary report shall be shared indicating overall conformance parity status (fully matching / partially matching with known gaps).

## 4. Definition of Done

- [ ] FAPI Conformance Test Suite successfully configured against Go-based eSignet in ES dev environment
- [ ] Mock RP client registered and validated for use with the conformance suite
- [ ] Applicable FAPI test plan(s) executed (PAR, DPoP, Auth Server Issuer Identifier)
- [ ] Conformance test report generated and archived for the Go-based eSignet application
- [ ] Side-by-side comparison completed against eSignet 1.8.1 (Java) baseline report
- [ ] Discrepancies/regressions identified and logged as separate defect tickets (if any)
- [ ] Summary comparison report documented and shared with stakeholders
- [ ] Documentation updated with steps to reproduce the conformance test run (for future re-runs)

title: eSignet-Thunder:[Feature] Add Consent Screen to eSignet OIDC UI Flow
content:
Problem description:

1. Problem Statement

Currently, the eSignet OIDC UI flow does not include a consent screen. Once a user authenticates, there is no intermediate step where the user can review and control which claims (essential and voluntary) are shared with the Relying Party (RP). This means users are not given explicit visibility or control over their personal data being shared, which is a core requirement of consent-driven identity sharing under OIDC.

A consent screen needs to be introduced post-authentication and pre-redirection, where the user can view the claims requested by the RP, understand which are mandatory vs. optional, selectively toggle voluntary claims, and explicitly approve or cancel the data-sharing action.

Purpose

  • To ensure informed user consent before any personal data (claims) is shared with a Relying Party, in line with privacy-by-design and OIDC consent principles.
  • To give users granular control over voluntary claims while ensuring mandatory (essential) claims required for the service are clearly communicated.
  • To provide a standard, reusable consent UI/UX across all RP integrations using eSignet.

Pre-Requisites

  • Backend API to fetch the list of claims requested by the RP (essential and voluntary), including claim metadata.
  • RP registration/configuration must include claim request definitions (essential vs. voluntary) accessible to the backend.
  • Client (RP) logo and eSignet logo assets/URLs available for rendering.
  • Session/timer configuration for the consent screen ({Timer}) must be available from config or backend.
  • RP homepage redirect URL must be available/configured for both "Allow" and "Discontinue" actions.

2. Goals

  • Display a consent screen after authentication, before redirecting to the RP.
  • Fetch and display the list of claims requested by the RP from the backend, categorized into Essential Claims and Voluntary Claims.
  • Provide an info icon next to each claims category heading with the specified tooltip/info messages.
  • Allow individual toggle (on/off) for each claim (essential and voluntary).
  • Provide a global toggle (on/off) for all voluntary claims collectively.
  • Provide "Allow" and "Cancel" action buttons.
  • On "Allow", redirect the user to the RP homepage with the consented claims.
  • On "Cancel", show a confirmation popup ("Do you wish to continue?") with "Stay" and "Discontinue" options.
  • On "Discontinue", redirect the user to the RP homepage to re-initiate login, displaying a "User have logged out" message.
  • Display page title as {Timer} reflecting the time remaining for the user to take action.
  • Display both Client (RP) logo and eSignet logo on the consent screen.
  • Display dynamic text: "{Client_name} is requesting access to the following:"
  • Display the disclosure message: "The information you consent to above will be shared with the {client_name} app or site."

3. Out of Scope

  • Backend logic/API implementation for computing or storing which claims are essential vs. voluntary (assumed to be provided via existing/related backend work).
  • Consent history/audit trail storage and management.
  • Consent revocation flow (post-consent, from a user profile/dashboard).
  • Localization/translation of consent screen text (unless explicitly required later).
  • RP-side handling of the claims/consent response.
  • Timer expiry behavior/session timeout handling logic (only UI display of {Timer} is in scope, not the countdown/session-expiry mechanism itself, unless already defined elsewhere).
  • Accessibility (WCAG) compliance audit — to be handled as a separate initiative unless specified.

4. Acceptance Criteria

  • Given a user has successfully authenticated, When the OIDC flow proceeds, Then the consent screen shall be displayed before redirection to the RP.
  • Given the consent screen is loaded, When the claims list is fetched from the backend, Then the claims shall be displayed under two distinct sections: "Essential Claims" and "Voluntary Claims".
  • Given the Essential Claims section is displayed, When the user views the info icon next to the heading, Then the tooltip shall display "Mandatory user information required by the service provider".
  • Given the Voluntary Claims section is displayed, When the user views the info icon next to the heading, Then the tooltip shall display "Additional User information that resident can choose to share with the service provider."
  • Given a list of claims is displayed, When the user views each claim, Then each claim (essential or voluntary) shall have an individual toggle to turn it on or off.
  • Given the Voluntary Claims section is displayed, When the user interacts with the global toggle, Then all voluntary claims shall be turned on or off collectively.
  • Given the user has reviewed the claims, When the user clicks "Allow", Then the user shall be redirected to the RP homepage with the consented claims shared.
  • Given the user wants to cancel, When the user clicks "Cancel", Then a popup shall be displayed with the message "Do you wish to continue?" along with "Stay" and "Discontinue" buttons.
  • Given the cancel confirmation popup is displayed, When the user clicks "Stay", Then the popup shall close and the user shall remain on the consent screen with prior selections intact.
  • Given the cancel confirmation popup is displayed, When the user clicks "Discontinue", Then the user shall be redirected to the RP homepage to re-initiate login, and a "User have logged out" message shall be displayed at the top.
  • Given the consent screen is displayed, When the page loads, Then the page title shall show the {Timer} value.
  • Given the consent screen is displayed, When the page loads, Then both the Client (RP) logo and the eSignet logo shall be visible.
  • Given the consent screen is displayed, When the page loads, Then the text "{Client_name} is requesting access to the following:" shall be shown, with {Client_name} dynamically populated.
  • Given the consent screen is displayed, When the page loads, Then the disclosure message "The information you consent to above will be shared with the {client_name} app or site." shall be shown.

Business Rules

  • Given a claim is marked as Essential, When the consent screen is rendered, Then its individual toggle shall be enabled by default and should not be allowed to be turned off (mandatory), or if toggle is shown, attempting to turn it off shall not permit proceeding with "Allow" (behavior to be confirmed with design).
  • Given a claim is marked as Voluntary, When the consent screen is rendered, Then its individual toggle shall be available for the user to turn on or off independently.
  • Given the global voluntary toggle is turned off, When any individual voluntary claim was previously on, Then all voluntary claims shall be turned off and reflected in the UI state.
  • Given the global voluntary toggle is turned on, When previously all voluntary claims were off, Then all voluntary claims shall be turned on and reflected in the UI state.
  • Given a user toggles an individual voluntary claim off while others remain on, When not all voluntary claims are on, Then the global toggle shall reflect an indeterminate/off state (exact visual behavior to be confirmed with design).

Exceptions & Error Handling

  • Given the backend API to fetch claims fails or times out, When the consent screen attempts to load, Then an appropriate error message shall be displayed to the user instead of a blank/broken screen.
  • Given no essential or voluntary claims are returned by the backend, When the consent screen loads, Then the corresponding section shall be hidden or shall display an appropriate empty state (behavior to be confirmed with design).
  • Given the RP homepage redirect URL is unavailable or invalid, When the user clicks "Allow" or "Discontinue", Then an appropriate error/fallback behavior shall be triggered instead of a broken redirect.
  • Given the session/timer expires while the user is on the consent screen, When the timer reaches zero, Then the expected system behavior (e.g., auto-cancel, session expiry message) shall be triggered (exact behavior to be confirmed — currently only UI display of {Timer} is defined).

Basic Flow

  1. User completes authentication in the OIDC flow.
  2. System fetches the list of requested claims (essential and voluntary) from the backend.
  3. Consent screen is displayed with:
    • Page title showing {Timer}
    • Client logo and eSignet logo
    • "{Client_name} is requesting access to the following:" heading
    • Essential Claims section (with info icon and individual toggles)
    • Voluntary Claims section (with info icon, global toggle, and individual toggles)
    • Disclosure message about data sharing
    • "Allow" and "Cancel" buttons
  4. User reviews and optionally adjusts voluntary claim toggles.
  5. User clicks "Allow" → redirected to RP homepage with consented claims. OR
  6. User clicks "Cancel" → confirmation popup shown.
    • User clicks "Stay" → returns to consent screen.
    • User clicks "Discontinue" → redirected to RP homepage to re-initiate login, with "User have logged out" message shown.

Scenarios

  • User consents to all requested claims (essential + all voluntary) and proceeds.
  • User consents to essential claims only and deselects all voluntary claims (individually or via global toggle) before proceeding.
  • User partially consents to some voluntary claims and proceeds.
  • User cancels the consent flow and chooses to "Stay" — returns to the same screen.
  • User cancels the consent flow and chooses to "Discontinue" — logged out and redirected to RP homepage.

Data Fields

Field Name | Data Type (String/Text/Number/Boolean/Date/DateTime/Enum/List) | Data Length | Mandatory/Optional | Field Validations | Error Messages -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- Page Title ({Timer}) | String | - | Mandatory | Must display remaining time | - Client Logo | Image | - | Mandatory | Valid image URL | Fallback/default logo if unavailable eSignet Logo | Image | - | Mandatory | Valid image URL | - Client Name Heading | String | - | Mandatory | Dynamically populated from RP config | - Essential Claims List | List | - | Mandatory | Fetched from backend; non-empty expected | Error message if fetch fails Essential Claim Toggle | Boolean | - | Mandatory | Default ON; may be non-editable | - Voluntary Claims List | List | - | Optional | Fetched from backend | - Voluntary Claim Toggle (individual) | Boolean | - | Optional | Default state per config | - Voluntary Claims Global Toggle | Boolean | - | Optional | Reflects aggregate state of individual toggles | - Info Icon (Essential) | Tooltip/Text | - | Mandatory | Static text: "Mandatory user information required by the service provider" | - Info Icon (Voluntary) | Tooltip/Text | - | Mandatory | Static text: "Additional User information that resident can choose to share with the service provider." | - Allow Button | Button | - | Mandatory | Always enabled | - Cancel Button | Button | - | Mandatory | Always enabled | - Cancel Confirmation Popup | Modal | - | Mandatory | Triggered on Cancel click | Message: "Do you wish to continue?" Stay Button | Button | - | Mandatory | Always enabled | - Discontinue Button | Button | - | Mandatory | Always enabled | - Logout Message | String | - | Mandatory | Displayed after Discontinue | "User have logged out"

Non-Functional Requirements

  • The consent screen must be responsive and render correctly across supported browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) and screen sizes (desktop/mobile), consistent with existing eSignet UI standards.
  • The consent screen must integrate seamlessly with the existing OIDC authentication flow without breaking backward compatibility for RPs not yet configured for consent (if applicable).
  • API calls to fetch claims must follow existing eSignet API performance/latency standards.
  • UI must be consistent with existing eSignet design system/branding guidelines.

Definition of Done

  • [ ] Code implemented
  • [ ] Unit tests added
  • [ ] Integration tests added (if applicable)
  • [ ] Existing tests passing
  • [ ] Documentation updated
  • [ ] Acceptance criteria validated

Documentation
