content: Problem description: ### Short Summary of the Bug User unable to authenticate using "Login with Biometrics" in mosipid-qabase plugin ### Description ### **Steps:** 1. Launch mosipid-qabase. 2. Navigate to Login with Bio. 3. Run the mock-mds. 4. Observe the issue. ### **Actual Result:** When the user attempts to authenticate using "Login with Biometrics", the system throws an error: "Auth Capture Failed because Capture Timeout has happened" and authentication does not proceed. ### **Expected Result:** User should be able to successfully authenticate using biometric login without timeout errors, and the system should complete the authentication flow. ### Attachments / Evidence / Links Discussion and resolution: [JanardhanBS-SyncByte]: [[MOSIP-43540] added required TLS version and cipher configurations](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/commit/b8c96645664f1e0bc8270b44e40b206cb1df2478) we started facing issue on mockmds for Auth because we where using 2.7.5 now changed to 4.12.0 which supports Tls1.3 with all cipher [MOSIP-43540]: https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/MOSIP-43540?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [prathmeshj12]: @zesu22 @rachik-hue While performing the MOSIP ID QA Base login for BIO authentication, I am encountering the error shown below. Is there any specific configuration that needs to be updated to resolve this issue? The same problem is not occurring in the mock environment. [SajidMannikeri17]: Biometric login fails with IDA-MLC-024 because the signed biometric carries domainUri: "null" instead of the real domain, so it doesn't match the request domainUri. On the /capture exchange with the mock-MDS, the request sends the correct domainUri but the signed response comes back with "null" — so the mock-MDS drops it. eSignet and IDA are both behaving correctly (IDA never flagged the request-side domainUri), and it reproduces identically on qabase and esdev against the same IDA. Root cause is the mock-MDS (v1.3.0-SNAPSHOT) not writing the real domainUri into the signed biometric; fix is a mock-MDS build that stamps it correctly. For the previous version, mock-MDS v1.2.1-SNAPSHOT, domainUri is coming in response as expected. **Decoded payload of /capture response v1.3.1-SNAPSHOT**: `{ "deviceCode": "b692b595-3523-slap-99fc-bd76e35f290f", "deviceServiceVersion": "0.9.5", "bioType": "Finger", "bioSubType": "UNKNOWN", "purpose": "Auth", "env": "Staging", "domainUri": "null" }` **Decoded payload of /capture response v1.2.1-SNAPSHOT**: `{ "deviceCode": "b692b595-3523-slap-99fc-bd76e35f290f", "deviceServiceVersion": "0.9.5", "bioType": "Finger", "bioSubType": "UNKNOWN", "purpose": "Auth", "env": "Staging", "domainUri": "https://esignet-qabase.esqa2.mosip.net" }`

title: Generic error message displayed for expired OTP instead of descriptive message
content: Problem description: ### Short Summary of the Bug Generic error message displayed for expired OTP instead of descriptive message ### Description ### **Steps:** 1. Launch mosipid-cre. 2. Navigate to enter mobile number. 3. Wait for OTP to expire. 4. Enter OTP after the expiry and observe the error message. ### **Actual Result:** When a user enters an expired OTP, the system displays a generic error message: “OTP authentication failed. Please try again.” ### **Expected Result:** When an expired OTP is entered, the system should display a specific and descriptive error message (e.g., “OTP has expired. Please request a new OTP.” to clearly inform the user of the issue. ### Attachments / Evidence / Links Discussion and resolution: [gk-XL7]: @rachik-hue this error occurs when verify-otp throw auth_failed error code. Please add your inputs for error message. [SajidMannikeri17]: This is not a UI bug. Proper error code should be propagated to UI which already handles the OTP expiry message. This is working as expected in esignet-qabase. Attaching screenshot in the next comment. 1. esignet-cre: IDA does detect the expiry correctly and raises IDA-OTA-003 ("OTP has expired") internally, but this is thrown as a business exception deep in the OTP matching logic rather than being returned as a normal authentication error. It is then wrapped into UNABLE_TO_PROCESS and ultimately surfaces to eSignet as a body-less HTTP 500, with no IDA error code in the response. The eSignet plugin only extracts error codes from a 2xx response, so on receiving a 500 it falls back to the generic auth_failed, which the UI renders as "OTP authentication failed. Please try again." This confirms the issue is not on the eSignet/oidc-ui side but on the IDA side, which should return IDA-OTA-003 in a proper error response instead of failing with a 500. **id-auth version in released env**: mosipid/authentication-service:1.3.0 [SajidMannikeri17]: esignet-qabase: Here it is working as expected becasue IDA returns proper error code IDA-OTA-003 which corresponds to "OTP expired. Please request a new one and try again." **id-auth version in qa11new env**: mosipint/authentication-service:1.2.2.x [SajidMannikeri17]: In the mock: OTP expiry is handled via a cache with a fixed validity (600s). The OTP transaction hash is stored on send-otp, and on kyc-auth the mock first checks whether that cache entry still exists. If the validity window has passed, the entry is gone, so the mock returns a normal HTTP 200 response with the error code invalid_transaction as the error code. It does not send a dedicated "OTP expired" message because the mock has no OTP-specific expiry code: once the cache entry lapses it cannot tell "expired" apart from "OTP never requested", so both map to the generic invalid_transaction. [rachik-hue]: As per discussion with @SajidMannikeri17 this is specific issue for the CRE env. So it has to be fixed in the IDA 1.3.0 release. @vadherhemant please prirotize this with @Varaniya

title: Inconsistent error message for invalid mobile number between mock, mosipid-qabase & mosipid-cre
content: Problem description: ### Short Summary of the Bug Inconsistent error message for invalid mobile number between Mock and MOSIP ID ### Description ### **Steps:** 1. Launch mock, mosipid-qabase & mosipid-cre 2. Navigate to enter mobile number. 3. Enter unregistered mobile number. ### **Actual Result:** When an invalid mobile number is entered, the error message differs between the mock, mosipid-qabase & mosipid-cre, leading to inconsistent user experience. ### **Expected Result:** For an invalid mobile number, the error message should be consistent across the mock, mosipid-qabase & mosipid-cre. ### Attachments / Evidence / Links Discussion and resolution: [KashiwalHarsh]: The primary reason for the error to be different is because the mock implementation is different from the mosip implemention For MOCK Implementation `throw new SendOtpException(responseWrapper.getErrors().get(0).getErrorCode());` which is SendOtpException with parameter, propogating to the UI ``` "errors": [{ "errorCode": "invalid_individual_id", "errorMessage": "invalid_individual_id" }] ``` which is ideal error code for mock implementation For MOSIP implementation When an invalid mobile number is submitted to the /send-otp endpoint, eSignet-CRE and eSignet-QABASE return different error codes to the UI. Ideally, both should return the same MOSIP business error code IDA-MLC-009, because the underlying validation failure is identical. for eSignet-CRE we are getting ``` "errors": [{ "errorCode": "send_otp_failed", "errorMessage": "send_otp_failed" }] ``` for eSignet-QABASE we are getting ``` "errors": [{ "errorCode": "IDA-MLC-009", "errorMessage": "IDA-MLC-009" }] ``` the error message we are seeing in eSignet-QABASE is correct as per the implementation. working on deep analysis of this difference [KashiwalHarsh]: Why CRE and QABASE error code are different while they shouldn't QABASE connects with `http://api-internal.qa11new.mosip.net` which return a 200 reponse with **IDA-MLC-009** error code which then returns it back to the UI - correct behavior CRE connects with `https://api-internal.released.mosip.net` which returns a 500 Internal Server Error which then returns send_otp_failed code, Now **send_otp_failed code is not the primary failure. It is a fallback that eSignet returns when it cannot extract the real IDA error code from a broken IDA response.** This critical difference is what happens during response signing : (Summary from the logs) : complete log file attached Provided JSON Data to sign is invalid Provided Data to sign is invalid JSON Throws KER-JWS-103 --> Data to sign is not valid JSON IDA returns HTTP 500 the error response body is apparently not valid JSON (KER-JWS-103), causing the signing step to throw, which propagates as an unhandled 500 from the servlet container and hence different error codes in UI, causing UI to render different errror messages [ida-otp-released-logs.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29594352/ida-otp-released-logs.txt) [ida-otp-qa11new-logs.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29594351/ida-otp-qa11new-logs.txt)

title: Consent defaults to “DISAGREE” from UI when not provided in UI spec or ID schema due to backend validation
content: Problem description: ### Short Summary of the Bug Consent defaults to “DISAGREE” from UI when not provided in UI spec or ID schema ### Description **Pre-requisite:** 1. Do not provide consent field in ui-spec & id-spec. **Steps:** 1. Launch https://signup.esqa2.mosip.net 2. Navigate to Register user. 3. Observe the issue. **Actual Result:** When consent is not defined in the UI spec or ID schema, the UI automatically sends the consent value as “DISAGREE.” This occurs because backend validation enforces a default value. **Expected Result:** When consent is not specified in the UI spec or ID schema, the UI should not automatically assign or send a “DISAGREE” value. Instead, it should either leave the field unset/null or prompt for explicit user input without backend-forced defaults. ### Attachments / Evidence / Links Discussion and resolution: [zesu22]: @prathmeshj12 After reviewing the RegisterRequest DTO, it is clear that consent and password are required fields in the validation process. As a result, these properties are obligatory in both the UISpec and IDSchema and must not be omitted from the registration flow. Then this bug will become an invalid one. [prathmeshj12]: @zesu22 @rachik-hue Can we perform this validation before the signup form is submitted? This would provide immediate feedback to users and make the issue easier to understand. Otherwise, users may need to return to the signup page and re-enter all the details again, which can impact the user experience. [zesu22]: @prathmeshj12 The consent field is mandatory in the ui-spec. Users must provide their consent to proceed with the signup process. The current issue is happening because this field is missing from your ui-spec. Please ensure it is included, as it is a required property. [rachik-hue]: As discussed with @prathmeshj12 and @gk-XL7 there should be a clear documentation for the developer to configure the consent and the password in the UI spec as they are mandatory. Alternative way is to remove the backend validations for these 2 attributes. My suggestion is to have a note added in the documentation for now. cc @anushasunkada @zesu22

title: ES-2943: FAPI 2.0 Conformance Failure – PKCE Not Enforced in PAR Authorization Request in fapi2-security-profile-final-par-ensure-pkce-required
content: Problem description: ## *Description:* While executing the *FAPI 2.0 Security Profile Final Authorization Server Test* with the test plan `fapi2-security-profile-final-par-ensure-pkce-required`, the authorization endpoint validation fails. This test verifies that *PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange)* is *mandatory when using the Authorization Code flow with PAR*. title: ES-2868: eSignet Signup – Invalid minAge and maxAge Negative Values Not Properly Handled
content:
Problem description:
## *Description:*

When the date field is configured with invalid negative values (`minAge = -1`, `maxAge = -5`), the system does not treat the configuration as invalid.

Instead, the UI behaves as if `minAge = 1` and `maxAge = 5`, indicating incorrect interpretation or normalization of negative values.

## *Steps to Reproduce:*

1. Launch *eSignet-Signup*.

1. Navigate to enter *mobile number*.

1. Enter OTP and validate the generated challenge.

1. Navigate to the *Signup form*.

1. Configure date field with `minAge = -1` and `maxAge = -5`.

1. Attempt to select any date.

## *Actual Result:*

- UI behaves as if `minAge = 1` and `maxAge = 5`.

- Negative values are implicitly converted instead of being rejected.

## *Expected Result:*

- Configuration should be treated as invalid.

- System should:
** Throw schema validation error, *or*
** Ignore invalid configuration and apply safe default.

- UI should not silently convert negative values.

title: ES-2852: esignet do not support jwt request parameter in authorize endpoint
content: Problem description: As per the test : oidcc-unsigned-request-object-supported-correctly-or-rejected-as-unsupported : This test sends a unsigned request object (by value) to the authorization endpoint. The server must either accept the request and process the authentication correctly, or return a request_not_supported error as per OIDCC-3.1.2.6. [[https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#JWTRequests](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#JWTRequests|smart-link)](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#JWTRequests](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#JWTRequests|smart-link)) *eSignet do not support the above feature. Error needs to be thrown when RP tries to use this feature.* *If there is* `request` *field in authorize call eSignet must return* `request_not_supported` *error.* *If there is* `request_uri` *field in authorize call eSignet must return* `request_uri_not_supported` *error*. ->State was passed in request, but is missing from response (or returned in the wrong place)(CheckStateInAuthorizationResponse) actual : expected : *B0TaIUVL81* *_state must be present in url query parameter_* → Nonce values mismatch(ValidateIdTokenNonce) actual : null expected : *NHepR4Bb02* ## 🔗 Linked Issues ### ISSUE - **ES-2808** Status: Closed - **ES-2930** Status: Canceled - **ES-2972** Status: PR Raised ## 📎 Attachments - [image (4).png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2852) - [image (7).png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2852) - [request_not_supported2.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2852) Discussion and resolution: [Ivanmeneges]: Harsh Kashiwal commented: !image (4).png|width=709,alt="image (4).png"! [exalate-issue-sync[bot]]: Harsh Kashiwal commented: For this ticket, the client's {{encPrivateKey}} must also be configured in the mock-rp-service secrets to enable JWE decoding. title: ES-2899: eSignet-MOSIP & MOCK: UserInfo endpoint returns generic 401 instead of proper error when encPublicKey is not configured for client
content: Problem description: ## *Prerequisite:* 1. Set the lobal OpenID Profile is Set to FAPI 2.0 in eSignet deployment. 1. Set the profile feature as nidsp. ## *Steps to Reproduce:* 1. Launch the postman collection for eSignet. 1. Perform all the E2E flow in eSignet. 1. Navigate to userinfo response endpoint. ## Actual Result: When the client encryption public key (`encPublicKey`) is not configured, the UserInfo endpoint fails with a generic 401 Unauthorized response without providing a meaningful error message. ![image-20260225-022619.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2899) ## Expected Result: Error message should clearly indicate that client encryption public key is missing. ## 🔗 Linked Issues ### ISSUE - **ES-2712** Status: In Progress - **ES-2954** Status: Testing ## 📎 Attachments - [image-20260225-022619.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2899) Discussion and resolution: [Ivanmeneges]: Rachik Sharma commented: This tickets were not actively worked as team was focusing on the LSH for eSignet 1.8.0. Hence moving the ticket to the next sprint. [anushasunkada]: This is a standard OIDC userinfo endpoint, so that endpoint error response should be as per https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#UserInfoError In case of failure due any issue in the access token - should return error as "invalid_token" with 401 HTTP status code. In case of encryption key not found, but the request is to give out userinfo response as JWE - should return error as "invalid_request" with 400 HTTP status code. In case of failure due to internal exceptions - should return error as "internal_error" with 500 HTTP status code. [KashiwalHarsh]: Scenario - "userinfo_response_type": "JWE", and encPublicKey is not provided, this should cause exception - invalid_pubic_key which as per the rfc spec should map to 400 invalid_request error code PR : https://github.com/mosip/esignet/pull/1955

title: ES-2924: OIDC Conformance Failure – invalid_id_token_hint Error During Second Browser Interaction
content: Problem description: ## *Test Suite:* OpenID Connect Core: Comprehensive Authorization server test (not part of certification program)*Test Plan:* oidcc-id-token-hint ## *Description:* While executing the *OIDC conformance test plan* `oidcc-id-token-hint`, the *second browser interaction fails with the error* `invalid_id_token_hint`. According to the OpenID Connect specification, when a valid `id_token_hint` is passed in the authorization request, the authorization server should *use it as a hint about the user’s existing session and continue the authentication flow*. However, during the *second browser interaction*, the authorization server rejects the request and returns the error `invalid_id_token_hint`, causing the conformance test to fail. ## *Steps to Reproduce:* 1. Launch the *OIDC Conformance Test Suite*. 1. Select the test plan `oidcc-id-token-hint`. 1. Start the test execution. 1. Complete the *first browser interaction* successfully. 1. Proceed to the *second browser interaction*. 1. Observe the response from the authorization endpoint. ## *Actual Result:* - The authorization server returns the error: ``` { "error": "invalid_id_token_hint" } ``` - The second browser interaction fails and the *OIDC conformance test case does not proceed further*. ## *Expected Result:* - The authorization server should *accept the provided* `id_token_hint`. - The authentication flow should *continue successfully without returning an error*. - The second browser interaction should *complete successfully*. Blocked by ES-2962 [exalate-issue-sync[bot]]: Harsh Kashiwal commented: I was able to reproduce this bug on sending the 2nd browser interaction to /oauth-detail with idTokenHint in the request body {code:json}"errors": [ { "errorCode": "invalid_id_token_hint", "errorMessage": "invalid_id_token_hint" } ]{code} this occurs when v3 request calls the {{handleIdTokenHint}} method which calls {{validateAndGetSubjectAndNonce}}in AuthorizationHelperService. exact exception is {{Failed to parse the given IDTokenHint as JWT}} at : {noformat}protected Pair validateAndGetSubjectAndNonce(String clientId, String idTokenHint) { try { String[] jwtParts = idTokenHint.split("\\."); if (jwtParts.length == 3) { String payloadString = new String(Base64.getDecoder().decode(jwtParts[1])); JsonNode payload = objectMapper.readTree(payloadString); String audience = payload.get(TokenService.AUD).textValue(); if(!signupIDTokenAudience.equals(audience) || !signupIDTokenAudience.equals(clientId)) throw new EsignetException(ErrorConstants.INVALID_ID_TOKEN_HINT); return Pair.of(payload.get(TokenService.SUB).textValue(), payload.get(TokenService.NONCE).textValue()); } } catch (Exception e) { log.error("Failed to parse the given IDTokenHint as JWT", e); } throw new EsignetException(ErrorConstants.INVALID_ID_TOKEN_HINT); }{noformat} validateAndGetSubjectAndNonce method is designed only for the signup client? because after signup redirect the idTokenHint is sent for signup client !image-20260512-115434.png|width=606,alt="image-20260512-115434.png"! conformance is sending it to the esignet client !image-20260512-122415.png|width=601,alt="image-20260512-122415.png"! title: ES-2931: OIDC Conformance Failure – JWKS Key Rotation Not Detected in oidcc-server-rotate-keys
content: Problem description: ## *Description:* While executing the *OIDC conformance test plan* `oidcc-server-rotate-keys`, the test fails during the *JWKS key rotation verification* step The conformance suite expects the authorization server to expose a *new signing key in the JWKS endpoint* after key rotation. However, the test did not detect any new key with the intended signing usage. ## *Steps to Reproduce:* 1. Launch the *OIDC Conformance Test Suite*. 1. Select the test plan `oidcc-server-rotate-keys`. 1. Execute the test flow. 1. Allow the test suite to trigger *JWKS key rotation verification*. 1. Observe the test results. ## *Actual Result:* The test suite fails with the following error: ```VerifyNewJwksHasNewSigningKey: No new keys with 'use':'sig' (or no 'use') found ``` ## *Expected Result:* - The *JWKS endpoint* should return an updated key set containing a *new signing key*. - The new key should include: ``` { "use": "sig" } ``` [image-20260309-065922.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2931) [image-20260309-070009.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2931) ## 🔗 Linked Issues ### ISSUE - **ES-2872** Status: New ## 📎 Attachments - [image (8).png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2931) - [image-20260309-065922.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2931) - [image-20260309-070009.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2931) Discussion and resolution: [Ivanmeneges]: Rachik Sharma commented: Key rotation is supported in eSignet and the rotation only happens only once the key is expired. This is not to be prirotized for now. We will have to check if we can find a way to trigger the rotation of the OIDC_SERVICE key. [~accountid:712020:4612a2b8-e962-4b34-a6cb-c083a836cbb3] [~accountid:557058:c955df2b-1615-45f5-8565-cbf63d54c49e] [~accountid:5c18fe9f16ac1e4f7cbb5d3a] . Also there is already a task for this, [https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2872|https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2872|smart-link] [Ivanmeneges]: Harsh Kashiwal commented: On manually triggering the key rotation the test passed !image (8).png|width=632,alt="image (8).png"! [KashiwalHarsh]: Original issue - https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2931 Key rotation is supported in eSignet and the rotation only happens only once the key is expired. To manually rotate the keys we have to change the expiry date to today's date in key alias table and restart esignet service to trigger the rotation On manually triggering the key rotation the test passed

title: ES-2954: eSignet-MOSIP & MOCK: fetchUserInfo Fails When encPublicKey is Configured and UserInfo Response is Set to JWE
content:
Problem description:
### Prerequisite:

1. Provide `"userinfo_response_type": "JWE"`

1. Add `"enc_public_key"`

[image-20260317-071703.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2954)

### *Steps:*

1. Launch https://healthservices.esqa.mosip.net/

1. Navigate to Login with OTP.

1. Perform L2 flow.

1. Navigate to fetchuserinfo and observe the issue

### *Actual Result:*

When the client configuration includes `encPublicKey` and the additional configuration specifies the UserInfo response format as JWE, the `fetchUserInfo` call fails with error "Failed to get the User Info." and status code is 500.

[image-20260317-071315.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2954)

*_NOTE: From Postman collections, userinfo response is getting encrypted._*

![image-20260317-064237.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2954)

### *Expected Result:*

When `encPublicKey` is configured and the UserInfo response type is JWE, `fetchUserInfo` should successfully return the UserInfo response in encrypted (JWE) format without failure.

[~accountid:5c18fe9f16ac1e4f7cbb5d3a] [~accountid:712020:4612a2b8-e962-4b34-a6cb-c083a836cbb3]

[Ivanmeneges]: Rachik Sharma commented: This tickets were not actively worked as team was focusing on the LSH for eSignet 1.8.0. Hence moving the ticket to the next sprint.

[exalate-issue-sync[bot]]: Harsh Kashiwal commented: For this ticket, the client's {{encPrivateKey}} must also be configured in the mock-rp-service secrets to enable JWE decoding.

When {{userinfo_response_type: JWE}} is added only to the *additional configuration* of the eSignet client — with {{encPublicKey}} and {{encPrivateKey}} configured in the deployment, {{fetchUserInfo}} works correctly.

This bug is not reproduced in the esdev environment as an encPrivateKey was not configured in mock-rp-serivce deployment config during the testing of this bug

CC: [~accountid:712020:c6ee5f54-fc2c-4d62-986e-97ddd067ffd0] [~accountid:5db271f47971ec0db25b80a8]

[prathmeshj12]: Issue Verification and Resolution
Verified the issue at esqa2 env. After adding the encPrivateKey in mock-rp portal, the user can correctly use the configured client encryption key for JWE encryption and successfully return the User Info response.

warning Impact of server_profile Update
When the server_profile is updated with enc, it overrides the userinfo configuration for all clients, forcing them to use JWE as the userinfo_response_type. This includes the signup client, which does not support JWE or encPublicKey

check mark button Current Fix Status
The issue is fixed for clients with the JWE userinforesponse in additionalconfig.

For more info please refer - https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2954

title: ES-2842: PAR client assertion is getting rejected if 'nbf' is 8 seconds in the future
content:
Problem description:
## 🔗 Linked Issues

### ISSUE
- **ES-2805**
  Status: Closed

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: Nandhukumar commented: [~accountid:712020:118c1f58-9ebe-44fa-8fe4-8562d85d4a24] Can you please add a description on what is actual behaviour and what is the expected behaviour?

[Ivanmeneges]: Sachin Rana commented: [~accountid:62b3fef5673f2103622f1692] The title is self explanatory. There is nbf claim is client assertion. It should be valid within certain limit (leeway) which is configurable already in eSignet. The configuration is not working for nbf field and a future value within limit is failing.

[Ivanmeneges]: Nandhukumar commented: Hi [~accountid:557058:c955df2b-1615-45f5-8565-cbf63d54c49e] [~accountid:712020:118c1f58-9ebe-44fa-8fe4-8562d85d4a24] 

Currently {{mosip.esignet.client-assertion-jwt.leeway-seconds}} is set to 5 seconds.

Since we are using {{JwtTimestampValidator(Duration.ofSeconds(maxClockSkew))}}, the {{nbf}} claim will be valid only if it is within current time + 5 seconds.

So if {{nbf = current time + 8 seconds}}, it gets rejected because it exceeds the configured leeway. This seems correct as per the current configuration.

Do we need to allow a higher tolerance for the leeway value?

title: ES-2712: eSignet - Add Default FAPI 2.0 Configuration in eSignet
content:
Problem description:
## *Purpose*

As a developer, want to add a global FAPI 2.0 toggle in eSignet default properties so that deployments can enable FAPI 2.0/nisp profile behaviour (PAR, DPoP and PKCE enabled flows) for eSignet transactions.

## *Basic Flow (System Behavior / User Journey)*

1. On application startup, eSignet reads the global OpenID profile value from
`mosip.esignet.server.profile` in `application_default.properties`.

1. The configured profile determines the *default standards behavior* for the deployment:
#* *fapi2.0* → PAR, DPoP, PKCE enabled
#* *nisdsp* → PAR, DPoP, JWE, PKCE enabled
#* *none* → No enforced defaults; behavior is driven by client-level configuration

1. eSignet loads the *profile-to-feature mapping* from a static database table that defines which features (PAR, DPoP, JWE, PKCE) are enabled for each profile.

1. When an OIDC client is created or updated:
#* If the global profile is set to `none`, the relying party may explicitly configure PAR, DPoP, PKCE (and JWE where applicable) via the client management API.
#* If the global profile is `fapi2.0` *or* `nisp`, any client-level flags provided are *ignored and overridden* by the selected profile’s enforced feature set.

1. During transaction initiation and runtime execution:
#* eSignet resolves the *effective configuration* for the transaction based on the selected global profile.
#* Authentication and authorization flows enforce PAR, DPoP, JWE, and PKCE strictly according to the active profile.
#* Client-specific overrides are applied *only when the profile is* `none`.

## *Business Rules*

1. A single global configuration property, `mosip.esignet.server.profile`, controls the OpenID/FAPI behavior for the entire eSignet deployment.

1. Supported values for `mosip.esignet.server.profile` are:
#* `fapi2.0`
#* `nisdsp`
#* `none`

1. Profile-to-feature mappings are centrally defined in a static database table and must not be hardcoded.

1. When the profile is set to `fapi2.0` *or* `nisdsp`:
#* PAR, DPoP, PKCE (and JWE for nisp) are *mandatory and enforced*
#* Client-level configuration flags are *not applicable and must be overridden*

1. When the profile is set to `none`:
#* No standards behavior is enforced by default
#* Client-level flags provided during OIDC client creation/update determine runtime behavior

1. Validation rules must ensure:
#* Clients cannot weaken or bypass profile-enforced requirements
#* AS-required profile constraints are validated during client creation and update

1. Existing clients must retain backward compatibility:
#* Clients created before this change continue to function
#* Their effective behavior depends on the selected global profile, unless profile = `none`

1. Runtime behavior must always be derived from the *resolved effective configuration*, not from raw client input.

## *Acceptance Criteria*

### Global Profile Configuration

*AC1:* A new property `mosip.esignet.server.profile` is added to `application_default.properties`.

*AC2:* The property supports only the values `fapi2.0`, `nisdsp`, and `none`.

*AC3:* eSignet loads profile-to-feature mappings from a static database table at startup.

### Client Creation & Update

*AC4:* When the global profile is `none`, client management APIs accept and persist PAR, DPoP, PKCE (and JWE if applicable) flags.

*AC5:* When the global profile is `fapi2.0` or `nisdsp`, client-provided flags are ignored and overridden by profile-defined behavior.

*AC6:* Client creation and update requests are validated against AS-required profile constraints.

*AC7:* PKCE support is explicitly added to client create and update APIs under additional configuration.

### Runtime Enforcement

*AC8:* During transaction initiation, eSignet resolves the effective feature set based on the selected profile.

*AC9:* When `fapi2.0` is active, PAR, DPoP, and PKCE are enforced for all relevant flows.

*AC10:* When `nisdsp` is active, PAR, DPoP, JWE, and PKCE are enforced for all relevant flows.

*AC11:* When `none` is active, enforcement depends solely on client-level configuration.

### Backward Compatibility & Validation

*AC12:* Existing clients continue to function without migration failures.

*AC13:* No client can bypass profile-enforced requirements at runtime.

## *Technical Changes Required*

### Configuration

- Add `mosip.esignet.server.profile` to `application_default.properties`

- Document valid values and default behavior

### Database

- Create a static table in the eSignet DB to store:
** Profile name
** Supported/enforced features (PAR, DPoP, JWE, PKCE)

### Client Management API

- Add PKCE flag to client create and update APIs

- Apply profile-based override logic during persistence

- Validate AS-required profile constraints

### Runtime Enforcement

- Update authentication and authorization flows to:
** Enforce PAR requirements
** Validate DPoP proofs
** Enforce PKCE
** Encrypt UserInfo responses as JWE when required

### Backward Compatibility

- Ensure existing client records remain valid

- Apply profile-based enforcement dynamically at runtime

### Documentation

- Update README and configuration guides

title: ES-2830: Compliance suite expects the content-type of userinfo endpoint to be application/json but we send application/jwt
content:
Problem description:
## 🔗 Linked Issues

### ISSUE
- **ES-2805**
  Status: Closed
- **ES-2922**
  Status: New
- **ES-2941**
  Status: In Progress

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: **Jira Assignee:** Anusha sunkada (no valid GitHub user found)

[Ivanmeneges]: Harsh Kashiwal commented: The UserInfo Endpoint MUST return a content-type header to indicate which format is being returned. The content-type of the HTTP response MUST be {{application/json}} if the response body is a text JSON object; the response body SHOULD be encoded using UTF-8.

If the UserInfo Response is signed and/or encrypted, then the Claims are returned in a JWT and the content-type MUST be {{application/jwt}}. The response MAY be encrypted without also being signed. If both signing and encryption are requested, the response MUST be signed then encrypted, with the result being a Nested JWT

I checked if there is a property to publish the supported userinfo response type, but i am not in confidence for the findings
[Final: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 incorporating errata set 2|https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html#ProviderMetadata]

[Ivanmeneges]: Anusha sunkada commented: 

[https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0-final.html#UserInfoResponse|https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0-final.html#UserInfoResponse] 

[https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-registration-1_0.html|https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-registration-1_0.html] 

userinfo_signed_response_alg

OPTIONAL. JWS {{alg}} algorithm [[JWA]|https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-registration-1_0.html#JWA] REQUIRED for signing UserInfo Responses. If this is specified, the response will be [JWT|https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-registration-1_0.html#JWT] [JWT] serialized, and signed using JWS. The default, if omitted, is for the UserInfo Response to return the Claims as a UTF-8 [[RFC3629]|https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-registration-1_0.html#RFC3629] encoded JSON object using the {{application/json}} content-type.

[Ivanmeneges]: Anusha sunkada commented: Issue opened with OIDC conformance test repo - [https://gitlab.com/openid/conformance-suite/-/work_items/1751|https://gitlab.com/openid/conformance-suite/-/work_items/1751|smart-link]

title: ES-2857: eSignet Signup – Mandatory file upload field does not show validation error and allows submission
content: Problem description: ## *Scenario-1* ## *Description:* During the eSignet signup process, the mandatory *file upload field* does not enforce validation correctly. When the user skips uploading a required file and attempts to submit the form, no inline validation error is displayed, and the *Submit button remains enabled*. ## *Steps to Reproduce:* 1. Launch *eSignet-Signup*. 1. Navigate to enter *mobile number*. 1. Enter OTP and validate the generated challenge. 1. Navigate to the *Signup form*. 1. Skip the *mandatory file upload field*. 1. Attempt to submit the form. ## *Actual Result:* - No validation error is displayed. - The *Submit button is enabled*, even though the file upload field is mandatory. ## *Expected Result:* 1. Inline validation error should be displayed: *“This field is required.”* 1. The *Submit button should remain disabled* until the mandatory file is uploaded. ## *Scenario-2* ## *Description:* In the eSignet signup form, when a user uploads a valid file in a mandatory file upload field and then removes it before submission, the system does not trigger validation. The required field validation message is not displayed, and form validation is not enforced properly. ## *Steps to Reproduce:* 1. Launch *eSignet-Signup*. 1. Navigate to enter *mobile number*. 1. title: ES-2861: eSignet Signup – File at Maximum Allowed Size Uploads but Registration Does Not Complete
content:
Problem description:
## *Description:*

When uploading a file that is exactly equal to the configured maximum allowed size, the file uploads successfully. However, registration does not complete after submission.

## *Steps to Reproduce:*

1. Launch *eSignet-Signup*.

1. Navigate to enter *mobile number*.

1. Enter OTP and validate the generated challenge.

1. Navigate to the *Signup form*.

1. Upload a file that is *exactly equal to the maximum allowed file size*.

1. Click *Register/Submit*.

## *Actual Result:*

- File uploads successfully.

## *Expected Result:*

- File at maximum allowed size should be accepted.

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: Rachik Sharma commented: [~accountid:712020:303fdb0d-0530-4789-be66-a93af3857e72] to recheck the the nginx config and then retest the scenario with maximum size possible in the Nginx. It should work and Nginx file size set supercedes the UI schema configuration

[Ivanmeneges]: Zeeshan Mehboob commented: Hi [~accountid:712020:303fdb0d-0530-4789-be66-a93af3857e72] ,

The error you’re seeing, {{413 Request Entity Too Large}}, occurs when the upload size exceeds the maximum request size allowed by the Nginx server configuration. This is a common behavior in applications that use Nginx, and it cannot be fixed from the frontend or backend application code.

To resolve this, we need to update the Nginx configuration. Specifically, we must set the {{client_max_body_size}} directive inside the appropriate server block and assign a value that is larger than the file you are trying to upload.

For example, if you are uploading a 6.5 MB file, you should set the limit slightly above that—such as 7 MB.

Here’s how it looks in the Nginx config: 

{noformat}client_max_body_size 7M;{noformat}

title: ES-2922: OIDC Conformance Test Failure – UserInfo Endpoint Returns Unexpected HTTP Status and auth_time Claim Mismatch in oidcc-prompt-none-logged-in
content:
Problem description:
## *Test Suite:*

OpenID Connect Core: Comprehensive Authorization server test (not part of certification program).

## *Test Plan:*

oidcc-prompt-none-logged-in

----

## *Description:*

While executing the *OIDC conformance test plan* `oidcc-prompt-none-logged-in`, multiple failures are observed during the *UserInfo endpoint validation and ID Token comparison*.

1. The *UserInfo endpoint test* `EnsureHttpStatusCodeIs200` fails because the endpoint returns an *unexpected HTTP status instead of 200 OK*.

1. The same issue occurs during the *second authorization flow*.

1. Additionally, the validation `CheckIdTokenAuthTimeClaimsSameIfPresent` fails because the `auth_time` *claim differs between the ID tokens generated during the authorization flows*.

According to the *OIDC specification*, when `prompt=none` is used and the user is already authenticated, the *authentication time should remain consistent*, and the `auth_time` claim should match across tokens.

----

## *Steps to Reproduce:*

1. Launch the *OIDC Conformance Test Suite*.

1. Select the test plan `oidcc-prompt-none-logged-in`.

1. Execute the test flow where the user is already logged in.

1. Observe the *UserInfo endpoint tests and ID token validations*.

## *Actual Result:*

Test failures observed:

## *Actual Result:*

Test failures observed:

## *Actual Result:*

Test failures observed:

```
Userinfo endpoint tests: EnsureHttpStatusCodeIs200:
resource endpoint returned an unexpected http status

Second authorization:
Userinfo endpoint tests: EnsureHttpStatusCodeIs200:
resource endpoint returned an unexpected http status

OIDCC-2 CheckIdTokenAuthTimeClaimsSameIfPresent:
The id_tokens contain different auth_time claims.
```

## *Expected Result:*

- UserInfo endpoint should return:

```HTTP Status: 200 OK
```

- Response should contain valid user claims.

- The `auth_time` *claim in ID tokens should remain the same* across authorization responses when the same authenticated session is reused.

title: ES-2923: OIDC Conformance Failure – Authorization Endpoint Does Not Return Error for prompt=none When User Is Not Logged In
content:
Problem description:
## *Test Suite:*

OpenID Connect Core: Comprehensive Authorization server test (not part of certification program)

## *Test Plan:*

oidcc-prompt-none-not-logged-in

## *Description:*

While executing the *OIDC conformance test plan* `oidcc-prompt-none-not-logged-in`, the authorization server does *not return the expected error response when* `prompt=none` *is used and the user is not logged in*.

According to the *OpenID Connect specification*, when `prompt=none` is included in the authorization request and the user does not have an active session, the *authorization endpoint must return an error such as* `login_required` *instead of issuing an authorization code*.

However, the authorization server is returning a *successful authorization response containing an authorization code*, which causes multiple test failures in the conformance suite.

## *Steps to Reproduce:*

1. Launch the *OIDC Conformance Test Suite*.

1. Select the test plan `oidcc-prompt-none-not-logged-in`.

1. Ensure the user is *not logged in* (no active session).

1. Run the authorization flow with `prompt=none`.

1. Observe the response returned by the authorization endpoint.

## *Actual Result:*

The authorization endpoint returns a *successful response containing an authorization code*, instead of returning an error.

Observed test failures:

FAILURE OIDCC-3.1.2.6
EnsureErrorFromAuthorizationEndpointResponse:
Authorization server was expected to return an error but did not

FAILURE OIDCC-3.1.2.6
RejectAuthCodeInAuthorizationEndpointResponse:
Authorization code is present in URL query returned but an error was expected

WARNING OIDCC-3.1.2.6
CheckForUnexpectedParametersInErrorResponseFromAuthorizationEndpoint:
Authorization server was expected to return an error but did not

FAILURE OIDCC-3.1.2.6
CheckErrorFromAuthorizationEndpointIsOneThatRequiredAUserInterface:
Expected 'error' field not found

## *Expected Result:*

- The authorization server should *not issue an authorization code*.

- The response should return an *OIDC error response*, such as:
```
{
  "error": "login_required"
}
```

[image-20260305-113715.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2923)

The conformance suite performs several *negative tests to validate DPoP proof handling*. In one scenario, the suite sends a request containing *more than one DPoP header*. According to the FAPI 2.0 and DPoP specifications, the resource server must *reject such requests and return a* `400` *or* `401` *HTTP response*. However, the resource endpoint returns an *unexpected HTTP status instead of* `400` *or* `401`, indicating that invalid DPoP header scenarios are not being handled correctly. A total of *22 failures* are reported in the DPoP negative test suite. ## *Steps to Reproduce:* 1. Launch the *FAPI 2.0 Conformance Test Suite*. 1. Select the test plan `fapi2-security-profile-final-dpop-negative-tests`. 1. Execute the test flow. 1. The conformance suite sends requests to the *resource endpoint with invalid DPoP scenarios*, such as: #* Multiple DPoP headers in the request #* Invalid DPoP proof structure #* Incorrect JKT binding 1. Observe the responses returned by the *resource endpoint*. ## *Actual Result:* Observed failure: ``` Try with more than one DPoP in the header: EnsureHttpStatusCodeIs400or401: resourceendpoint returned a different http status than expected ``` Additionally, *22 failures* are reported across the DPoP negative test cases. ## *Expected Result:* For invalid DPoP scenarios (such as multiple DPoP headers), the resource endpoint should reject the request and return:- ```HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request ``` [image-20260310-054945.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2941) [image-20260310-055006.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2941) ![image-20260310-055035.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2941) ## 🔗 Linked Issues ### ISSUE - **ES-2841** Status: New - **ES-2830** Status: New - **ES-2950** Status: Documentation - **ES-2953** Status: Documentation ## 📎 Attachments - [image-20260310-054945.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2941) - [image-20260310-055006.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2941) - [image-20260310-055035.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2941) - [image-20260311-103401.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2941) - [image-20260311-103414.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2941) - [Screenshot 2026-03-13 092522.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2941) Discussion and resolution: [Ivanmeneges]: Sachin Rana commented: This needs to be tested with server profile fapi2.0 . title: ES-2939: FAPI 2.0 Conformance Warning – Access Token Not Revoked After Authorization Code Reuse in fapi2-security-profile-final-attempt-reuse-authorization-code-after-one-second

title: ES-2942: FAPI 2.0 Conformance Failure – User Session Already Authenticated in fapi2-security-profile-final-par-ensure-reused-request-uri-prior-to-auth-completion-succeeds
content:
Problem description:
## *Description:*

While executing the *FAPI 2.0 Security Profile Final Authorization Server Test* with the test plan `fapi2-security-profile-final-par-ensure-reused-request-uri-prior-to-auth-completion-succeeds`, the test fails due to an *unexpected authenticated session during the first login attempt*.

This test validates that a *Pushed Authorization Request (PAR)* `request_uri` *can be reused before authentication is completed*. The conformance suite expects the user *not to be authenticated during the first visit to the login page*.

## *Steps to Reproduce:*

1. Launch the *FAPI 2.0 Conformance Test Suite*.

1. Select the test plan `fapi2-security-profile-final-par-ensure-reused-request-uri-prior-to-auth-completion-succeeds`.

1. Execute the test flow.

1. The suite sends a *PAR request and obtains a* `request_uri`.

1. The suite attempts the *first authorization request using the* `request_uri`.

1. Observe the login behavior on the authorization server.

## *Actual Result:*

The following error occurs during execution:
```unexpected exception caught:
java.lang.RuntimeException:
The user was authenticated on the initial visit to login page.
This must not be attempted until the second visit.
If no login was attempted then please delete related cookies
or logout from the server before re-running.
```

## *Expected Result:*

- During the *first visit to the login page*, the user should *not be authenticated automatically*.

- Authentication should only occur when the test suite explicitly performs the login step.

- The *second authorization request using the same* `request_uri` *should proceed correctly*.

[image-20260310-055912.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2942)

[image-20260310-055932.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2942)

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: Humair Kankudti Md commented: !image-20260415-050737.png|width=646,alt="image-20260415-050737.png"!

Steps to test:
Run the test
Proceed with test - eSignet login page opens, close this page
Again proceed with test and login now.
Then come back to conformance test page and upload screen shot of the error displayed
on uploading and back to conformance test page you will see finished with review.
After review if this fails it will be a warning and not failure. Hence moving this to fixed state.

No changes from needed from eSignet side.

[prathmeshj12]: Closing the bug- please refer the comments for the bug here - https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2942

title: ES-2945: [ES-2851] Update API Automation Tests for Prompt Validation Changes (none/login → login_required)
content:
Problem description:
## Background

As part of the OIDC conformance fix under *ES-2851*, the `prompt` parameter validation has been updated in the *OIDCPromptValidator*.

The validator now *rejects specific prompt values at the request validation layer*, returning a `login_required` error *before the request reaches the service layer*.

Previously, `prompt=login` was widely used in test requests. With this change, those requests will now fail validation and return `login_required`.

All *happy-path and non-prompt related tests* must therefore use `prompt=consent`..

----

1. Behavior Changes

## Previously

| Prompt Value | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `login` | Accepted and processed |
| `none` | Processed by service layer |
| Unknown values (`touch`, `select_account`) | Rejected with `invalid_prompt` |

----

## Current Behavior (After ES-2851)

### Rejected Prompt Values (Validator Level)

| Prompt | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | `login_required` |
| `login` | `login_required` |

These are rejected *during request validation*.

----

### Accepted Prompt Values

| Prompt | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `consent` | Accepted |
| Unknown values (`touch`, `select_account`) | Passed through to service layer |

Unknown values are *no longer rejected by the validator*, aligning with *OIDC Core Spec Section 3.1.2.1*.

----

## *Space-Separated Prompt Values*

As per the *OIDC specification*, the `prompt` parameter supports *space-separated values*.

Example:

```prompt=consent login
```

The *OIDCPromptValidator splits the prompt value by spaces and validates each token individually*.

If *any token* equals `login` or `none`, the *entire request is rejected* with:

```error=login_required
```

This validation occurs *before the request reaches the service layer*.

----

## Space-Separated Prompt Examples

| Prompt Value | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `consent` | ✅ Valid — passes through to service layer |
| `login` | ❌ Rejected — returns `login_required` |
| `none` | ❌ Rejected — returns `login_required` |
| `consent login` | ❌ Rejected — `login` token detected |
| `consent none` | ❌ Rejected — `none` token detected |
| `consent select_account` | ✅ Valid — forwarded to service layer |
| `touch` | ✅ Valid — unknown value, forwarded to service layer |
| `login none` | ❌ Rejected — both tokens invalid |

1. Affected Endpoints

| Endpoint | Method | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/authorization/oauth-details` | POST | `prompt` in request body |
| `/authorization/v2/oauth-details` | POST | `prompt` in request body |
| `/authorization/v3/oauth-details` | POST | `prompt` in request body |
| `/oauth/par` | POST | `prompt` in PAR request body |

The *same prompt validation logic applies to all endpoints* above.

----

1. Impact on API Automation Tests

## 1️⃣ Update All Happy-Path Requests

Affected endpoints:

- `/authorization/oauth-details`

- `/authorization/v2/oauth-details`

- `/authorization/v3/oauth-details`

- `/oauth/par`

### Required Change

Replace:

```prompt=login
```

with

```prompt=consent
```

### Reason

`prompt=login` is now rejected during validation and returns:

```error=login_required
```

This causes unrelated tests to fail *before other validations execute*.

----

## 2️⃣ Update Prompt Error Tests

### Previous Test Case

```prompt=touch
Expected: invalid_prompt
```

### New Behavior

```prompt=touch
Expected: Accepted and forwarded to service layer
```

### Required Change

Tests expecting `invalid_prompt` *for unknown values* must be updated.

To test `login_required`, use:

```prompt=none
prompt=login
```

----

## 3️⃣ Update Flow / End-to-End Tests

Any *flow test using* `prompt=login` during setup must be updated.

This includes flows involving:

- `/oauth-details`

- `/v2/oauth-details`

- `/v3/oauth-details`

- `/oauth/par`

Example flow:

```/oauth/par
   ↓
request_uri returned
   ↓
/authorization/par-oauth-details
```

If `prompt=login` is used in the PAR request, it must be changed to:

```prompt=consent
```

----

1. 4. Space-Separated Prompt Test Updates

Automation tests using *space-separated prompt values* must also be reviewed.

If the prompt string *contains* `login` *or* `none` *anywhere*, the request will now fail with:

```error=login_required
```

### Example Test Update

Old request:

```prompt=consent login
```

Updated request:

```prompt=consent
```

1. Summary for QA & Automation

Required updates:

1. Replace `prompt=login` *→* `prompt=consent` in all happy-path tests.

1. Update *invalid prompt tests* to reflect new behavior.

1. Use `prompt=none` *or* `prompt=login` when testing `login_required`.

1. Update *PAR + OAuth flow tests* accordingly.

1. Review *space-separated prompt values* and remove `login` or `none` tokens if present.

----

✅ This change ensures *OIDC specification compliance and correct prompt validation behavior.*

title: ES-2987: API - Use schema API to build Add Identity request automatically
content:
Problem description:
## 📌 Current Problem

In *eSignet* and *Signup API Test Rig*:

- We are sending *random values* in the request

- We are *guessing field names and regex rules*

- Because of this, APIs sometimes *fail with validation errors*

## 🎯 Proposed Solution

- Call the *identity schema API*:
`[https://api.envname.mosip.net/v1/mock-identity-system/identity/identity-schema`](https://api.envname.mosip.net/v1/mock-identity-system/identity/identity-schema}})

- From the response:
** Get the *correct field names*
** Get *validation rules (regex, type, required fields)*

- Use this data to:
** *Dynamically build the Add Identity request body*

## ✅ Expected Result

- Requests will use *correct fields and formats*

- No more *guessing or random values*

- Fewer *API failures*

- More *stable automation tests*

title: ES-2972: UI does not redirect to redirect_uri with error=request_not_supported when oauth-details returns request_not_supported error
content:
Problem description:
## Summary

When the `/oauth-details` API returns a `request_not_supported` error (e.g. when `request` param is sent in authorize call), the eSignet UI displays the error message on screen instead of redirecting the browser back to the `request_not_supported` with the error as a URL parameter as required by OIDC Core spec §3.1.2.6

Steps to Reproduce

1. Send an authorization request with `request` param:

```curl --location 'https://esignet.esdev.mosip.net/v1/esignet/authorization/v3/oauth-details' \

--header 'X-XSRF-TOKEN: nsuwvngT7NMw-tUr3i7UvnBRLM4VEMAVALiSsKTQ-GdV_QN3pv6EjE8m3ucdnuwc7wPgjBFpAfcgJfc4NIqr05XknVZhmTFH' \

--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \

--data '{
    "requestTime": "2026-03-26T11:01:56.947Z",
    "request": {
        "clientId": "IIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAkjNuU",
        "scope": "openid profile",
        "responseType": "code",
        "redirectUri": "http://localhost:5000",
        "request": "eyJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.."
    }
}'
```

1. UI calls `/oauth-details` internally

1. `/oauth-details` returns:

```
{
    "responseTime": "2026-03-24T05:24:56.341Z",
    "response": null,
    "errors": [
        {
            "errorCode": "request_not_supported",
            "errorMessage": "request.request: request_not_supported"
        }
    ]
}
```

---

## Current Behaviour
UI displays `request_not_supported` as a text message on screen and stops. No redirect happens.

---

## Expected Behaviour
UI must redirect the browser to the `request_not_supported` with the error as URL parameters:

## Impact

- Causes `oidcc-unsigned-request-object-supported-correctly-or-rejected-as-unsupported` OIDC conformance test to fail

- The conformance suite expects the error in the redirect URL, not displayed on screen

## 🔗 Linked Issues

### ISSUE
- **ES-2852**
  Status: Documentation

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: Gurukiran P commented: [~accountid:712020:46054c49-742c-483c-8c0b-9fc2069d4d73] need your inputs for the following:

# Provide the proper error message that to be shown in the RP after the redirection from esignet to RP due to oauth response throwing errorCode = “{{request_not_supported}}“
# Should it always redirect to RP with some error message, whenever there is an error thrown by oauth endpoint or only when the errorCode = “{{request_not_supported}}“?

cc: [~accountid:557058:c955df2b-1615-45f5-8565-cbf63d54c49e]

[Ivanmeneges]: Anusha sunkada commented: [https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0-final.html#AuthError|https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0-final.html#AuthError] 

As per this section, all these error codes should be informed to RP when redirect_uri is valid.

So [~accountid:712020:8f896061-a759-4928-a5b9-627130474bdc], let's do a small implementation change. Instead of adding this as a DTO validation. Lets add it in the service layer.

validation must be the below order:

# validate ClientId - if invalid, then display error on the esignet UI
# validate redirect_uri - if invalid, then display error on the esignet UI
# check if “request” parameter is non-null or empty string - it should throw “request_not_supported” error, and this error should be sent in the redirect_uri to RP portal. 
# if the prompt parameter is anything other than “consent”, it should throw “login_required”  error, and this error should be sent in the redirect_uri to RP portal. 

As per analysis, if conditions for point 3 & 4 should be added in this method

[https://github.com/mosip/esignet/blob/master/oidc-service-impl/src/main/java/io/mosip/esignet/services/AuthorizationServiceImpl.java#L422|https://github.com/mosip/esignet/blob/master/oidc-service-impl/src/main/java/io/mosip/esignet/services/AuthorizationServiceImpl.java#L422]

title: Add PKCS12 keystore support to mock-identity-system as an alternative to SoftHSM
content:
Problem description:
## Context
mock-identity-system currently only supports SoftHSM for its keystore, provisioned unconditionally via a secret/configmap copied from a separate `softhsm` namespace. There's no way to use a file-based PKCS12 keystore instead.

## Changes
- `install.sh` now prompts to opt into a PKCS12 mounted-volume keystore instead of SoftHSM, creates the keystore password secret (default `1234`, overridable), and wires the corresponding persistence/env config into the helm install.
- SoftHSM provisioning (secret/configmap copy, env vars) is now only applied when PKCS12 is *not* selected — previously it was applied unconditionally regardless of choice.
- Helm chart (`helm/mock-identity-system`):
  - Added a `PersistentVolumeClaim` template (didn't exist before — persistence.enabled had no backing PVC resource).
  - Fixed the volume-permissions init container, which had a literal unfilled `%%commands%%` placeholder and stub `foo`/`bar` volume mount names — this caused a YAML parse error (`found character that cannot start any token`) the first time `persistence.enabled`+`volumePermissions.enabled` were actually exercised together.
  - Wired the persistence volume into the main container's `volumeMounts` and the pod's `volumes` (previously absent).
  - Added `extraEnvVarsAdditional` support (additive on top of `extraEnvVars`, doesn't require restating the whole list), matching the existing pattern in the `esignet` chart.

title: Migrate GPG Artifact Signing to GitHub Organization Secrets
content:
Problem description:
## Problem Statement 

Currently, GPG signing keys used for artifact signing are stored within individual repositories (for example, under the `key` directory). This results in duplication of sensitive signing material across repositories, increases the security risk, complicates key rotation, and makes centralized management difficult.

### Purpose 

Migrate the artifact signing mechanism to use GitHub Organization Secrets for managing GPG signing credentials. This ensures that private signing keys are never committed to repositories, are decoded only during workflow execution, and are managed centrally in accordance with the MOSIP Artifact Signing policy.

### Pre-Requisites

* GitHub Organization Secrets `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` and `GPG_SECRET` are configured.
* Repository is using the latest reusable GitHub Actions workflows from `mosip/kattu`.
* Repository has appropriate permissions to access organization secrets.

---

## Goals 

* Remove repository-specific GPG key files used for artifact signing.
* Update GitHub Actions workflows to consume `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` and `GPG_SECRET` from GitHub Organization Secrets.
* Ensure signing keys are decoded only during workflow execution and are not persisted on disk after the workflow completes.
* Standardize artifact signing across repositories using the reusable MOSIP signing workflows.
* Improve security by centralizing signing key management and enabling easier key rotation.

---

## Out of Scope 

* Generation or rotation of GPG signing keys.
* Changes to the artifact verification process for consumers.
* Updates to the KEYS file or signing documentation.
* Sonar analysis workflows, as they do not require artifact signing.

---

## Process Flow 

1. Remove existing GPG key files from the repository.
2. Configure the repository to use GitHub Organization Secrets for signing credentials.
3. Update the reusable workflow invocation to pass `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` and `GPG_SECRET` as secrets.
4. During build and publish, the reusable workflow imports the private key from the secret, performs artifact signing, and discards the key after execution.
5. Verify that signed artifacts are successfully generated and published without requiring repository-local key files.

---

## Acceptance Criteria 

* No GPG private or public key files are present in the repository.
* Artifact signing succeeds using GitHub Organization Secrets.
* Repository workflows invoke the reusable MOSIP signing workflows with the required signing secrets.
* Signed artifacts are published successfully without any change to the consumer experience.
* The repository no longer depends on locally stored signing keys for build or publishing.

title: Ingest KT session recordings from Confluence (transcript-first, Whisper fallback)
content:
Problem description:
## Summary
Crawl Confluence pages labelled `kt-session`, extract transcripts from attached caption files (`.vtt`/`.srt`) where available, and fall back to Whisper audio transcription only when no captions exist. Chunks are embedded and stored in pgvector.

## Background
Internal KT sessions are recorded and stored as attachments on Confluence pages. These contain team-specific walkthroughs and troubleshooting knowledge that exists nowhere else. The **transcript-first** strategy reuses any caption files already on the page, avoiding unnecessary Whisper compute for recordings that already have captions (e.g. auto-generated by Teams/Meet).

## Pre-conditions (complete before starting development)
- [ ] Label all Confluence pages hosting KT recordings with the label `kt-session`
  - Example title: `KT Session – IDA Module Overview – 2025-03-15`
  - Backfill this label on all existing pages
- [ ] Verify `CONFLUENCE_TOKEN` has attachment-read permission:
  ```
  curl -u user:token "https://yourorg.atlassian.net/wiki/rest/api/content?label=kt-session"
  ```
- [ ] Install `ffmpeg` on the ingestion machine (only needed when Whisper fallback triggers):
  - Windows: `winget install ffmpeg`
  - Docker: `RUN apt-get install -y ffmpeg` in Dockerfile

## Technical Approach

### Step 1 — Discover KT pages
```
GET /wiki/rest/api/content?label=kt-session&spaceKey={KT_CONFLUENCE_SPACE}&expand=children.attachment
```

### Step 2 — Transcript-first strategy (per page)

```
For each KT Confluence page:
  ├── Look for .vtt / .srt / .txt attachments
  │     → Found: parse caption file directly (no video download needed)
  │
  └── No caption file found:
        Look for .mp4 / .mkv / .mov / .webm / .m4a / .mp3 attachments
          → Download to ./tmp/kt/
          → Extract audio: ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -ar 16000 -ac 1 audio.wav
          → Transcribe: whisper audio.wav --model {WHISPER_MODEL}
          → Delete temp files

  Neither found → skip page, log WARN
```

### Step 3 — Chunking
- ~500-word chunks with 50-word overlap
- `source` URL = Confluence page URL

### Step 4 — Embed and Store
Use existing `intfloat/multilingual-e5-base` and `documents` table.

| Metadata field | Value |
|---|---|
| `source_type` | `kt_session` |
| `source` | Confluence page URL |
| `title` | page title |
| `kt_date` | parsed from title or page `created` date |
| `space_key` | Confluence space |
| `transcript_method` | `caption_file` or `whisper` |

> `transcript_method` helps audit which sessions used Whisper vs. existing captions.

### Step 5 — Summary output on completion
```
✅  12 pages processed
   ├── 8  transcribed via caption file (.vtt)
   ├── 3  transcribed via Whisper (base model)
   └── 1  skipped (no usable attachment found)
```

## Files

| File | Action |
|---|---|
| `ingestion/crawlers/kt_crawler.py` | NEW — Confluence page discovery and attachment handling |
| `ingestion/transcribe.py` | NEW — VTT/SRT parser + ffmpeg + Whisper pipeline |
| `ingestion/ingest_kt.py` | NEW — orchestrate crawl → transcript → embed → store |
| `pyproject.toml` | Add `openai-whisper>=20231117`, `ffmpeg-python>=0.2`, `webvtt-py>=0.4` |
| `config/settings.py` | Add `KT_CONFLUENCE_LABEL`, `KT_CONFLUENCE_SPACE`, `WHISPER_MODEL` |
| `.env.example` | Add KT-related vars |
| `app/app.py` | Add KT session icon and source label |

## New Environment Variables

```env
KT_CONFLUENCE_LABEL=kt-session     # Label on all KT session Confluence pages
KT_CONFLUENCE_SPACE=               # Optional: limit to one space key (e.g. ENGG)
WHISPER_MODEL=base                 # base | medium | large
```

> `CONFLUENCE_URL`, `CONFLUENCE_USER`, `CONFLUENCE_TOKEN` are reused — no new credentials needed.

## Run Command

```powershell
uv run python ingestion/ingest_kt.py
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Script finds all `kt-session` pages, extracts transcripts (caption-first, Whisper fallback), stores chunks in pgvector
- [ ] A question about a KT session topic returns a `kt_session` source with the Confluence page link
- [ ] `transcript_method` metadata correctly shows `caption_file` or `whisper` per chunk
- [ ] Pages with `.vtt`/`.srt` files do **not** trigger a video download or Whisper call
- [ ] Temp files under `./tmp/kt/` are deleted after each successful page
- [ ] Pages with no usable attachment are skipped — WARN log, not a crash
- [ ] Re-run is idempotent — same page not ingested twice
- [ ] `.env.example` updated and committed

## Known Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Most recordings have no captions → lots of Whisper runs | Check a sample page first; if mostly caption-less, run overnight on a GPU machine |
| `medium`/`large` Whisper gives better accuracy for MOSIP technical terms | Start with `base` to verify pipeline; switch to `medium` for final production ingestion |
| Confluence token lacks attachment read access | Run the `curl` pre-condition check before writing any code |
| KT pages not consistently labelled | Team lead to audit and backfill labels before dev starts |

title: Ingest MOSIP YouTube channel (@mosip16) videos into knowledge base
content:
Problem description:
## Summary
Add MOSIP YouTube channel videos as a new knowledge source. The crawler fetches video metadata and transcripts (manual captions preferred, auto-generated as fallback) and stores them in pgvector so the RAG pipeline can retrieve them when answering MOSIP questions.

## Background
MOSIP publishes tutorials, module walkthroughs, webinars, and release demos at https://www.youtube.com/@mosip16. This content is not in MosipNexus today. Adding it fills a gap for onboarding and process questions such as "how does the registration flow work?" and "demo of IDA authentication?".

## Technical Approach

### Step 1 — Fetch video list
Use YouTube Data API v3 with `forHandle=mosip16` to list all public videos from the channel.

```python
youtube = build("youtube", "v3", developerKey=YOUTUBE_API_KEY)
channel = youtube.channels().list(part="id", forHandle="mosip16").execute()
channel_id = channel["items"][0]["id"]
# list all videos via the channel's uploads playlist
```

### Step 2 — Fetch transcripts
Use `youtube-transcript-api` per video:
- Prefer manually-created captions
- Fall back to auto-generated captions (`en` first, then any available language)
- If no transcript exists → skip video, log `WARN: no transcript for {title} ({video_id})`

### Step 3 — Chunking
- Group transcript segments into ~500-word chunks with 50-word overlap
- Preserve `start` timestamp of first segment per chunk
- Deep-link URL: `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={video_id}&t={start_seconds}s`

### Step 4 — Embed and Store
Use existing `intfloat/multilingual-e5-base` embedder and `documents` pgvector table.

| Metadata field | Value |
|---|---|
| `source_type` | `youtube` |
| `source` | `https://youtube.com/watch?v={id}&t={start}s` |
| `title` | video title |
| `published_at` | ISO publish date |
| `channel_name` | `MOSIP` |

### Step 5 — UI
Add YouTube icon and label to `app/app.py` (`_SVG_ICON` and `_SOURCE_LABEL` dicts).

## Files

| File | Action |
|---|---|
| `ingestion/crawlers/youtube_crawler.py` | NEW — fetch video list and transcripts |
| `ingestion/ingest_youtube.py` | NEW — orchestrate crawl → chunk → embed → store |
| `pyproject.toml` | Add `google-api-python-client>=2.100`, `youtube-transcript-api>=0.6` |
| `.env.example` | Add `YOUTUBE_API_KEY`, `YOUTUBE_CHANNEL_HANDLE` |
| `app/app.py` | Add YouTube icon and source label |

## New Environment Variables

```env
YOUTUBE_API_KEY=your_key_here      # Google Cloud Console → APIs → YouTube Data API v3
YOUTUBE_CHANNEL_HANDLE=mosip16     # No @ prefix
```

**How to get a YouTube API key:**
1. Go to https://console.cloud.google.com
2. Enable **YouTube Data API v3**
3. Credentials → Create API Key → copy into `.env`
4. Free quota: 10,000 units/day (listing videos costs ~1 unit each)

## Run Command

```powershell
uv run python ingestion/ingest_youtube.py
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Script completes and all videos with transcripts are stored in pgvector
- [ ] Query "MOSIP registration flow" returns at least one `youtube` source with a timestamped URL
- [ ] YouTube sources render with icon and clickable deep-link in the Sources panel
- [ ] Videos without any transcript are skipped — logged as WARN, not a crash
- [ ] Re-run is idempotent — existing `video_id + start` combinations not duplicated
- [ ] `.env.example` updated and committed

title: [Mosip Nexus] Build web crawler and index eSignet Documentation as a knowledge source
content:
Problem description:
Add eSignet Documentation (https://docs.esignet.io/) as a dedicated knowledge source in MOSIP Nexus.

eSignet is MOSIP's digital authentication solution. Questions about eSignet APIs, integration steps, and configuration are currently unanswerable because the eSignet docs site is outside the existing crawl scope. This task builds the shared web_crawler.py infrastructure (reused by E6b) and indexes eSignet docs as the first target.

Reusable crawler that accepts a base URL and outputs structured JSON:

Parse /sitemap.xml first; fall back to recursive link following

Polite crawl delay between requests (CRAWL_DELAY_SECS from settings)

Output: [{"url": ..., "title": ..., "content": ...}]

Run crawler for eSignet

uv run python MosipNexus/crawler/web_crawler.py \
  --base-url https://docs.esignet.io \

title: [MOSIP Nexus] Deploy MOSIP Nexus on Rancher — Lower Environment Setup
content:
Problem description:
## Context

MOSIP Nexus is an AI-powered internal knowledge assistant for the MOSIP team.
This issue captures everything the DevOps team needs to deploy it on Rancher 
in a lower environment.

**Repo:** `https://github.com/your-org/mosip-labs`  
**K8s manifests:** `MosipNexus/k8s/`  
**Point of contact:** @Mohanachandran (engineering queries)

---

## What Engineering Will Provide

Before deployment begins, the engineering team will hand over:

- [ ] Filled secret values for `k8s/02-secret.yaml`
- [ ] Confirmation that Docker image is available at 
  `mohanachandran45/mosip-nexus:latest`

---

## 1. Docker Images

| Component | Image | Pull Policy |
|---|---|---|
| API | `mohanachandran45/mosip-nexus:latest` | Always |
| UI | `mohanachandran45/mosip-nexus:latest` | Always |
| Database | `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` | IfNotPresent |

---

## 2. Resource Requirements

| Component | CPU Request | CPU Limit | Memory Request | Memory Limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nexus-api | 500m | 2 cores | 1500 Mi | 4 Gi |
| nexus-ui | 250m | 1 core | 1500 Mi | 4 Gi |
| nexus-postgres | 250m | 1 core | 512 Mi | 2 Gi |

> **Note:** The initial ingest Job (`08-initial-ingest-job.yaml`) runs crawlers 
> and embedding for all knowledge sources. It is CPU/memory intensive and takes 
> **4–8 hours** to complete on first run. Resources listed above are for 
> steady-state operation only.

---

## 3. Ports

| Component | Container Port | Service Port | Protocol |
|---|---|---|---|
| nexus-api | 8000 | 8000 | HTTP |
| nexus-ui | 8501 | 8501 | HTTP + WebSocket |
| nexus-postgres | 5432 | 5432 | TCP (internal only) |

---

## 4. URLs / Access Paths

| | URL |
|---|---|
| **Chat UI** | `https://mosip-nexus.env.mosip.net/` |
| **API** | `https://mosip-nexus.env.mosip.net/api/` |
| **API Docs** | `https://mosip-nexus.env.mosip.net/api/docs` |
| **UI Health** | `https://mosip-nexus.env.mosip.net/_stcore/health` |
| **API Health** | `https://mosip-nexus.env.mosip.net/api/health` |

> Please confirm with the team whether routing is path-based (`/api/`) or 
> subdomain-based (`mosip-nexus-api.env.mosip.net`) and update `06-ingress.yaml` 
> accordingly.

---

## 5. Health Check Paths

| Component | Path | Port | Initial Delay |
|---|---|---|---|
| nexus-api | `GET /health` | 8000 | 60s |
| nexus-ui | `GET /_stcore/health` | 8501 | 60s |
| nexus-postgres | `pg_isready -U mosip -d mosipnexus` | 5432 | 30s |

---

## 6. Persistent Volumes Required

| PVC Name | Mount Path | Size | Used By |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nexus-data` | `/app/MosipNexus/data` | 10 Gi | nexus-api, CronJob, ingest Job |
| `postgres-data` | `/var/lib/postgresql/data` | 20 Gi | nexus-postgres |

> Please set `storageClassName` in `01-postgres.yaml` and `07-cronjob.yaml` 
> to match your Rancher storage class before applying.

---

## 7. Environment Variables

### 🔴 Mandatory

| Variable | Notes |
|---|---|
| `GROQ_API_KEY` | Provided by engineering |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | Set any strong password — must match `PG_CONNECTION` |
| `PG_CONNECTION` | `postgresql+psycopg://mosip:<password>@nexus-postgres:5432/mosipnexus` |

### 🟡 Required for full knowledge base ingestion

These are needed by the initial ingest Job to crawl all knowledge sources. 
Without them, the job will skip those sources.

| Variable | Notes |
|---|---|
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | Provided by engineering — needed to crawl GitHub issues |
| `CONFLUENCE_URL` | `https://your-org.atlassian.net/wiki` |
| `CONFLUENCE_USER` | Atlassian login email — provided by engineering |
| `CONFLUENCE_TOKEN` | API token — provided by engineering |
| `CONFLUENCE_SPACE_KEYS` | `QT,ENGG,PMS,MSD` |

### 🟢 Optional (not needed for lower env)

`JIRA_*`, `LANGCHAIN_*`, `HF_TOKEN`, `SMTP_*`, `NOTIFY_EMAIL`

> All variables go into `k8s/02-secret.yaml`. Engineering will provide a 
> pre-filled version — **do not commit this file to git.**

---

## 8. Ingress Requirements

- Ingress controller: **nginx**
- WebSocket support required for Streamlit UI
- Proxy timeout: **300s** (AI responses can take up to 30s)

---

## 9. Deployment Steps

```bash
# Step 1 — Apply core manifests in order
kubectl apply -f k8s/00-namespace.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/01-postgres.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/02-secret.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/03-deployment-api.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/04-deployment-ui.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/05-services.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/06-ingress.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/07-cronjob.yaml

# Step 2 — Verify all pods are running before proceeding
kubectl get pods -n mosip-nexus

# Step 3 — Run the initial ingest job
# This crawls all knowledge sources and builds the vector database.
# Expected runtime: 4–8 hours on first run.
kubectl apply -f k8s/08-initial-ingest-job.yaml

# Step 4 — Monitor ingestion progress
kubectl logs -n mosip-nexus job/nexus-initial-ingest -f
