title: MOSIP  ConfigForge AI — Unified Configuration & Customisation Agent for MOSIP
content:
Problem description:
## Description

**As a** System Integrator (SI) deploying MOSIP for a country/program,
**I want** a single AI-driven agent that consolidates every configuration and customization decision across all MOSIP modules, explains each one's purpose, captures my inputs, and then auto-applies the changes to the correct repositories,
**So that** I no longer have to manually navigate multiple modules and repos, understand each in isolation, and risk inconsistent or error-prone configuration during deployment.

---

##  As-Is

Today, configuring and customizing a MOSIP deployment is a fragmented, expert-dependent activity. To enable country-specific features, an SI must work across many modules and repositories independently — updating seed/master data (unique per country), defining which biometrics to capture, specifying documents required at registration, defining the fields/attributes collected from a resident, authoring the UI Spec, defining the ID Schema, and configuring data-sharing policies, among others.

Each of these lives in a different place, follows a different format, and requires the SI to already know *where* the change goes, *what* it does, and *how* it interacts with other settings. There is no consolidated view of "everything that must be decided" for a deployment, and no automatic propagation of a decision to the right repo. The result is a steep learning curve, duplicated effort, configuration drift, and a high likelihood of misconfiguration — especially because application, infrastructure, and performance settings are intermingled rather than presented in a way the SI can reason about by concern.

## To-Be

A single AI agent (ConfiForge) acts as the consolidated entry point for all deployment-time configuration and customization. It presents the SI with the complete set of configurable items across all modules, organized by concern, and for each item it explains the purpose, the expected input, the default/recommended value, and the target repository where the change will land.

The SI reviews and provides inputs in one place. The agent validates those inputs, shows a preview of what will change and in which repo, and — on confirmation — auto-configures the relevant modules and repositories accordingly. Critically, the agent separates **application configuration** (further split into **feature-related** and **UI-related**), **infrastructure configuration**, and **performance configuration**, so the SI (or different teams owning each concern) can review and modify only what is relevant to them.

## Goals

1. Provide a single consolidated interface for all MOSIP deployment configuration and customization, removing the need to visit modules one by one.
2. For every configurable item, surface a plain-language explanation of its purpose, its impact, and the input it expects.
3. Capture SI inputs, validate them, and auto-apply the resulting changes to the correct repository/module without manual file editing.
4. Categorize every item by concern: Application (Feature, UI), Infrastructure, and Performance — and let the SI filter/modify by category.
5. For each item and change, explicitly name the target repository and file/path that will be modified.
6. Show a reviewable preview (diff/summary) of all pending changes before anything is committed.
7. Support country-specific variation (seed data, biometrics, documents, fields, ID Schema, UI Spec, data-sharing policy) as first-class configurable inputs.
8. Reduce time-to-configure and configuration errors for a new deployment relative to the current manual process.

## Out of Scope

- Building or modifying the underlying MOSIP modules themselves (the agent configures existing modules; it does not change their source behavior).
- Provisioning or managing the actual infrastructure (e.g., spinning up Kubernetes clusters, databases, object store); the agent edits *configuration*, not live infrastructure resources.
- Functional/regression testing of MOSIP after configuration; the agent applies config and validates inputs but does not certify the running system.
- Day-2 operations such as monitoring, alerting, backup, and incident response.
- User/role administration of the deployed MOSIP instance and live resident data.
- Migration of an existing live deployment's data; the focus is deployment-time configuration.
- Custom code generation for net-new features not already supported by MOSIP configuration points.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Consolidation & discovery
- Given a supported MOSIP deployment, when the SI opens the agent, then it displays the complete set of configurable/customizable items across all modules in one consolidated view.
- Each item shows: a name, a plain-language purpose/description, the expected input type, the default or recommended value, and the target repository (and file/path) it maps to.

### Categorization
- Every configurable item is classified as Application, Infrastructure, or Performance.
- Items classified as Application are further sub-classified as Feature-related or UI-related.
- The SI can filter and view items by category and sub-category, and can edit items independently within each category.

### Input capture & validation
- When the SI provides an input, the agent validates it against the item's expected type/constraints and shows a clear error for invalid values without applying them.
- Country-specific items — seed/master data, biometrics to capture, documents required at registration, resident fields/attributes, ID Schema, UI Spec, and data-sharing policy — are all captured as configurable inputs.

### Repo mapping & preview
- Before applying, the agent presents a preview listing every change, the value being set, and the exact repository/file each change will be written to.
- The SI must explicitly confirm before any change is committed.

### Auto-configuration
- Upon confirmation, the agent writes each change to the correct repository/module automatically, with no manual file editing required by the SI.
- After applying, the agent reports per-item success/failure, and any failure does not silently leave the configuration in an unknown state (the SI is informed of partial application).

### Traceability
- For any applied change, the SI can see what was changed, the value, the target repo, and the timestamp.

# Platform Upgrade to v1.2.1.0 (Repos v1.3.0)

## Overview

As part of the post-release activities, the Collab environment platform version must be upgraded to **v1.2.1.0** (Repositories **v1.3.0**). The following activities should be completed to ensure a successful end-to-end upgrade.

## Upgrade Activities

| S.No | Activity | Description | Owner |
|-------|----------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | Database Backup | Take a complete backup of the existing Collab database before initiating the migration process. | DevOps |
| 2 | Version Verification | Confirm the versions of Database, ID Schema, mosip-data, and mosip-config before starting the upgrade. | Dev |
| 3 | Database Analysis & Testing | Analyze the database changes introduced in the target release and perform validation testing. | Dev |
| 4 | Schema Comparison | Compare the CRE and Collab database schemas after upgrading Collab to v1.2.1.0. Ensure that custom changes introduced for Inji and eSignet support are retained and no regressions are introduced. | Dev |
| 5 | Artifactory Validation | Verify whether any repository, image, or artifact updates are required in Artifactory. | DevOps & Dev |
| 6 | Rollback Plan | Prepare, review and signify rollback plan | DevOps & Dev |
| 7 | Repository Upgrade | Upgrade all repositories from the current version to the latest released version (v1.3.0). | DevOps |
| 8 | Automation & DSL Deployment | Deploy Automation and DSL components and execute sanity validation tests. | DevOps |
| 9 | User Acceptance Testing (UAT) | Perform end-to-end UAT to validate platform functionality after the upgrade. | PO |
| 10 | Community/ External Party Announcement | During pre and post migration share the upgrade information to stakeholders and third party integrators (Inji/ eSignet/CRVS/PMS/ARC/ Partner Eco System/ DST) | PO |

## Risks and Validation Points

| S.No | Area | Validation Required |
|-------|------|---------------------|
| 1 | Dynamic OTP | Verify that Dynamic OTP is enabled by default in the latest version and confirm expected behavior across all applicable workflows. |
| 2 | eSignet & Inji Integration | Validate data-sharing dependencies and integration points with eSignet and Inji to ensure uninterrupted functionality. |
| 3 | CAPTCHA Validation | Verify CAPTCHA functionality and ensure successful validation across all applicable user journeys. |
| 4 | Automation & DSL | Confirm successful deployment and execution of Automation and DSL sanity tests after the upgrade. |

## Deliverables

- Highlight any deviations from the proposed upgrade approach, along with the rationale and impact.
- Identify any changes to the estimated timelines resulting from the proposed approach or findings.

## Prerequisites for Migration

- Perform pre-upgrade and post-upgrade verification using the selected UINs to ensure:
  - Existing data remains accessible and intact.

title: Interactive Activity Metrics with Drill-Down Details
content:
Problem description:
## Problem Statement

Currently, the GitHub Activity Tracker displays team member activities in a table with the following columns:

```
Team | Project | Role | Commits | PRs | Reviews
```

The table shows **aggregated numeric values** (e.g., "45 commits", "12 PRs", "23 reviews") for each team member, but these numbers are:

1. **Just static numbers** - No way to see which specific commits, PRs, or reviews they represent
2. **Not interactive** - Users must manually search GitHub to find related items
3. **No navigation** - Clicking on the number does nothing
4. **Limited context** - Can't quickly understand what work was done
5. **Requires external navigation** - Must switch to GitHub to verify the data

### Current Situation

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Team | Project | Role | Commits | PRs | Reviews     │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Core | MOSIP   | Dev  | 45      | 12  | 23          │
│      |         |      | ↑       | ↑   | ↑           │
│      |         |      | Just a  | Not | No drill-   │
│      |         |      | number  | interactive │ down  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**The Problem**: Users need to click the number to see what commits/PRs/reviews it represents, but currently they can't.

---

## Goals

### Goal A: Add Interactive Hover Functionality

**What We Want**:
- When user hovers over a metric number (Commits, PRs, or Reviews), a dropdown box appears
- The dropdown shows a list of related items:
  - **For Commits**: List of commit messages/hashes
  - **For PRs**: List of PR titles/numbers
  - **For Reviews**: List of reviewed PR titles/numbers
- The dropdown is easy to read and visually highlighted
- Dropdown includes links to view details

**Why It Matters**:
- Users can quickly see what work was done without leaving the page
- Provides context for activity metrics
- Improves user experience and reduces friction

---

### Goal B: Add Drill-Down Navigation

**What We Want**:
- When user clicks on a specific item in the dropdown (e.g., a PR number), they are navigated to the actual GitHub PR
- Links open in the same tab or new tab (configurable)
- Navigation works for:
  - Commits → GitHub commit page
  - PRs → GitHub PR page
  - Reviews → GitHub PR review page

**Why It Matters**:
- Users can verify details directly in GitHub
- Seamless integration with GitHub
- Reduces manual searching on GitHub

---

### Goal C: Maintain Performance & Usability

**What We Want**:
- Dropdowns load quickly (no noticeable delay)
- Numbers are clearly highlighted (visual indicator that they're interactive)
- Mobile-friendly (hover on desktop, tap-to-expand on mobile)
- Works across all browsers

**Why It Matters**:
- Good user experience
- Accessible to all users
- Professional appearance

---

## Non-Goals

❌ Change the existing table structure or add new columns  
❌ Modify how metrics are calculated or aggregated  
❌ Add export functionality for the dropdown data  
❌ Create new database tables (use existing data)  
❌ Add filtering by specific commit/PR/review  
❌ Change the overall page layout  
❌ Add analytics on hover/click behavior  

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Acceptance Criteria 1: Hover Over Commits Number

**Given**: A team member with 45 commits is displayed in the table  
**When**: User hovers over the "45" in the Commits column  
**Then**:

- [ ] A dropdown box appears below/near the number
- [ ] Dropdown title shows: "Commits (45)"
- [ ] Dropdown displays a list of commits with:
  - Commit hash (first 7 characters, e.g., "a1b2c3d")
  - Commit message
  - Date committed
  - Author name
- [ ] Each commit in the list is displayed as a clickable link
- [ ] Dropdown appears within 200ms (no noticeable delay)
- [ ] Dropdown is properly positioned (doesn't go off-screen)
- [ ] Has a scrollbar if more than 10 commits

**Example Dropdown**:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Commits (45)                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ • a1b2c3d - Fix login bug (May 28)  │ ← Clickable
│ • d3c2b1a - Update docs (May 27)    │ ← Clickable
│ • 7f8e9d0 - Add tests (May 26)      │ ← Clickable
│ • ...more items                      │
│ [scroll]                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Acceptance Criteria 2: Hover Over PRs Number

**Given**: A team member with 12 PRs is displayed in the table  
**When**: User hovers over the "12" in the PRs column  
**Then**:

- [ ] A dropdown box appears below/near the number
- [ ] Dropdown title shows: "Pull Requests (12)"
- [ ] Dropdown displays a list of PRs with:
  - PR number (e.g., "#1234")
  - PR title
  - PR status (Open, Merged, Closed)
  - Date created
- [ ] Status is color-coded:
  - Green = Merged
  - Blue = Open
  - Red = Closed
- [ ] Each PR in the list is displayed as a clickable link
- [ ] Dropdown appears within 200ms
- [ ] Has proper formatting and visual separation

**Example Dropdown**:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Pull Requests (12)                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ • #1245 - Add user authentication (Merged)  │ ← Clickable
│ • #1234 - Update API docs (Merged)          │ ← Clickable
│ • #1223 - Fix cache issue (Open)            │ ← Clickable
│ • ...more items                             │
│ [scroll]                                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Acceptance Criteria 3: Hover Over Reviews Number

### Acceptance Criteria 8: Dropdown Behavior

### Test Scenario 2: Click a Commit Link

### Test Scenario 4: Click a PR Link

**Expected Results**:

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Dropdown shows exactly 45 items
- ✅ No duplicates
- ✅ No missing items
- ✅ Dates match GitHub data
- ✅ Commit messages are accurate

## Implementation Details

### Frontend Components Needed

1. **Metric Number Component** (React/Vue)
   - Renders the number with styling
   - Handles hover/click events
   - Triggers dropdown on hover

2. **Dropdown Component**
   - Displays list of items
   - Handles positioning (stays on-screen)
   - Handles close/escape logic
   - Shows loading state if needed
   - Has scrolling for large datasets

3. **Dropdown Item Component**
   - Single item in dropdown
   - Clickable link
   - Hover effect
   - Keyboard navigation support

### Backend API (No Changes Needed)

- Can use existing activity API response
- Existing API should already include:
  - List of commits (with hashes, messages, dates)
  - List of PRs (with numbers, titles, statuses, dates)
  - List of reviews (with PR numbers, comment counts, dates)
- If data isn't available, might need small API enhancement

### Data Structure Example

```json
{
  "team_member": {
    "id": 123,
    "name": "John Doe",
    "activities": {
      "commits": [
        {
          "hash": "a1b2c3d",
          "message": "Fix login bug",
          "date": "2026-05-28",
          "url": "https://github.com/.../commit/a1b2c3d"
        }
      ],
      "pull_requests": [
        {
          "number": 1245,
          "title": "Add user authentication",
          "status": "merged",
          "date": "2026-05-28",
          "url": "https://github.com/.../pull/1245"
        }
      ],
      "reviews": [
        {
          "pr_number": 1245,
          "pr_title": "Auth module",
          "comments": 5,
          "date": "2026-05-28",
          "url": "https://github.com/.../pull/1245"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

---



## Definition of Done

This story is complete when:

✅ All 15 acceptance criteria are met  
✅ All 10 test scenarios pass  
✅ Dropdown appears on hover (desktop) and tap (mobile)  
✅ All links navigate to correct GitHub URLs  
✅ Keyboard navigation works  
✅ Mobile-friendly and accessible  
✅ No performance issues  
✅ Code reviewed and approved  
✅ Unit tests written (>80% coverage)  
✅ Integration tests passing  
✅ QA sign-off obtained  
✅ Documentation updated  
✅ Deployed to staging and verified  

---

## Notes for Developer

### Technical Considerations

1. **Performance**: Use React/Vue memoization to prevent unnecessary re-renders
2. **Data Source**: Get data from existing API response, don't make new requests
3. **Positioning**: Use a library like Popper.js for smart dropdown positioning
4. **Animations**: Keep animations smooth but not distracting
5. **Accessibility**: Use semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and keyboard events
6. **Mobile**: Use `@media (hover: none)` to detect touch devices

### Potential Challenges

- Dropdown positioning (ensuring it stays visible)
- Performance with large datasets (1000+ items)
- Keyboard navigation in nested structures
- Screen reader announcements
- Browser compatibility for modern CSS

title: Interactive Activity Metrics with Drill-Down Details
content:
Problem description:
## Problem Statement

Currently, the GitHub Activity Tracker displays team member activities in a table with the following columns:

```
Team | Project | Role | Commits | PRs | Reviews
```

The table shows **aggregated numeric values** (e.g., "45 commits", "12 PRs", "23 reviews") for each team member, but these numbers are:

1. **Just static numbers** - No way to see which specific commits, PRs, or reviews they represent
2. **Not interactive** - Users must manually search GitHub to find related items
3. **No navigation** - Clicking on the number does nothing
4. **Limited context** - Can't quickly understand what work was done
5. **Requires external navigation** - Must switch to GitHub to verify the data

### Current Situation

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Team | Project | Role | Commits | PRs | Reviews     │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Core | MOSIP   | Dev  | 45      | 12  | 23          │
│      |         |      | ↑       | ↑   | ↑           │
│      |         |      | Just a  | Not | No drill-   │
│      |         |      | number  | interactive │ down  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**The Problem**: Users need to click the number to see what commits/PRs/reviews it represents, but currently they can't.

---

## Goals

### Goal A: Add Interactive Hover Functionality

**What We Want**:
- When user hovers over a metric number (Commits, PRs, or Reviews), a dropdown box appears
- The dropdown shows a list of related items:
  - **For Commits**: List of commit messages/hashes
  - **For PRs**: List of PR titles/numbers
  - **For Reviews**: List of reviewed PR titles/numbers
- The dropdown is easy to read and visually highlighted
- Dropdown includes links to view details

**Why It Matters**:
- Users can quickly see what work was done without leaving the page
- Provides context for activity metrics
- Improves user experience and reduces friction

---

### Goal B: Add Drill-Down Navigation

**What We Want**:
- When user clicks on a specific item in the dropdown (e.g., a PR number), they are navigated to the actual GitHub PR
- Links open in the same tab or new tab (configurable)
- Navigation works for:
  - Commits → GitHub commit page
  - PRs → GitHub PR page
  - Reviews → GitHub PR review page

**Why It Matters**:
- Users can verify details directly in GitHub
- Seamless integration with GitHub
- Reduces manual searching on GitHub

---

### Goal C: Maintain Performance & Usability

**What We Want**:
- Dropdowns load quickly (no noticeable delay)
- Numbers are clearly highlighted (visual indicator that they're interactive)
- Mobile-friendly (hover on desktop, tap-to-expand on mobile)
- Works across all browsers

**Why It Matters**:
- Good user experience
- Accessible to all users
- Professional appearance

---

## Non-Goals

❌ Change the existing table structure or add new columns  
❌ Modify how metrics are calculated or aggregated  
❌ Add export functionality for the dropdown data  
❌ Create new database tables (use existing data)  
❌ Add filtering by specific commit/PR/review  
❌ Change the overall page layout  
❌ Add analytics on hover/click behavior

**Given**: A team member with 45 commits is displayed in the table

**Then**:

- [ ] A dropdown box appears below/near the number

  - Commit hash (first 7 characters, e.g., "a1b2c3d")
  - Commit message
- [ ] Each commit in the list is displayed as a clickable link
- [ ] Dropdown appears within 200ms (no noticeable delay)
- [ ] Dropdown is properly positioned (doesn't go off-screen)
- [ ] Has a scrollbar if more than 10 commits

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Commits (45)                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤

### AC 13: Browser Compatibility

- [ ] Works on Chrome/Chromium (latest 2 versions)
- [ ] Works on Firefox (latest 2 versions)
- [ ] Works on Safari (latest 2 versions)
- [ ] Works on Edge (latest version)
- [ ] Responsive on mobile browsers
- [ ] No console errors

---

### AC 14: Accessibility

- [ ] Keyboard navigation: Tab through metrics, Enter to see dropdown
- [ ] Screen reader friendly: Alt text for numbers, ARIA labels
- [ ] Color contrast meets WCAG AA standards
- [ ] Not relying on hover alone (keyboard support)
- [ ] Focus indicators visible
- [ ] Dropdown content is accessible to screen readers

---

### AC 15: Code Quality

- [ ] No hardcoded values (all configurable)
- [ ] Modular, reusable components
- [ ] Well-documented code
- [ ] Unit tests for dropdown logic
- [ ] Integration tests for navigation
- [ ] No console warnings

---

## Testing Scenarios

### Test Scenario 1: View Commits Dropdown

**Setup**: Team member with 45 commits is visible in the table

**Steps**:
1. Move mouse over the "45" in Commits column
2. Wait for dropdown to appear
3. Verify dropdown shows list of commits
4. Verify count matches "Commits (45)"
5. Move mouse away
6. Verify dropdown closes

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Dropdown appears within 200ms
- ✅ Shows 45 commits in the list
- ✅ Each commit shows hash, message, and date
- ✅ Dropdown disappears when mouse leaves

---

### Test Scenario 2: Click a Commit Link

**Setup**: Commits dropdown is open

**Steps**:
1. Click on the first commit in the dropdown (e.g., "a1b2c3d - Fix login bug")
2. Wait for page navigation

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Navigated to GitHub commit page
- ✅ URL is correct: `https://github.com/Varaniya201/mosip-labs/commit/a1b2c3d`
- ✅ Commit details are visible in GitHub
- ✅ No errors

---

### Test Scenario 3: View PRs Dropdown

**Setup**: Team member with 12 PRs is visible in the table

**Steps**:
1. Move mouse over the "12" in PRs column
2. Wait for dropdown to appear
3. Verify dropdown shows list of PRs
4. Verify all PRs are shown with title and status

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Dropdown shows all 12 PRs
- ✅ Each PR shows number, title, status, and date
- ✅ Status colors are correct (green for merged, blue for open, etc.)
- ✅ Dropdown displays properly

---

### Test Scenario 4: Click a PR Link

**Setup**: PRs dropdown is open

**Steps**:
1. Click on a merged PR (e.g., "#1245 - Add user authentication")
2. Wait for page navigation

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Navigated to GitHub PR page
- ✅ URL is correct: `https://github.com/Varaniya201/mosip-labs/pull/1245`
- ✅ PR details visible
- ✅ Can see merged status

---

### Test Scenario 5: View Reviews Dropdown

**Setup**: Team member with 23 code reviews is visible in the table

**Steps**:
1. Move mouse over the "23" in Reviews column
2. Wait for dropdown to appear
3. Verify dropdown shows reviewed PRs
4. Verify comment counts are shown

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Dropdown shows 23 reviewed PRs
- ✅ Each shows PR number, title, comment count, and date
- ✅ Comment counts are accurate
- ✅ All items are clickable

---


### Test Scenario 7: Multiple Dropdowns Not Simultaneously Open

**Setup**: Multiple metric numbers visible in table

**Steps**:
1. Hover over Commits number → dropdown appears
2. While first dropdown is open, hover over PRs number
3. Observe what happens

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Commits dropdown closes
- ✅ PRs dropdown opens
- ✅ Only one dropdown is open at a time
- ✅ No overlapping dropdowns

---

### Test Scenario 8: Keyboard Navigation

**Setup**: Using keyboard only (no mouse)

**Steps**:
1. Tab to a metric number
2. Press Enter to open dropdown
3. Tab through dropdown items
4. Press Enter on a link to navigate

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Can tab to metric numbers
- ✅ Enter opens dropdown
- ✅ Can tab through items in dropdown
- ✅ Enter navigates to GitHub

---

### Test Scenario 9: Large Dataset

**Setup**: Team member with 200+ commits/PRs/reviews

**Steps**:
1. Hover over high metric number (e.g., "245 commits")
2. Verify dropdown appears with scrollbar
3. Scroll through the list
4. Click on an item near the bottom

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Dropdown still appears within 200ms
- ✅ Scrollbar is visible and functional
- ✅ Can scroll to see all items
- ✅ Clicking items works smoothly
- ✅ No performance lag

---

### Test Scenario 10: Data Accuracy Check

**Setup**: View dropdowns for different team members

**Steps**:
1. Note a team member's "45 commits"
2. Open commits dropdown
3. Count items in dropdown
4. Check first and last commit dates against actual data

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Dropdown shows exactly 45 items
- ✅ No duplicates
- ✅ No missing items
- ✅ Dates match GitHub data
- ✅ Commit messages are accurate

---

## Implementation Details

### Frontend Components Needed

1. **Metric Number Component** (React/Vue)
   - Renders the number with styling
   - Handles hover/click events
   - Triggers dropdown on hover

2. **Dropdown Component**
   - Displays list of items
   - Handles positioning (stays on-screen)
   - Handles close/escape logic
   - Shows loading state if needed
   - Has scrolling for large datasets

3. **Dropdown Item Component**
   - Single item in dropdown
   - Clickable link
   - Hover effect
   - Keyboard navigation support

### Backend API (No Changes Needed)

- Can use existing activity API response
- Existing API should already include:
  - List of commits (with hashes, messages, dates)
  - List of PRs (with numbers, titles, statuses, dates)
  - List of reviews (with PR numbers, comment counts, dates)
- If data isn't available, might need small API enhancement


---

## Definition of Done

This story is complete when:

✅ All 15 acceptance criteria are met  
✅ All 10 test scenarios pass  
✅ Dropdown appears on hover (desktop) and tap (mobile)  
✅ All links navigate to correct GitHub URLs  
✅ Keyboard navigation works  
✅ Mobile-friendly and accessible  
✅ No performance issues  
✅ Code reviewed and approved  
✅ Unit tests written (>80% coverage)  
✅ Integration tests passing  
✅ QA sign-off obtained  
✅ Documentation updated  
✅ Deployed to staging and verified  

---

## Success Metrics

| Metric | Target | Why It Matters |
|--------|--------|----------------|
| Dropdown Load Time | <200ms | Users perceive it as instant |
| Click-through Rate | >30% of hoverers | Users find value in the feature |
| Completion Rate | >95% of attempted navigations | Feature works reliably |
| User Satisfaction | >4.5/5 stars | Users like the feature |
| Error Rate | <1% | No broken links or errors |
| Mobile Usage | >40% of interactions | Mobile support is working |

---

## Notes for Developer

### Technical Considerations

1. **Performance**: Use React/Vue memoization to prevent unnecessary re-renders
2. **Data Source**: Get data from existing API response, don't make new requests
3. **Positioning**: Use a library like Popper.js for smart dropdown positioning
4. **Animations**: Keep animations smooth but not distracting
5. **Accessibility**: Use semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and keyboard events
6. **Mobile**: Use `@media (hover: none)` to detect touch devices

### Potential Challenges

- Dropdown positioning (ensuring it stays visible)
- Performance with large datasets (1000+ items)
- Keyboard navigation in nested structures
- Screen reader announcements
- Browser compatibility for modern CSS

title: Modify Report & Audit Log Filter Options
content:
Problem description:
## Problem Statement

Currently, the Resource Management Portal provides report and audit log filtering options for **daily, weekly, and monthly** timeframes. However, this granularity doesn't match business reporting needs:

- **Daily filters** are too granular (too much noise in audit logs)
- **Weekly filters** are useful for quick status checks
- **Monthly filters** are standard for most reports
- **Missing**: Quarterly and yearly views which are essential for:
  - Quarterly business reviews (QBR)
  - Annual performance reviews
  - Yearly trend analysis
  - Compliance reporting

**Current Limitation**: Cannot easily view or filter role changes and audit logs by quarter or year, requiring manual data consolidation.

---

## Goal

Update the filter options in the Resource Management Portal from:

❌ **Current**: Daily → Weekly → Monthly

To:

✅ **Updated**: Weekly → Monthly → Quarterly → Yearly

This enables better reporting and analysis aligned with business cycles.

---

## Non-Goals

- ❌ Custom date range selection (separate story if needed)
- ❌ Automatic scheduling of reports
- ❌ Email distribution of reports
- ❌ Historical data recalculation
- ❌ Changes to dashboard metrics display

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Acceptance Criteria 1: Remove Daily Filter

**Given**: An admin is viewing reports or audit logs  
**When**: The filter dropdown is displayed  
**Then**:

- [ ] The "Daily" filter option is **removed** from all dropdowns
- [ ] No reports can be filtered by "Daily"
- [ ] No audit logs can be filtered by "Daily"
- [ ] Help text/tooltips no longer mention "Daily"

**Example**:
```
Before: ⭕ Daily  ⭕ Weekly  ⭕ Monthly
After:           ⭕ Weekly  ⭕ Monthly
```

---

### Acceptance Criteria 2: Add Quarterly Filter

**Given**: An admin is viewing reports or audit logs  
**When**: The filter dropdown is displayed  
**Then**:

- [ ] A new "Quarterly" filter option appears
- [ ] Filter options are: Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Yearly
- [ ] This should be a dropdown value for user to select the quarter
- [ ] Quarterly filter works for:
  - Audit log filtering (show changes from a specific quarter)
  - Report generation (Q1 2026, Q2 2026, Q3 2026, Q4 2026)
  - Date range automatically calculated (e.g., Q2 = Apr 1 - Jun 30)
- [ ] Works for current year and previous years

**Example Usage**:
```
Admin needs Q3 2026 activity report
Filter: Q3 2026 (Jul 1 - Sep 30)
Result: Shows all role changes and activities from that quarter
```

**Quarterly Logic**:
- Q1 = January 1 - March 31
- Q2 = April 1 - June 30
- Q3 = July 1 - September 30
- Q4 = October 1 - December 31

**Example**:
```
Before: ⭕ Daily  ⭕ Weekly  ⭕ Monthly
After:           ⭕ Weekly  ⭕ Monthly ⭕ Quarterly
```
---

### Acceptance Criteria 3: Add Yearly Filter

**Given**: An admin is viewing reports or audit logs  
**When**: The filter dropdown is displayed  
**Then**:

- [ ] A new "Yearly" filter option appears
- [ ] This should be a dropdown
- [ ] Admin can select any year (2024, 2025, 2026, etc.)
- [ ] Shows complete year data (Jan 1 - Dec 31)
- [ ] Yearly filter works for:
  - Annual performance reviews
  - Year-over-year comparisons
  - Compliance and audit trails
  - Annual reports

**Example Usage**:
```
Admin needs 2026 performance review data
Filter: 2026 (Jan 1 - Dec 31)
Result: Shows complete year's data for all role assignments and activities
```
```
Before: ⭕ Daily  ⭕ Weekly  ⭕ Monthly
After:           ⭕ Weekly  ⭕ Monthly ⭕ Quarterly ⭕ Yearly
```


---

### Acceptance Criteria 4: Update All Report Types

**Given**: Any report type in the system  
**When**: The admin accesses filtering options  
**Then**:

The new filter options (Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Yearly) are available in:

- [ ] Activity Tracking report
- [ ] Audit Trail / Change Logs
- [ ] Activity by Role Reports

**All filters work consistently across all reports**

---

### Acceptance Criteria 5: Display Filter Label Clearly

**Given**: An admin has selected a filter  
**When**: They are viewing report results  
**Then**:

- [ ] The selected timeframe is displayed clearly (e.g., "Q3 2026" or "2026")
- [ ] The actual date range is shown (e.g., "Jul 1 - Sep 30")
- [ ] Users always know what timeframe they're looking at
- [ ] Cannot accidentally view data without knowing the timeframe

### Acceptance Criteria 6: Update Monthly Filter

**Given**: An admin has selected monthly filter  
**When**: They are viewing report results  
**Then**:

- [ ] The monthly filter should be a drop down
- [ ] It should give value from January to December
- [ ] Once admin selects the month, the report for that particular month should be displayed
---

## Testing Scenarios

### Test Scenario 1: Quarterly Filter Works

**Setup**: Admin wants to see Q2 2026 audit logs

**Steps**:
1. Admin navigates to "dashboard"
2. Selects "Quarterly"
3. System shows Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 options
4. Admin selects "Q2 2026"

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Shows changes from Apr 1 - Jun 30, 2026
- ✅ Displays "Q2 2026 (Apr 1 - Jun 30)" as header
- ✅ Number of entries reflects Q2 only (not entire month range)
- ✅ All changes within that quarter visible

---

### Test Scenario 2: Yearly Filter Works

**Setup**: Admin needs annual performance review data for 2026

**Steps**:
1. Admin navigates to "Reports" 
2. Selects "Yearly"
3. System shows year options
4. Admin selects "2026"

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Shows all data from Jan 1 - Dec 31, 2026
- ✅ Header shows "2026 (Jan 1 - Dec 31)"
- ✅ Complete year data included
- ✅ Can compare with 2025 if available

---

### Test Scenario 3: Daily Filter Removed

**Setup**: Admin tries to use old "Daily" filter

**Steps**:
1. Admin opens filter dropdown
2. Looks for "Daily" option

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ "Daily" option is NOT present
- ✅ Only Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Yearly shown
- ✅ No broken links or error messages

---

### Test Scenario 4: All Reports Support New Filters

**Setup**: Test that all report types use new filters

**Steps**:
1. Open "Team Structure Report"
2. Change filter to Quarterly
3. Switch to "Activity by Role Report"
4. Verify filter is available
5. Repeat for each report type

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Quarterly filter available in ALL reports
- ✅ Yearly filter available in ALL reports
- ✅ Consistent behavior across all report types

### Test Scenario 4: Monthly filter works

**Setup**: Admin tries to use Monthly Filter

**Steps**:
1. Admin move to dashboard page
2. Selects Monthly filter and chose month
3. Verify filter is available


**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Quarterly filter available in ALL reports
- ✅ Yearly filter available in ALL reports
- ✅ Monthly filter updated
- ✅ Consistent behavior across all report types


---

## Implementation Details

### Frontend Changes Needed

1. **Filter Dropdown Component**
   - Remove "Daily" option
   - Add "Quarterly" option (with Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4)
   - Add "Yearly" option (with year selector)
   - Update styling and labels

2. **Report Display**
   - Update header to show selected timeframe
   - Example: "Q3 2026 (Jul 1 - Sep 30)"
   - Update chart/table data based on new filter


### Backend Changes Needed

1. **API Endpoints**
   - Modify filter parameters
   - Update date range calculations for quarterly data
   - Ensure yearly data aggregation works correctly

2. **Data Queries**
   - Adjust SQL queries to handle quarterly date ranges
   - Ensure yearly aggregations are efficient
   - Maintain backward compatibility

### Database

No database schema changes needed - only data query logic updates.


---

## Acceptance Checklist

Before marking this story as DONE:

- [ ] Daily filter completely removed
- [ ] Quarterly filter working in all reports
- [ ] Yearly filter working in all reports
- [ ] All report types tested
- [ ] Audit logs tested with new filters
- [ ] Help documentation updated
- [ ] No broken UI or error messages
- [ ] Performance acceptable (<2 seconds for any filter)
- [ ] QA sign-off obtained

---

## Business Rationale

### Why This Change?

**Current Problem**: 
- Managers need quarterly data for QBR (Quarterly Business Review)
- HR needs yearly data for annual reviews
- Manual consolidation of daily/weekly/monthly data is tedious

**Solution**:
- Direct quarterly filtering for QBR reports
- Direct yearly filtering for annual reviews
- Aligns with standard business cycles
- Reduces manual work

### Who Benefits?

- **Managers**: Quarterly data for business reviews
- **HR**: Yearly data for performance reviews
- **Admins**: Better organized report filtering
- **Finance**: Annual trend analysis

title: User Story: Resource Management Portal - Team Role Management System
content:
Problem description:
## Problem Statement

Currently, the GitHub Activity Tracker can monitor and record all GitHub activities (commits, pull requests, issues, code reviews) from team members across MOSIP and Inji projects. However, **there is no way to track what role each team member has** and **no mechanism to manage role changes over time**.

This creates several business problems:

1. **No Role Visibility**: We cannot see who is a developer, tech lead, architect, or in any other role
2. **No Role-Based Metrics**: We cannot generate reports showing "How many commits did Tech Leads make?" vs "How many commits did Developers make?"
3. **Manual Role Tracking**: When someone gets promoted or moves to a different project, there's no system to record this
4. **No Historical Data**: When doing yearly performance reviews, we cannot see what role someone was in during each quarter
5. **Project Transitions Not Tracked**: When team members move from MOSIP to Inji project or vice versa, there's no record of when or why
6. **Team Composition Unknown**: We don't know the current team structure (how many developers, architects, QA engineers, etc. we have)

### Current Situation
- ✅ We have GitHub user data
- ✅ We track all activities
- ❌ **We do NOT have role information**
- ❌ **We cannot track role changes**
- ❌ **We cannot generate role-based reports**

---

## Goals

### Goal A: Implement Role Assignment & Management System

**What We Want To Achieve**:

Enable administrators to **assign specific job roles to each GitHub team member** so that we can:
- Know who has which role (Developer, Tech Lead, Architect, Product Owner, Leadership, QA Engineer, DevOps Engineer)
- Track when roles were assigned
- Track role changes (promotions, demotions, lateral moves)
- Maintain complete history of all role changes
- Support team members moving between MOSIP and Inji projects

**How It Benefits Us**:
- Managers can see team composition at any point in time
- Role-based analytics become possible
- Yearly performance reviews can show work by role
- Team structure is documented and auditable

---

### Goal B: Restrict Access to Administrators Only

**What We Want To Achieve**:

Ensure that **only authorized administrators** (those with admin access to our GitHub repository) can:
- View the role management portal
- Assign roles to team members
- Change team member roles
- Deactivate accounts when people leave
- Manage project transitions
- View audit logs of who changed what

**How It Benefits Us**:
- Protects sensitive team information
- Prevents unauthorized changes to role assignments
- Creates accountability (audit trail of who made changes)
- Follows security best practices using existing GitHub authentication

---

## Non-Goals

The following are **NOT** part of this requirement:

❌ Self-service role assignments (team members assigning their own roles)  
❌ Automatic role changes based on activity patterns  
❌ Integration with MOSIP's identity management system  
❌ Email notifications for role changes (can be added later)  
❌ Role approvals or workflows (admins decide, no approval process)  
❌ Custom role creation (fixed set of 7 roles only)  
❌ Role-based permissions/access control for code repositories  
❌ Machine learning to suggest roles  

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Feature 1: Role Assignment

**User Story**: As an admin, I want to assign a role to a GitHub team member so that we start tracking their role.

**Given**: An admin is logged into the system  
**When**: Admin selects a GitHub user and assigns them a role (Developer, Tech Lead, Architect, Product Owner, Leadership, QA, DevOps Engineer) for a project (MOSIP or Inji) with a start date  
**Then**:

- [ ] The role assignment is saved in the system
- [ ] The system prevents assigning multiple active roles to the same person in the same project
- [ ] A record is created with: User, Project, Role, Start Date, End Date, Who Created It
- [ ] An audit log entry is created showing: "Admin username assigned role X to user Y for project Z on [date]"
- [ ] The user can see this assignment in their profile/history
- [ ] The system shows "Role active since [start date]" when viewing the user
- [ ] End date  should be null

**Example**:
- Admin logs in → Sees "Assign Role" button
- Clicks button → Form appears
- Selects: "john_doe", Project: "MOSIP", Role: "Developer", Start Date: "2024-01-15"
- Clicks "Assign"
- System shows: "John Doe successfully assigned as Developer for MOSIP since Jan 15, 2024"

---

### Feature 2: Role Promotion/Change

**User Story**: As an admin, I want to change a team member's role (promote or demote) with clear tracking of when the change happened.

**Given**: A team member has an active role assignment  
**When**: Admin changes the role (e.g., Developer → Tech Lead) and provides a new start date for the new role  
**Then**:

- [ ] The old role automatically ends the day before the new role starts
- [ ] The system creates a NEW role record for the new role
- [ ] The old role record shows "ended on [date]"
- [ ] Both old and new records are visible in the member's history
- [ ] An audit log shows: "Admin username promoted john_doe from Developer to Tech Lead on [date]"
- [ ] Yearly reports can show: "Q1 role: Developer, Q2 role: Tech Lead" etc.

**Example**:
- Admin selects john_doe (currently a Developer since Jan 2024)
- Admin clicks "Update Role"
- Form appears with: New Role: "Tech Lead", New Start Date: "2024-06-01"
- Admin clicks "Update"
- System shows:
  - Old record: Developer, Jan 15 - May 31 (CLOSED)
  - New record: Tech Lead, Jun 1 - Present (ACTIVE)

---

### Feature 3: Project Transition (MOSIP ↔ Inji)

**User Story**: As an admin, I want to move a team member from one project to another while maintaining their role and history.

**Given**: A team member is assigned to one project (MOSIP)  
**When**: Admin transfers them to a different project (Inji) with an effective date  
**Then**:

- [ ] Their assignment to the old project ends on the day before transfer
- [ ] A new assignment is created in the new project
- [ ] Their role can stay the same or be changed during transfer
- [ ] History shows both projects in their record
- [ ] Audit log shows: "Admin username transferred john_doe from MOSIP to Inji on [date]"
- [ ] Annual reports can show: "First half of year: MOSIP project, Second half: Inji project"

**Example**:
- john_doe: MOSIP/Developer since Jan 2024
- Admin transfers to: Inji/Developer starting July 2024
- System shows:
  - MOSIP assignment: Jan 15 - Jun 30 (CLOSED)
  - Inji assignment: Jul 1 - Present (ACTIVE)
- Yearly report shows activities split by project and role

---

### Feature 4: Account Deactivation & Reactivation

**User Story**: As an admin, I want to deactivate a team member's account when they leave and reactivate it if they return.

**Given**: An admin needs to remove a team member (they left the company)  
**When**: Admin marks the account as "Inactive" with a deactivation date and reason  
**Then**:

- [ ] The account status changes to "INACTIVE"
- [ ] All active role assignments automatically end on the deactivation date
- [ ] All their historical data is preserved (not deleted)
- [ ] An audit log shows: "Admin username deactivated john_doe on [date], reason: [provided reason]"
- [ ] The user no longer appears in "active members" lists
- [ ] Historical reports still include their data for the period they were active

**And When**: Admin reactivates the account (person returns)  
**Then**:

- [ ] The account status changes back to "ACTIVE"
- [ ] A new role assignment is created for their return
- [ ] An audit log shows: "Admin username reactivated john_doe on [date]"
- [ ] They appear in active members lists again

**Example - Deactivation**:
- Admin: "john_doe left the company on May 28, 2026"
- All of john's assignments close on May 28
- All historical data preserved
- Audit log: "Admin deactivated john_doe - Left organization"

**Example - Reactivation**:
- Admin: "john_doe is returning on June 1, 2026 as a Tech Lead on Inji project"
- New assignment created: Inji/Tech Lead starting June 1
- Account marked ACTIVE
- Audit log: "Admin reactivated john_doe - Returning to organization"

---

### Feature 5: Viewing Role History

**User Story**: As an admin or manager, I want to see the complete role history of a team member so I understand their career progression.

**Given**: An admin views a team member's profile  
**When**: Admin clicks "View History"  
**Then**:

- [ ] A timeline is displayed showing all role changes
- [ ] Each entry shows: Role, Project, Start Date, End Date, Duration
- [ ] Current role is clearly marked as "ACTIVE"
- [ ] Past roles show with end dates
- [ ] Examples:
  - "Developer @ MOSIP, Jan 15 2024 - May 31 2024 (5 months)"
  - "Tech Lead @ MOSIP, Jun 1 2024 - Present (12 months, ACTIVE)"
- [ ] The timeline is sortable and filterable by date/project/role

---

### Feature 6: Admin-Only Access Control

**User Story**: As a system administrator, I want to ensure that only GitHub repository admins can access the role management portal so that sensitive information is protected.

**Given**: A user tries to access the Resource Management Portal  
**When**: They click on the portal link  
**Then**:

- [ ] They are redirected to GitHub login
- [ ] After GitHub login, the system checks: "Does this person have admin access to Varaniya201/mosip-labs repository?"
- [ ] **If YES (Admin)**: Grant access to the portal
- [ ] **If NO (Not Admin)**: Show message "You don't have access to this portal. Contact an administrator."
- [ ] Session expires after 24 hours of inactivity (auto-logout)
- [ ] Every action is logged: "Admin username performed action X at [time]"

**Example Access Scenarios**:

| User | GitHub Status | Portal Access |
|------|---------------|---------------|
| Alice | Admin of Varaniya201/mosip-labs | ✅ ALLOWED |
| Bob | Collaborator (not admin) | ❌ DENIED |
| Charlie | No access to repo | ❌ DENIED |
| Diana | Recently removed as admin | ❌ DENIED (immediately) |

**Why This Matters**: 
- Sensitive role information is protected
- Only authorized people can make role changes
- All changes are auditable (we know who did what)

---

### Feature 7: Audit Trail & Accountability

**User Story**: As a compliance officer, I want a complete audit trail of all role changes so we can track who made what changes and when.

**Given**: Any admin action occurs (assign role, change role, transfer project, deactivate account)  
**When**: The action is completed  
**Then**:

- [ ] An audit log entry is created with:
  - Who did it (admin username, GitHub ID)
  - What they did (action: create, update, deactivate, etc.)
  - Who it affected (team member name)
  - When it happened (timestamp)
  - What changed (old value → new value)
  - Why they did it (optional reason/notes)
- [ ] Admins can view the complete audit log
- [ ] Audit log cannot be deleted or modified (immutable)
- [ ] Reports can be generated showing all changes in a date range

**Example Audit Log Entry**:
```
Timestamp: 2026-05-28 10:30 AM
Admin: sarah_admin (GitHub: 789456)
Action: ROLE_CHANGED
User: john_doe
Details: Promoted from Developer to Tech Lead
Old Role: Developer (since Jan 15, 2024)
New Role: Tech Lead (starting Jun 1, 2024)
Reason: "Demonstrated technical excellence and leadership potential"
```

**Why This Matters**:
- Compliance and auditing (who changed what when)
- Accountability (can't hide role changes)
- Dispute resolution ("When was I promoted?" → Check audit log)

## Acceptance Criteria - System Level

### Non-Functional Requirements

**Performance**:
- [ ] Portal loads in less than 2 seconds
- [ ] Role assignment takes less than 3 seconds
- [ ] Reports generate in less than 10 seconds
- [ ] System can handle 1000+ concurrent users

**Reliability**:
- [ ] System uptime: 99.9% (max 4.4 hours downtime per year)
- [ ] All data is automatically backed up daily
- [ ] Failed transactions are logged for troubleshooting

**Usability**:
- [ ] No admin needs training to use the portal
- [ ] Forms have helpful hints and validation messages
- [ ] Error messages are clear and actionable

**Security**:
- [ ] Only GitHub admins can access (verified via GitHub API)
- [ ] All sensitive data encrypted in transit (HTTPS)
- [ ] Passwords never stored (using GitHub auth)
- [ ] Session expires after 24 hours

---

## Testing Scenarios

### Test Scenario 1: Happy Path - New Team Member

**Setup**: Sarah (admin) wants to add alex_dev (new GitHub developer) to MOSIP project

**Steps**:
1. Sarah logs into the portal with her GitHub account
2. System verifies she's an admin of Varaniya201/mosip-labs
3. Sarah clicks "Assign Role"
4. Sarah fills form: alex_dev, MOSIP, Developer, Start: "2026-05-28"
5. Sarah clicks "Assign"

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Confirmation message appears
- ✅ alex_dev appears in team structure
- ✅ Audit log shows assignment
- ✅ alex_dev's activities from May 28 onwards will be attributed to "Developer" role

---

### Test Scenario 2: Promotion

**Setup**: john_doe (Developer since Jan 2024) gets promoted to Tech Lead

**Steps**:
1. Admin navigates to john_doe's profile
2. Clicks "Update Role"
3. Selects "Tech Lead" as new role
4. Sets start date: "2024-06-01"
5. Adds reason: "Demonstrated technical excellence"
6. Clicks "Update"

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Old record closes: Developer, Jan 15 - May 31 (5 months)
- ✅ New record created: Tech Lead, Jun 1 - Present
- ✅ History shows both roles
- ✅ Activity attribution changes: Jun 1 onwards = Tech Lead activities
- ✅ Audit log shows promotion

---

### Test Scenario 3: Access Control

**Setup**: Test that non-admins cannot access the portal

**Steps**:
1. Bob (developer, not admin) tries to access portal
2. System redirects to GitHub login
3. Bob logs in with his GitHub account
4. System checks his GitHub permissions

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ Bob is NOT admin of Varaniya201/mosip-labs
- ✅ Portal shows error: "You don't have access to this portal"
- ✅ Bob is NOT allowed to view any role data
- ✅ No audit log entry (access denied)

---

### Test Scenario 4: Deactivation & Reactivation

**Setup**: mike_qa is leaving the company

**Deactivation Steps**:
1. Admin goes to mike_qa's profile
2. Clicks "Deactivate Account"
3. Sets deactivation date: "2026-05-28"
4. Reason: "Left organization"
5. Confirms

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ mike_qa appears as "INACTIVE"
- ✅ All his open role assignments close on May 28
- ✅ Historical data preserved (for reports)
- ✅ No longer in "active team members" count

**Reactivation Steps** (6 months later):
1. Admin reopens mike_qa's profile
2. Clicks "Reactivate"
3. Sets new role: "QA Engineer", Project: "Inji", Start: "2026-11-15"
4. Confirms

**Expected Results**:
- ✅ mike_qa marked as "ACTIVE" again
- ✅ New role assignment created
- ✅ Appears in team count again
- ✅ Complete history visible: Left May 28, Returned Nov 15

---
## Definition of Done

This feature is complete when:

- ✅ All acceptance criteria are met
- ✅ All tests pass (>80% code coverage)
- ✅ All scenarios tested and passed
- ✅ Admin documentation written
- ✅ User guide created
- ✅ All data is encrypted and secure
- ✅ Audit logs functional and tested
- ✅ Performance targets met
- ✅ Security reviewed and approved
- ✅ Admins trained and comfortable using it
- ✅ Production deployment completed


**Impact**:
- Better team planning and resource allocation
- Accurate performance metrics by role
- Compliance and audit readiness
- Improved decision-making with role-based data

title: MOSIP-42813: Collab | Un-Subscription & UIN Data Deletion via email
content:
Problem description:
*Problem Statement*: Community users currently lack a simple way to unsubscribe from Collab emails, leading to unwanted communications and a suboptimal user experience.

*Proposed Solution*: Introducing an unsubscribe mechanism will empower users with control over their communication preferences, improve compliance with privacy regulations, and build greater trust in the platform by ensuring that only relevant and opted-in communications are delivered.

*Title*
*As a* Community User, 
*I want the ability to* unsubscribe from Collab emails through a simple process, 
*So that* I can stop receiving communications that I no longer find relevant.

*Basic Flow:*

1. Every email contains an *Unsubscribe* link at the bottom.

1. Clicking the link redirects the user to a https://forms.gle/EDFs6gi7pdjmAgZ36 to capture relevant details for unsubscribing.

1. The form includes the following fields:
## *Header:* MOSIP Collab – Email Un-Subscription Form
## *Description:* We are sorry to see you go. Please complete the form below to unsubscribe from all future emails from the MOSIP Collab environment.
## *E-Mail** (enter the email you wish to unsubscribe)
## *Form Fields:*
### *Reason for Unsubscribing** (dropdown):
###* I no longer wish to receive these emails
###* The content is not relevant to me
###* I receive emails too frequently
###* I didn’t sign up for these emails
###* Others 
## *Additional Comments* (optional)
## *“I agree to unsubscribe”** (checkbox)
## *Submit* (button)
## A clear note is displayed on the form: Unsubscribing will also delete your associated UIN. Once unsubscribed, you will not be able to use this UIN in the future.

1. On click of the “Submit” button, the user sees a success message: _“_You have successfully unsubscribed. Your associated UIN and related data have been deleted._”_

*Alternate Flow:* TBD based on technical feasibility
Approach 1: Redirects to Form but Submission Detects Already Unsubscribed

1. User clicks on the *Unsubscribe* link in the email.

1. The system navigates the user to the *Unsubscribe Form*. (as detailed above)

1. The user enters required details and clicks *Submit*.

1. The system checks the database and identifies that the email address is already unsubscribed.

1. The system displays a clear message:
*“You are already unsubscribed from MOSIP emails. No further action is required.”*

Approach 2: Directly Identifies Already Unsubscribed

1. User clicks on the *Unsubscribe* link in the email.

1. The system immediately checks the status of the email address in the database.

1. If the system finds that the email is already unsubscribed, it does not show the form. 

1. The user is redirected to a page that clearly states:
*“You are already unsubscribed from MOSIP emails. No further action is required.”*

*Acceptance Criteria:*

1. Every email contains an *Unsubscribe* link at the bottom (as per the UX design)

1. On submitting the form, 
## The user sees a confirmation message: _“_You have successfully unsubscribed. Your associated UIN and related data have been deleted._”_
##  The system triggers a cleanup process: The email ID is identified in the database, and the associated UIN along with any linked personal data is permanently removed from all relevant databases and tables. (What if the email ID is associated to multiple UINs?)

1. No further emails are sent to the unsubscribed address unless the user registers again and a *new UIN* is issued.

1. All unsubscribe submissions should be tracked in the backend for reporting and analytics.

*Business Rules:*

- NA

*UX Design:* TBA

title: Team Activity Tracker & Leaderboard for Project Managers
content:
Problem description:
**Description**

As a Project Manager, I want to track, visualise, and compare my team members’ activities across projects in a single dashboard, so that I can monitor progress, identify high and low engagement, recognise contributors, and take timely corrective actions.

**Acceptance Criteria**

- PM can view team-level and individual-level activity.
- Activity is aggregated by user, time period, and activity type.
- Leaderboard ranks team members based on configurable activity metrics.
- Insights help PMs identify trends, risks, and top contributors.
- Access is role-based (PM vs team member).
